Many moons ago i got this little game for my ps4 called nidhogg, it was fun and yet i can not tell you why. It reminded me a little of IK+ (a commodore 64 title when i played it) I loved the quick short combat of it but my friends would look at it and go “That is not what i bought a ps4 for” when i eventually forced a friend to play it he got bored of it fast.
Now i had an opportunity to try Nidhogg 2 before release, sadly only the pc version, (which did cause me a tiny issue with testing local multiplayer till i found i could plug a ps4 pad into the pc in attention to my xbox one pad lol) and i discovered it is more of the same but everything improved.
The friend i coerced into playing it with me sadly did not like it and got bored of it fast again however, clearly not a man of good taste! (see why i say it will divide friendships in more than one way lol)

This is a game you will want to have two pads for (there is single player arcade mode but the ai is not hard to beat and not as fun as playing vs humans you know) however if you wish to majorly inconvenience a soon to be ex friend you can let them use the keyboard while you use a pad.
One of the cool things this time out is you get a random weapon each time you spawn (in vs mode) and each weapon has its strengths and weaknesses (there is also a bow an arrow which the ai can be somewhat lethal with) it can make for some cool little fights and playing on the pc there has been a couple of times i have reached instinctively for the ps4’s share button to quickly save a clip only to remember i am on pc lol.

Again a vast improvement over the original and i really like the random characters you can make, the graphics will still put off some though who still do not fully understand that gameplay is king not graphics (makes me sad when i hear people moaning about a games graphics without playing it)
The environments are also improved this time around it almost seems a shame to mess them up with the blood of your enemies….almost…. :)

It will take a little while to work out how to throw stuff, the weapons pros and cons but ultimately you grasp the core concepts pretty fast.



If you liked the first one then this is a no brainer, it maintains the feel of the original while at the same time surpassing it in every way.
If you are new to Nidhogg then know what you are getting is a cheap game that is fun in short doses. I like the game, i liked the original, so i am recommending it, however it should be noted that my friends who tried it did not like it, but this is my review, not theirs lol.

Loved the original Nidhogg, lost many hours to it.  Not a fan of the new art style, feels like I should be taking a psychadelic while playing...  that said, it's more Nidhogg, further refined.  GOTY.

+ The graphics were decent for a game that was released in 2010. There are quite a lot of details on characters. The areas look pretty neat as well.
- Many characters are clones and animations could be smoother here and there.
+ The music is good overall but really not as amazing as it was in past Gothic games. The voice acting in the English version is completely horrible and makes you cringe at times. Stream should allow players to decide themselves which sound packs to install. The german voice acting is much better.
- The environment does not make too much sound. You would expect to hear animals and other things.
+ You can clearly feel that your character is developing and there are 4 difficulties.
- The 4 difficulties are meaningless. Having played the game on 'Gothic' which is supposed to be the hardest difficulty I have never felt like the game was hard. I have never died a lot except for the last boss which was the first time I started using pots and buffs. Funnily enough I only died 3 times on the last boss which isn't even a lot.
+ Many dialogues are neat if it wasn't for the horrible voice acting. You can feel part of the world. You keep meeting characters you met before and NPCs seem to be moving with you. You also meet old characters from past Gothic games which is a big plus for fans of the franchise.
- The world is very stale and boring. There is nothing to explore except things that you are meant to explore. You can only quest in the area you are meant to quest. All areas are cut off and you can only progress once you do the required main quest. The atmosphere is long not as brilliant as in past Gothic games.
+ The UI is decent and I never had issues with controlling my character. You can put up to 10 items and spells on your bar which is more than enough. In addition you can bind the keys.
- The character gets 'stuck' pretty often when he shouldn't be. Sometimes he gets stuck while simply running which forces you to jump occasionally.
+ The game is somewhat long. It took me 40 hours to finish but that's including doing extremely boring quests which forces you to run through the entire world to look for hidden artifacts.
- Many areas have nothing special in them. Sometimes you run through a jungle area in which you do nothing at all except run. Why not put one quest where nearby orcs have stolen or killed a friend? Instead there are just random little camps with orcs which you clear and move on. A lot of potential was lost. There are also barely any side-quests at all.
+ The questing is very bad in Arcania. There are nearly no side-quests. However the story starts off in an interesting way.
- Most quests are only about either killing a few monsters or bringing the NPC a few items. The quest stories are also very boring and even when you can do it in more than 1 way it has no effect on the story or even the rewards.
+ The charactersystem is decent. Most of the abilities are useful and you can specialize in things.
- However the system is very simple and boring. You barely have a choice in what to specialize in since there are so little abilities and you will learn all by the end.
+ The comatis fast and interactive. You have to dodge certain attacks which you cannot parry. Other attacks can be parried if you are fast enough.
- The AI is horrible. Many monsters simply keep hitting you with special attacks which force you to dodge. They also hit so slow that it is no challenge to get away from them before they hit you. There are also only 3 spells in the game which make being a Mage pretty boring.
+ There are many items and you can craft a lot of items yourself.
- The crafting is useless though. I played the entire game on the hardest difficulty and have never crafted a single pot. When the game was over my inventory was still filled with all kinds of materials. I only crafted around 3 items to wear. Many items were simply useless. You also get new armour very rarely when the game decides you should get a new armour.

Arcania is a futile attempt at an RPG.
The graphics are bad and bland, and the game runs slow even on a decent computer. You can't turn off the unnecessarily dense grass (which is probably the main reason for my low fps count) and there isn't much other choice for changing the graphic options. I thought the ability to alter the saturation and contrast was nice, though, especially since the game is extremely grey by default.
The characters are boring and the voice-acting is atrocious. The lip-syncing is really terrible to behold (honestly, games that are 5 years older than this have better lip-syncing) and the cutscenes are a joke. Speaking of jokes, character who make jokes in this game deliver the lines in a completely unconvincing manner and nothing about it is funny. The main character himself sounds like a whining, petulant sook.
The controls are clunky and unresponsive. Fighting in this game is particularly difficult because of the multiple keys required for different fighting techniques. Hit detection is off and a lot of the time you'll just flat-out miss your target. The general movement feels jagged and the gravity is really... wrong. Some objects have particularly large collision boxes which means you'll often get stuck on nothing, and there are a lot of places where you can be standing on thin-air. On the other hand, there are also objects where the collision is entirely missing, so you'll just walk straight through them.
Picking up objects off the ground is hard, for crying out loud!
The UI is confusing and laggy, and finding stuff in it is overly complicated. I was afraid to go into the menus because I didn't feel like I had sufficient control to do what I wanted to. Finding things on the map was difficult at times, and I got lost a lot because it was hard to tell which direction I was facing. Some of the tutorials in the game were unhelpful and I often had to look online how to do stuff.
I didn't care about the storyline and there was no drive to continue playing after the first few missions. As I said before, the characters are uninteresting and I didn't care what happened to them. For some reason, you start off as a King in an evil looking castle, fighting some skeletons and stuff, and then all of a sudden, you're playing as that young, annoying farmer guy. The first missions were a series of side-quests which appeared to have no relevance to anything besides "teaching" you to play the game, and to introduce you to characters who you completely leave behind about an hour into the game.
The most fun I had with Arcania was when I stopped playing it and uninstalled it. Do you know how pleasurable it was to click uninstall? VERY!
Honestly, this game feels incomplete. No, wait, scratch that. This game IS incomplete. I wouldn't even consider this game Early Access, let alone a full release. It is a sad excuse for a game, or even any form of entertainment. It was a chore.
Do yourself a favour and don't buy this game. I got it in a Humble Bundle for cheap as chips and still feel like I was ripped off.

Pyre
It's hard to stand out in the crowd. We live in an age where gaming has never been more popular, and as a result, the temptation to stick to known genres is stronger than ever. A game doesn't have to be original to achieve financial success or notoriety, it just has to iterate on standard designs. Pyre takes this practice and throws it to the wind. It creates its own path. Instead of following a blueprint, it takes some ideas and blends them into something original. Pyre is brave, unique, and a strong game.
So, rather than try to define Pyre by genre, let's just look at it piece by piece. The narrative framework of Pyre is that you play as the "Reader"; an faceless outcast to the "Downside". Naming the world the "Downside" is perfect for what this place is; a purgatory for exiles from the world proper. Not hell, but a place where one's inner characteristics and traits are personified. This is the characters' downside, literally. You will meet other exiles and given opportunities to discover their story. What were they before coming to the Downside? Why were they exiled? Hyperlinks in the conversations provide a good way of relaying contextual information. As your journey in the Downside progresses, you become part of the team known as the Nightwings and do battle against other triumvirate teams in battles known as "Rites". These culminate in a "Liberation Rite" in which, if you win, you can choose to liberate one of your teammates from the Downside. Post the first liberation rite, the world opens up from the linear track it took to get there. There is a significant lore dump, which felt somewhat awkward. This cycle repeats a few times until, ultimately, you have to decide your own fate.
The story is well told and interesting. World lore is conveyed by the Book of Rites which you gain access to piece by piece. There are tones of social change, revolution, and individuation. There is a really nice balance between darker themes, while maintaining some whimsical trappings. The fantastical setting provides a good canvas to tell a daunting story. Supergiant has always shown expert level ability to convey themes and tone through both writing, music, and visuals, and that continues in Pyre.
Early on in Pyre, the narrative is fairly linear. There are few real choices early on, with a couple dialogue trees. Dialogue is sort of a 'choose your own adventure' path choice. This escalates later in the game, and dialogue choices start to have consequences. Pyre's mechanic for making your choices feel meaningful is by referencing that choice several times is subsequent dialogues. Sometimes characters will receive stat boosts or penalties based on a choice you made, whereas other times it will alter a relationship in some way. A good example is when you are given the task of naming the stowaway character. Whatever you choose, her name will be fully voiced by the narrator in the game. It evokes a sense of infinite options. The downside (pun intended) of the focus on dialogue, is that there are really only two methods of interaction in Pyre; dialogue and combat.
Ah, the combat. If you have read anything else about this game you have seen the multiple ways it has been described. Pyreball, Sportsdunking, etc. Whatever you want to call it, combat in Pyre is different from any other video game you've played. Personally, I really enjoyed it. There is certainly some patience involved in getting comfortable with it, and a learning curve to feel competent in executing certain strategies. Initially, it almost felt too easy, even tedious. It gets more intense over time. In fact, once you realize that you only get one shot at each rite, I found myself narrowly getting the win and feeling really satisfied. A common theme with Supergiant games is the ability to coordinate talents and skills, and this holds for Pyre. Finding builds and synergies amongst your team feels good. Speaking of feel, Pyre has to be played with a controller for any semblance of coordination. Fortunately, the game seamlessly switches between controller and keyboard controls on the fly.
I own the soundtrack to all three Supergiant games, and if I had to rank them Pyre would be my favourite (although Bastion is close). Each Supergiant game could be seen as an album in its own right; their music is that good. In Pyre, there is a greater variety of musical genre represented than the previous games. It mixes guitars, bass, piano, and other more exotic instruments to create tracks that wander the spectrum of rock, electronic, and acoustic folk music. The music of conveys the mood of the game. A nice touch is the ability to select the music in the wagon. Furthermore, each enemy team you face has its own theme music. This gives them great personality ranging from formal, menacing, humorous, and chaotic. It reminded me of Star Control 2 when you meet different species. The music becomes instantly associated with that race/team. Speaking of old games, I was absolutely convinced that "The Voice" was played by David Warner (aka Jon Irenicus/Morpheus/Gul Madred). It's not, but listen to it again and tell me it wasn't at least inspired by his performances.
In Bastion, you had different weapons which you levelled up as you saw fit. The same idea is here, just in your companions. This is where Pyre offers the greatest level of customization. Your favourite characters are yours to develop and create a truly capable team. In my first play through, I thought the first liberation rite signaled the end of the game, but it is only the first of several. Herein lies one of the most vexing choices you as a player have to make; who to send back, your favourite character because they deserve it (thereby weakening your team), or a character you have not invested as much time in. It is one of those moments that makes you remember a game long after completing it.
The story within the story of Pyre, is the characters relationships to each other and how your choices impact their outcome. There are so many unique interactions, I was really trying hard to pay attention and understand the relationships to get the most out of the game. Herein lies one of my issues with Pyre. I stayed engaged as long as I could, but near the end of the game, Pyre felt like it was stalling the inevitable, almost grandstanding. At this point I was fatiguing badly, and tended to click though some of the content. Regretfully, this is the point where many of your choice consequences become apparent. It just felt like it needed to be a little more efficient it its use of endgame set up.
Pyre is a great game that deserves commendation for its willingness to take a chance and break the conventions that have become easy for game developers to fall back on. Glorious. Supergiant gets a Super giant thumbs up from me.
One part adventure, one part sports game. A very odd combination, but is pulled off due to the characters you meet. This game is held up by how you see the characters, and they are great. You have characters that you give a lot of respect to that you face, like the Fate. You also have one character that is made to be hated. Yeah, he's great to win against, every single time. There's your own team, and every single one of them can be loved in different ways. Also, I want a Ti'zo plushie.  At the same time, curse you Supergiant for making great characters. Ahem. Anyway.
It's a story of freedom, exile, and bonds. Not just a story about those themes, but then enforced by the game itself.
The sports aspect is also very well done. Instead of giving potentially a half-baked AI for your team, and giving the other team a great one, a single rule is enforced. Only one player can move at any one time for either team. This ends up putting an interesting twist when dashing around a unit that isn't moving. The different traits of different players makes them all feel very unique, and each one will end up giving an odd twist to the way you'll play that match. Although, it'll be more than just the opponents that will likely push you towards new tactics. That's a good thing though.
Soundtrack is glorious. All three of them.
Oh yeah, there's three soundtracks. Because just one wasn't enough. Game costs $22 CDN, and the soundtrack? $11 CDN. Is the soundtrack of high enough quality to demand half the price of the game?
Yeah. Oh yeah. It's worthy.
But seriously, this game is glorious. Don't miss out on this just because adventure, or just because sports. This game is worth your time. And then a second and maybe even a third playthrough on top of that.

For a game that got mixed reviews, I'm on the side of the more positive. As a fan of the older Gothic games, I was glad to see another Gothic game come around. After playing both XBox and PC versions of this game, hands down the PC version is the best. Not because of the better graphics, but the menus as well. On the console, the menus were kind of a pain to use and not thought out very well, whereas the PC version had easy to use menus. The game just felt as if it was designed to be played on the PC rather than a console.
One thing that striked me as odd was the disapearing foliage. I understand something like that if there's no machine that can handle playing it, but why have this in a game at all? It really felt out of place, AND a menu option didn't show up for it until I messed with the game settings saved on my hard drive....just odd..
The overall story was very good, but lacked substance. Not because it was a bad story, but because the game didn't do a very good job of explaining it to you. I had to play through the game to completion before I could get an overview of the story and why you do what you do. Still, I don't understand half of it, and had to actually read about it.
The gameplay is by far the most outstanding portion of this title. I really enjoy the combat in this game as it just feels more free than your standard hotkey RPG like most MMOs. Hotkeys are present, but their more for selecting weapons and skills rather than combat.
Overall, I give a 7.5/10. If you're a hardcore RPG fan and a fan of the older Gothic games, I recommend picking up this title. It's worth the $20.

Survarium is an online, free to play, FPS game with a post-apocalyptic style. The first thing I would like to say is that the community is great around this game. The few interactions I have had with the in game player have been very enjoyable and the player seem very enthusiastic about Survarium. While being free to play Survarium is far from pay to win. This being said you can buy nearly everything in the game at the beginning with real life currency, but CANNOT buy weapons or anything that allows you to have a great advantage other players. The only thing you can buy in this game is fast track to unlocks and customizations.
Right now Survarium is just a team based fps, but the devs have said they are planning to add more content as well as a freeplay (PvE) mode. Right now Survarium is just a typical fps game with different gamemodes but the freeplay mode is really what I think will make Survarium stand out in the crowd. While the freeplay mode is what seems the most interesting thing to me, the PvP portion is done well and most of the weapons feel really good/impactful. There is plenty of customizations (clothing, weapons, items, and different camos). The best part of the PvP to me is the interesting large maps and the well done gunplay. While I can’t say Survarium is the best game, but if you enjoy competitive FPS games you should check this out. I personally looking forward to the PvE mode and can’t wait for it to be released.

An underwater story driven horror adventure set in the Atlantic that plays quite similar to their earlier title - Amnesia: The Dark Descent.
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬
Back in 2010, I was always looking for games that would run on my♥♥♥♥♥♥poor PC. Amnesia was pretty hyped (thanks to YouTube let's plays) so I got that and played it at like 15fps on that PC. It was an impressive horror game from a small studio that led to the monster chase horror game trend of which most were just as bad as my PC. SOMA however is one of the better story driven horror games from a small studio since 2010's Amnesia. It has the expected list of upgrades - better(okayish for 2016) graphics, smoother gameplay and no load screens other than when loading from a save.
I loved this story more than Amnesia's. The monsters also have some variety to them - some cant see but listen, some can - little variations like that. Even the underwater setting, at least for me, is spookier than a castle. It has mod support and thanks to a dedicated fan community there are already a few custom stories that you can play through.
This game isn't a masterpiece, it follows the usual horror tropes, in this case, waking up in an unknown place, something's odd and soon there are monsters blocking your progression through the level/story. Although SOMA does some improvements over Amnesia, it's pretty much the Amnesia formula. At least Slender and FNAF tried new things. Then there's the complete lack of an inventory system. In horror games, I find that running out of bullets/batteries and managing inventory space adds to the tension. Here, your flashlight battery never runs out. This makes the game very linear and discourages exploration and puzzle solving, at least for those who aren't so inclined towards it.

While BSG as a series features 3 'units': The Battlestar, the Viper and the Raptor, an actual strategy game needs more meat than that. There are a handful more units, such as a scout-type corvette and a missile cruiser, but there are far too few strategies and tactics made available by them to really call combat deep. There is really only one strategy: Literally stacking broadside warships, like the Adamant. Anything else is a waste of fleet space.
The AI is predictable; they rush headlong at your forces, launch an initial volley, and then break and scatter, exposing their weak sides with few guns. Your corvettes can stay in their rear and tear them apart easily; your Adamants can take the first volley head-on, then turn and broadside without their flank armor being stripped by the first strike. Your vipers absolutely cream Cylon raiders, and for the most part, are just a slight annoyance of telling them to go do something rather than an integral part of a battle.
Unfortunately, the relatively shallow combat suffers from some extremely crippling bugs. Ship movement doesn't account for collision detection prior to resolving the round of combat, which means that tight formations (Like is necessary with the only valid tactic, the full broadside fleet) can very easily result in ships ramming each other and exploding instantly. Worse, or perhaps not depending on your experience, is damage calculation.
Your ships have 6 armor values, for different facing sides. Damage counts the side that your ship was initially on at the beginning of a battle; I've had ships lose 30-40 HP turning into an enemy and taking 90% of the fire head-on, because the game is still dealing damage to their rear flank which has no armor, since that's the side that was exposed at the start of the battle. Left and Right armor are virtually non-existant, with a ship going straight from taking Rear armor damage to Front armor damage with their flanks being completely unscathed.
If this were X-COM, it would be like a character getting flanked on the enemy's turn, and then running into full cover and still dying because you BEGAN that turn exposed rather than ending it exposed - absolutely inexcusible in a squad strategy game, and absolutely inexcusible here. This not only screws up how combat actually resolves, it severely cripples what little potential maneuverable ships like the Manticore had, further relegating the game to nothing but massed Adamant broadsides, a battle you will repeat very, very, very, very, very, very, very, very often... and get tired of very quickly.
Like many others, I can't recommend it in its current state. Not only does the central gameplay fall flat, it feels so unfinished and untested that it feels like a game which was pushed out the door instead of letting it fall into development hell, which does not inspire any confidence that it will progress beyond its release state. Unless you really, really love the BSG setting, wait until it's on sale for a really great price - and even then, think 3 or 4 times before you get it. Other games have done the same style of play, much better than this.

I recently bought the Ultimate DOOM from steam instead of playing the original because I wanted to play the prequel for the second game.  This game began the FPS franchise.
This game will always be the most legendary FPS of all time.  The level designs are exceedingly creative and out of this world.  The levels become more complex and exciting as the player progresses because they can bring unexpecting things to the eyes of the player.
There is a large array of demons that have many strengths and weaknesses.  My favourite demon is the Pinky for it's speed and endurance.  There is also a wide range of weapons for the player to kill the demons in their desire.  My favourite gun will always be the BFG9000, known as the BIG ♥♥♥♥ING GUN!  This behemoth of a gun shoots a large green plasma ball to pulverise any demon with 100-800 hit points of damage.
The bosses in this game are memorable.  They can be extremely challenging to defeat at such a high difficulty like nightmare mode, which is the hardest difficulty in the game.  The final boss to finish off the game is called the spider demon.  The spider demon has been included in every game in the franchise to intimidate and♥♥♥♥♥♥the player off.
The secrets and easter eggs in this game are very surprising.  There are lots of hidden doors and elevators in the walls for the player to venture secret areas littered with exciting loot eg. soul spheres which will increase your hp to a substantial level, ammo boxes to fill your weapons up to their maximum carrying capacity, superarmour increases your armour rating up to 200 hp, and more.  In the levels, the seemingly endless amounts of rooms are scattered with exploding barrels for the player to shoot to incinerate the demons.  They can be a real pain in the♥♥♥♥♥most of the time because the player may accidently shoot the barrel to kill themselves!
The ost for this game is marvellous.  It is well made and well chosen for the levels.  The sound of the ost is very similar to anthrax and metallica.  It is so remarkable, I have even created a playlist specifically for the whole soundtrack on amazon music.
There are a couple of downsides to this game unfortunately.  Firstly, you have to purchase the expansions to fully complete the game.  eg. shores of hell and the final expansion inferno.  Luckily, with the Ultimate Doom, it is packaged with every single expansion even including the prequel for DOOM 2: Hell on Earth, Thy Flesh Consumed.  Secondly, the game is launched with the DOSbox emulator which downgrades the video resolution.  I would recommend replacing the DOSbox program with ZDOOM or GZDOOM which adds loads of graphical features to the renderer and even adds a multiplayer! This will allow you to set the resolution to your desire.  I personally prefer DOSBOX because ZDOOM and GZDOOM ruins the nostalgic feel for a 1995 shooter.

Sniper Elite V2 features good graphics, sound effects and a nice soundtrack. The story is also nice - you play an American sniper in World War II that must combat both the Russians and the Germans in hopes of ending the war in the favor of the Allies.
Sniper Elite V2 features a bullet cam, which occasionally pops up to enable the player to see the travel of the bullet into the target. Sometimes the bullet cam enables an x-ray mode showing the damage caused by the bullet, such as destruction of bones. Personally, I
this feature, but it does make me cringe out of sympathy a good amount of the time, especially during "crotch shots"; the bullet cam is
thorough in showing destruction.
Sniper Elite V2 does have some downsides, though. Firstly, there are a few bugs e.g. bullet cam showing different damage compared to bullet travel path. Most of the bugs are fairly uncommon - I only witnessed them once or twice my entire playthrough. Secondly, the AI seems to be, for lack of a better word, dumb at times e.g. standing still in the middle of a firefight or not seeing you when you are directly in front of them 10 feet away as you climb up a ledge.
The story is not very long, perhaps a few hours; however, the campaign is fun while it lasts. You can snipe people, use various traps or even be stealthy by using a silenced pistol and/or leading enemies away by throwing rocks in a different direction.

The game feels as thought it were rushed together using an unintuitive Game Maker-esque software. The visuals are right out of a generic Unity 3D Game, the music (if you could call it that) is lacking and bland, and the game as a whole runs terribly. On a GTX 970 + i7-5820k, I struggled to stay above 30fps, and doing something as simple as zooming in (with right-click) would tank my FPS.
The gameplay itself is poorly-explained, and your only sense of progression is through VHS tapes which you unlock via completing the main objective. The issue with this however, is that the game is so difficult, you'll struggle to complete any of it before demanding a refund. The tutorial is a <1 minute video, and then you're thrown in.
After failing to complete the objective, my game restarted itself and forced me into a new file. After loading my new file, all of my configurations were reset.
Overall, I cannot consciously recommend this game. As a proof of concept it exists, but as an execution it demonstrates why developers shouldn't have free reign over the Steam store.

Dark Souls - a frenetic knights & skeletons offering that puts the full emphasis of gameplay on combat, which is excellent if you have the machine to run it. Arcania 4, like the past titles in the series does not cater exclusively to the speed smasher of buttons, but does offer a bit of storyline, great graphics (remember, it's not a new title), enough action to keep the player awake and on edge and there's plenty of small details that push the game up the scale to an overall 7.8, in my humble opinion. Graphics are slightly dated as is the copyright so I don't slam the title for graphics that don't meet the standards set by Skyrim! Graphics 8 / Action is plentiful and combat is adjustable in the settings menu so you can adapt it to your personal style of melee combat. Our hero is seen from a 3rd person POV, a slight downer. Action 8.5 / Storyline is simple and straight forward, boy loves girl, girl's father dislikes boy, boy must complete 3 quests to win his approval. Along the way he finds others in need and helps them out, which generally means killing monsters and bad guys like it's a Olympic game and he wants nothing but gold!  Weapons, armor, and bottles of potions are found in chests and these are accessed easy enough by pressing the "E" key, there are no locks, or at least, I have yet to encounter one. Storyline 7 /  Presentation is done with a somewhat humorous approach, though mostly dark humor is used. I only played for 3 hours, but I want to play a lot more, and I will, once I get some sleep! Being retired has advantages, but there are dangerous facets to it as well. I stay up at times for 36 hours, 24-29 of those spent in Skyrim, or in a pitched combat situation whilst playing Battlefield 4 on the PS4, and there are times when I simply randomly select one of the 40+ games I have on Steam and reintroduce myself to it. It's all good, but there's no time for other things, like playing excellent titles such as Aracnia 4 on my laptop. Overall game 7.8 but I always bear in mind the date it was first introduced and the number of serious upgrades from then to now, which shows how the industry really feels about us gamers, the ones who buy their titles without too much price ♥♥♥♥♥ing, and play them until we're blind. Before I start my review, I need to state that I am technically one of the developers of the game. I made about half of the games music, and I also helped the lead dev with some ideas. That being said, I am going to give my fair and honest opinion about this game.
I like this game. This game is not for everyone. I don't know who this game could be targeted towards, but I do still think that everyone should atleast try this game. The concept is that you have to follow instructions from a computer screen, finding and editing papers in order to fufil the correct amount of tasks per hour. The paper that you need to find and insert is almost never in the same room as the required computer, thus you need to edit the paper in the editor machine. The concept is fairly simple, but it is effective. I am finding it rather easy at the moment, but I have been assured that it gets harder.
Story:
After finishing the game, I can say that the story is sadly lacking. There are some hidden features, and twists and such, but unless there is something hidden or something I missed, the story doesn't really go anywhere. Even so, the twists are cool, and I do believe that I might have missed something somewhere along the line.
I like the music, but don't take my word for it. I made a little more than half of it so I may be a little biased.
All in all, I do recommend this game. I think that it could do with a little optimisation and maybe some fixes, but the game is worth trying.

I am not sure if you noticed, but I don't play multiplayer first person shooters at all. With the exception of games like TF2 that I played a long time ago, and that was just goofing around on my computer that barely boot up. I mostly avoid it because I suck at these sorts of games. I have terrible aim, terrible reaction time, terrible eyesight, and add in a pinch of just being plain crap. So why this? And better question, if I am so bad, how can I even possibly do well and recommend this game?
Well I started playing the game because a friend told me to buy it to play with them. Everyday they would ask me to buy the $20 version of the game so I could play with them. Keep in mind this was maybe 5-6 months after the game launched, so I know it had a rough launch and was not well received. Eventually I just caved and bought it so they would not bug me anymore. I played some matches, I was understandably bad, as expected. Sarah being bad at first person shooters is not a new thing, it is just a fact of life. The game still felt really cool and tactical feeling though, so I kept with it until I unlocked some new operators to try out.
After unlocking them, I was also bad with them. I messed up bad, felt embarassed, wanting to hide in a corner and cry for embarassing myself in front of the everyone. But I stuck with it, learned, and was to a lesser degree, a useful member of the team. As long as I got whatever my operator ability was used up, I could experiment without worrying about being useless to the team. I tried things out, practiced more, got better, tried new things.
Where did that put me? Well my aim is still bad, I still miss obvious stuff, and I still cant peek a door and get someone before they get me. But what I did learn was that you can still win with better tactics, instead of always needing more skill. See, I just need an extra half-full second, if I can use spacial positioning or some other way to gain that extra reaction time, I stand a chance. With better tactics, you can usually counter many skilled players. Thats how I can get the success I have had in this game. It feels like it rewards more than just raw aiming/reaction time skill.
The game is good, and has only gotten better. Over time they have ironed out many problems the game had early on, and the new characters are always a treat to use. The only thing that has gotten worse is the community, with all the csgo kids moving over to playing Siege, but that is tolerable at the very least.
As for which game pricing option to get, the $20 one is not a bad choice to check out the game and see if you like it. If you do, you can spend $40 in the in game credits to unlock all the base game operators (thus equalling the normal game purchese price, meaning no net loss for you). It is what I did.
So in other words, I highly recommend it. Coming from someone who does not like multiplayer first person shooters, I think that is saying a lot

I'm new to the gothic series and i heard it was good so i grabbed gothic 4. This is my first steam review.
Yeah i've played it all the way through and i felt that the story was weak, all it was to me is that the main character tells people "Hey, i need to find X" and the other person says "You want to find/speak to X? well you need to prove yourself worthy" and run to a cave and kill one random monster out of the 10 different types of mobs in this game and get a item to bring it back to the to prove yourself worthy to speak to X and then you move on the the next area/town and repeat.
As for the combat, it was a bit.. Eh.. I like that I have my bow, sword and magic equipped all at once so it brought a fable feeling to me. I havent dug deep into combat with a ranger or mage so I cant type about that but with the melee, i thought the flourishes were kool and the way you can combinate regular attacks with flourishes but your left vulnerble for a second or so. But heres the problem with it. Regular attacks are limited to 6 strikes in a row, so you can hit hit flourish hit flourish and chain another flourish if u have the stamina for it and thats a sick combo but if you max out one of the melee dmg and health tree (i forgot what its called) it'll allows unlimited stirkes in a row without being left vulnerable... which kinda defeats the purpose of using a flourish because most enemies dont attack if your hitting them, so you can basically smack them until they die. (cough cough demonlords and bosses)
Some enemies can charge up a skill while your smacking them and you would think you would stop your endless strike rage on them when they charge a move to hurt you right? Nah, if you get one of the three mage skills that allows you to stun an enemy you could just cast that spell while theyre charging a move and they would stop and you could go back to your endless rage with no worry. im serious... its like an infinite (fighting game gamers understand infinites) thats the only mage spell i touched in the game and just made me wonder "how overpowered is a mage and oh, i forgot i had a bow"
Its about an 14-15 hour run, it kinda felt repetitive.. maybe because the way i played but if you played this game im pretty sure theres other ways of cheapness in the game. As for the ending **Spoiler**... i don't wanna speak about it, you walk to the boss and literally say like 2 lines and you fight him.. easy boss all you have to do is smack smack smack (endless rage strikes) until he teleports and throws beams at you which u can easily hide behind the portal doors and dont get hit by none of em.. he comes back and u repeat and he teleports and spawns enemies and comes back then, repeat and he dies. THE SECOND HE DIES AND TOUCHES THE FLOOR, NO ENDING CUTSCENE AND CREDITS APPEAR, AFTER THAT YOUR BACK AT THE MAIN MENU! so the 14-15 hour journey with a weak storyline comes to a end with not knowing what happened after shepard kills the final demon and you feel cheated of your time invested to see what would happen and nothing happens...
All i can really say is thank goodness i bought this game on a steam sale for dirt cheap and i dont recommend you to get this game.
3/7/2014: Edit - I've decided to fight the final boss again because i figured it was weird there was no ending so i killed the boss and the ending scene actually showed this time... But i still don't recommend this game.

As someone who enjoyed the first game, Nidhogg 2 is good fun with a lot of laughs just like the classic game we love.
Very easy to pick up and have fun with: Just like the first game, this game will bring back the good times with your buddies while not costing you a long tutorial just to learn how to play the game.
New art style: Nidhogg 2 is introduced with a new neat art style which frankly, I like.  It seems that a lot of people don't like it but, I like something new.
Character customization: Along with the new art style come with a pretty funny charatcer customiaztion. You can make your dude a total punk to hipster and other pretty neat stuff.
New weapons: There are three new weapons to the game. A bow, a broadsword and a dagger. I think this brings a nice good addition to the game.
More maps: There are new cool maps to fight on and quite a lot of them. Every map has its own music too. One slight con though, the maps all kind of feel the same with a different background.
Single player: The single player is a little dull against the AI.
Recommended with friends: Nidhogg is for sure more fun with friends. As said above, the single player is kind of boring.
Bows: I find the bows although a cool feature but honestly really annoying. They are super easy to avoid and are no match to a bladed weapon which usually is a free advancement to the next stage.
Game is fun but gets old FAST: Just like the first game, it is a great pick up and play game with your friends. The first 30 minutes are a great laugh with your friends but then the game starts wearing off its affect. Definintly a short playing sessions.
The price: Oh man. This is kind of the killer here for this game. The game is $15 USD at full price which is a
steep price from what you are getting. I would say this game is worth about $7 max.
Nidhogg 2 is a great pick up and play with your buddies to screw around to have fun when bored. With the low replayablity and the pretty high price for what you are getting, I am going to have give it a thumbs down.
That being said, I am going to give it a 6.5/10.

If you don't like running from scary things, you can turn them off before the game begins. But I recommend leaving them on for the full experience. It doesn't happen often enough to be too much of a nuisance.
This game does a great job of storytelling through scenery implication - my favorite part (no spoiler) is early in the game when you first show up for your brain scan appointment in Canada. Why is this mess here? What happened there?
What do you think of cloning? What if you could clone your mind, but not your body? This is explored in this game.
The human brain has over a quintillion synapses and connections. Would you delete or kill your old version so there was only one of you? Would you consider a body of a robot which has a digital replica of your mind to be human? The game explores these questions. Some decisions are completely optional, but some difficult "choices" must be made to progress through the game.
Finally I will leave you with this surprisingly apt poem, originally about the international telegraph cables laid on the ocean floor.
The Deep Sea Cables
by Rudyard Kipling
The wrecks dissolve above us; their dust drops down from afar -
Down to the dark, to the utter dark, where the blind white sea-snakes are.
There is no sound, no echo of sound, in the deserts of the deep,
Or the grey level plains of ooze where the shell-burred cables creep.
Here in the womb of the world - here on the tie-ribs of earth
Words, and the words of men, flicker and flutter and beat -
Warning, sorrow and gain, salutation and mirth -
For a Power troubles the Still that has neither voice nor feet.
They have wakened the timeless Things; they have killed their father Time;
Joining hands in the gloom, a league from the last of the sun.
Hush!  Men talk to-day o'er the waste of the ultimate slime,
And a new Word runs between:  whispering, "Let us be one!"

For a game to qualify as an RPG for me, it has to deliver some sort of vaguely coherent world and story. The world feels like it was written by a phrase randomizer. While everything has a name and probably even some backstory it is all completely inconsequential. Most of the first 5 hours or so the characters ask you to make some life-changing decision for them. You usually get a choice of 1 option which you have to pick in the most amateurish UI I have seen in decades (yes I am that old, yes I have been playing that long). The worst part is that the entire visual novel/ RPG part feel completely interchangeable. You could scrap it entirely and replace it with a different story and the second part of the game could remain untouched.
The second part: The most favorable description I could borrow from other reviewers would be 3 on 3 Fantasy Rugby. It it frantic, chaotic, frustrating and boring all in one, which is quite a feat to pull off. In a sense it acts like a sports game. You pick a team of 3 characters to play in some ritual against the opponent 3 characters. However the opponent doesnt do the same. While you pick, let's say, a runner a fighter and a blocker you will be up against 3 clones of one type. Like all such games the AI doesn't feel like a human. Perfect micromanagement and pixel-accurate timing while being tactically and strategically dumb as a brick.
Later in the game there is even a sort of league where the standing of each team can be compared. Sadly that in turn only break the RPG-esque worldbuilding they are trying to do. For some arbitrary reason you are always at the top of the board. Actually the reason isn't arbitrary, it is just required by the game design and the world design has to bend over.
I can't care a about a world where only narrative causality (The author wrote it, so it happened, no mater how unlogical) determines the outcome of the next event. I can't care about an ensemble cast of roughly 20 characters that blather on about their self made problems
If you love crashes and car violence this is the game for you!

I've enjoyed plenty of time in this game but overall it's clear that the fighting system is not well thoughout. Beyond the obvious problems of connectivity issues (thankfully this only ruins about one in ten of my games) and the lack of decent matchmaking (any 4v4 mode, for me, ends up unable to match on skill so the teams are clearly wildly uneven leading to a high level of stomps which aren't fun regardless of whether you win or lose) the issue is that the gameplay is lacking.
Due to the inescapable efficiency of blocking the more defensive characters are clearly extremely viable. The more attacking characters are unable to open up the block because the guard breaks (throws) require being close and many (sometimes unblockable) moves involve pushing the enemy away. Worse still the guard breaks are easily countered (unless you are in a very slow attack wind up or dodging) so they are essentially pointless if your enemy is ready to counter them. Overall someone who is blocking and counter guard breaking well is impossible to open up and the game becomes a war of rather dull attrition. In 4v4 this becomes a game of exploiting revenge mode using gear which maximises that state and to play well you end up backing off a lot from players who are in that mode.
I did enjoy playing this game for many hours, but that was at the point where these problems were not glaringly obvious.

This is a hard game to review.
Reason being, I'm a fan of Supergiant's games, of the style, the beautiful visuals, the amazing music.
First off, you have to be a fan of both sports games and visual novels. In that sense, its a strange hybrid.
It's rare to find someone who's a fan of both those extremes.
As you probably already know, it's basically a 3v3 ball game, with a story built around them through a visual novel.
It's all very pretty, and the 3v3 ball game is fun.
The issue is that, after the first 6-7hours it becomes terribly repetitive. You just play one team after the next over and over and over. At some point, I stopped caring about the story, and just wanted to rush to the next match and get the game over with. It is a sad way to play, but I couldn't help it. It just gets very repetitive and boring.
I think it would've made more sense to just make it a visual novel or a sports game but not both.
Independently they are both good, but together it seems like a never ending drag and you don't enjoy either much.
When I started this game, I thought to myself this is awesome, I'm going to give it the best review, but by the end of it, it left a sour taste in my mouth.
I can understand why someone would like it, and why others would hate it, personally I neither loved nor hated it, but I didn't enjoy it much. And as such I cannot recommend it.

Both a sci-fi masterpiece and a horror masterpiece.
Sublime audiovisuals.
Fantastic story that probes lots of interesting existential/transhuman questions.
Great attention to detail making the underwater science outpost seem believeable.
There are some choices in this game that you will agonize over. The game won't respond much to your questions, but the decision making process itself will impact you. You will mull your choices for some time.
The monster moments may not please everyone, however. They are really frightening, and at times frustrating. You have to proceed slowly through these parts and may end up repeating sections after death. This may be offputting for those who just want the story.
On the other hand, these moments are not as prevalent as in Amnesia (the story and location is a bigger focus here), and the monsters are not hugely different in design to previous games. So veterans of Amnesia who are after the next big step in challenging monster action may feel disappointed.
But the monsters are more varied than previous games and personally I think they got the balance right.

NOTE: I try to spoil as few as possible about the Story!
„Pyre“ is the newest Game from Developer „Supergiant Games“ (Creators of the Games „Bastion“ and „Transistor“)
The Game plays in a World where the „Commonwealth“, a Union of many Races and Lands, punish Criminals with Exile in the „Downside“
This Downside can only be entered via a River which ends in a very deep Waterfall down.
Escaping back to the Commonwealth is impossible.
They are forced to spent the Rest of their Lifes in these Lands which consists mainly of Deserts, Bogs and other harsh Climates.
The Player was also cast down as an Exile. On the Brink of Starvation and Thirst, a Wagon comes the Way and 3 masked Persons come out. One of them gives some much needed Food and Water.
After being invited into the Wagon, a Question is raised if he can read a mysterious Book they have with them.
Through reading the Book, there is a possibility how to escape the Downside and thus the Journey to Redemption begins...
The Game consists of 2 Parts:
-          Story (Exploration, Dialogues, Party-Management, Choices, etc.)
-          Action (Rites)
In the Story Part, you travel with your Friends and other Team Members through the Downside to the Locations where the Rites will take.
The Wagon will act as your central hub where you can manage your Party, study the Book of Rites and interact with many other objects you later will receive.
There will be later an Option to train everytime against the AI for testing new Tactics/etc. Equipment/Artifacts which can be equipped on Team Members can be bought/sold at the „Slugmarket“ before the Start of any Rite.
During the Travels you will have the choice of selecting 2 different paths which will have different Events (Bonus) depending who requested the path.
Besides those Events you will also get the usual Story Events which can be also slightly random. At the Beginning you will find active Rites through the Navigation of a Start which indicate the Spot.
Later you can choose between different Stars and therefore also decide which Enemy Team you want to confront.
In the Action Part, 2 Teams consisting of 3 People each („Triumvirate“) tries to extinguish the Pyre of the Enemy Team.
To reach this Goal, a Character must throw or dunk the „Celestial Orb“ into the Pyre.
The Flame grows weaker afterwards (Default is 100 Units at Start). When a Character successfully weakens the Pyre, he will be banished until the Enemy Team scores a Hit or someone else from the Team hits the Pyre.
Every Character has also emits an Aura which will temporarily banish enemy Players.
This Aura can also be used as Projectile to send it as a Wave. If a Character takes the Orb his Aura will be absorbed fully by it, which then in Return makes him defenseless against enemy Auras.
Since this is a Team Game, the Orb can be passed to other Team Members, but only one Person at a Time can be moved while the others remain stuck and defenseless against Enemy Attacks.
Each Race has its own set of unique Movements, Aura and Abilities. Participating Characters gain Experience and unlock unique Abilities which are divided into 2 different Categories.
Every Character has 4 Attributes:
-          Glory (This Value describes how much Damage is dealt to the Enemy Pyre)
-          Quickness (This Value describes how fast a Character moves on the Field)
-          Presence (This Value describes how wide one’s Aura is)
-          Hope (This Value describes how fast, the Character can return back from the temporary Banishment)
During the Game i thought that it would get repetitive going from one Rite to another, but i was suprised how much the Story unfolds and new Events take Place. New Options also will get unlocked during the Game which makes it more appealing.
I also thought about the Action Part itself being stale later on, but was surprised how much depth it has and later gaining new options which makes it more difficult with also more stronger getting Enemy Teams.
Here are my positive/neutral/negative Points:
Positive (+):
-Excellent and very good Soundtrack!
-Good and tactical Action Part
-Your Decisions can influence the Outcome and Destiny of involved Characters in the Story
-Well written Characters
-„Fluent“ Artstyle and Graphics which remains in Future still good to look at
-Great Replay Value, since many Decisions and Wins/Losses can influence the Story
-Characters can Level Up and gain new Abilities
-No Real Game Over. The Story continues nonetheless how much you loose in the Rites
Neutral (o):
-This Game plays like a „Visual Novel“ since more then 60% of the Game consists of reading and making Decisions. For those who want more Action should be aware of this Fact!
-Character unique Artifacts, that can be earned during specific trials, can make the Items in the Slugmarket somewhat useless later on
Negative (-):
-No Possibility to talk with the Team-Members outside specific Events
-Versus Mode is only local with no Network Options
Fazit:
The Graphics and the Music are one of the Trademarks of this Studio which itself makes it worth getting it. The Characters growed on me during the Story and i also felt later their absence if they are liberated.
Since your Decisions can alter the End on multiple Things, it offers a great Replay Value!
For me its one of the few Games, which i can still play in future and still will be amazed of it!

From the sole developer, Ricardo Pratas, comes The 111th Soul; a horror game that revolves around mystery and minor puzzle solving. Players will take on the role of Richard Silver, a guy that has inherited his grandparent's house after they both mysteriously died. Richard and his brother David decide to rennovate the home, and Richard heads over to the house late one night. This is, of course, where things start to get weird.
Headphone users beware! There are some very small 'spooky' jumpscares in this game, but the worst one is some extremely loud and obnoxious static that doesn't go away until you find its source. Even coming through my speakers, this sound was nearly intolerable and it needs some quick attention from the developer. Other than that, the scares are alright for a cheap, one-man indie title; for some reason, they involve a lot of hands. One weird element to the game is that a lot of the graphics, especially any involving humanoid figures, look very clay-like. I'm not sure if this was intentional, but it adds to the overall weird factor.
There's quite a bit of replayability in The 111th Soul. Even though the game itself can be completed in about 15 minutes, it offers three different endings depending on the choices made at the very end. Getting through all three extends the game an additional 15-25 minutes, depending on how bad you are at the final challenge. Having branching endings is a nice touch, and overall the game is well polished. It runs at a solid 144 FPS on my 144Hz 1080p monitor, with my 6700k/GTX 1080 combo. I also did not experience any crashing.
For what it is, The 111th Soul is pretty good. It's definitely one of the better cheap indie horror titles that you can buy, most are abandonware garbage that have no flavor to them at all. It's nice to find a game that you can genuinely tell where the developer is proud of his work. Don't go in expecting to have your socks blown off for $2.29 CAD, but it's a good filler on a slow night. In the future, the developer may want to consider adding a title screen just to make everything feel a little more polished. As well, the text font used is a bit distracting.

Awseome game for six bucks. It's relatively short and for twenty bucks I think I would have felt short shrifted. But for six it delivers in spades. It has interesting graphics. An excellent, engaging, intelligent and expertly interwoven story.  I've seen some things in this game that I've never seen in a game before, and it was done well certainly a game to be emulated. The pure brutality and reasonable gore satisfied my primal urge for hunting, revenge, justice, blood and a bit of lust. The game has good polish.
If they make a darkness 3, and It's longer with deeper content I wouldn't hesitate to pay full price.  As a more casual ex-intense game player I loved the choice of having a familiar gently hint at the way forward, instead of a map and radar. That added to the inescapable immersion. The narrative and story were expertly weaved together, and the art was very well done. The game felt well crafted, despite some non-game crashing hiccups for me and it didn't require a lot of graphic futzing to get the game to run well on my now moderate hardware.
I would have liked more interaction and more free play and choice in how to solve each level and would have enjoyed an even deeper story with Jenny. Maybe darkness 3, will interleave more than just two planes of existence which gives us the possibility of more than two Jennies.  We should be able to explore a different relationship with a gaggle of Jennies. (we are exploring insantity, why settle for just two; maybe make the Jenny's vary a bit too physically? Dolly Parton Jenny vs Jennifer Anniston Jenny) This is the first franchise that let me experience slow paced problem solving and fast paced fps in a game where I appreciated both versions. I'd like to have had an even longer time to spend in the asylum exploring, interacting, and being challenged with that world.  Part of the fun and interesting part of the game is DECIDING which world you wanted to be real for you. In the end it shouldn't matter which world the developers thought was real. They should expand on the idea of you  be able to choose the reality you want to follow as the primary (and they should be equal in depth and breadth). Do you want a more love-lorn relaxed problem solver, or a justice blood gore vendetta.  I hope to be able to explore and choose more with the next version of the franchise.

Dragon Saga is a very unique mmorpg in its activeness and the amount of control you have over your characters. If you enjoy very active hack and slash gameplay in a mmorpg setting, this game will provide you countless hours of just that.
The art style is very colourful and even childlike at places, but there are also vast dark sections like gloomy caves and fiery volcanic areas. The abilities are simple, yet combine to be very satisfying for both casual and more hardcore players. There are many classes, each with their own unique skill sets that give them all a different feel and look.
The community is very nice for the most part, the staff are active on social media and on the forums. So there's always someone to help. Support team responds quick enough and is polite, though sometimes the best help comes from the players themselves on the forum. The developers listen, take suggestions and engage in conversation with the players. We players have a lot of control over the direction the game goes in, and that's one very important thing.
The game has problems due to incompitent developers of the past. Pvp, while being very fun, is not supported by good game modes, ranked pvp or any sort of matchmaking. The group pvp modes have lots of problems. The economy is still recovering and shifting because of the vast history of abuse that has now ended. The translations are quite bad and the game doesn't explain it's self very well.
But those problems are slowly being fix and the future is, for the first time in a long long time, looking bright for this game.  Overall I recommend everyone to give this game a shot!

Where to begin? I guess with the beginning.  Evil Genius starts with a short FMV giving you the basics of what your about to do.  Build a secret lair in a mountain, perform various Act of Infamy, research various things, and ultimately create your Doomsday Device.  When you start in the game proper you have but a handful of Minions and a single Henchman, your pick of Genius determines which Henchman you get at the start.  I quickly set off and ordered my Minions to build me base, starting with the Corridors and moving on to Barracks, Control Room, and a Mess Hall.
All this base building costs money, and while you do start with a few funds, it’s nowhere near the amount that you’ll need if you plan on creating a Doomsday Device that will bring the Forces of Good to their knees.  For this we have the World Domination Map, where you send your minions off to different regions to steal money or preform Acts of Infamy.
Now here’s where one of my little personal tricks comes into play.  I discovered this about two or three playthroughs ago.  The best way to get the most money right at the start without the heat or agents from the regions getting suspicious of you and investigating your island.  You can do any Acts of Infamy or Stealing, as much as you want, before you complete the mission involving capturing the maid.  No agents will come looking for you until you capture her.  So, I recommend building your Lair as much as you can, and build a massive Barracks full of Lockers(these determine how many Minions you can have).  With enough you can hit your Minion cap and send all of them out to different regions to steal money.  Leave the game running and come back later, I let it run overnight, and you will have a nice pile of gold to get you started.  Just also remember to bring all your Minions back and let it run for a little longer.  Since you will steal acquire Heat, so you want to give some time to let that fade off.
Now is that cheating?  Or is that truly winning at the game and bending the mechanics to better suit your needs?
Now after a few hours you’ll have a pretty nice Lair going for you, probably with some spiffy traps, and plenty of Minions of various types wandering around doing your bidding.  And yes, I do mean hours.  My personal biggest complaint about Evil Genius is it’s lack of game speed control.  There is no way to speed up time in any manor, and so there can be times where you just play to wait.  And that can get boring.
Eventually you’ll make it to the second Island, and this is where the fun really begins.  The is the best part of that game, in my opinion, and really this whole thing is all about my opinion, so therefore, this is the best part of the game!
What do you do first on the second island?  Why build a new Lair of course!  That old island with that old and inferior base that you spent hours getting perfect is now replaced with a new and improved Lair.  You’ve got more space to spread out with and the experience to know how you want to be set up.  But you also have the Forces of Good still being a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥ the amount of which is directly proportional to how much of a ruckus you created prior to moving to the new island.
At this point I stop telling you how to play, or what exactly happens when you play.  You have to just go and play it.  Trust me on this.  While you’ll complain at the total number of hours you’ve spent playing it, you’ll know that every minute of that time was spent being the best Evil Genius you could and loving every minute of it.  You may, probably will, get irritated at your Minions from time to time, as the AI does seem to just slip here and there.  But overall it’s never anything truly gamebreaking, and these time are sparse enough that you wont even remember all of them.
You can really push yourself, and your own morals, as to what it takes to be an Evil Genius.  Does it end with beating the game?  Or is it more than that?  After all, almost all the game files are written in Excel spreadsheets, and can altered in any way you choose.  A quick Google search will result with a list of in game cheatcodes.  Is using these cheating?  Is altering the games core files to better your success cheating?  These types of actions could be considered being nefarious, something which the game itself rewards you for being.
The graphics and stylized look of Evil Genius both seem to have held on well with the times.  While you can tell it’s a dated game, its not so blinding obvious.  The music too is a perfect fit for it’s visual look.
I have only three real complaints about Evil Genius.  One you cannot effect the passing of time, two you cannot zoom out far enough, to my personal liking, and three I had to fix the resolution every time I started the game.  But hey, if that’s my only compatibility issue, I’ll live.

One of the finest first-person-shooters I've ever played. Where do I even start? The story is actually quite interesting and it makes sense (somewhat). Every character is unique, interesting and memorable. This game does a really good job of getting you immersed. I spent half of the time playing just looking around at all small details they put in the levels. The graphics are also quite beautiful. They look like they've been drawn-in and they are pleasing to the eye (almost Borderlands style). The gameplay is a standard first-person-shooter, but you have two demon arms that help you in combat. One demon arm helps you grab things, like hearts from your dead enemies to restore health, or throwable items. The other one is like a whip that you can attack with. The addition of the demon arms bring a new strategy to your fights. There are plenty of weapons you can find in the field from your fallen enemies and each of them feels different. Even though I beat this game in 6 hours, I might get into NewGame+ someday. I got this for $5 on sale and it was well worth the money.

As always, pros and cons are personal preference and may differ by player.
For list of what is good about the game, I definitely recommend to actually play the game.
There are much to be found as a game player.
I would give my two cents about what I wasn't so thrilled about this game.
Game play pace is much slower than anticipated.
Progress is so slow, sometimes I wonder what it would take to expand overall game play.
Between mission play on overall map could use more variety.
While mission is running on play, it feels close to modern space game, but between mission feels like rigid 3D cartoon.
3D mission map opens interesting possibility in formations, but ship's limited movements and ship types restricts scale of formation to minimum.
Game having very few ship and ammo types is limiting ship stat scaling as well.
I wouldn't want a capital ship standing against large fleet of basic ship, but it should be able to take on 3-4 basic ships in essence.
Add insult to injury, ship hull and armor are too dense for available fire power options.
It feels as if limited ammo types make the play bit mundane at times due to need for tight formation to dish out damage.
A lot of straight run to your death play by AI is bit weird and could use basic military formation to make experience more authentic and open new possibility for actual counter formations.
As result, prolonging combat will likely ensure losing ship or two at least, while powering through one at a time does much better than strategic play.
As per top of my wish list is something that would expand game to be more strategic.
While I can see why limited movement is desired on grand scale to ensure play doesn't get ridiculously large, I do desire movement boost mode would cover at least 50% additional distance if not more.
Turn ratio and elevation could use at least 50% boost and higher depreciation for ship size.
Adding multi-level to movement boost and multi-level turn ratio/elevation boost mode is highly desired to add another layer of tactics for both player and AI.
I can go on and on about my wish list, but game is what it is currently.
It's definitely fun game to play.
Overall very satisfying game, but as always there's room for player's greed.

first off, sniper elite v2 is a very fun game.
the developers aim seems to be a mix of arcade and simulation elements and for the most part does that very well.
there's nothing quite as satisfying as hitting an enemy sniper in the head from a 1km distance, the x-ray bulletcam takes care of that.
but on the other hand the gameplay often derails into hectic run&gun tactics, as shooting your sniper rifle will almost always alert every enemy of your position, despite being in an active warzone with plenty of fighting going on in the background at all times. for a game that's being advertised as a "stealth" game, there're just too many portions of the game where the level design forces you out of hiding.
I massively enjoyed the old splinter cell games simply because you always had the option to sneak by everyone and didn't need to reveal yourself ever.
sniper elite does not offer that. that in itself might not be a big drawback to many, but it kind of diminishes some of the fun I got from this game.
the AI is nothing outstanding but does its job sufficiently well, though especially on the higher difficulties it's sometimes frustrating that once alerted, they always seem to know your position.
as a whole I can definitely recommend sniper elite v2, though, as graphics, sound and controls are generally pretty good and do their job well.

I've enjoyed plenty of time in this game but overall it's clear that the fighting system is not well thoughout. Beyond the obvious problems of connectivity issues (thankfully this only ruins about one in ten of my games) and the lack of decent matchmaking (any 4v4 mode, for me, ends up unable to match on skill so the teams are clearly wildly uneven leading to a high level of stomps which aren't fun regardless of whether you win or lose) the issue is that the gameplay is lacking.
Due to the inescapable efficiency of blocking the more defensive characters are clearly extremely viable. The more attacking characters are unable to open up the block because the guard breaks (throws) require being close and many (sometimes unblockable) moves involve pushing the enemy away. Worse still the guard breaks are easily countered (unless you are in a very slow attack wind up or dodging) so they are essentially pointless if your enemy is ready to counter them. Overall someone who is blocking and counter guard breaking well is impossible to open up and the game becomes a war of rather dull attrition. In 4v4 this becomes a game of exploiting revenge mode using gear which maximises that state and to play well you end up backing off a lot from players who are in that mode.
I did enjoy playing this game for many hours, but that was at the point where these problems were not glaringly obvious.

But the monsters are more varied than previous games and personally I think they got the balance right.

Get the game for the soundtrack! You have heard Bastion and Transistor. I consider Pyre to have an even better score.
Get the game for the visuals. Beautifully drawn scenes and some nice animations. The Supergiant art department outdid itself.
Only don't get game as a game. There are two parts to it: a visual novel with extremely limited choices which never feel like they matter. For a game to qualify as an RPG for me, it has to deliver some sort of vaguely coherent world and story. The world feels like it was written by a phrase randomizer. While everything has a name and probably even some backstory it is all completely inconsequential. Most of the first 5 hours or so the characters ask you to make some life-changing decision for them. You usually get a choice of 1 option which you have to pick in the most amateurish UI I have seen in decades (yes I am that old, yes I have been playing that long). The worst part is that the entire visual novel/ RPG part feel completely interchangeable. You could scrap it entirely and replace it with a different story and the second part of the game could remain untouched.
The second part: The most favorable description I could borrow from other reviewers would be 3 on 3 Fantasy Rugby. It it frantic, chaotic, frustrating and boring all in one, which is quite a feat to pull off. In a sense it acts like a sports game. You pick a team of 3 characters to play in some ritual against the opponent 3 characters. However the opponent doesnt do the same. While you pick, let's say, a runner a fighter and a blocker you will be up against 3 clones of one type. Like all such games the AI doesn't feel like a human. Perfect micromanagement and pixel-accurate timing while being tactically and strategically dumb as a brick.
Later in the game there is even a sort of league where the standing of each team can be compared. Sadly that in turn only break the RPG-esque worldbuilding they are trying to do. For some arbitrary reason you are always at the top of the board. Actually the reason isn't arbitrary, it is just required by the game design and the world design has to bend over.
I can't care a about a world where only narrative causality (The author wrote it, so it happened, no mater how unlogical) determines the outcome of the next event. I can't care about an ensemble cast of roughly 20 characters that blather on about their self made problems

This is a hard game to review.
Reason being, I'm a fan of Supergiant's games, of the style, the beautiful visuals, the amazing music.
First off, you have to be a fan of both sports games and visual novels. In that sense, its a strange hybrid.
It's rare to find someone who's a fan of both those extremes.
As you probably already know, it's basically a 3v3 ball game, with a story built around them through a visual novel.
It's all very pretty, and the 3v3 ball game is fun.
The issue is that, after the first 6-7hours it becomes terribly repetitive. You just play one team after the next over and over and over. At some point, I stopped caring about the story, and just wanted to rush to the next match and get the game over with. It is a sad way to play, but I couldn't help it. It just gets very repetitive and boring.
I think it would've made more sense to just make it a visual novel or a sports game but not both.
Independently they are both good, but together it seems like a never ending drag and you don't enjoy either much.
When I started this game, I thought to myself this is awesome, I'm going to give it the best review, but by the end of it, it left a sour taste in my mouth.
I can understand why someone would like it, and why others would hate it, personally I neither loved nor hated it, but I didn't enjoy it much. And as such I cannot recommend it.
