Something to make clear about this review: This review is solely based off of the experience that The Darkness 2 offers as an individual video game. I have not been influenced by The Darkness 1 because I never played it, nor the narratives in the comic series because I have never read them, so this review has ONLY been generated based off of the experience that The Darkness 2 provides.
The Darkness 2 is an action-packed FPS game with a few small stealth segments thrown in, that is overall fun and satisfying experience, despite a few flaws.
PROS:
The gameplay in this game is pretty solid, and shots that you are sure will land will almost always hit, and in my preliminary playthrough I wasn't frustrated at all by any shots that should have hit but didn't. Gunplay is tight and exciting, and strays from the standard linear military shooter by adding in the Darkness powers to mix up gameplay. Despite the semi small skill set that the Darkness adds (slashing arms, grab ability, a swarm mass stun power and gun channeling are the only main ones), they are enoug to keep gameplay fresh and have satisfied me through my first playthrough, and enough for me to start another game. My favorite gameplay addition, however, has to be the light system. Without the darkness-destroying lights in this game, it would have been too easy. However, when you are exposed to light, your sound rings, your vision goes black and white and blurry, and most importantly, you lose health regeneration capabilities and all of your darkling and darkness powers. Most lights you can shoot out, however some either need a far away generator to be disabled, or can't at all. This really shook the game up at times and forced me to think more tactically, keeping the experience fresh.
The graphics, while not very "impressive" on the scale of Crysis or The Witcher, are still nice with decent texture resolutions on the high setting, cool light and shadow effects, and a fitting comic book-esque style. Not much else to say, besides the fact that this game runs very very well also.
Audio quality is pretty good, with well done voice acting, gun sounds, and power effects. Lip syncing with the in game characters was also spot on, which I have noticed not too many games get right. The gore effects were also a nice grimacing feature, where you could really hear your enemy getting torn in half by the darkness on executions and whatnot.
The story is also well done, with most of the plot centered on getting revenge for a gang hit and Jackie's lost love, Jenny. I won't spoil anything in this review, and I have only done one of the two end decisions, but there is (at least on my ending, possibly the other too) a plot twist, however I had seen that one coming for a little while so it didn't really catch me too off guard. Not the best story ever in a game, but good enough to keep you playing to see what happens at the end.
THE CONS:
The biggest con for this game is one you probably already know: the short length. I have played the game for just 6 hours and have beaten the entire story mode of the game. This includes looking for collectibles, menu tweaking, load times, and the time where I had to replay a segment of a level because I had quit at a point where it didn't actually save anything for a while. That's not very long for a single-player based game. Games like Battlefield and Call of Duty have short single player games, but the real reason most people buy those games are for the multiplayer, which they spend vast amounts of time on to justify their purchase. For this game, there is no multiplayer. The only options once you finish the game is New Game Plus and some side missions called Vendettas which can be done solo or with a few friends, the problem being I want to play those co op but none of my friends have this game!
Also, I feel as though the gameplay will have gone stale before I finish a second playthrough, because while it is better than a standard FPS game, it still doesn't shake things enough to have me play through the same exact story two times and still stay interesting.
Overall, this game was a lot of fun to play through. I got it for $8 with a ton of other games on the Humble Bundle, but I would say this game is worth the buy at the current price. For more than $20, I may say no however. It's definitely worth a try though!

At its core, Pyre is an RPG where you'll advance the story by talking with characters you'll meet along the way and by controlling them in sports-like gameplay sequences called rituals. A combination I had never seen before and left me very intrigued when I first saw the game trailer.
First thing you should know about Pyre I think is that it is the kind of RPG filled with dialogues for you to read. Most of the game is not voice acted and a big part of the lore is handed to you in the book of rites which you'll fill along your progression in the story. So if reading is something you don't particularly like in a game, Pyre might not be for you. Your loss, really.
On the other hand, if you like an RPG with an insane amount of branching paths, complex and beautifully written original characters and a fun original gameplay to go with all that, then you should definitely get Pyre.
I know I said original twice, it's not my fault this game is not like anything I've seen before.
First thing you'll notice about it is the incredible art direction which is strikingly beautiful with vibrant colors and charismatic characters. The music is wonderful too, Darren Korb delivers another soundtrack you'll want to listen outside of the game, I especially loves the tracks where Ashley Barrett sings.
I won't talk about the story too much here because it is something everyone should discover for itself and because yours will very likely be different from the one I experienced.
You have so many choices to make about the characters you'll encounter that the story can unfold in a lot of different ways. There is no real failure state in Pyre, you can win or lose in rituals and it will affect the story accordingly. You might sometimes even want to lose on purpose to help an adversary which is something you very rarely see.
And this is where Pyre shines the brightest in my opinion, you'll truly become attached to theses characters and care about what happens to them. It also gives the game an immense replay value.
Aside from the story, rituals are the main gameplay sections of the game.
Imagine a 3v3 basketball-like game where each character has a protective aura and where the goal is to throw a magic orb into the adversary pyre. The thing is, when you hold the orb, you lose your aura and can easily be removed from the game.
At first, I though these mechanics might be a bit limited and might not hold for the whole game but I was wrong.
Every character has its own abilities which allows for more and more complex tactics has the game progresses.
Also, the IA is very competent, surprised me from time to time and even taught me a few tricks.
Know that you can play rituals in a PVP fashion outside of the story mode but I didn't try it so I don't know whether it is as fun or not against another person..
If I absolutely wanted to say something bad about Pyre, I would say that there are some clunky piece of UI here and there but nothing to be really worried about. Also the rituals might get a little repetitive towards the end of the story as you tend to fight the same adversaries multiple times.
But to be honest, this game is absolutely wonderful and it is baffling to me to see such a small team can come out with such a streak of incredible games.
I can't thumb up this enough.

Arma is literally the best game I've ever played in 20+ years of gaming. Perhaps the only drawback to this masterpiece is how poor the optimization is. The game is an absolute glutton for processing power, so keep that in mind when trying it out.
Some great key points:
---Replayability :  Singleplayer/Multiplayer options, Servers all over the globe.
---Modding : An amazing modding commnity. Everything from workshop missions to new weapons, vehicles and models are available, free of cost.
---Variety of Play : You can be running around in the trenches with an assault rifle one minute, then jump in a tank for an armored assault while calling in your buddy to do a CAS strike with an attack chopper. It has all the mobility of battlefield without the feeling of being constrained.
---Sandbox : Exile mod, Wasteland, etc. offer base building, scavenging, interesting multiplayer opportunities and plenty of combat.
Arma has literally spun off so many other games that were adopted just from a small portion of what Arma is... Titles like H1Z1, PUBG, DayZ, etc. are all a result of an idea that started in Arma... and in my opinion, Arma continues to do all of them better.
If you're considering buying this game, the only thing that should hold you back is if your PC is beast enough to run it.

I don't usually write reviews, but this game needs one. So let's start:
It's free-to-play, you should try it even if it has mixed or negative reviews. You don't lose anything.
This is not their first game, they also developed "The Last Stand" franchise, "Warfare 1917" "Warfare 1944", "Crush The Castle" 1 and 2, and few other games.
So, about this game:
PROS:
It's free-to-play.
If you're bored, you can spend your time on this game.
Decent graphics.
You can customize your soldier's loadout (by unlocking & buying upgrades with in-game currency, but every upgrade has a downside).
You can customize your platoon. (Choose what troops you want to deloy in-combat).
CONS:
It takes some time to learn how to play this game properly.
The upgrades for your troops are expensive, and you have to play the game for some time to get them (with in-game currency).
There are only 2 factions: USA and Russia. They are not properly balanced. USA does have Anti-Tank infantry by default, Russia doesn't have that (you have to edit your platoon for that). When in close quarters combat, RUS infantry tends to throw a lot of grenades. This is not balanced at all, because a grenade can kill a whole squad (2 to 6 soldiers).
Snipers are unbalanced (From what i've seen, the RUS snipers). Sometimes a sniper can one-shoot one of your soldiers from a big distance, sometimes they miss 5 shots in a row.
The Russian BTR-90 and the American LAV-25 are very weak vs. 2 squads of infantry. They miss a lot of shots, and they have a lot of health (it takes around 4 or 5 rockets to take them down).
The Russian T-90 Tank and the American M1A1 Tank shoot very slow. They should increase their default firerate by a little bit.
In conclusion, i recommend this game. Even if there are more CONs than PROs, you should try it. I mean, it's free-to-play.

A mediocre turn-based tactical space strategy game that puts you to the seat of an admiral in the Battlestar universe.
So far I've completed 1 skirmish and 5-6 missions.
The pros and cons I've seen are as follows:
Pros:
1. The game is rather easy to understand and learning curve is smooth.
2. As far as I know this kind of turn based game play is the first in the genre. Basically at each turn you and the AI issue orders to the ships simulatenously. Once you click the turn button the battle commences and the next 10 seconds are simulated and you watch. This alleviates the stress over your shoulders and removes the need of micro-managing in real time battle. And gives the game a very good tactical aspect.
3. Although the options in battle are limited (most ships will have 2-3 skills at most) situational placement and orientation of the ships in battle counts to a significant degree. For example I've just finished a freighter rescue mission in which I had to block incoming missiles (to the freighter) by placing one of my tanky cruisers in between the cylon ships and the freighter. And this was the only way I could find to rescue the freighter after 4 attempts on the mission. The game forces you to use your wits.
4. The game has a strange difficulty setting which may be a negative point for some people. Basically you have very limited idea on what to face in each mission and odds are that you will be greatly outnumbered. But I like this setting because it forces you to think tactically and create wonders with the limited amount of ships and resources you have.
Cons:
1. The UI is terrible in general and inefficient. Although it lets you do whatever you wish in the battle, issuing orders is a very slow process. The movement, elevation change and rotation orders are hard to control. You cannot grasp where exactly you've placed your ships, where exactly it is facing and what is the elevation difference between the enemy ship and your ship for instance. The UI gives very limited information.
2. The UI controls are ambiguous as there are multiple ways of giving the same order to ships (around 3).
3. Ship silhouette icons (that you drag to issue a movement order) are prone to  accidental clicks. When you accidentally click it you cannot cancel the click and are forced to renew the movement order you've given.
4. Just because of the cumbersome UI controls it can take up to 3-4 minutes to plan a turn. And you only watch a 10 second simulation afterwards.
5. There is no multiple selection as far as I know. So you are forced to click each of the viper squadrons one by one and give the same attack order.
6. There is no way to understand what your ships are doing unless you select them. You may have up to 8-9 ships (including the fighter squadrons) you have to control at once. And you easily forget what the ship you've selected first is doing.
7. There is no way to understand when the cooldown on ship skills end unless you select them.
8. Other than tactical battle, I think not much effort is spent on the remaining parts of the game. The grand strategy map for instance is composed of just 4 star systems (and a few other planets). Its presentation remembers me of the 1998's game Star Wars Rebellion. I know that the BS universe revolves around 12 colonies but come on... this is space we are talking about :D.
9. There are very limited variety of ships and skills on both human and cylon sides.
Conclusion:
I think the game is a mediocre turn based strategy game. As far as see it is mostly bug free and playable from day one. But I am amazed by the tactical aspect so I am rather tempted to ignore the other issues about the game. So I will give a positive vote.

Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing

As it is now, I cannot recomend this game. Perhaps later I will be able to recomend it, but currently, there are a great many problems.
But let's get into the Pros and Cons of it, and break it down.
Pros:
-It hits that BSG feel pretty damned well. When you first get to pull a battlestar out, it's awesome. The music and sound design are on point, and the ships look phenominal.
-Combat gameplay is pretty solid. I have a few beefs with it, but on the whole the way the tactical battles plays out leaves me thinking plenty hard on how I intend to accomplish my objectives.
-The Campaign map has a great deal of pottential, and provides a nice sprawling warmap for you to play on . . . but . . .
Cons:
-Voice acting and some plot elements are just . . . bad. Turn your brain off for this plot. The over-arching elements are quite nice, and much of the broad strokes will likely be fanfic fodder for some time. It's just that the story itself reads like a mediocre fanfic so far.
-The combat sometimes runs into problems. Big ones. I found myself scratching my head at how my ships were taking damage sometimes, and other problems were not quite so intuitive. I think that the damage model could use with a good bit more forginess on the 'defenders' part, and I think that the weapons could do with a bit of a buff to accuracy (to compensate for the more forgiving armor modeling). The ability to have turrets intercept missiles would also be nice.
-The warmap has MANY problems. The biggest of which is it's sheer brutality. You will find your fleets vastly out-numbered, and strategically outmaneuvered, even in the earliest parts of the game. This is stupidly frustrating, as it can set you up to lose council members without you even really having made a mistake on your part. The biggest frustration here is the fact that your ships use up resources to travel around, and the cool-down on free jumps can be painfully slow. This must be fixed.
The things I think most need fixing for this game are the difficulty curve and the armor modeling. But there's a lot of potential here, and I hope the devs can fix it. Frankly, I'm surprised, and a bit distressed, that they did not do so already.
Pick it up when it's on sale. Don't buy it right now.

If you love playing Half-Life and co-op as much as I do then this is the free piece of software to bond them together!  Half-Life 2 is great playing with friends.  Synergy enables Half-Life 2 to be played co-op.  Here is what I did to get it working.
Enjoy!!
Playing Half-Life 2 co-op using Synergy
Both game host and client:
Download and install Half-Life 2:
Download and install Synergy (free):
Game host:
1) Open port 27015 TCP and UDP on your router
2) Get your REAL internet IP address (shown at the bottom left hand corner) and give this number to the client joining your game:
3) Start up Synergy
4) Start server for Half-Life 2 from the Synergy menu options
Note: Them trying to join your game via Steam friends or sending them game invites will NOT work. It will try connecting to the actual IP address of your PC (usually 192.168.x.x) which is local and not public. You will get host connect failures.
Client:
1) Start Synergy
2) Enable Developer Console:
The console starts disabled by default. To enable it, load the game and visit Options > Keyboard > Advanced. There will be a pop-up that will include two options, one of them labeled "Enable Developer Console". Once enabled, it can be opened and closed by pressing the button above Tab ⇆, known as the "tilde." ~
3) Enter Developer Console with the ~ key and enter connect command to the host internet IP address:
~
connect xx.xx.xx.xx
You then should be connected and able to play co-op!

I don't wanna spoil it for people but I also really do wanna give a rundown of the story, Even with the information, reading the novel itself makes it feel so much more real. I looked at comments before I downloaded it myself and I thought that it needed something like this.
NOW HOWEVER, IF YOU DON'T WANT ANY SPOILERS STOP READING NOW (But mind you to be aware of not jumping to conclusions).
Basically this girl, Ambre suffers from "Cinderella Syndrome" which was caused from how society wants women to look, act, and how they must achieve it by any means to attain a "happy ending" such like a disney princess would.
Now our protagonist, Tristan, is depressed, this is because his wife (Ambre) has "gone away"
Because of Ambre's "Cinderella Syndrome", she has made herself so mentally unstable that she will force herself to forget her reality and live one of a child until it is "possible" to attain this fairy tale ending. But as she is in reality not the fictional princess world, she cannot attain this ending because like every human she has her improfections. She cannot deal with this, and thus, will restart her life over and over again thinking it will make a difference.
Essentially she's locked herself in a type of psychosis to live in an illusion that if she "restarts" enough times, eventually things will turn out properly. Starting as a "child" every time. However, this is not the case like you're originally lead to believe.
Since Ambre believes in "restarting" as a child. She has effectively trapped her mental state into a box mentally she will not age. thus retaining the mindset of a child. However, everytime restarting, she is continuously exposed to the truth of being the same person sticking her into a sort of purgatory.
Ambre wants a child. That is the last thing she wants to fulfill her dream life. To have a family. But (MAJOR SPOILER STOP HERE IF THIS IS ENOUGH)
she is sterile. thus cannot have one. Resetting her psychosis. And restarting the process over and over again.
So she's basically living a cinderalla story in her mind. But in reality, is hoping for an outcome that will not come.
So the story repeats again, and again, and again, forever.
Now for my thoughts: This spoke a lot to me as a child who grew up surrounded by Disney princesses who were all perfect. And your stereotypical woman. As someone with mental issues that can occastionally throw me into a type of psychosis, the forming of mental barriers, makes it hard to break a cycle.
I think this is a good reflection on how many girls feel about society and how they should be and such. Taken to an extreme, which honestly, I could see being a reality for someone(s).
I really do suggest this game, if you want a quick, however-not interactive game. Which I know for some isn't what they like. But this touches on things that are a real issue for young people. Even with the information I've given, it's nothing compared to how it's written in the text.
Just don't let the imagery fool you, things are not as it seems in this twisted Cinderella Story.

The story, game engine, and themes are superb and the game is worth playing just to experience the universe and environments that has been so brilliantly created.
However the use of monsters actually weakens the game, with a lot of the encounters feeling more like annoying distractions. They aren't especially scary or disturbing, and quickly feel more like lethal (and sometimes tedious) obstacles to be passed.
One type is able to teleport, which just felt incredibly cheap, especially as the area it was located in was very interesting, and provided some story. Which made me wish they hadn't bothered with the monster.
Another time I opened a door only to have a monster kill me, seemingly only because it happened to have walked to that area as I opened the door. So it was just literally bad timing, as it could have been anywhere.
One monster is scripted and I died needlessly to find that out, and again, the way it was used just felt cheap and poorly written.
So ultimatley I would say the monsters are by far the weakest part of the game, and distract (and irritate) you from an otherwise superb and brilliantly realised experience.
The plot also feels unfinished, with so much of the backstory and character stories left untold. Which I felt were missed opportunities. I would have gladly swapped the monster sections for a few extra puzzles and discovering more about the environment and characters.
Grab it when it's on sale, and hopefully you won't find the monsters are annoying as I did.

I would absolute recommend this game for everyone who wants a strong story-build game with a bright and refreshing sense of horror.

Comipo is a software developed to help you create manga without being able to draw, but is it really working as good as it is telling you?
The answer have to be yes. The software is nice and you are provided with a good asset and big amounts of items to use, however, i can't say i recommend this software.
There are diffrent art styles, or at least it looks like it. The characters have a good details, while the backgrounds are a mess in my eyes, some of them even looks like they've just taken a picture with a camera and just done some quick photoshop editing to put it in place, while others are poorly made in my eyes.
As for the dlcs, they are overpriced. You get what you pay for, the name litteraly says it all. You only get clothes and one small asset of maybe 5 objects with that dlcs. So for owning a RPG Costume DLC i can litteraly just use modern backgrounds.
Now, before you all complain on my review, this software is ADVETISED to say you don't need to be a good artist, however, the software is a tool to artsists. Then again, if you can draw, it won't feel the same unless you match the art of the character. This is an issue which i have come to terms with and gave up on the software.
Notes: I had a 30 days trial of this software earlier, and i didn't buy this, i got it through Humble Bundle.
Conclusion:
Once again have they advertised a tool as a software that anyone can use without any skill at all. This software is good for people who can draw, but i cannot, and therefor have to stick to the original asset. I give a bad recommendation due to the DLC content, which costs a lot, and really doesn't provide you with the content the store page shows you.
Software itself is good as mentioned, but you are limmited without being able to draw yourself.
I bought it, Played it, and hated it. Maybe in a year when they add more content and fix some bug issues. Catch it on a steam sale, not worth the price at the moment.

I am playing Dragon Saga / Dragonica for almost 4 years now and I used to play on the former german servers but after these server closed I decided  to start again on this last official server about a year ago and I really enjoyed all the time of it.
The game offers so many opportunities either you prefer it to play PvE or PvP, also the classes can be played in many ways, same for the equipment, so everybody can focus on his/her preferences.
Also, provided the players got equal equipment, the pvp system isn't such unbalanced as some people are stating, it's always fun to compete with other players and to improve your own skills and gain some experience. There are also various available PvP modes, so it's kinda diversified.
The same fact applies to the PvE contents in this game, there are many dungeons and with some practice and equipment it's even able to clear them alone but there's always the possibility to create a party for more fun or faster runs, also the search system for partys is neatly arranged so you can always find a party easily. Additionally, the mission maps are always good alternative to farm if you're rather a "grinder".
At the same time there are plenty quests you can complete beside leveling or farming and in general there are so many things you can do in this game even if you don't expect it at the first sight.
At this point I also want to emphasize the work, which has been done by WarpPortal. They rescued a great game and in the recent past there were so many great changes made to improve the gameplay, help the community or simply fix bugs. The support is also a good address if you need some help, since I only had good experiences with it.
It's very impressive how much work has been done in the past year and with how much enthusiasm the team is working on this game. The amount of players also increased continuously while I play here and that's the result of the great work of WarpPortal and the fact that this is simply a great game.
Finally, I gotta say, that the community on this server is great compared to many other games I played, also the forums are good for information, help requests, guides and many other things.
Maybe we see each other ingame and sorry for my bad english, I am not a native speaker!

I just got this game today and I am hooked.
This is such a brilliant game, whilst the gameplay itself is fairly simplistic, it is the story and how player choices affect the plot that is the true driving force of this game. different companions have various troubles and each has their own personality, background and personal trials that they must overcome. Even the opponants and the side characters all have their backgrounds and personalities, this is a game that gets you really invested in the characters.
The gameplay is a mix of ball game and 3 vs 3 combat, each team is made up of a maximum of 3 combatents, each having their own atributes and abilities that can help you secure victory which requires strategic use of abilities and picking the right team for the right challenge. You ccan also equip each of your companions with a talisman which often provide bonus traits, such as moving faster or having a longer range attack.
As far as content goes, you will find a wealth of it here. So far I have spent 8 hours in the game and have only finished the first part of the campaign. As well as the campaign (which by the way has various different pathways that you can choose and can be played more than once), there are vs matches that can be played against other players or AI opponants, there are various difficulty settings, ranging from easy to moderate, to extreamly hard.

It's a fine program with many limitations, but may not be useful for everyone, here's an extended review for the potential costumer and hopefully feedback for the devs.
ComiPo by it's own grounds is very limited, you can't edit the character's height, proportions, width, etc. so you'll never see old people looking old, nor a younger character looking younger from the rest, so you've got all cookie cutter models, you can't even adjust parameters such as eye size and such (I wanted to adjust the chin and cheek width so badly but I can't).
There's not many customization options, there's some very limited set of accsesories and hair styles, so the combinations end up very limited, you can't customize the colors of items or clothing either (altough there's some very nice filters for the final images), so far it seems like there's no in-game option to change the character's skin colours.
The DLCs barely add anything to the mix, I bought a bundle, I think it contained 2 or 3 DLCs and when I used the program it felt as if I didn't had any DLCs, as they are pretty missleading telling you they offer a two digit amount of clothing each, but in the end it's just 1-2 clothes palette swapped, if they allowed you to recolor the clothing it would be very helpful and add many possibilities, but as it is, the DLC is good to have but not a must buy.
Now, with all this said, you may be wondering why I recommend this program.
To me it's helpful, I like to draw to relax, I use CSP, but the dummies included (on CSP) are extremely hard to pose (altough more versatile), but it consumes A LOT of time to get the desired pose and angle to me at least, so I prefer to use this, make a vanilla character, pose it as I need, convert to png and use as reference on CSP, on the downside, even when there are a lot of poses here, camera angles and such (which btw is very fast compared to CSP's), they arn't very flexible, you can rotate the head and such, but (may be a newb mistake here, so I apologize if I'm mistaken, I'll make sure to edit if I find out later on) it seems like you can't rotate hands or other body parts.
With that said, I think the devs can have a very nice and versatile program if they work on it, specially the customization options, Steam workshop for this would be awesome to allow people to upload their models and such.
To the costumer: if you want a quirky program to have a giggle and such, this may be for you, if you need some quick reference dummies like me, this works as well, but if you're looking for something serious to do comics and such, you may not find what you're looking in here (mainly the customization, it's so limited, otherwise the filters are awesome).
To the devs: I think the hardest part is done (the core software), just add more customization options (body proportions and clothing), more interactions betwen models, more hair, and accesories and such and you'll have a solid program backed by a clean and intuitive interface, just stop with the DLCs please as they barely add anything, they're quite expensive and may be overwhelming to the new users, unless you plan to add more to the current DLCs so they're more worthy of buying and owning, as it is, it's just not worth it.
Also some glitches need to be fixed, it's kind of silly that firefox and ComiPo can't co-exist without comipo crashing.
I hope this review helps potential costumers with their purchase and the devs on improving the experience so we can get a better product.
Cheers!

Supergiant was already praised for their previous games, especially for their visual, musical and storytelling achievements. Pyre (2017) honors the beauty of both Bastion (2011) and Transistor (2014), and its soundtrack is on pair with the previous games' too. It resembles Bastion more than it does the 2014 title, which fits well with the game in general and keeps the unique charm of Transistor, well... Unique. What Pyre is one step ahead in is its storytelling, which is a paradigm shift in itself. Forget the simplistic concepts of multiple endings or a good/bad ending: this game will challenge you to leave your comfort zone and make significant choices that
influence your every step in the Main Campaign, with a Undertale-like level of revolution to storytelling and unmeasurable replayability.
Along with its amazing story, Pyre has a fun, engaging and new gameplay, which offers as many possibilities for different styles and approaches to its strategy and skill as an RPG, but with the simplicities of a sport/e-sport, with local multiplayer available for some couch-friendly fun.
Pyre a is beautiful, fun, touching, intriguing game worthy of laughs and tears.
There is no perfect game, but Pyre is as perfect as it could be for what it was set out to achieve. 10/10

I intended to do a fuller review (Yes, even more than this) but I ran out of space, so long story short this game has some issues but overall its my favorite game ive played in a very long time even with its issues. And I hope you can ignore the circlejerk of anti Ubisoft enough to realize the devs are working on the issues, that being said let's dive into it.
So what can I say about For Honor? Amazing combat that has a huge amount of depth, anyone who says otherwise didn't attempt to learn and stuck with an endless cycle of the three basic mechanics, blocking, attacking, and guard breaking. I will agree that right now some characters are clearly a cut above the rest but the developers are being cautious with the buffs and nerfs to prevent kneejerk changes, and I respect that, that should be encouraged instead of ♥♥♥♥♥ed about.
The campaign is pretty important as it helps you learn mechanics, but where you get to really master certian mechanics is practicing with another player who you can get good at a specific mechanic with, 5 minutes of practicing counter guard breaks with a friend is more useful than 5 hours in pubs.
The community is generally pretty good and pretty nice, you do have a few groups that you can encounter that can be annoying though, there are those who try to enforce a sense of "Honor" into the game, citing that throwing people off edges and fighting them 2v1 is unfair despite the game giving them very good tools to deal with such a situation, as far as my opinion goes there isn't anything wrong with throwing someone off or ganking them because if it works on them they need to improve, that being said you shouldn't exclusively rely on these things because it hinders your improvement as a player. There are also one trick ponies who only spam one thing, these people are pretty easy to beat once you learn their strategy and they are some of the best ways to get good at dealing with a certian mechanic.
In a way the game is a giant 3D game of Rock Paper Scissors, with many mechanics countering others and needing to know what to use and when, personally I love this, because as you learn to spot what is a "Rock" you can feel yourself instinctively responding with "Paper", but it isn't always over there, as there are feints and mixups and other tricks that can turn the metaphorical Rock into Scissors, its an intense mind game that never ends and you constantly improve at.
*Obvious Spoilers about the Campaign (completed on Hard the final real difficulty)*
Back to the Campaign though it needs to be mentioned just how entertaining it is despite how repetetive it is, in the campaign you get a mixed bag of trying many characters, in the Knight Campaign you try the Warden, but you also have a level to let you learn the Lawbringer, and one for the Peacekeeper too, the Conqueror is left out however and I feel he could have been utilized.
In the Viking story you get to play as the Raider, whom is Legendary, which has become a meme among the community due to the boss he fights having a seemingly broken voice line that repeats every couple seconds saying "You're a Raider, legendary", however the boss in question is a Samurai and there is some speculation that since the story is all just a retelling by warriors from each faction, that its just classic Viking exaggeration to brag about their leader. You also get to play as the Valkyre and the Warlord, the Berserker being the odd man out this time. The humor in the Viking section is especially well written and casual even in the midst of battle, whereas the Knight humor came from circumstance, a stark but very enjoyable contrast that kept things light.
Lastly there was the Samurai story, where you are for the first time not playing as one of the Vanguard classes but instead the Orochi, an Assassin, the logic here being based on the fact that they are the equal of 100 men and the strongest the Samurai have to offer. In this campaign you only play as the Orochi and Kensei, while Nobushi and Shugoki are present they are not playable, this caused the Samurai campaign to feel especially repetetive, as the Orochi is both poorly suited to deal with the weak foot soldiers, and also very much based around punishing mistakes from opponents, and since the ai is largely reactive the Orochi more than other classes is left spamming a few attacks to defeat most foes. That being said it wasn't entirely unentertaining and it still had it's enjoyable moments, had the campaigns had more than 6 missions for any of them I might have been more drained than I was. The Samurai campaign was topped off with the absolute final boss and big villian fight, the fight against Apollyon, who long story short is a typical Warden that is a little more aggressive and has some of her mechanics down, honestly though a level 3 (max level) difficulty bot would have been a harder challenge than her, the only real challenge came from having such a low health pool that you would often find yourself playing the dodge game until your heal feat came off cooldown and then got back to whacking her. She had one cool special attack but overall was fairly dissapointing, with most of my deaths being the result of mostly unpredictable falling rocks in her arena rather than her capability to finish you off.
The Story Mode was good and overall pretty fun, I imagine it is far more enjoyable with friends, something I didn't realize was an option until I finished it. On hard it took about 7 hours to complete without searching for every observable and breakable (Find the breakables though, they drop good stuff, I went back for them) I had a pretty good time and I think the length was right, though I wish that each campaign was structured around letting you play every class and then 3 of the main class instead of arbitrarially not letting you play one or two of them, as not letting you play them didn't really help the story at all since a perspective switch was done for the Lawbringer mission  despite the warden being present and it didn't seem to negatively impact the story, I have also confirmed that at least early on co-op doesn't let you replace the npcs either so that is a missed opportunity as well.
*The one issue that really is worth mentioning*
As you have no doubt seen from other reviews there are some issues that need fixing that make the game worse than it could be at the moment (Most if not all of these have been acknowledged by the devs though) the Gear system is blatantly unenjoyable, it gives substantial buffs to stats that you can choose and put simply a prestige 3 player has no reason to ever lose to a gearless one because they can get their revenge meter up with ease and one to two shot someone without gear. The Revenge gear is the biggest issue because it's spread out across all the gear options instead of concentrated on a piece or two, allowing players to buff up nearly every aspect of it to max, making it horrendously overpowered. Frankly even massive tuning can't really bring it to reasonable levels, and I personally feel that the best solution is to add gearless versions of the 3 gear modes, Dominion, Elimination, and Skirmish. That way the modes with gear are kind of like playing Smash Brothers with the items on, you expect stuff to get silly and op and can opt out, at least until you have competetive gear. Gear also makes you look cooler, figured I should mention that. Gear by no means makes the game pay to win though, there is this nasty rumor going around that this is the case and anyone who has actually gotten to the prestige character level neccessary to get the best gear would realize that good gear is handed out like candy once you get to the right level, all you can pay for is a slight (and I mean pretty damn slight) xp boost to get there a bit quicker, which can be earned fairly easily in game too.
Oh also Skirmish is a garbage mode but I lack the space to elaborate.

The translation is rather subpar, to say the least, with countless grammar errors, typos, and some sentences so poorly constructed that even by reading them three times over you can't figure out what they were actually supposed to mean. As well as some basic errors in programming, like having someone's name show up as the start of their dialogue, instead of being in the box their name is supposed to be.
That aside, the actual story is good enough to make up for it, which I won't go into detail about, because, as with any story, the less you know about it going in, the better the experience you can get from it. I would actually recommend this episode on its own merits, regardless of whether you intend to read the other two episodes of the series, this episode can stand alone as a story by itself, and honestly, after this one, I'm on the fence about whether reading the others is even worth it.
As far as the series goes, a huge point against the series is that from episode to episode, the names of several things change each time. It really deals a huge hit to the immersion when after switching between episodes you have to relearn what all the names of things are because they aren't kept consistent. And, to be honest, the names that are used in Episode 1 are the more sensible names by far in almost all cases.
To just give some examples of the name inconsistencies.
-In Episode 1, the character the story follows is nicknamed "Hal", in Episode 2, he becomes "Haru", in Episode 3, it's back to "Hal"
-In Episode 1, this story takes place on Earth's moon, in Episode 2, they call it "Terra" instead of "Earth", seemingly implying it's supposed to be a fictional planet, however, references to Japan and Europe are still in the story, which didn't make any sense. In Episode 3, it's "Earth" again.
-In Episode 1, there is a character named "Lisa", and the name makes sense because they're not supposed to be of Japanese origin or anything, despite that, they go with the name "Risa" for the character in Episodes 2 and 3.

It's not a good game. But it is a fun game. And that's what's important right?
Most of the reviews seem to cover the gameplay pretty well, so I mainly want to talk about whether or not players who spent more money or have been playing longer have an advantage. Is the game pay 2 win? Yes, definetely. But I didn't spend any money on the game and I have no problem wiping the floor with 90% of the players I come across, whether they are paying players or not. And there is nothing that affects game balance that cannot eventually be earned for free. Some would call this more of a "pay2skip" system where you can pay to accelerate your progression.
One thing that is nice about the game is that with rare exception, every bonus you get has a drawback. There are a few things in the game that are straight upgrades with no downside, but I have played well over a hundred matches at this point and I can count on one hand the number of times I saw another player with a setup that felt unfair or overpowered.
The game is more balanced than most people think. Even the stuff that seems obviously overpowered is not always so strong in practice. For example, the reinforcement upgrade for tanks. Sure, you get 3 tanks. But, I can spawn my tanks faster. So, who cares if you get more tanks in the long run, if I can rush your base before you ever get a chance to do so? Or, maybe you have some really powerful support cards which let you spawn 3 tanks at once for very little cost. Sure, that's nice, but now you have a bunch of vehicles grouped together with no infantry support, and you have no resources left to support their push either, while meanwhile I'm well stocked on cruise missiles and soldiers with rocket launchers.
I even make the same mistake as well at times. "Oh, this long range upgade is going to make my sniper so powerful," I think to myself as he gets rushed down and grenaded to death. My conclusion is, yes the game is pay2win, in the sense that you can spend money to get an advantage over thsoe who don't, but the game is usually more balanced than it seems, and it mainly just comes down to who is the better player in the end.

At its core, Pyre is an RPG where you'll advance the story by talking with characters you'll meet along the way and by controlling them in sports-like gameplay sequences called rituals. A combination I had never seen before and left me very intrigued when I first saw the game trailer.
First thing you should know about Pyre I think is that it is the kind of RPG filled with dialogues for you to read. Most of the game is not voice acted and a big part of the lore is handed to you in the book of rites which you'll fill along your progression in the story. So if reading is something you don't particularly like in a game, Pyre might not be for you. Your loss, really.
On the other hand, if you like an RPG with an insane amount of branching paths, complex and beautifully written original characters and a fun original gameplay to go with all that, then you should definitely get Pyre.
I know I said original twice, it's not my fault this game is not like anything I've seen before.
First thing you'll notice about it is the incredible art direction which is strikingly beautiful with vibrant colors and charismatic characters. The music is wonderful too, Darren Korb delivers another soundtrack you'll want to listen outside of the game, I especially loves the tracks where Ashley Barrett sings.
I won't talk about the story too much here because it is something everyone should discover for itself and because yours will very likely be different from the one I experienced.
You have so many choices to make about the characters you'll encounter that the story can unfold in a lot of different ways. There is no real failure state in Pyre, you can win or lose in rituals and it will affect the story accordingly. You might sometimes even want to lose on purpose to help an adversary which is something you very rarely see.
And this is where Pyre shines the brightest in my opinion, you'll truly become attached to theses characters and care about what happens to them. It also gives the game an immense replay value.
Aside from the story, rituals are the main gameplay sections of the game.
Imagine a 3v3 basketball-like game where each character has a protective aura and where the goal is to throw a magic orb into the adversary pyre. The thing is, when you hold the orb, you lose your aura and can easily be removed from the game.
At first, I though these mechanics might be a bit limited and might not hold for the whole game but I was wrong.
Every character has its own abilities which allows for more and more complex tactics has the game progresses.
Also, the IA is very competent, surprised me from time to time and even taught me a few tricks.
Know that you can play rituals in a PVP fashion outside of the story mode but I didn't try it so I don't know whether it is as fun or not against another person..
If I absolutely wanted to say something bad about Pyre, I would say that there are some clunky piece of UI here and there but nothing to be really worried about. Also the rituals might get a little repetitive towards the end of the story as you tend to fight the same adversaries multiple times.
But to be honest, this game is absolutely wonderful and it is baffling to me to see such a small team can come out with such a streak of incredible games.
I can't thumb up this enough.
Storyline and gameplay is nice, definitely worth a shot.

While I haven't completely finished the game yet, I still wanted to leave a review for anyone looking to buy this game when it's not on sale. I'm really on the fence, and while I would recommend buying it at a discount, not at full price,

There are only a few sprites per character, a very limited number of backgrounds, and sometimes the visual doesn't completely match what's happening in the story. If they don't have a visual that somehow matches the storyline at that point, they just show a black screen. Given that this is a "visual" novel, that feels incredibly lazy to me.
Also the translation feels weak to me as well. I don't speak Japanese, but the English translations are sometimes so weird that I doubt they're accurate. One character was "exuding question marks" at one point. Yeah, that's not a thing. Again, it just feels like a rushed, lazy translation that kicks you out of the story somewhat.
So, it's a thumbs down for me, unless you can catch it on sale. If the devs put in the effort to update the visuals and the translation, I could easily see myself changing my recommendation. But not as things stand right now.

This is obviously an early review with only a couple of hours played. Overall, I rather enjoy it. You play as a Colonial Fleet commander charged with defending the Twelve Colonies from the Cylons. The game consists of two layers, tactical and strategic. On the strategic layer, you build ships to assign to fleets. You start with one fleet but almost immediately get the ability to have many more. The effect of this is you quickly get into the meat of the game, I really appreciate this because I hate games that get you going in little dribs and drabs. Better ships are locked by story missions, so that's a bit disappointing but it is ok. Cylon forces quickly accumulate everywhere and you simply do not have enough fleets to handle them all, so you have some difficult choices to make. Commanders can level up and ships can be customized to a limited degree. If I have any complaint it is, it feels like it might be shallow but it is hard to say. Honestly, though sometimes less is more and there might be enough depth here to keep the game fun. Tactical combat is good, AI is sufficient, although you'll almost certainly win in a matched encounter (I believe cylon raiders have an AI flaw that I've reported to the devs). In particular, if you want a game where there's a lot of decision making to make at the strategic layer I think you'll enjoy this experience.
Overall: Very good, I really like it. 8.5 out of 10.

I picked this game up on launch day for myself and a friend as a gift. We both have been looking forward to this game and for myself I saw some potential in the hour long announcement/gameplay reveal stream. At point of writing I've played almost 3 hours and gotten to mission six. I can't recommend this game to anyone.
The game has a solid framework, no doubt. The combat is well structured and the different ship classes are uniquely designed and instantly recognizeable, if a bit samey in terms of capability. The only two Cylon ships that stand out are the tech corvette and the frigate-carrier. The rest just seem to be scaling tiers of bigger warship. The Colonial ships also suffer a bit of same capability with the difference being if they have vipers, missiles, or torpedoes. The CIC mechanics, including the resource management and fleet deployment, are also a bit confusion and impenetrable for someone who is starting out for the first time. It's also not helped that everything is so resource intensive. I have to pay requisition to get the plans, then pay tylium to build them, and either wait for X number of turns (which aren't really defined) to pass or pay quadrouple the price to get them now. It also doesn't help that it costs as much as a new ship to jump the Daidalous fleet. Combine this with the fact that most missions that aren't story missions pay only tiny amounts of tylium, and it feels like I've been set up to fail.
The story itself feels like the writers set up some bullet points and cliffnotes, planned out the first three missions, then just gave up on the rest. There's no real rhyme or reason for anything that happens. For some reason everything the Cylons do gets pinned on the Colonial Fleet, which is so poorly understaffed and underfunded that the "fleet" Cain inherits after Picon is nuked is just a pair of corvettes but apparantly can afford to be building three battlestars at once. Speaking of the battlestars, the fact that we have to give our only operation one away to Picon itself is head scratching. The Colonial Fleet is supposed to be the unified military of the Colonies. So why are we giving away our biggest warships to the individual colonial militaries? It also doesn't help that once we give away that battlestar, we lose the reason why we have to keep sending our mobile fleet HQ and shipyard into battle over and over again. It was excusable when we had a battlestar that needed something bigger to jump it to combat zones but after we gave it away the dialoge implied it was going back to its safe haven.. except it didn't was in fact required by the game to advance.
An indepth comprehensive tutorial explaining all of the mechanics, reducing costs by half or increasing rewars pay out, and fleshing out the story and progression path would make this game worth 40 USD. As it is I'd probably only buy it for 20 USD, if at all.

soma is the kind of game you give someone who says "games are for kids. they offer nothing of value or substance to the world". why? not to make them shut up but to make them wake up. this game is a prime example of what good narrative  looks like. this game makes you ask yourself some hard questions. what does it mean to be real? is there a soul. am i just moving thinking meat? it doesn't provide an answer, just the question. at its core i think that is what soma is trying to get you to ask. it is a game however so lets talk about that for a sec.
this first person game has simple usable controls. the game play is varied somewhat in that there are puzzles stealth and exploration bits. the game really doesn't hold your hand the way most games do. your not following a way marker. you have to use context clues to figure out were you are going. you might walk right past a puzzle because you didn't know you were looking for one. this can be frustrating at times but i think it really comes down to what you enjoy in a game. if you come to a cave in skyrim that looks to be more then what it seems and relish the challenge of figuring out what to do in it, then soma is gonna be more on the fun side. if you however would go "hmm bet ill find a quest for this later that tells me what to do" you may find this more frustrating.
graphics are better then passable. not really worth talking too much about. it gets the job done and then some. what is worth talking about is the atmosphere and tone. you really feel alone, isolated and in my case often tense. the music and sound effects really immerse you in the game. its really dark and creepy and you relish any time you get to spent with npc's. you learn to want for the light. you dread when static and artifacting creeps into the game because you know something is about to go down.
the story really shouldn't be talked about too much because this is the selling point of the game and anyone who ruins that for you should be frowned at. all I'm going to say is its very compelling. there is allot of flavor and context if your willing to slow down and read some stuff. there aren't collectibles but you can run right past juicy context if you hold down the sprint button all the time.
in closing i liked soma. its not a game everyone is going to frequent all the time but i think its one anyone can play through it once. the narrative is solid, the game play is pretty fun and the atmosphere is creepy. give it a play if you find it on sale. you owe it to yourself.

I've never written a Steam review in my life, but I felt inclined to do so for Friday The 13th for three reasons. One, because the reviews for this game were Negative to Mixed (they're now a well-deserved Mostly Positive!) Two, because I've never met so many cool people in any other title. Finally, the third reason is because this is some of the most fun I've ever had playing an online survival horror game.
If you've read the game description or watched YouTube videos, you know how the game works. You play as either a counselor trying to survive a night with Jason Vorhees, or you play as the hockey mask-wearing killer himself. Within its first week, F13 garnered hundreds of unforgiving negative reviews based on its bugs and stability issues. Within a WEEK, on PC, the developers singled out and addressed many of those problems. All it takes is a quick visit to their Twitter or Steam Discussion Forums to realize these folks really are listening and working their asses off to improve the game. If you've been playing since day one, there's no denying the improvements, and I believe this game can only get better from here.
I was afraid, even after having helped Kickstart this game, that the gameplay would grow stale after a couple dozen hours. How many rounds of Hide & Go Seek could you possibly play before getting bored? Well, I've spent 35.7 hours in two weeks without tiring of the game once, so I couldn't tell you. Many people I know have put in twice that many hours.
Whether or not you will enjoy F13 depends on who you play with. While the community at large seems to be great, the longevity most players seek will come in the form of new friends. I've never added so many people to my friends list from one game. When you're playing with randos, the game is still good but you don't feel the same sense of "We're a tight knit unit up against one bad motherf-----." When you're playing with either friends you've had for a while, or new names and voices you've come to grow fond of, that's when F13 absolutely shines and reaches new levels of fun. Whether you're banding together to achieve numerous objectives, or you're just running around trash-talking whoever's playing as Jason, Camp Crystal Lake (or any other map) becomes your gory, hysterical playground.
If you're old enough to remember long nights spent split-screen gaming with your buddies, this game will bring those feelings back and you'll have an amazing time.
If you're a fan of the Friday the 13th films, you're DEFINITELY going to have an amazing time.
If you're an anti-social derptrain who takes things too seriously and gets frustrated dying in a game where, 85% of the time, you die, this probably isn't the game for you.
I'm not going to tell you how the counselor mechanics work, because figuring them out for yourself or asking your fellow counselors is half the fun. All you know for sure, starting out, is that you need to survive. You'll go from not knowing which weapon stuns or does damage to knowing exactly which weapon works best for your current situation. You'll go from not knowing the ins and outs of stealth to carefully watching the blips on your radar so as not to make too big a ripple. Hell, it took me two games before I even realized I could slow jog. Thank god for slow jogs.
Regarding Jason, a lot of players jumped on the "He's too OP!" bandwagon at first because they wanted to get into a game, escape easily and level up. Why they expected a "How To Easily Escape Jason Vorhees" training simulator is beyond me. I'm going to guess they've never actually seen a Friday The 13th film and assumed they were G-rated romps where a few camp counselors had s'mores over a fire as Jason played the Ukelele. Playing as Jason is deeper than "Morph, Grab, Repeat," especially now that people have grown craftier as counselors. You've got to know where to trap, when to throw those precious knives, how to dodge any number of projectiles, where to cut the power and focus on the spots YOU would hide if you were a counselor. It's fun as hell, but when you're getting juked by a car that keeps going forward/reverse on you, you've got to have a gameplan.
Are there problems with F13? Yes. Here are my biggest caveats:
- Jason's reach is a good 2000 ft. long.
- When Jason grabs you, you'd better hope you've got a switchblade or you're going down in two seconds.
- Sometimes when you're trying to do things like set a trap by the door, you end up unbarring the door.
- Hit detection can be a pain in the butt for Jasons AND counselors.
- Tommy Jarvis sounds less like the experienced badass he's supposed to be and more like a rich kid who was just told Abercrombie & Fitch is going out of business.
- Spawning right next to a car or major cabin (usually any Jason's first stop) is probably the most groan-inducing experience in the game.
Some of these problems seem like no-brainers. For example, why not make the time it takes to break out of Jason's grasp dependent on how injured/afraid you are instead of where Jason happens to have enough space to pop your skull? This way, your game isn't over when you're grabbed just because, woops, you don't have a switchblade.
A couple of bugs and glitches exist, of course, but I personally forgive them based on the proactive nature of the developers and because, for me at least, they've never been game-breaking.
This review's been long enough already, so
Friday The 13th is a ridiculously fun survival horror game that will reward immensely those who play with people they like and have a mic. You will make friends. You will love playing with those friends. It's a damn good time and it can be either heart-poundingly suspenseful or downright hilarious. BUY IT!

SOMA is a science fiction horror by Frictional Games, the same people who bought you Amnesia and Penumbra.  SOMA relies on chase scenes, soundtrack and psychological horror to build tension as you take the role of someone lost in a strange facility prowling with highly aggressive mutants controlled by a malfunctioning station-wide intelligence.
SOMA has undoubtably the most incredible storyline of all Frictional's titles, it's plotline is immersive and incredibly detailed, the game has a 10-12 hour playthough if you take your time, 4-6 if you rush it and I've played this game 3 times and am on my 4th playthough and am still finding new little details, like who each of the monsters are, the history of the environment and many more things which I won't spoil.  Every time you play again, you'll notice something new.
The scares are terrifying.  SOMA employs close to no jumpscares, opting for more advanced themes such as music and visual effects.  It could be said that you will never be surprised when you see the monster, you will always know when it's in the same room as you, but that doesn't make it any less frightening.
The encounters in SOMA are heavily planned and scripted, even in a second playthrough I know exactly when I'm going to have a bad time, but that's a good thing.  Frictional have planned monster appearences right when they're due, right when they've been mounting tension by having it stalk you, scaring you for the past 20 minutes.
Unlike other horrors I've played, SOMA always finds a way to make the encounters unusual and different.  Is it because you run into a new monster that hunts in a different way almost every time?  Maybe because your environments are so vastly different.
Additionally, the game has segregated the scares from the story incredibly well so you know you can enjoy every juicy bit of plot without the threat of a mutant [spoilers] chasing you.  And in the same sense, when you do have said enemy chasing you, you don't have to worry about much more than getting the hell out of whatever room you're in as quickly as reasonably possible.
Gameplay-wise, the controls are basic and remeniscent of Amnesia only without an inventory system.  Shift to sprint, ctrl to walk quietly, right-click to pick up and throw, left click to interact with environment.  The environment is nice to look at, it's not winning any awards for graphics, but it's definately a step up from Frictional's previous releases.  Most challenges could be described as either retrieving an item, escaping an area or solving a puzzle on a computer to unlock a door.  These of course splinter off into many sub-puzzles, most of which are accompanied by an angry mutant.

Love the product, but, frankly, I'm very disappointed in some of the actions taken by the developers. Developers should fix the exploits and glitches in their game instead ofpunishing players by perma-banning them without warning, which is draconian to say the least (it didn't happen to me, but it did to someone I know). I don't see why a three strike rule (three warnings then perma-ban) can't be implimented. At the very least, present evidence to the player of the offense and allow them the opportunity to repeal the ban. The whole process needs to be transparent. It's one thing if they pirated the game, but it's another to do it to someone who paid money for the product. If they are going to perma-ban people based on their behavior (can team killers be banned? They are really the ones "killing the spirit of the game") then they shouldn't take their money, and give them a refund for their now defunct game as it would seem disingenuous to happily take someone's money, but prohibit them from partaking in their purchase that the provider has... well...provided. It's like a baker who bakes the apple pie, the customer pays for the whole apple pie, then the baker takes the apple pie away just as the customer took a bite, because the baker dislikes apple pie. Continuing to do so is a sure way to self-destruct a video games community.

Okay so I have had some time to play with the program and this review is just based on the time I've had with it.
This is a fun program for any and all anime fans that want to make barebones manga or images (things for forums, backgrounds, or avatars) and is easy to use. The interface is easy to pick up. If you want something to bring your idea of the next big manga to life, this isn't it. So I say get it when it is on SALE. But if you enjoy playing with preset tools and have to money to get the DLC, then this is right up your alley.
In reality this is a drag and drop program with preset expressions, backgrounds, and models. While i have limited time with this, take it all with a grain of salt. It seems that i can not play with the pre-rendered models. But this isn't something that should turn you away as there is quite a few to chose from. The only thing i would advise you to do is look at you talents. If you are a skilled artist then don't get this, but if you can't stand at the level of an anime artist then this is for you.
The things you have the potential to create are nice, but it is up to you to truly make it our own. This is cookies cutter, but you have the ability to upload your own images and models. So to someone who is skilled, this could be fun to use as a storyboard. To others like myself, this is just mindless fun to make wacky anime images just for the lulz.
All in all on sale, you can't go wrong as this program it has enough features to make it worth it. But like I said, if you want something that will make your visions come to life this may not be for you. This is what it looks like and promises nothing more. If you want a program that does more or you feel you could do the illustrations yourself then this, again, isn't for you. But for all of those that just want something to play with to make some solid anime pics, or to possible use it to the limits, then this is great. You will have fun with it no matter what as long as you have some imagination and vision. But if you have ADD and want it to do all the work....i say just draw it or just watch more anime.
Anyway I give it 8/10

Quick summary: an Intro to Economics class coupled with a rollercoaster of emotions. If you liked Spice & Wolf or even have a passing interest in the world of finance, get the three-part bundle and don't look back.
(No spoilers review)
So, World End Economica; a VN that showed up on my "Recommended" feed so often I felt I just
to try it, but never did for some reason. Until I finally did, and boy I'm glad.
Let's start with the basics: graphics ain't a strong point of this VN. Character illustrations are good, but reused too often; meanwhile backgrounds are simple but *also* overused. CGs are pretty nice and fit well with the artistic style of the VN, but the fact you unlock the CG gallery only after finishing the game is a minus overall. Still, it does its work and it's never distracting.
No voice acting whatsoever, and the music ranges from decent to downright irritating. You don't lose much by playing the game on Mute, to be honest.
And here we finally get to the chewy center of this VN. So, how is it? in a word, delightful. It's sci-fi, but
sci-fi; no green-skinned aliens, no space battles, nothing but a space elevator between Earth and its new colony on the moon and the hopes of someday, maybe reaching Mars.
To avoid spoilers I won't go into much detail, but I'll say this: the game is an emotional rollercoaster, which will have you on the edge of your seat multiple times throughout the entire volume, with characters that are all flawed, act on realistic motivations, and come into conflict for believable reasons; definitely one of the best reads I've had in years. Contrary to other reviewers, I found the economics jargon simple to follow, and the game offers definitions and examples through the plot itself on the most important terms, like short-selling and margin-buying.
Within the series itself, I think this chapter is somewhat self-contained; the plot does have a clear beginning, a climax and a conclusion, so you could buy it and skip the rest if you didn't like it, or found the jargon confusing. It does leave a few plot points hanging for its sequels, obviously, but it's not a complete cliffhanger either.
It's a kinetic novel, so there are no branches whatsoever; it's a linear story from start to end. I finished it in around 4.5 hours, but I'm a fast reader so it'd probably take most people around 6 hours of reading; not too long, but a decent length for its price.
Still, replay value is high, both to catch foreshadowing of later events, as well as re-reading complex points after you understand the jargon better. Or hell, just for the pleasure of it.
As I already said, this is the best VN I've read in years; if you're undecided I'd recommend you to buy this volume and give it a try, but most people should really go for the bundle, install it ASAP, and enjoy the best economics class in existence.

World End Economica is basically G-Senjou no Maou meets Spice and Wolf in a futuristic setting after humans have colonized the moon, with enough tragedy throughout to rival Clannad Afterstory. I normally quickly describe the premise as being about "a guy who trades stocks on the moon", similar to how most people summarize Spice and Wolf as being about "medieval economics". The descriptions leaves out a lot, but it sparks curiosity and grasps the core of the content.
I extremely enjoyed part 1. Part 2 was just as well written as part 1, but I personally didn't like it as much for the sorry state of the MC and the rushed ending. Part 3 is basically an economics textbook with tasty plot on the side. It wraps up the series well, but for reasons I can't state due to spoilers, it does have room for improvement. I don't read visual novels often, but this is one of my favorites. I even respect it a lot more than most of the good anime I've seen. Here's to praying it gets an anime adaptation eventually and the studio doesn't screw everything up.
As one final note, World End Economica is a kinetic novel. There aren't any choices, and there is only one outcome. This shouldn't waylay you from reading, though, as the content is unrealistically well written, despite there being no choices.

Well we finally had someone from Development contact us in regards to some bugs.
They are still interacting despite what we were told. So we have to disagree with people thinking this game is not still being cared for.
The gameplay is great, and it is addictive. People who do not practice enough will be frusterated in PvP unless they gain exp vs Random Bots.
We use the following setup to play, with no problems or crashes to date;
Running at 61-63 FPS
NVidea GTX 960
Intel I-7
Samsung Monitor
DDR3 12GB
A few notes;
The game is intense either with Bots or a real person. Regardless, you get rewarded for winning or losing, but naturally victory is a better payout.
This is NOT pay to win, I did not spend money for months, and held my own. I recently spent for some in game currency just to get a few extra perks since we are staying to keep playing.
The graphics are fantastic and the sound is without saying.
We recommend doing at least 75-100 Bot battles before you even dare playing a human. Many factors for this... learning the game, speed of reaction, strategy, getting cards and leveling up your troops in their various specialties.
Enjoy this gem of a game, that initally had those quick to react when they had a setback that lasted barely a month. SO they have since rerecovered nicely and have really moved foraward in all facets of the game.
Lastly, if you do plan on playing, then I suggest investing so when you do encounted people with 100's of games, you stand a chance.
Good luck!

The game comes with crafting system that is actually useful - the items you can craft do come without any real cash spending and believe it are not - are wanted, useful and do have a purpose.

I hate sports games. With a passion. The primary reason for this is that I am very much not a sports person in general and have always taken a dim view of the supposed value of them.
With that said, I hope this illustrates how much I absolutely adore this game despite the main gameplay being a fantasy set NBA Jam.
I think the reason why this resonates with me is both the absolutely drop dead gorgeous artwork and the fact that the story has a great of stakes to it. Succeeding in the Ritual (what the game calls a tournament) results in one of the characters that you gather in your journey to be the very best like no one ever was, forever leaves you.And these characters have a great deal of depth and story behind each one of them. They also possess tactical abilities that can assist you in the game and thus, you must choose between keeping a character with you in your journey and gameplay or let them be free to live out their own lives. It perfectly intertwines story and gameplay in a way I have scarcely seen in game. Not to mention it gives it great replay value. This couple with a deep well built world, hauntingly beautiful music and simple but challenging gameplay, I think this is as good as a game can get with someone like me who loves both art and story.
For fans of visual novels, NBA slam or simply gorgeous illuminated artwork, I cannot recommend this game enough.

Written by Isuna Hasekura (Spice and Wolf, Magdala de Nemure), this Visual Novel is not just entertainment, but also a lesson about capitalism, the stock market and the problems and merits of it. The author has already proven in the past that he is well versed in terms of business and trade, but World End Economica now sports a science-fiction scenario instead of his usual historical fantasy setting.
Pro:
- Extremely well written
- Roughly 13+ hours long
- Teaches you the stock market 101
- Good background art
Con:
-  Character art is likeable but average in quality
There is not much to complain here, so if you like Visual Novels or have read Spice and Wolf, you should definitely take a look at World End Economica.
