Kinda rough around the edges now, needs some balancing. Here are a few points after a little play. AI strategy can be summed up in three words - "hack and run" see #6 below. As other have said, price is too high wait for a sale. Wait for the first few patches now, this is one of those games that needs a few patches. Also this game could use a sandbox campaign because there isnt a lot of replayablility. I see DLC in our futures...
1. As the campaign progresses, you have no idea how well you are doing and you have have no idea what the goal is (hint: maybe there isnt a goal).
2. Difficulty scales poorly. One mission you fight three ships then the next mission you fight six with another wave of two that come in because the AI decided you were doing too well (at least someone knows how well I am doing, see #1 above).
3. Some missions seem un-winable. The rescue a freighter comes to mind. Even with the fastest ships I have in turbo mode it is not possible to interecpt the enemy before they destroy the ship. Balance needed.
4. 7 ships per fleet max is just bad design (this is 2017 after all, try harder). It becomes painfully obvious when you will get to a point where your old ships are useless. Since you can not concentrate your bad ships, they are doomed to die and the player is forced to grind to that end.
5. There does not seem to be an estimation of the size/power of enemy fleets until you are there beside them. Considering there are many humans live on these worlds with ships flying around, you would think someone would give the defense forces a heads up. Edit: I found out how to see the enemy strength. Is it on the campaign map maybe displayed with the enemy fleet icon? NO. Is it visable when you click on the enemy fleet? NO. It only seems visable when you open the enemy fleet sub-menu.
6. Hacking is basically an omni-direction, long range, weapon used to prop-up the AI and give it a chance. If the AI was limited to firing arcs and special weapon types, it would be too easy. Now the AI knows to hack your ships and run. Even their mid sized ships run and scatter when there is a lot of hacking going on (hint: this is the main enemy strategy for the ENTIRE game, as far as I have played. Hack and run, the end).
7. The battle maps are pretty plain despite there being a mechanic for debris. Some of the maps have one of two asteroids, but most objects are on the edges of the map and therefore worthless (decoration). The game might actually have a tactical element if there were real decisions to make.
8. There is no way to skip the cut scenes or some of the talking scenes. It is maddening to wait for them to stop talking after you have read the message while they talk. This is also bad when you start a new campaign and have to replay the tutorial with sooo much talking...
9. Because of the lack of variety between fleet intercept missions, it looks like the designers paniced and used the only tool left in their tool box - varied start locations. But since the battlemaps are just big open fields and the fleets are ALWAYS at least 3 turns distant, the start locations seem boring. Saddest of all is that the start locations are not random, per se, the enemy fleet always starts on one of your flanks and at a significant height difference.  Since the fleets are always so far apart, the fleet setup before the battle is kinda worthless (there is no reason to waste your time setting up). In short there are 4 general enemy fleet spawn points - left flank, high and low, and right flank, high and low.
List of lost opportunities -
1. The game is all about using a small number of big ships, but individual ships are so unimportant and disposable. If you are going to play with the limited number of ships (as if they are important), give each ship - upgrades, individual officers, and ship exp.

This is my first vn. As far as reviews go, none really reflect on what Ambre really is.
Ambre is a mix of consenance and distortion. Basically, it plays on good and bad feelings together. For example, the title calls this a heart breaking novel, but the description talks about how a man meets a little girl and takes her in. Typically, giving someone shelter would seem rather kind if it was coming from complete strangers. But the "heart breaking kinetic novel" tosses a wrench in things. You don't know what to expect. (Btw pretty sure steam doesn't allow pedophilia so don't worry about it while reading.) The feeling of uncertainty is what hits the audience hardest. You're fearful because you're not sure of what happens next. In my opinion, the VN doesn't do excellently in executing this. It's something that you have in every thing, from music to movies. Resolution is very important to having a story. It doesn't have to be satisfying, but it does have to be gripping. I'll admit that I felt like puking out of fear of what might have happen in the early/mid parts of the story. But instead of going the obvious route, they toss a twist and the story is different. (Phew.) But it's out of the frying pan and into something slightly worse than a frying pan. At this point, the twist makes the story very redundant and, quite frankly, not as intriguing. It doesn't introduce new plot elements, only repeats the same elements from a new persective which you probably read a few minutes ago considering this is a short kinetic novel that should take less than a couple hours.
This game made me sick and it had me hooked but small things keep the novel from being entirely captivating. The story isn't heart breaking in my opinion. The characters aren't developed enough to grow attached to as they both come off as extremely mentally ill. Like seriously. Minor spoilers-the intro is the 30 year old dude acting paranoid and lonely in his house freaking out about a forbidden room. Slight larger spoiler-The little girl starts acting more like a teenager and grows an obsession for pop culture's portrayal of the perfect lifestyle.
These characters aren't good. The girl is cute at a few points where it seems like mindless rambling but the moment anything is serious, it loses character. The male character is such a mystery as well, never truely revealing much about himself until the end.
Keep in mind that this kinetic, meaning you don't get a say in what happens. The ending isn't very good, in my opinion. It is a solid conclusion, but it ends in an awkward position. It's like if I was writing a paper about how private prisons are corrupted corporations that exploit prisoners for labor-and gave a really gripping intro and body, but ended it by saying something like "this is very bad and i don't like it." I could end it like that and it'd be okay, but it'd be better if I proposed a solution to the issue. Ambre just kinda ends on a conversation that rehashes the feelings of the charaters that we probably already understood by this point. (This was probably my favorite part though because it is something new that is introduced at the end instead of reused quotes that I had read 10-20 minutes ago and still remembered.
Conclusion
It made me feel anxiety, uncomfortable, a little meloncholic, and a little charmed. There were a few sweet moments in there. (Too bad for that twist and also moments priors.)
I give it a 3/5
It's not perfect. It has nice music and an appealing art style. The story is short but interesting. It does fail on a few levels to deliver a heart tearing story. It isn't revolutionary. And it's not something many people would consider buying. But I do think that if you have a spare 3 hours, it's a nice little read. I really promise that there isn't pedophilia. Some of these reviews critized it's lack of gameplay or how the story is pro pedophilia. They either didn't read the whole thing or they didn't understand the genre.
(Essential this is like a picture book except the pages are huge and have a lots of text.)
WARNING: Not for the weak of heart or the weak of mind/eyes/brainpower. If you can't read, just stay far far away from this book.

Bought this game on a sale, and it was well worth it. Took me about 12 hours to complete, so not the longest game. But those hours are quality.
It's a very story-driven experience with plenty of exploration and problem-solving in an imposing environment. The game also has horror and minor puzzle elements. The horror plays mostly on a sense of dread and perilous situations rather than cheap scares.
SOMA does a good job at breaking up the gameplay and atmosphere, so in some places you're creeping around, afraid of your own shadow, in other places exploring with a sense of wonder or you're giving the grey matter a little shake to solve a more technical task. In a few places the game breaks its own rules, which can feel a little unfair. But it's a minor thing. The story is thought-provoking and it's difficult to not wonder what you'd do if put in the same situations as the game's character. The voice-acting does a good job of delivering good chunks of the plot, and you'll probably find yourself thinking on its themes after reaching its conclusion.
The entire game is a very seamless experience. There is not a single loading screen, although in a few places the screen fades to black or you spend time traveling in a vehicle. Perhaps some loading is happening during those sequences, but either way it makes for a very immersive experience that you'll rarely see in a video game.
Graphically it's quite nice and the designers did a great job at delivering a near-perfect setting. What drives you forward is often a sense of wonder and desire to explore the visuals surrounding you.
Overall I highly recommend you try this game.  I'd love to see this as a movie.

Friday The 13th: The Game
Asymetrical multiplayer games have had a troubled past. Most notibly in recent history is Turtle Rock Studio's Evolve released a few years ago, a game that was fun at launch for a few games at a time, but never grew or "evolved" its gameplay as you would only play one mode, Hunt (yes I know there were other modes, but nobody voted for them), where you chased the monster forever and it just got old.
While some players may say this game is no different, I believe there is great potential here for a great game.

I believe this game will be more successful than Evolve.
Why? Well, first off, the game is great fun to play as either the counselors on a cooperative team, or as the Blood Thirsty Jason. The counselors need to work together if they want to survive, having one person find all of the parts for the car or the boat or to call the police is not only slow but not effective. Having people look together and communicate makes it really fun to look for parts (which you will be doing all the time when playing as the counselor). I've had a game where I had the keys to the car and someone else had the gas, we were all heading for the car when the guy with gas gets killed by Jason. I distracted Jason long enough for someone to grab the gas, and fill up the car. Then the dead player returned as Tommy Jarvis and shot Jason to stun him. We all then got in the car and I drove all of us to safety. Only one person died and we had a blast. Those moments really make this game great and better than Evolve, as anyone can be any role to the team. If you want to go look for car parts, go do that, if you want to be the anti-grabber, go find the flare gun, firecrackers, and pocketknife. Because there are no classes you are bound to, and anyone can pick any character they want to be, it is like life, you can be who you want to be. The character progression unlocks and perks can further specify how you want to play.
I will not say much for being Jason as it is obviously fun to be the killer who is pretty much unstoppable and can taunt the other players.
As a twitch streamer, this game is great. A lot of players I have come in contact with role-play and this adds a layer of hillarity to the game and it enhances the experience.
Not everything is perfect in this game, the biggest being the value this game brings. At 40$, this may not be full retale price, but this game is a tough sell none the less. There is only one map, one mode, and only so much randomness to the spawn of players and items. The same intro to start the game can get repetitive and shows this game should still be in Early-Access, but it's not. The developer has promised more free content to come in the future, but it is currently not here.
There are also a lot of bugs, not enough to ruin the game though, but they are prevelent. Server disconnects are there from time to time, but have improved since the game's launch.
There also some balance issues, manly with Jason's shift ability (move very fast while invisible) and grab kill combo. Good Jasons can abuse this combo and not give you a chance to escape or survive it unless you have the pocketknife and other stunning items. Maybe Jason's cooldown on the grab kill could also be increased a little bit, feels to short which makes killing people with your melee weapon too slow and pointless. Other than that, Jason should feel op because he is supposed to be, he's Jason. Those people who argue that he is too op should try and work together with other players on their team, as a team you can fight Jason, the game is 1 versus 7, not 1 v 1 v 1 v 1.
TL;DR
Pros:
- Atmosphere is fantastic! Music is spot on and wonderfully spooky

- Graphics for enviornment are great, models pretty good, faces look a little weird
- The kills are violent and gruesome just like the movies
- Role-Playing of players, great for Twitch and Youtubers
- Meaningful play as either Jason or the counselor
- Deep character progression system and unlocks
- Free content to come
Cons:
- Game is currently not worth 40$
- The game can vary from fun to not so much depending on the cooperation of team
- Buggy, though not a game killer
- Jason's grab kills and in combo with shift ability can be exploited a little bit

- One map and one mode currently
Overall, I am going to give this game a thumbs up and hope this review has been helpful!

Dragon Saga. Where do I begin? This game brings back so much nostalgia that it means more to me than my education. I played this game back when it was called "Dragonica" and the basic feel is still there. Same simple, yet difficult to master gameplay, Same classes, with even more to add to the mix, and same community. The players in this game are awesome.
Gameplay: 9.5/10
You'll encounter a few glitches here and there, but the gameplay throughout is fun, consistent, and active. Early in the game you get a feel for fighting in the arcade-style scenarios, and you'll be using that knowledge you gain to expand your skills as you level. There's a ton of variety in the classes and skills that allows seasoned players to seamlessly switch between punishing monsters with powerful ground combos, and tossing the mobs like ragdolls to deal even more damage in the air! While some of the bosses can get a bit repetitive, you'll love wailing on them and watching your reward explode out of them!
I've never been a fan of party play, personally, but you'll want to team up with other players to tackle the bigger dungeons. If you don't like the group aspect of gaming, never fear, as a skilled player can handle most of the content on their own, if they have the funds to build a perfect character.
Story: 7.5/10 - SPOILERS in this section!
There are TONS of quests in Dragon Saga. Tons of little storylines for many npcs, as well as the main story. You're a decendant of one of the five legendary hero on an adventure to join the Dragon Fellowship and seal away the Dark Dragon Elga, who was released by the Black Witch Paris, a legendary hero who has gone rogue. Your adventure brings you through Paris' path of destruction on her way to the Tower of Drakos, Elga's prison. You battle her, and defeat her (if her damage reflect skill doesn't one hit you first!) with her final breath (is she dead? hmmm.) she is able to release the Dark dragon, who roosts at the top of your final destination. The Black Claw Nest. Seal him away before he can lay waste to the entire world. Not to mention there's loot in it for you.
Besides the main story, there are a lot of little sidequests to do. I personally don't find them all that interesting, but there is tons of funny dialogue.
Graphics: 9/10
The colorful, rich graphics make wailing on foes and other players a ton of fun! Some of the skill animations are hilarious, and make me smile every time I see them. One class actually summons an early boss in his underwear to freeze your opponents, while another spawns a huge wrestler spinning towards your foes! My personal favorite character designs are those of the Shaman class. Their summons/familiars are very well designed, and look intimidating. That huge Dark Knight strikes fear into the hearts of pvp players!
The world is beautiful, which each area of the continent of winds, and the continent of chaos having their own unique look. You travel from a nice meadow, that slowly transitions to a volcanic area in the early-mid game, which gives you a feeling of "growing up" in your fist playthrough, as you watch as your charater makes their way from such a welcoming place, to a treacherous area. While there are a lot of reskinned enemies in later areas, it's forgivable, as many games do it. The visuals are great.
Support: 10/10
The Support team for Dragon Saga is wonderful. They're always willing to help in any way they can. Their polite, knowledgeable staff show that they care for the players. I've had issues taken care of  very quickly, and with the sheer number of tickets I've sent about different things ranging from bugs, to unruly players to suggestions are always handled with professionalism. Trust me, you may not see them, but the staff are lurking in-game, and they're watching out for rulebeakers.
Community: 7/10
This really can't be helped by the developers, but the community is a little small, and naturally, small interpersonal issues between players can escalate rather quickly. This  is apparent with the pvpers of the game, with players occasionally shaming each other in the trade chat channel, using foul language, and personal insults. On the other hand, a friend in Dragon Saga is a great friend. Begging  for items and gold is surprisingly uncommon, which is wonderful. I've met some awesome people here, and I've opened a facebook group for the community, where I've met some interesting people.
F2P vs P2W: 8.5/10
I've never been afraid to invest in a game that I enjoy. As an experienced gamer, I have to say that I'm impressed with Dragon Saga's cash shop. The items are reasonably priced, and dare I say, you can build a nice character without spending a cent. Be prepared to farm your butt off if you want to keep your wallet full, but the option is certainly there. The general agreement on the forum is that Dragon Saga is "pay to go faster" as opposed to "pay to win." Most of the premium items can be obtained without spending money. Insurance scrolls to prevent your items from breaking during the upgrade process can be bought for gold in the market, or exchanged for Silver coins which are an uncommon drop from monsters. There is no shortage of events in which you can earn premium items, as well!
Overall: 8.5/10, yes, I'm biased.
This game holds a very special place in my heart. It kept me sane throughout university, and continues to provide me with tons of entertainment and friends to hang out with. I highly recommend checking it out, despite it's many bugs and flaws. I have nearly 3000 hours of LOGGED IN time on my main character, and another 1000 or so spread throughout my alts, none of which I regret. except that one time where I overpayed for something in the market! :P
Dragon Saga is my favorite F2P MMO, and certainly worth checking out for it's unique gameplay and community.

WORLD END ECONOMiCA episode.01 is a kinetic novel, the first part of a 3 part series, that takes place in the distant future on the moon, where humans have been able to colonize it and make it another home. This story is told from a boy nicknamed Hal, who was one of the first born on the moon. It has been 3 months since Hal ran away from home, to pursue his dream of making as much money as possible. At first, this sounds like he wants to become a typical businessman on the moon version of Earth's Wall Street but as you delve more into the story, you discover that there is another reason he wants to accumulate a lot of money. (As this is a kinetic novel, though, I'll do my best to leave out spoilers.) So Hal is on the run since it's illegal for minors to be out on their own when they should be in school when he meets Lisa who wants to take him in and shelter him. Lisa lives with Hagana, a mysterious girl who seems cold to Hal at first but later, her true personality opens up the more that Hal spends time with her. As Lisa lives in a poor area of Newton City, one of the cities on the moon, and there are certain social, economic problems in regards to that (again, won't reveal spoilers), it turns out that Hal's main skill of making money will end up coming in handy. However, how will the story end? We find out and that leaves us with anticipation for episode.02.
Having finished playing this first episode, here are my thoughts. The story was well-written, albeit there were typos and such. An English proofreader would have come in very handy. I like that the story was engaging and had this serious, dramatic, exciting tone although I do have one criticism. There were clearly fan service moments catered towards the male audience. I think it would have been fine to leave them out but yeah. The art was beautiful and I liked that there was a CG gallery unlocked after you finished the story, along with a music gallery. It can get confusing at times to follow the business, economic lingo that Hal explains about how stocks work and such but you can pretty much gloss over that and follow the main story. Episode.01 can be played as a stand-alone kinetic novel although I'm happy that there are other episodes. I'm looking forward to playing episode.02 next and hopefully, we'll see episode.03 here on Steam. ^^
Overall, I'd give WORLD END ECONOMiCA episode.01 a very high recommendation. It's a great kinetic novel and if you want a game that's more relaxing and one just to follow the story, then this one is good. Also, it's already implied but it's on the sci-fi side so it's different from a lot of KNs and VNs that are fantasy-based or Japanese school-based. I'd totally give it a try and as I said, I can't wait to give episode.02 a go. ^^

Homeworld meets Battlefront Combat Mission - superb
This game is a real GEM. Singleplayer has 99% of what I have ever wanted in a tactical fleet combat game about BattleStar Galactica. I am a big fan of the new BSG and always wanted a game set in the first cylon war.
* I LOVE that it uses a WEGO system rather than straight turn based or real time system. This means the game pauses to let both sides give orders. Once both people are ready the action is played out in real time. During the action sequence orders and adjustments are not allowed. The action sequence lasts a short period.... I think it's 30 seconds or so and can be adjusted... then pauses for the next set of orders. This ensures that you can enjoy the action while still having the time to really drill down and get each ships orders right. It also means that sometimes you can be caught off guard as it should be, watching things like missiles come towards your ships, hoping the real time action reel stops so you can give new avoidance orders to your ship.
* I loved homeworld but homeworld does not offer anywhere near the tactical possibilities that this game does. By that I don't mean gamey mechanics but rather combat mechanics. In this game you have to consider things like the top and bottom armour of the ship and how to bring your best weapons to bear. Unlike homeworld you can move ships to avoid missiles and change subsystems and how they work. You will lose engines and things like that. Not sure if you can specifically target enemy sybsystems like in homeworld though buy the part of the ship you angle to fire at probably does this anyways.
* Vipers are a joy to watch during replays.
* Movement is up and down like in homeworld. But unlike homeworld, it's not confusing to orient yourself to where they are. Primarily because it's not real time and going up and down takes a while.
* Graphics are fairly spectacular imho and do the job well. Some though won't like them because they are not Battlefield cutting edge graphics.
* Sound effects are insanely good. As far as I can tell they are lifted straight from the TV series.
* You get to buy ships and customise munitions and what small ships are being carried by your fleet.

I would recommend this visual novel however; just like Spice and Wolf, this is definitely not everyones cup of tea. The story; ignoring the obvious and fairly minor romantic sub-plot, is highly focused on economics, stock trading and a small amount of personal story for each character. And while I would be lying if I said I didn't enjoy it, it was really oddly paced and nearly lost my attention at several points; there are a few minor problems in the first half of the story and after that, things remain calm until the latter part, where the story piles all of the major plot points and problems on and it felt odd.
The story, in a few lines, is about a boy who has lived his life on the moon after his parents migrated there. Not desiring to live in their supposedly-dull footsteps, he ran away from home to try and fulfill his dreams of becoming incredibly rich and helping to further humanity and he would build his riches by stock trading. In his misadventures he comes across several people whom either help him, or he wants to help. But things take a turn for the worse and episode one ends there. No joke, they decided to end the episode where things turned to crap after all the problems had piled on. But since I fairly enjoyed the story, I don't mind that. However, had I not enjoyed the story that would be the final nail in the coffin to convince me to not buy the next part and I reckon that will be true for a significant number of people.
The characters weren't bad but the main character does manage to conjure up some seriously irritating thoughts and questions that make him seem like a bit of a dunce. In the end a final questionable decision rounds off the story for the episode. The main supporting character named "Hagana" could probably be labelled as a tsundere but as it should be, she does have a decent amount of depth beyond that. The second supporting character is named Lisa and is the caring adult who has an almost dishearteningly-positive outlook on life because she has clearly had a fair amount of hardships herself. She was definitely my favourite character out of the lot. Besides these three characters you have Serrault, the pervy net cafe owner and Barton, the kind and hearty big-shot company owner. And there are developments involving each one, even some of the minor characters I haven't mentioned. This is one of the few times I would be willing to say that the characters are better written and developed than the rest of the story.
The music while relaxing and definitely suited to the subject matter, does not loop perfectly on some tracks. For the most part you can ignore it but it can be difficult to ignore and get damn irritating. The artwork is nothing to write home about. It looks decent but nothing stood out to me.
Final words: Nicely developed characters but the story is definitely not for everyone; especially those who tire of hearing about trading stocks or want a more in depth romantic sub-plot. The artwork is decent but the music tracks don't all loop perfectly.

Definitely a fun game. Maybe this was already apparent to some of you, but for those for whom it's not (like me), the concept is like Battlefleet Gothic: Armada, if that game is familiar to you. You have basic resource points such as Tylium which you can spend on ships, or other types of points, which you can use for hiring or promoting officers, or unlocking new blueprints.
Combat is turn based, where you make your orders, and the enemy makes theirs and then the orders play out in real time, regardless of new developments. I've had a couple times where an enemy moved in a completly different direction than i planned for, and thus he left my firing arc for my ships.
The campaign map is also turn based. You have story missions which advance the plot, side missions which offer resources if you win, and then the enemy can also just make random incursions. The replay feature is really cool, since it lets you watch what happened again in full 360 degree range.
The only bugs I see so far is that sometimes when you are doing say, a full frontal assault on a Cylon ship, it not only damages their frontal armor, but curiously also damages their rear a bit too. Nothing else, not the sides, or the top or bottom, just the front and rear. Weird.
I'd like to see more of a sandbox option in the future, but other than that, I really dont have any complaints about this game. Definately check it out, even if you arent specifically a fan of the series.

Even though alot of FPS games exist nowadays which have alot more technical complexity and graphical quality, my personal favourites in the first person shooter genre, are definatly Doom and Doom 2.
1. Graphics and Level Design:
Doom was always really limited when it comes to level design. The whole game was constructed as a top down shooter, but rendered in the first person perspective with the Doom engine, which caused some notable problems. The biggest problem though was that you couldn't build a room on top of another room. Even with this limit, the levels are really well made and have a really good flow, especially with the asymmetrical level design at hand.
The graphics are simply put timeless, yes the textures aren't HD and everything else consists of pixel sprites, but really, the game in itself is really appealing.
2. Sounddesign:
The sounddesign is spot on. The weapons feel powerful and satisfying, the enemies sound frightening and quite unique and the goddamn music is fantastic.
3. Gameplay:
Doom has a quite simple premise, shoot demons and collect keycards to proceed to unknown areas of the map, all the way to the end. Doom in itself is a really simple game, but the shooting and movement in itself is fantastic. Memorizing attack patterns, switching weapons mid- fight, watching Doom Guy gritting his teeth while shooting hordes of demonspawn, is extremely satisfying.
4. Mods:
Mods enshured the games longevity and the community is extremely creative when it comes to mods. Source ports, graphics enhancements, gameplay mods, violence mods, map packs and much more are available for free on the internet for other people to download and enjoy. Why buy an expensive AAA game, when you can get Doom 1 and 2 for a cheap price and mod support?
I think everyone should try out Doom. These games truely stood the test of time and shine even today. Everyone can get this game running by just downloading a source port and I would totally recommend it.

This game isn't worth $20 yet. Yet. It has the potential to be, but in its current state it's barely functional in terms of actual gameplay.
The progression system is drawn-out, burdensome, and unbalanced between herbivores and predators. For herbivores, many of the flora are still inedible, leading to frequent death by starvation, and the fresh water sources are so sparse you can and might literally die of thirst before you reach one if you spawn with a slow dino too far off - or if you're driven off of your current one by the surplus of predators. You also only gain progression from eating blue plants, but good luck finding them - the patches that aren't isolated will be a dangerous hotbed of other desperate herbivores and the predators hunting them.
And, naturally, you lose your progression points in death. There's also no carry-over when you progress to a new dino.
Unsurprisingly, many favor the carnivore side, leading to an overpopulation and struggle on that side as well. While they get a point for every minute of survival, they naturally have to kill to eat, which strikes a dangerous but favorable balance. Or it would be, if there weren't so many of them, leading to a cycle of carnivores eating carnivores, with usually only "murder packs" reaching apex.
Again, this game is early access, so hopefully this will be balanced out in time, and I'll be able to give a more positive review. There's been a lot of drama about the development and the direction it's going in, which I'm not going into, but needless to say there may be some reason for trepidation regarding the game's future. For now, though, it's not worth the pricetag - my advice is to wait and see.

First off, I'd like to say that I whole-heartedly support Dondi and his vision for this game. I am blown away by his dedication, even with all the people holding a gun to his head crying about sandbox - a mode never even intended to be in this game - being gone, and people with no idea about how game development works tearing apart his decisions. I have never seen a community of such self-absorbed morons backing a game.
That aside, well over half the community is great. They're supportive and understanding and fun to play with. They're just drowned out by the louder, negative portion of players. I myself head a discord primarily full of players I've met through The Isle and they're some of the best people I've ever met online. We all support and love this game and we've made a nice not-so-little-anymore family because of it.
I'd also like to note the sheer hours spent in-game of some of the people putting up negative reviews. How can you play a game for over 500, 700, 1000 hours and more and say "not reccommended"? How can you KEEP playing said game? Because it has nothing to do with the game. It has to do with the community retaliating for features that are incomplete in an EARLY ACCESS game and not having an easy mode bird-bath simulator (sandbox).
The game itself has a great vision and it looks great as it is now. The mechanics in progress are greatly enhancing gameplay and it'll only get better from here. When there's an issue, the devs fix it. It may not be fixed immediately, but they get to it ASAP. You just have to be patient and understand not all problems can be fixed overnight (even though oftentimes THEY ARE). As for the gameplay itself, you just have to learn a good playstyle. Be patient, use your brain, learn safe and unsafe areas. Smart "back roads" if you will. Especially as a carnivore, take advantage of any and all cover to both avoid the eyes of your prey and anything wanting to hunt you. Stalk things quietly from a distance, follow tracks, slink around populated areas looking for outliers. Learn each dinosaur's specific strengths and weaknesses and take advantage of them. It's not that hard, actually, if you're aware of your surroundings and tactical. It just takes practice and persistence. If what you're doing doesn't work, try something else. Don't blame the game. And don't be afraid to ask people for help or advice!
I understand that's not what everyone wants. They want to be the dino of their dreams and just keep it forever. Well guess what? Not the game for you.
This game is meant to be a challenging, survival experience and if you think hunting and defending yourself, memorizing water source locations and just not stomping around out in the open is hard then maybe, just maybe, you need to go play something else. It's going to get harder as time goes on. Because that's what it says in the description of the game.
HARDCORE SURVIVAL.
I don't know what's so hard to understand about that.
P.S. Dondi, you should update the trailer for the game once V4 is released. Much love from ayFAM (over 100 strong)! We support your vision!

Imagine you're walking along a busy convention hall and wander past the dedicated indie section of the game stands.
There's alot going on, but one stall catches your attention... a big screen and a few guys stood there. A charasmatic cheeky chappie on a PA system is explaining the controls to some players before looking around the room.
"We need one more player!" he says with passion equivalent to a herald of the gods on mount olympus declaring the next ascendant of a mortal.
You turn and raise your hand, can't be that difficult right?
The lads eyes flare into life, "Yes sir. Right this way!" he says, ushering you into the spotlight, the gathering growing crowd ushering you forwards with applause.
You take the controller, he rushes through the controls.
"Well i'm gonna mess this up" you think fumbling the controls.
The game begins, instantly you scramble to build a ship, "What am I dodging? What am I shooting? Who am I?" you think to yourself as you're eliminated by the man next to you.
You look to the screen, these guys have you by the tail and you know it. There's no hope for you now. They're weaving, holding corners, dogding and diving.... How can you beat that?
The round ends, you get back in the game.
Another round, another loss. But you learnt that the green blocks give you power. Should have spotted that earlier right?
You get into it, managing to take out two players, then that one guy gets you again. It's 2 rounds a piece, you're dead last but hey you're having fun right?
You're dam right, that adrenalines flowing and your palms are ready to give up on that controller but never fear, You're in for the long haul!
The round starts, if you're going out then you're gonna make sure they know you fought hard to get this far.
One ship down, you're wiedling a comparable star destroyer at this point against the tiny interceptors, you destroy one more of them as they fall into line. You detach a block as the last intercepter out manouveres you... it's so close, the block swings. Blocking their stray rocket. A new tactic... You detach two points of your ship as you drop down, the block hits his core and the ship blows.
The crowd go wild, your friend on the PA shouts in amazement as you take your first point. The crowd thought you were a gonner but not today zerg!
The second round begins, you've scared them straight now. they're gunning for you. You get that speed boost, dodging your buddies rocket. Too predictable.. you dive into the gun and let loose a fire storm, he's always gone for power over speed. it's finally let him down, he hasn't got the skill to dodge your rockets. He falls. The PA goes nuts, you pick up his cannon and begin covering fire. Red block and blue block ignored you, they know eachother already and have been having a mini fire fight. Blue moves in for the kill, as your rocket plows through his defences and destroys his core. Red panics, and flies into the crusher.
One more point. The PA is filled with the sound of amazement as the crowd are in disbelief, "YOU WERE A GONNER!" The PA rings out through the crowd. He asks you your name just before you start the round. Adding it to a board.
The round begins, Your buddy tries to be eratic and flies up for more upgardes. But you have him now, the patterns are memorised. You fly up and grab the gun, hammering the shoot button for all you're worth. He crashes and burns. You detach your cannon and fly to the battling friends. They've teamed up, but never fear. Your star destroyer has it in hand, you unleash a barrage of missiles, Blue explodes and red is dodging debris and missiles left right and centre. He gets a lucky few shots, it's ok. You love the faster ships anyways, and dive towards his core. He's done for.
You get the point, the crowd go insane and everyone shakes hands. You go to leave, the guy on the PA stops you and says "we'll be back soon folks!" as the crowd ramble.
"Well done mate! You're in the finals!" he says.
"What?" you ask, as he moves your name to the final leaderboards..... you walked into a tournament. But you were so caught up in the adrenaline of this finely master crafter 8 bit shooter that you didn't realise!
THAT IS WHAT THIS GAME DOES TO YOU.
You stand there shaking, it's surreal how much you've got into this game. You enter the tournament, and after everyone gets 2 points, you lose.... but you're still shaking.
The dev shakes your hand and you leave. Still high on adrenaline you walk off into the sunset, ranked 4 on blockships in London....
And you're dam right I returned the next day to shake that devs hand again for that opportunity.
This is what this game did to me.... and i'm still recovering.

Different light levels, full texture mapped environment, stairs and elevators, all in a 3D world (kind of).
What seems completely irrelevant for today standards, was absolutely mind blowing in 1993, and changed the FPS industry forever.
Now, let's look at the game from a 21st century perspective. Is it still a good game? Yes, it is.
It may not be the best game ever (some would say I'm wrong) but it's insane that, 23 years after it's release, DOOM is still a really fun game, with a fast paced action that is hard to find nowadays. Enemies are braindead (just like every other game from the 90's) and most of them aren't any threat individually, but when you have 30 of them in your face, things start to get really complicated very quickly, and if you don't have the necessary reaction speed, you're dead. As simple as that.
The story isn't anything great, but honestly I wasn't expecting that kind of ending (I won't spoil it ;)
Another thing is the community. This game probably has one of the biggest modding communities of all time, having thousands of maps, mods and TCs.
Play it. You probably will need a source port, since DOSBox doesn't work very well. There's a lot to choose from.
Those are just a few, but they're the best ones in my opinion.
PS: All of you people worried that new generations don't appreciate these gems, hope isn't lost! I'm 16!

My rate for this game is
, that means "
". At least that's the spirit how I played it.
So, I actually won't un-recommend it because it doesn't deserve it but surely it deserves critics.
Because this game is wrong from the basis: it is supposed to be a "stealth game" but it is clearly not; a "sniping game" but sniper rifle isn't the most useful weapon; a "realistic game" and it is definitely not!
Before explaining my critics let me tell in advice that i played at the highest difficulty. So, let's start with the stealth factor.
I won't definite this a stealth game because you can't complete any level stealthly. Well, actually you can't complete any ROOM stealthly: The only stealthy weapon you have is a silenced pistol that is way the most useful weapon of the game (But "Silenced-Pistoler elitè V2" didn't sound good enough); then you have an un-suppressed sniper rifle who aggros enemy just by pointing them (if you point them with the binoculars you will not be caught that easily); and a nice arsenal of explosives. It doesn't sound like a very quite equipment.
In game you fight against troopers, and snipers: the latter will shoot at you anyway (so there's no need for stealth) the firsts don't act at all like a real trained soldier: no one soldier will "pound the alarm", not even after an explosion (that's why to this game sound logical give landmines as a stealty weapon). Any un-quite action will only alarm the soldiers in nearby: it doesn't matter if you shoot away everything, blast them with grenades, or snipe efficently: you will never be in permanent trouble.
Also, if a soldier finds a dead body he doesn't pound the alarm of call for reinforcements (there's no such a thing in this game) he just stays close to the body, wondering what could this mean.
If you try instead to move the body you will alarm the enemy because you are being loud.
So: leaving a body is not a negative beavior because it doesn't get you in trouble, actually is a POSITIVE beavior because you can fill the body with mines. Stealth. Sniper.
Another example of the lack of logic is the tank AI. They act like dogs. Indeed, like dogs: If a tank see you it will shoot cannonballs as long as you are in his line of sight, than it just go away. Like a dog barking to defend its territory.
Oh, yes, and of course a tank shooting does not alarm nearby soldiers.
Another disturbing element is that the game gives you an arsenal for a preparatory game: you should know the territory, what will happen, then you plant mines and choose your position accordingly. But this never happens: you just follow the track, snipe the main target (or snipe some explosives, just to remain stealth) from a position unknown from the beginning, and at last you fight your way out without knowing in advice what way will be.
So: what's the point with mines?
I think the game is the result of a developing team that didn't follow the same line guide: some one wanted to make a stealth game, and some one other said that didn't sell enought.
Obsidian Conflict is a little better than this but that doesn't mean Synergy isn't awesome when playing with a few friends.

Soma, however, shines brilliant as a perfect example of just how artistic videogames can be: it arises questions all of us bury when we go to sleep. What does it truly mean to be human? What does it mean to live? What if we were to lose all we have and are? The characters exude and breath anguish, constantly trying to find something to truck on for. The ambience, story, sounds and characters make Soma a must have for anyone who enjoys putting oneself through extreme mental anguish. The choices I made weigh down upon me, the isolation and despair Simon felt felt like my own. I know that tomorrow, once the sun is out, i'll go outside and breathe in. Thanks for this amazing experience with gorgeous design, amazing sounds, complex storyline, hidden plots and poetic questions.

A smorgasbord of sex, violence, and swearing, trying to have an appearance of maturity...
Technically speaking, its got everything right to make a good game:
1. Good graphics.
2. Good physics.
3. Good voice and animated acting (the mental-patient who thinks he's adolf Hitler comes to mind.)
But seriously, games (and movies and TV shows) that takes the road of sex, violence, and swearing to appear mature are getting really really old.
Violence: you get to rip your enemies in so many ways - vertical, horizontal, pull their spines and skulls out through their♥♥♥♥♥ Geez. Tone it down several notches and instead give its atmosphere (and the music) a boost. Ever heard of Alan Wake? There's Darkness there too and man did I feel that one.
Sex: There are scenes of oral sex, sex from behind, moaning ala porn stars, and beating up women in the sexual context. References of snorting drugs from private parts of women I mean seriously.

Phenomenal story telling with excellent graphic and sound design blended to great impact. Praise should also be given for what they've been able to do with the engine here - the game feels great, and runs smoothly on a 2013 rMBP with Intel integrated graphics (although not with settings jacked to the max, obviously).
Like The Fall however (which if you haven't played already, is highly recommended), another moody sci-fi story-centric game with action segments awkwardly bolted on, Soma winds up a few pitches short of a perfect game.
This class of title walks a difficult edge: if it's developed with too heavy a focus on story it might end up a "walking simulator", which can play well but may also fail to provide players with the necessary impetus to progress through the carefully crafted world and story.
On the other hand, if too much "game" is crammed in and if that gameplay is not up to the level of quality of the narrative aspects of the title, the carefully built atmosphere and story can suffer from the inane mechanics.
I played through Submerged recently, and found that the pleasant if slight story and accompanying world-building were undermined by being padded out with the constant need to climb all over things. The platforming was never challenging and never very interesting - it was just in the way. Sure, there wouldn't have been much game left without those segments, but at the same time I can't honestly say that they added anything except playtime, which is not a virtue in and of itself.
This title falls likewise in that latter category. It really wants to tell you a story, and it has a good story to tell, but it's afraid that you won't stick around if it doesn't give you enough to do, so it makes you hide and sneak around a bunch.
It's telling that the most subscribed Workshop content for Soma is a mod that neuters the mortal threats of the game. Not having tried that mod, I can't say if the danger was necessary to ground the feeling of dread, but I can say that when encountered in regular gameplay, I found these passages to be cumbersome.
If anything, the threat of hollow failure detracted from immersion. These segments were agitating, not because they engaged me at the level of limbic fear, but because it was going to be annoying to have to do it again if I failed the first time.
The story actually has such grist for the mill built in that the player's resurrection could have been incorporated into the game in some interesting ways, thereby sapping failures of some of their immersion-busting impact. However, no such concession was made and after being presented with a screen notifying the player that "You Died", the player is right back at it from the most recent (mercifully liberal) checkpoint.
In all fairness, nothing in the game is too hard, although the lack of hand-holding may lead to some trial and error troubleshooting, which again, can get kind of annoying.
Finally, I'll mention again that the story has some well laid turns and should reward a playthrough with its great world-building throughout. That said, you'll never quite be able to shake the on-rails feeling that is often another side-effect of narrative propulsion. So let Soma tell you its story - chew the fat because the steak is pretty good.

The Darkness II is a FPS with a lot of unique mechanics that I've only experienced for the first time in playing a game  with this  genre (grabbing stuff with tentacles, using them to heal yourself, I can hear a bad hentai joke coming...)
You play the game as Jackie, a gruff, angry, imposing man whom has a dark power that he inherited from his father. Tormented by his memory of his girl friend Jenny he struggles to try to get revenge for an attempt on his life.
I found it amusing that the game basically makes Jackie a crime boss, it game the game and the story an interesting tone. And the game carried it very well. The story was extremely well executed down to the very end of the game. I don't want to give anymore away, I will say that the game lets you select an introduction that explains what happened in the first Darkness game, if you (like me) never played the first game.
while I was playing I was confused at the key mapping from the start of the game, but I picked up on the controls really quickly, like I've said I've only played the easiest difficulty so I just hack and slashed my way through the whole game and didn't die once.
There are a few main combat mechanics: 1) you use guns. Hence why I categorize it as a FPS 2) You have two shadow arms that wreak havoc with basic swing attacks 3) your shadow arms can grab and throw objects 4) your arms can grab other humans and mutilate them to gain ammo, health, amusement, etc.
By combining these various moves and abilities you can create some really awesome combination attacks. If you're aware of your surroundings and have good reflexes the game is really fun to play. I get tired of playing the same type of game over and over, but this game takes a great spin on traditional FPS's and gives it interesting mechanics to make the game just that much more interesting and engaging.
One more note on game play: Progression. I find that just killing hundreds of npc's for the sake of killing npc's isn't very interesting *cough cough* Brutal Legend *cough cough*. Anyway, the game has a level system that you can spent points to get new abilities, making that mass slaughter I had, actually have a purpose.

As usual this game has the standard "you beat the game" achievements. The "beat the game on this difficulty" achievements. there are also a few multiplayer achievements (which I haven't worked on yet), And then there are the "do this special thing in the game".
The achievements seem straightforward. But I haven't earned them all yet (08/09/14) so I don't know if there are any really note worthy achievements at this time. but so far the achievements look very straightforward.
The Darkness II is $29.99, at this time I've only put 5 hours into the game, but I can see myself  playing this game for about 10-20 hours. I really enjoyed the game, but I don't know how high the replay value is for someone whom isn't going for achievements.
I really enjoyed the story, and don't have anything really negative to say about the game (other than at time the gore was a bit much, but that won't bother most people), as I usually say at this point, is that I'd recommend getting this game in a Humble Bundle or waiting for it to go on sale. I personally purchased mine in a Humble Bundle.

to recap,  the story was excellent, the game play was engaging and interesting, the achievements were alright, the price was kind of high but the quality in the game was good.
I recommend this game to anyone who knows they know FPS's, don't mind gore, like a bit of a darker story (pun not intended), and likes a good story.
I have a few things to add about the game. I've all but earned all the achievements on this game. So in a way I've given a bit of a preview of how much work it takes to get the various achievements. The game has actually gotten better.
I played through the Vendetta's, which is a multi-player element to the game. But you also have the option of solo-playing through the whole thing. You have access two 4 new characters that run a "side quest line" parallel to what is happening to Jackie in the main story. This element gives the game more replay-quality, which for me is great! I love continuing to work through a game after I've beaten it, and have a different experience.
A quick updated note about the achievements: Most of the achievements aren't very difficult, but actually require you to try out different things in the game. I didn't find myself particularly frustrated with any of them. This game actually had an almost-perfect balance in their achievements for my tastes.

First of all, Comipo is a great software where you can develop your story-making skills with certain constrains. The User interface is very user-friendly and easy to use. If you're the type that can't come up with character ideas, this software is a big help to you.
Don't get confused by the sofware name, Comipo is more like a story maker with built-in characters rather than a manga maker. Most of the users say that it's not worth it because the biggest reason is that they were expecting more like the Manga Studio. Comipo is drag and drop story maker presented in manga/comics form.
For me, Comipo is worth the money and worth the time.
Pros:
1. It's the first software with this kind of story making system.
2. If you're bad with drawing, the built-in characters can cover that up.
3. The limitations can exercise your mind in coming up with story ideas.
4. A lot of character poses and facial expressions are available.
5. Tests your efficiency in using limited backgrounds and characters.
Cons:
1. Costly because of the DLC packs.
2. Limited character modifications.
Note:
If you plan to buy this, I reccomend that you buy at least 3 DLC packs depending on what story you want to make. I planned to make a shoujo school life manga series out of this so I bought Swimwear, Summer & Sports, and Casual wear.
If you plan to make a manga series, this software is very worth it. If not, then practice your drawing skills and try Manga Studio.
It cost me quite a lot but this is like my hobby now. I already made 15 chapters of my manga series using this sofware. If you keep on whining and ranting about this software then go on. In some way, you're just not just flexible enough in making stories.
And one more thing regarding DLC, buy only what you NEED and not what you want. I save up some money for DLC that can help my manga series become more and more interesting.
For good story writers out there who want a visualization of their ideas, this is the software for you. Be a good story writer, Be a Comipo user! :D

Supergiant have really suprised me with Pyre. Because Bastion and Transistor were so similar to one another I was expecting more of the same, but what they've done here is something else entirely.
Pyre is part visual novel and part sports game. While this may seem like a strange combination, the story facilitates the meshing of the two genres very well. When you aren't getting to know the world and its many characters during your travels, you're participating in the Rites - an intense game that pits you against a rival team for the chance at earning freedom from the Downside. Its not just your freedom on the line however; you're also fighting for the freedom of your friends.
Thats what I really love about this game. Unlike Bastion and Transistor, Pyre places a lot more emphasis on world building and character development. You'll get to know every character, learn their story and progress with them on your journey. You really start to connect with them - and if a game can effectively make you care about its world and the characters living in it, you know the writing is good.
And yeah, the soundtrack is amazing but I'm sure you would have guessed that already. Come on, its a Supergiant game. That being said, I sincerely hope Darren Korb never stops making music. And Supergiant keeps making fantastic games.

As someone who has played the whole trilogy, I would say this:
If good narrative is your thing, get this game.
If an interesting premise is your thing, get this game.
If characters being very and absolutely human in their actions is your thing, get this game.
Naturally if you have an understanding of the finance world, get this game.
If you are looking for a commercial visual novel, absolutely steer clear from this game.
It takes a very incomprehensible and unfriendly concept - the financial world - and shows how human it is, and all it's fragility. It's also easy to keep up with, even if you don't understand what the hell all these concepts are (that was me). It's extremely exciting and once you are sucked into it you really can't stop. Seriously. I played the first two parts in one night each just because it was that exciting. I had to be torn away (almost literally) from the computer for the third part, so I finished that in two days.
The premise sounds complicated, but true to it's theme, it is simple and universal at heart.
After playing episode 3, I started playing from episode 1 again just to experience it all over again - the excitement, the despair, everything.
It's a really good story. And for those who do have financial knowledge: this game has its bases pretty much covered. I don't think there will be any complaints about incorrect information. It is after all written by Isuna Hasekura.

I must admit that without the downloadable content for the Manga Maker it is a bit flat. Once you have the DLC all kinds of creative possibilities open up. In my opinion out of all the DLC available, I believe the two most important would be the Office Wear and Business Person collections. Also one of the most surprising and over looked features of Manga Maker are the built in filters that you can not only apply to the preloaded 3D models, but also to your own imported models, it is quite nice. After applying these filters the models begin to look really nice, and it truly does in some cases give the image a realistic hand drawn look. My personal view on where Manga Maker falls short is in its lack of diversity of skin tone. Yes even with the software coming from Japan I find this inexcusable, especially considering the wide range of popular Manga characters that are not single color pale-ish. Look carefully at popular manga such as One Piece for example, or even the Dragon Ball series. I mean some of the characters in the Dragon Ball series have blue skin for gosh sakes! The characters in One Piece all have different skin tones. Plus some of the more classic stuff like Nadia: The Secret of Blue Water, Mihoshi: Tenchi Muyo!, Kaolla Su: Love Hina and of course Momo Adachi: Peach Girl. I do hope that a selection of skin tone will be added in soon coming update.

Isuna Hasekura is currently the only Light Novel writer that is worth reading if your beard hasn't grown down to your neck. This Visual Novel has a touch of uniqueness to it just like his previous works. However, I wouldn't recommend it to anybody who doesn't know the first thing about ecomomics or perhaps wasn't a bright math student. This VN appears to be a promising read, but you're stuck trying to figure out what's going on as you're going to face tedious lines regarding the economics' subject. I gave up after several attempts that resulted in headaches, I wasn't bored either or disappointed with the cast, but grasping the economics in this novel is just beyond me. On the other hand, I gladly wished to support the author and developers, but after it dawned on me what their next product is I questioned myself whether I should have thought twice or not before spending my bucks on this.

Somehow Supergiant manages to make every game better than the last. Pyre outclasses both Bastion and Transistor in every way.
Do not be turned away by the appearance of a "weird sports game" or a "visual novel". The devs of Pyre know very well their game is an experiment and they put in all the effort to make it as accessible as possible. They also respect your patience, you will never have to read paragraphs of text appearing on the screen (unless you wish to do so, the game has a tone of backstory which you can obtain and read)
The world of Pyre is one of the most creative, most beautiful and most charming. Imagine if the artstyle of Transistor, the humanization of people in Undertale and weirdly enough the Nemesis system from Shadow of Mordor were mixed together into the most polished videogame in 2017.
Worth mentioning, that despite an importance of a fantastic story, the game's gameplay isn't just functional, it's really freaking fun and  full of depth
Please give Pyre a chance, because it's really, really worth it.

The first levels are really easy : you need to remove all hooks one by one by pressing the related button to clear the screen. There is only one rule : you can't remove a hook blocked by another. If you do so, you lost a life. In the earlier levels you have only one try but you'll get an extra life while you progress up to 3 lives.
After finishing several levels you'll unlock some new gameplay mechanics : several buttons, rotatings tracks and wireless remotes.
As said earlier, the difficulty is mostly casual as you can almost always make "short circuit" to make only one hook to be removed at a time : simplifying the thing and avoiding making a mistake with all of those hooks.
The latest levels contains many hooks and require more time and patience to solve them.
I would recommend this very good game even if the game is short.

How much I longed to play it again, but this time here, on Steam. The last time I replayed Doom was... wow, I don't even remember. I might have launched it few times in last 10 years but I know for sure that I didn't finished it from begin to end in all this time. So here I am, replaying another classic and legend of PC gaming.
Game from 1995 should feel really old, right? Outdated graphics, sounds, controls and more. It's not the case with Doom. Even low resolution (which can be somehow fixed/changed to higher anyway) is not a problem. Graphics still looks great, soundtrack is one of best made in gaming history and controls... playing a FPS game using only keyboard never felt more comfortable than in id Software games. After so many years it's still played by many players - be it original version or with single and multiplayer mods. It's so much fun, game where killing is fun, level designs makes you use your head and SECRETS, who doesn't love secrets? Fighting your way in 4 episodes, which are filled with many missions. Even if you are playing on "normal" difficult level, it's easy to nice that with every next level game is getting harder. And getting 100% on kills, items and secrets on every level is harder that it looks, that is if you are playing without any guides.
Some people will probably think that this price tag is kinda funny - paying this much for 21 years old game!? I bought my copy at sale but still, in my opinion, Ultimate DOOM is worth every price. It's legendary game, so if you never played it - do it right now or wait for sale, if you think they are asking too much for old game.

My first Steam review. This is my opinion but I'll be as fair as I can. Here goes...
(Today's edit has change my recommendation. I can't whole-heartedly recommend this game to future players anymore.)
In short...
PROS:
-Dinosaurs! Who doesn't like living out their childhood dreams. Seriously! It's why I joined, it's why I've stayed. The models are also (for the most part) really well done and smooth overall.
-Graphics! The aesthetics of this game have generally been rather pleasing. I've always been bummed that my computer couldn't handle epic settings, but I've seen enough screenshots to see what even I'm missing.
-Friends! 75% of my friends list is from The Isle. I have this game to thank for the many good friends I've made. Sometimes it's a bit difficult, but it's a rather social game where you can meet like-minded people to hang out with.
-Potential! This game is early access. It is important to remember that what you're seeing now is not the final product. In the past I have enjoyed the PvP aspect of The Isle and I have even come to enjoy the survival of progression.
-Patches! Frequency of patches, to be fair, has gone down in the past few months, but the players are typically in the know of what's going on most of the time. There was a time where we were getting one or two patches a week. I appreciate the hard work!
CONS:
-Community! I won't go too far into this. Ever heard of the League of Legends community? You can probably compare it to that. I feel bad for the devs on this one. I'm certain the general attitude of the masses can be extremely trying at times.
-Bugs! Yes, yes I know. Early access! I get it. I don't know what it's like to be a dev. I imagine it's hard work, and I won't question the workload. What I do question, though, is why constructive feedback about some bugs is met with such hostility, and I guess I don't understand the priority. Sometimes we're even punished in-game for asking things. Which leads me to...
-The Team! This is my biggest issue with this game. As mentioned above, I understand perfectly that the devs might feel overwhelmed by the mob mentality. This isn't a single issue, this is a problem in every game. You're going to have your whiners anywhere you go. What I don't like is the utter disrespect towards the players who /don't/ act like that. The players that care about this game and the direction it's going. Calling your playerbase derogatory names on a regular basis is extremely unprofessional, so is roasting individuals on your public stream and/or forums. I don't actually like calling this out in a Steam review but I'm not really sure how else to project how serious this is.
Some personal musings...
I used to love this game. You could definitely say I enjoyed sandbox over progression, though it's not fair to say that it's only because of sandbox. If sandbox made an appearance tomorrow, I'd probably play it for about 10 minutes, get bored and go back to progression. I miss the magic of the old maps and the fluidity of the old combat system. Call me a sentimental fool, I'll not deny that. I'm personally not that into the new map and do not have high hopes for the next. In my opinion, they are too large for the capacity of the servers. Even with a high cap, the servers cannot handle the workload which causes heavy amounts of lag. To be fair, there are aspects of the new map that I enjoy, but just not enough to hold my interest. Size aside, there wasn't much interesting about it. The previous maps had personality and charm. Beautiful scenery coupled with memorable landmarks made for an enjoyable experience. Those days are gone, however.
I'd like to say this game can be saved, but in good conscience I really can't. You absolutely cannot cure the poor attitude of the people in power, therefor this game will suffer for it.
PS. The game in the video you see on the store page? It's nothing like that anymore.

This game is not fully released yet so I can't make a full review but I have confidence in the developers for getting this game out of development hell when early access games failing was the norm. They're continuously adding new features and fleshing out the game while doing their best to cultivate as much hype in the community as they feel for the game. The devs are passionate about this game, and this shows in its carefully cultivated atmosphere and gameplay. I can't wait to see what they have in store for us. Now that I've done my spiel...
In the current state of the game you can play as an extensive cast of carnivorous and herbivorous dinosaurs, with coming updates adding human mercenary and tribal/mutant cannibal factions. Survival as a dinosaur is pretty much what you would expect it to be, with food and water being the main concerns. You can also breed and raise other players as your dinosaur children, which takes a lot of time but is great for starting packs and herds. Combat and hunting are carefully balanced with the goal of creating a realistic food chain among players so that while larger dinosaurs will usually win a stand-up fight, smaller ones usually have a better chance to escape from danger; those rules aren't absolute though, as smaller dinos can frequently pick off larger ones, either by attacking wounded ones or by hunting in packs, though even then it isn't necessarily an easy fight. The graphics are absolutely gorgeous and most of the bugs and glitches are ironed out, and none of the remaining ones are game-breakingly bad. Overall I have really enjoyed watching this game progress and I hope it gets a larger playerbase when it releases fully, as it's a good game with a lot of work put into it.

Well........
I just finished the game and my first thought was that this was a unique kinetic novel? Unique in the bad way and not the good way. Unlike most visual novels, kinetic novels don't give the player a choice so it's more like a short story in a game format. So no matter how weirded out you feel reading through the scenario, there is only one ending and nothing you can do to avoid it.
Well this is a free kinetic novel so I didn't expect too much of the art, music, and story. But even when I knew the premise of the story, the insinuations and pedophilic undertones sort of disturbed me.
The art isn't bad, it's simple and neat. I also like the light colors of the characters. Though at times I thought it was weird how the characters eyes become blocks when they weren't speaking.
Simple music. Nothing too memorable.
Some grammar issues. The story is also sort of predictable (at least in my opinion). I also didn't like how the second half was repetitive even though it showed new things. I can see how the creator wanted the story to be sad and heartbreaking but the final execution really wasn't all that heartbreaking and sad. This game is free after all so I didn't expect an amazing mind blowing story but I felt the writing could be improved and polished upon.
Well, this was a short kinetic novel, which took me less than an hour to complete. I started it because of the title "heartbreaking kinetic novel" but I didn't experience any heartbreak or anything of the sort throughout the novel. After about 20 minutes in it sort of felt like a tedious task to finish and get to the end because around then everything I thought would happen happened and there was no longer any suspense. Also... this novel disturbed me because the dude felt like a pedophile. Well people who don't finish the game won't know the real story so the dude will really be a pedophile in their mind but even then.... wow I still felt like I witnessed a pedophile assaulting a little girl even though I know the premise of the game.
Would I recommend this? Not really, even though it was a quick game and free, I wouldn't recommend it because of the initial feelings of disgust I had when I first started and even when I confirmed the premise of the game, the feelings didn't really dissipate. Seeing the other reviews, I don't think I'm the only one who felt this way :P (if you want to see what I mean then feel free to go ahead and play this game)

One of the big deals with this game is that people think it's Pay to Win, I have to dissagree. There are premium weapons and they can give a slight advantage (maybe 10%) the majority of stuff that you can buy with real money is aesphetics such as a flag to put on you're top or bottoms.
With reguards to a premium weapon, yes it is fully upgraded with 3 modifications, however you cannot change these mods, so generally they only have 2 that improve the weapon and the 3rd that allows more income. When you upgrade weapons from scratch it's possible to have 3 upgrades that benifit the weapon.
I should explain that mods are random you use one weapon to upgrade another of the same type (e.g. you upgrade a Mosin with a Mosin). There is a risk when upgrading, if you use in game currency, there is a chance of failing and if you're upgrading a weapon that's aready upgraded there is a chance of losing a modification.
Hopefully this review has sparked some interest and I'll see you on the battlefield.

Somehow Supergiant manages to make every game better than the last. Pyre outclasses both Bastion and Transistor in every way.
Do not be turned away by the appearance of a "weird sports game" or a "visual novel". The devs of Pyre know very well their game is an experiment and they put in all the effort to make it as accessible as possible. They also respect your patience, you will never have to read paragraphs of text appearing on the screen (unless you wish to do so, the game has a tone of backstory which you can obtain and read)
The world of Pyre is one of the most creative, most beautiful and most charming. Imagine if the artstyle of Transistor, the humanization of people in Undertale and weirdly enough the Nemesis system from Shadow of Mordor were mixed together into the most polished videogame in 2017.
Worth mentioning, that despite an importance of a fantastic story, the game's gameplay isn't just functional, it's really freaking fun and  full of depth
Please give Pyre a chance, because it's really, really worth it.

All the negative reviews on Steam state the truth: this software is extremely limited, expensive, the DLC is absurdly overpriced and doesn't grant enough variety... but. I got it discounted for about 10 €uros and the fun I'm getting from it is more than enough. It's great to make silly little comics to share with friends or reference material.
As a standalone product it's extremely lacking, but the community is pretty great with providing additional customization in hairstyles and objects.
The poses are nice (although SO Japanese), the camera angles are easy to adjust and the layer system is great to do some last-minute corrections. They added the ability to customize skin colors within the program and there have been several neat updates overall.
So if you intend to just have fun and maybe gain some experience in designing a comic page, get it (discounted). If you want to use the model as reference, get it as well (discounted). But at the normal price, I wouldn't ever suggest you to buy it.

TLDR: It's a Battlestar game for Battlestar fans
Okay, so, after playing the first few story missions, I think I can offer a decent first impression.
If you're a Battlestar fan, you're going to get that huge rush of nostalgia from seeing Battlestars slug it out with Cylon ships, just like in the Re-Imagined series during the battle of the ressurrection ship for example. There are also cool little tie ins with the show itself, a rather nifty one involving your main command ship/space shipyard.
Visually, it's nothing special, it gets the job done, but that's pretty much all there is to say about it.
The gameplay is pretty solid. If you're hesitant about this because it's a turn based RTS, then trust me when I say this; this game would not be as fun as an RTS. The level of control you get with your ships, from selecting which targets to focus on, what direction, speed and altitude to deciding where to best deploy flak walls and where to send your fighters, there is just too many things there for it to be a solid RTS only game, which is fine. A really cool feature is the replay system which allows you to watch back the large battle you just had, and the shaky camera we all know and love from the Re-imagened series returns with it.
