The TL;DR Version:
The game is mediocre at best with several good moments. However much of this is smashed by glaring grammatical, editing, and technical flaws. I am also disappointed in the fact that this visual novel has no choices or decisions to be made. 3/10.
A little bit more:
Okay, so you see that playtime above my review. It's fair to say I've given the game quite a fair shake. I will not spoil anything, but I will tell you the absolute truth as I see it.
This game suffers from a number of technical glitches. Background transitions are often mistimed and I ran into several intances where the background flashed between two entirely unrelated scenes before settling on the right one. The music, while not bad in and of itself (for the genre of visual novel), is so littered with random, jarring restarts and sudden halts that it really interrupts any chance of getting engaged into the story. Transitions between the various character's expressions sometimes results in the entire text box flickering wildly for a moment. These are all things that could have been solved with a little extra time spent proofing the scenes and should have been before a $13 price tag was attached.
Additionally, the writing itself had moments that made my brain hurt. Sentences repeat themselves in places (twice with what is clearly a poorly translated first draft of the actual text) and many places had the text unnaturally split between several windows. I got the sense as I read through the novel that whoever translated and/or wrote it was working without a full understanding of the english language. Many passages feel bland or artifically lengthened.
The story itself I shall resist on critiquing. Every artists has a vision and while one might like or dislike their work, that does not make it bad or good. I rather enjoyed a majority of it, but there were portions that could have been vastly shortened and retained their same impact.
As a parting note I wish to reiterate to any potential purchasers that this "visual novel" contains no actual choices in it. You do nothing but click through the screens and watch what comes up. This is not stated in the game's description but really should be.

Since the recommendation compares Ethan: Meteor Hunter to Braid, I bought it hoping for challenging and well-designed puzzles, but the challange and the difficulty of this game comes solely from jumping on and over things at the right time. As far as puzzles go, you can freeze time and rearrange some parts of the area you are in, but it is not too hard to figure out what you need to do and when you need to do it. The platformer part, on the other hand, is frustratingly hard, and you can't make it easier by being smart with the puzzles. After the first couple of levels, I can't even get from checkpoint to checkpoint without dying a million times, which simply prevents me from enjoying this game at all.
On the whole, I don't recommend the game for it's original price, especially if you'd buy it for the puzzles. If you like difficult platformers, you might like it though.

Every writer has their pet theme. Asimov had his robots and their glitchy laws. Tolkein had his languages and hyper-complex backstories. Clancy had his military tech. They say to "write what you know," since you write better from experience than from academic study; Isuna Hasekura, while no Warren Buffett, is most definitely an economics man. The charm for story conflict grounded in nothing more than fluctuating prices and market intrigue that he snagged readers with in
very much carries over to World End Economica, giving us yet
series for which fans must exapseratingly explain "I watch it for the economics!"
An important thing to note about WEE is that, strictly speaking,
It is a Kinetic Novel, specifically - a visual novel with no choices whatsoever. While this is a perfectly valid medium and one that offers great opportunity for storytelling (ref Planetarian: The Reverie of a Little Planet [10/10 go read it NOW]), this fact isn't well communicated in the "game's" description and might catch you off guard if you wonder when the hell the choices intrinsic to VNs will show up. Just enjoy the story!
While the story is good, the characters fairly well established, and the world itself an interesting one I look forward to reading more about in Episode 2, that's not to say this port is without fault. Namely, WEE suffers from
bad technical polish. Scroll up to the demo pictures, one where the text box is up, and look in the bottom right. "Title." A friggin'
There's no excuse for that save sloppiness. Bugginess also extends to other aspects of the novel, in rather annoying ways - at times, the text box bugs out, flickering like a damaged VHS on fast forward.
The music suffers the most, as the tracks aren't properly looped, resulting in rather jarring transitions that you'll hear
for the entire read. This wouldn't be so bad if it wasn't for the fact that there are maybe six song tracks total... and the worst loop cuts are in the tracks that play during "calm" parts of the story. Again, sheer sloppiness - this is an issue that should've been caught literally ten minutes into the first playtest. It is
to avoid, given some sections of the story literally won't autoscroll through fast enough to avoid looping the song!
Thankfully, gien that this is essentially a novel, the technical crumminess isn't a game-changer (oh, damnit, puns). The story stands on its own merit, and is well worth the read - $12 for a 20-30 hour read isn't that bad (as for my 112 hours, I kinda left the game on. A lot).

Visual novels are mostly amateur affairs. WEE may be better than some or most of its peers, but it still fails to be good by a reasonable standard.
The premise is original and the plot mostly hangs together - but with a few pretty big holes. There are only three 'real' characters, and their development arc is not satisfying. I'm sure somebody will say that it is necessary to finish all episodes of WEE, but there is simply no good reason to continue if this is the level of quality.
Art, music, and presentation are all amateurish. There are few drawings available for the few characters, and even then it's relatively flat and simple illustrations. There are only a handful of music tracks, and they loop awkwardly. The generic presentation UI is bland at best. The translation is workaday, with a number of questionable choices.
WEE is passable at its best points and is lousy during the in-between moments. Additional care in the presentation and a willingness to avoid tropes and crutches in favor of authentic character development could help elevate future works.

-Peer to Peer connection in a fighting game which means that hosting = a far better match performance, and that connection drops frequently.

Lets get one thing straight above all else:
This community is mostly very ignorant and because of that very toxic. Most of the bad reviews come from those people who failed to read the store page and what The Isle is intended to be.
Some say the Devs are d*cks. Well I'd say they're partially right but that's because their hand was forced due to the shear inconceivable incompetence of the community. Many times the main Dev tried to give some sense to the bad side of the community but everytime it's like talking to a brick wall.
Despite all this the Devs are extremely confident and determined to see this game meet its promise. Then it will become the best Survival game ever made by a long shot, in my personal opinion of course.
Well it's obviously Early Access (not obvious to 40% of the community, though) so bugs are a common occurrence.
Right now you can only play dinosaurs and you're offered two progression trees: Carnivore and Herbivore.
You choose your tree and you're dropped into The Isle as the lowest tier dino. Your objective is to eat drink and survive. Live long enough and you'll gain enough progression points for the next tier and become a stronger dinosaur. In general you'll take exponentially longer time to reach higher tiers.
As a carnivore you gain 1 point per minute by stayling alive and not dehydrating or starving. You could either hunt alone or be in packs, just watch your back.
As a herbivore you gain points for eating a specific type of plant that appears blue to you. This forces you to travel rather than staying in one place. It's always best to stay in a herd for increased survival.
It's always best to play with friends as any multiplayer game but whatever virtual friends you make just be careful. No matter how friendly someone is to you, DON'T trust anybody fully. It's a survival game after all. Expect to get frustrated quite a lot.
That's basically what you can expect from The Isle right now
> Introduction of Humans. You'll be able to choose 3 factions: Dinosaurs, Human Mercenaries (technology stuff) and Human Tribals (in sync with nature in a way)
> Combat improvements. Right now combat is rather lame but in the future an Armor system and Locational Damage System will drastically improve the combat among other stuff
> AI dinosaurs
> Tameable Dinosaurs. Tribal Humans will be able to tame, ride and garnish their dinosaurs (yes you can tame player controlled dinosaurs).
> Weather and climatic hazards (volcanos and stuff)
> Playable Pterosaurs, crocodiles, sharks and others.
This just a few stuff that will happen one way or another apart from other undisclosed features.
Would I recommend you to buy the game right now? If you want to experience a handful of bugs and frustrations in order to help development, by all means join in. Otherwise, maybe give it a pass for now. I highly recommend you to keep a close eye to this game however.

First and foremost, you have to remember this is a survival game - you play, you die, you start over. Secondly, you have to remember this is early access, and yes there are going to be the occasional bug (however rare - a la Shant vortex rn as of the 30th of November 2016) and yes things might seem a bit skewed in terms of balance.
But just because it may SEEM like the devs aren't working on it/replying to whining thread, doesn't mean they aren't pushing to sort mechanics that would make the game have a lot more depth. They're not gonna reply to a steam thread screaming about YOU TOOK THIS AWAY SCREW YOU M8.
I just want whoever is reading this to know, you will see people putting negative reviews about the game complaining about "SANDBOX IS GONE". Yes, it is. But this is a survival game, not a sandbox game - in terms of game development it was good to use to test dinosaurs and whatnot with little to no negatives, but ultimately was NEVER going to be a major part of a SURVIVAL game.
You will see people saying that the progression system is too punishing; that's likely because they either A) died to stupid like a bug or going base jumping, B) got steamrolled by the currently (and I say currently because it is due to change) easy to obtain Shantu C) engaged a large pack of carnivores/herbivores and expected it to end well, as opposed to doing their best to avoid them BEFORE they became an issue.
The only way you're going to pause before engaging someone - be it carnivore or herbivore - is if the looming threat of death and starting hours of progression all over again is there. It makes you weigh the pros and cons and I understand that from a development view.
You see, you can't make people act like dinosaurs - but those that play Carnivores are always going to have the upper hand in an ambush situation if they know what they're doing - it's just a matter of picking your fights.
For example... If I'm a Carnotaurus, perfectly camoflaged in the bushes and a Utahraptor or Gallimimus (same sprint speed) trots past me while I'm hungry and doesn't even see me (cuz eyy I know render distances~)... I'm not going to lunge out in front of them. I'm going to wait for him to get almost parallel to me knowing I'd be in their blindspot, charge out and take advantage of that 2-3s (current) grace period of silent sprinting from a crouch and bite the snot out of him - He can run, but the first couple impact bites + bleed is going to ruin a solid 3-4 hours of progression for that person, and they're going to come here and write a negative review because I took advantage of the situation and caught them off guard.
People will complain for the sake of complaining.
Pick your fights wisely, listen to the calls of dinosaurs, take advantage of cover if you're small, LISTEN.
And if you think it's clear, it's not. Always be on guard.
Seriously, the sound in this game is phenomenal and more than enough warning if you know what sounds like what... well, in that weight class - if it sounds bigger, it probably is and you should run or hide unless they give you reason to suspect they'll take you in. Even then, be wary of betrayals. Carnivores gotta eat sometime yo.
This is a great game, with an incredibly devoted developer team that isn't going to roll over and give into peoples whims; they have plans for the game, they're working on it, and calling them unprofessional when people - who haven't made a game in their life - try to tell them what to do, is just asking for snark. Patience is a virtue.
Just remember, that early acess tag is there for a reason - if you enjoy dinosaurs and if you enjoy an enormous world where you WILL struggle to survive... this is pretty damn good for such an early incarnation.

This is an Early Access Review so what i say now may change.
What I liked:
Progression system: The progression system is the main draw of this game. It is not recommended for people who do not have time to play, but the longer you survive the higher you can be on the foodchain. You have one life to live and when you die you start over from the very beginning. It is great fun if everyone is participating in the spirit of the game.
The Food/Water system: You need food and water that is a given. People say it is unfair and imbalanced because they have to actually go looking for their food and water. However, it is a needed process as it keeps everyone moving and wary. There could be an ambush laying in wait in the next food/water location. Many people do not see that this method of gameplay creates an ecosystem where the herbivores will have to move instead of hiding. This allows carnivores to hunt and keeps the herbivores involved in the game to survive.
The game delivers on the survival pvp: There are loads of possible scenarios where players can be forced to fight for their lifes or run away. From herbivores driving away competition to fighting off carnivores, to carnivores pushing and bullying eachother off a kill in order to survive. The way the progression system is set up makes survival pvp more tense and realistic where players are forced to pick their battles instead of mindlessly slaughtering everything.
Realistic Attributes and Niche's for certain dinosaurs: To my knowledge the dinosaurs are pretty accurate in size/strength and their projected speeds/ strength.
The developers stance on dealing with problems: So far the developers have been very transparent for an early access game. With how much flack they get from disgruntled players, for the devs doing their actual jobs. One would assume they would become less transparent. But no they are remaining transparent allowing people a glimps at what is going on "behind the screens" allowing people to know what may be coming in future updates. If anything they have been extreamly good developers who have been honest about what they are trying to make.
What I disliked:
Sandbox: Sandbox is the opposite of good gameplay. It turns the game into a deathmatch/rp/chatroom where death no longer matters where hordes of players fight and die mindlessly and ceaslessly. Increasing the stress on the servers due to the amount of corpses left behind. There is no effort to stay involved, No thought. No survival, just pure chaos.
The Community: The vocal steam community simply doesnt understand things that should be common sense. They dont undestand what goes into making a game and feel entitled to trying to push their opinions as facts. Hell they even fell for Plecebo effects and became quiet after their supposed "problem" got fixed. This just tells me that the more vocal parts of the community were simply complaining for the sake of complaining. And did not really care enough to pay attention to the actual game to notice.

This is a great horror game that holds a intersting plot and horrorfying moments. In Soma you play as a character that has seemingly ended up in the deep depths of the ocean where all sorts of terrible creatures lurk in the shadows. You will find yourself travelling the ruins of underwaters sea bases while also travelling on foot at the bottom of the ocean, and while you explore there will be monsters ready to kill. Soma has some serious moments that end up making the player feel guilty and leave the given player with the painful memory of that same dreadful moment that just had to be done. These moments are then tied with some creepy monsters that will of course try to kill you and a bit of lore to discover what happened. As you progress, you will figure out more about yourself and how you ended up at the bottom of the ocean, yet as the game goes on the creepier it gets. The game is made by the creators of the Amnesia series so be warned that if you did not enjoy the Amnesia series than you may not enjoy this game for dealing with monsters are closely tied together, yet if you enjoyed the series and want more of the Amnesia scares than get this game. I reccomend the game to anyone who is okay with exploration while being hunted by monsters and to those that enjoyed the Amnesia series. I give Soma 9/10 Multitools

I got this for sale for $3 and have had free iPhone games more fulfilling than this at the moment.
It's a classic case of "YOU SHOULD NOT HAVE RELEASED YOUR GAME YET"
To give this game a score of anything above 50 (looking at you, MetaCritic) is a joke.
It has a TON of potential, however, and I'm keeping it installed just to watch patch notes.
Right now the bad makes the good not even worth holding looking for in game. Keep your eye on the reviews and patch notes as the game keeps updating and see if it ever picks up before considering the purchase.
Now for the details behind that:
Massive issue number 1: You have to pay real money to buy certain items (think F2P MMO's where the devs stay afloat by people buying cute extras. These extras also give you a leg-up in the game by quite a bit).
Massive issue number 2: Communication is next to non-existent. You WILL NOT have any semblence of co-operation unless you have a buddy you're playing with over voice chat. When you start the game your only way of communicating is a "taunt" style emote which is either "Cower" and "Wave" (both lock up your character for the duration of the animation). There is no text chat yet. From a social perspective, this means there's really no way to meaningfully connect with a player, and it shows. Going up to a stranger in the world and waving, after, say, you just saved their life from a monster, will result in that player killing you because you had the audicity to lock up your character with a wave animation in the presence of a potential rival.
Massive issue number 3: Death penalty is enormous. Don't get me wrong, I've played many survival horror hardcore whatevers, and I understand that most of the game is about survival and if you die well then you dun goofed. The problem is, the game runs on an RPG-style stat system that is also reset every time you die. This makes player versus player balancing a nightmare for new players, or even players who just died after a survival streak of X ridiculous hours. One more note on that, in case you think I'm still being a wuss about it: The engine is buggy enough, and the servers are unstable enough, that you WILL die randomly by some glitch in the terrain, or whatever. Incidentally, I quit the game after gaining TONS of levels, getting a nice gun, feeling real great about surviving in spite of all the nonsense in the game, and then died because my character glitched and got stuck in a lake because he couldn't handle a gentle slope to get up and instead glitched partly into the floor, drowning slowly with no control interface for movement working.
Massive issue number 4: Random deaths because the engine is buggy/unstable. See previous for more details.
Minor issue number 1: Net code needs a lot of work. When you're fighting monsters and, even worse, players, you will have stupid deaths that amount to "on my end I killed that sucker, but on the server end they ate me slowly with a spork and I didn't put up a fight." This kind of thing is rare, I admit, but paired with the death penalties...
Minor issue number 2: The server browser is terrible. Simply, truly, uninspired, clunky, badly managed.
Minor issue number 3: A lot of the game world is, to be blunt, boring. Where in DayZ you have cities that look like actual cities and gorgeous country side and rhyme/reason to the layouts of things, the Nether LOOKS like something someone threw crap all over and said "There. That's our new game map." At no point in the game did I feel like I actually was walking around an old ruined city. I've had more immersive city-scapes in Unreal Tournament 99.
And, to be fair, the good:
Positive Points 1: The concept of the monsters is really neat. To make the applicable comparison to survival games trying to be "different" (looking at you, 7 Days to Die) you're not running from the same mindless horde of dumb but persistent once-humanoids (with perhaps some variations Left 4 Dead style at best. Again looking at you, 7 Days.) The Nether monsters look cool, have some neat behavioral patterns, and the teleportation, while maddening, really does add to the frantic and terrifying nature of urban exploration with one or more of those hunting you down. That said, I once heard a criticism that once a Nether monster has engaged you it will not back down until you are either in a safe zone, dear, or its own killer. How's that for survival horror?
Positive Points 2: Graphically there are lot of beautiful moments in this game. While I maintain that the cityscapes look dull and uninspired for layout, the graphical team did put a few little gems that you feel the need to screenshot as the sun comes through the debris the right way, etc. You can watch the video on the store page to see what I mean, they really threw some of their best feet forward, graphically, to show off the game there.
Positive Points 3: It went on sale for $3. I'm glad I never paid more for it than that, esp. when they're asking for in game purchases. Maybe they'll do that again.
TL;DR Give it a couple years maybe and it'll be worth playing. The bad far outweighs the good and unfortunately it's not in any kind of "fun playable" kind of bad right now. Unless you're a masochist and hate your life, then go right ahead.

This game is incredible. It is one of my personal favourite games of all time. If I don't have anything else to play, I hop on to Rainbow. Usually, I like to play with friends in other games but this one I'll make an exception. In my opinion, I have the same amount of fun while solo queueing and playing with friends. Here are my personal opinions about this game.
Pros:
Realism -
In my opinion, this is one of the most realistic games of all time (despite the bugs, glitches and hackers). The shooting mechanics feel great, the recoil is pretty easy to control (except buck's C8-SFW and other nameable weapons), and the innovation makes the player feel like they're in the game. Which leads me to my next point.
Tactics -
A lot of players in this game are competitive (Me being one). Most of the time in competitive, everyone will have a mic to communicate with their team. They will use the communication to give themselves an advantage while attacking and or defending. They will talk to their team about their location, cameras, where the objective is, and they will warn their team of an opposing attacker.
Operators -
Most of the characters in Rainbow are balanced. I'm not looking at Ash's f*cking head hitbox.There are currently 36 operators in the game. Each operator has there own backstory and everything you would find in a biography (Name, DOB, etc.) so you can learn something or two about an operator by looking at their bio.
(There are a lot more pro's but I would rather go into the cons now.)
Con's:
Servers -
I really don't need to explain this one.
Bugs -
Oh god, there are a lot of bugs. There have been many patches to fix these bugs but more appear every day. Operation Health tried to fix it, I'll let you finished the rest (It did f*ck all). I can't list all the bugs in this single review, but I will list a few. You can glitch through objects, hit registrations, hitboxes and last of all, Blitz.
Hackers -
Ubisoft has done very little to get rid of hackers. There are a lot of ways to hack in this game. Wall hacking, aimbot, you name it, they have it all. They are trying to get rid of them... but at a very, VERY, slow pace. Just like the bloody Ubisoft support tickets. (get incredibly insulted.)
The Community -
I think it's pretty toxic. I am not saying everyone is toxic, most people are very friendly but also very competitive. Most games I have played in has at least one salty guy on our team and their team.
That is my Rainbow review and the experiences that I have had in it. The game has been an incredible experience for me so far. I hope it's good for you too!

I got this on a first day release Steam discount of -25%. In less than 1.5 hours of cold start with the program I had two pages of panels, backgrounds, character, balloons and text put together. It is fairly impressive in its hit the ground running with ease of use.
Now on the negative side this is a very basic tool without a lot of built in flexible options. You basically get one male and one female model, some coloring and hairstyle options, and a few dozen basic "school life" style backgrounds.
So if you want to do fairly simple panel comics with basic character models without needing any drawing skills, this program can get the job done pretty easily with a very minimal learning curve. If you want a lot of flexibility and complexity in your options, then their is no actual substitute for learning to draw it yourself here. In terms of making something interesting, you'll still need some creativity, but most of it will be in the form of selecting and using the poses available creatively with shifting camera angles and trying out expressions for the right look.
If you want a complex manga drawing tool, then an illustration program is probably more appropriate, with the attendant ramp up in learning difficulty and drawing skill required.

I'm a fan of the original two flash strategy games con artist has put out : warfare 1917 and warfare 1944. When I saw this game I was instantly excited because I remembered those fun classics that entertained me when I was younger.
It feels like a sequel to those warfare games; but more like a card game than the originals. The overall battle scheme still feels similar in how it plays out.
Things to keep in mind:
Pros:
*Great card based strategy.
*Simple and easy to pickup : hard to master.
*Clear counter pick strategies both on and off the battlefield.
*It's early access : it's going to only get better.
Neutral:
Feels more like a card game than a strategy warfare game. While retaining elements of both.
Cons:
-Multiplayer functionality is a bit lacking at the moment.
-Limited "reinforcements" so your strategies are a little less flexible once your on the field.
-Only a couple orders you can give to troops on the field (currently)
-It's early access : it's still lacking some features you might expect.
I'm not entirely sure how to feel about this game personally, but I certainly feel like it's a high quality game I would recommend to fans of strategy card games, and for that reason : I give it a thumbs up.
I'd love to see this game improve and expand on what's already here, but what's already here is already entertaining enough to be fun.
I especially want to see some new strategy options in the future (being able to tell your soldiers to retreat and hold position would be a great start). I feel like the reinforcement cap is a double edged sword as well: while I feel every loss, I also feel constrained in my strategies. No "grand infantry charges" or anything like that. (maybe a different game mode?) Lots of room to change the game and improve,

Alright. So i believe after 65 hours (and more to come) gametime it's time to write a review. Myself, I've never seen any of the Friday the 13th movies. I just know the backstory relatively. But this is a review on the game and I am keeping in mind that bugs can be fixed. So I'm going to start with the pros and end with the cons as well as make some concluding thoughts.
PROS:
1. The game (in my opinion) has very good graphics. There are some visual issues though including: Stuff not showing up, hair flailing, etc.
2. It's very immersive. You could almost feel like you're in the game with all the sound, etc. As well as feel you are in a Friday the 13th movie.
3. The rank system is great. It does go kinda slow, but you feel rewarded when you level up and you pretty much always unlock new things at some point.
4. The controls are great. I've never had an issue with controls. Everything flows so well (I do use keyboard and mouse. Don't know about controllers).
5. It's great to play with friends. You get to hang out with friends and have a nice laugh in this game.
6. The counselor/jason system and characters are all great. They're fun, cool, etc. Perks and kills are just awesome!
7. There so many ways to escape and interact with the map.
8. You can choose who you want to be involving your playstyle (Like preferences and characters).
9. The maps are great. They're cool, nice and flow freely. You don't feel very limited.
10. Jason is balanced. So many games get this wrong. Even though many say he's overpowered... he really isn't. Almost ALWAYS somebody escapes. The game isn't ment to be easy and get free wins 4 dayz. This game would get boring quit.
11. You always feel you're on your toes like a true horror game. Through sounds, ambiance, etc. you always have that scary, but fun vibe of Friday the 13th.
CONS:
1. BUGS. There are many bugs. Visual, flying through map, getting stuck, car flipping over, boat glitches, etc.
2. If you don't have a mic: No interaction, less fun, etc. But I am not using this against the game.
3. You don't unlock much. Pretty much everything past lvl 31 is the same. Just clothes changing colors n stuff.
4. Not enough maps (not using against game).
Conclusion:
Overall, this game is amazing. It's so well made. It creates a great vibe, the devs are great, and it's super fun. This is a game that i could play for a long time. You should get it! I rate: 9/10 just do to the fact of bugs and low amount of lvl up rewards.

One of my most favorite strategy games. I suck so much at Heartstone and many other strategy games (including ones like chess), but here you have control over how things go as things play out instead of pure luck or absolute control (which can suck if you can't think that far ahead). Based on your quick decision making like a true commander on the field, you will have either an AMAZING success or be an ABSOLUTE failure... or even PERFECTLY draw :D! There are many tactics to use and many strategies so you can become a master in various different ways (i.e. defensive, offensive, all infantry units, dependent on tanks, dependent on light vehicles, etc.). You can always change your strategy midbattle if needed so if you do an all out offensive and destroy yourself it's not too late to go defensive if you play things out right and the other gets cocky.
Basically, it's a really well made strategy game and definitely a great game in general to have in your collection if you somehow do not get addicted to playing it everyday.

WORLD END ECONOMiCA episode.01 is a VN where there are no choices for the reader to make. It is pretty long considering how it is just a third of the full story. It is written by the same author who wrote Spice and Wolf. I would recommend having a basic knowledge of stocks and margin trading to fully enjoy the story, since most of the exciting parts are about stock trading.
Story: The story is well written. It is about a boy who runs away from home and makes a living by trading stocks. At times, I feel the story really dragged on, and could be condensed. I really liked the twist at the end. I have studied a lot of economics, finance, statistics, mathematics and computer science, so I thought the story was pretty amazing since it incorporated a lot of material I had learned into a plot. But without basic knowledge of stocks or an interest in economics, you probably will not undestand or be interested in the most exciting parts of the plot and the plot is pretty dull without those components. Overall I would rate the plot 8.5/10.
Characters: The characters differed from the stereotypical characters in most Anime/VN and were well developed. Nothing too special about them though. I would rate the characters 7/10
Music: The music was okay. Better than a lot of other games. A few catchy tunes. I would rate it 7.5/10.
Artwork: The artwork was nice. But there were still a lot of scenes that had black/blank backgrounds and lots of scenes where I feel the background should be updated to different one. Overall, I would rate the artwork 6.5/10 since there were too many scenes with black backgrounds (no artwork) and too many reused backgrounds.
Overall: I would rate it 8/10. The story was great. There are several typos, and too many black backgrounds and reused to backgrounds which took away from my enjoyment.

A very good game. Survarium has a feeling of the good-ol' FPS games (CoD, CoD2 and more) mixing fast-pace and tactical feeling, coplex mechanics (bleeding, breath and so on), RPG elements and 3-dimensional map design. Survarium is as much about surviving as finishing your objectives.
Although PVP is very fun, with interesting modes and TDM (Team Deathmatch), I can't wait to play the open-world mode, which is said to increase the level of complexity with the character building and gameplay.
With the more tactical feeling than other FPS games around, I would like to see some features added, such as leaning (peeking over to the left or right), prone (should add yet another way of surviving), weapon attachments (to increase further the way to modify and upgrade a weapon), team-mate healing (essentially giving the option to become a medic) and more weapons, armor and factions (weapons from all around the world and such).
Map and match-making needs slight improvements aswell. Often times, teams are not equal skill-based, leading to 'ownage' of the weaker team. It seems like adding layers of comparison between players (K/D ratio, W/L ratio and such) would improve match-making.
Map design is great for the most part. Spawn locations and the easy way for the opponents to access them is problematic. Even though there are systems which defend new spawned players (you can't damage someone who just spawned or something like that), 'spawn♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is definitely a thing you see from time to time, especially with poor-made and unequal skilled matches.
Survarium is definitely a recommend, with great gameplay now and many things to look for.

Please remember, the game is still being worked on. Early Access. Pre-Alpha/Beta.. whatever you wish to lable it as. It -will- have its rough edges as most of these types of games do.

Even though Amnesia: The Dark Descent will always be and always remain the best horror game I have ever played (mainly because I am a fan of gothic and lovecraftian horror), SOMA isn't far off. It's immersive, it's atmospheric, it has an incredible soundtrack, and the overall design of the game once again proves to the world that when it comes to survival horror, few companies can measure themselves with the niche Frictional Games has found for themselves. And now it seems that Frictional Games has set the bar a little higher with the most amazing and thought-provoking sci-fi story I have ever had the fortune and pleasure of playing.
Those who are expecting this to be a common "hide-and-run" game are only halfway right. The majority of the game does not rely on cheap scares, but rather the story, the ambience and the very enviroment around you. It will downright put you in a place where you will neither feel comfortable or safe, and leave you little option but to either persist and continue on this nightmarish journey or chicken out with the Save and Exit option.

This game brilliantly illustrates the disastrous consequences of not being properly educated on the importance and criticality of procreation; its ultimate function being the ensured continuation of the species.
This cautionary tale give us a brief glimpse into the life of a young girl forced by her progenitors to stagnate in the putrid swamp of ignorance, reduced to mashing plastic dolls together in a pitiful imitation of intercourse.
The dolls themselves (most likely Chinese made, and coated with toxic lead paint) are the idealization of the human form and thus ferment feelings of inadequacy and low self-esteem when compared to the average body.
All of these factors can coalesce into a potentially dark future where the game's protagonist is unable to relate to the opposite sex and finds herself well into her 40s; childless and unwed, surrounding herself with small domestic animals to satiate her deprived maternal instinct.
Perhaps if she had a healthy amount confidence and social skills she'd have found a mate and started a family, which, as the great André Maurois said, "Without a family, man, alone in the world, trembles with the cold."

Understandably so of course, one can hardly expect the program to provide a repository of all manga-styles in the known universe but there are barely enough characters present to make even a rudimentary Shonen.
Themes

If you know any kind of 3d program and know how to import the files, your options open up but if you're without a clue as far as 3d modelling goes, you're kind of screwed.

Do NOT buy this program! Massive ripoff and extremely limited!
Let me be straight with you, I bought this program from the official site shortly after it came out years ago for $50. It was a gigantic waste of money.
Here's the deal. First off, the program is insanely limited. You are given virtually no freedom whatsoever to design or pose your characters. By default the ONLY outfits are school uniforms in only a couple colors and identical styles. There's maybe less than 10 different hair styles per gender and only a handful of hair and eye colors. The poses for your characters are fixed and you cannot freely move them at all, and there's only a few dozen poses to work with.
There's also a problem with layering. For example, if you wanted two characters to hug each other... well, you can't, because every character is on it's own layer. You cannot pose two characters "together" and have them wrap their arms around each other or something. There's also no real guideline for perspective either so it's really hard to measure characters' positions if they're not at roughly the same distance in the background.
The backgrounds, comic effects and the like are all acceptable. Very little to complain about there. Aside from the fact that there's quite a few backgrounds that simply do not match with the character designs as they're basically just photos that have been run through photoshop filters to look more animated.
But there's more problems. For example the text input has no option to center your text, so all of your text must be manually centered. The program is also extremely slow and takes a long time to load pages and export things even if you have no custom assets on the page. Speaking of custom assets, there's a 3D model importing feature, but it only allows models done in a very specific format and in my experience, half the time they don't import properly and either come out incomplete or outright invisible.
But possibly the worst part of the entire program is the DLC and lack of updates. Here's an interesting fact - the Japanese version came out well over a year before the English version did, and when the English version did come out, it launched with LESS CONTENT than the day 1 Japanese version did. Their excuse was that the English version was cheaper, so they didn't want the Japanese people to just download the English version. They felt it was more appropriate to give the foreigners an outdated product. It was SEVERAL MONTHS with absolutely NO updates to the program before we even got what was available AT LAUNCH for the Japanese version. Of course, by then, the Japanese version was more than a year and a half ahead of the English version in updates and features. I would not doubt that this has continued to be the case.
But it gets worse. The Japanese version had several extra packs of free props to insert into your scenes released prior to the English launch. Several of these did make it into the English release for free, however they actually had the nerve to charge foreigners extra for some of them. When they first launched this pack, it was $15, which again, cost nothing to the Japanese users.
Then there's all the other DLC. If you want to make ANYTHING besides a generic school life series in precisely one single outfit, then they expect you to shell out extra money for crap that should have been in the program from the beginning for free. Well, then again, you can't make anything beyond generic school life series. You've got packs of more school uniforms, some casual clothes, some swimsuits, and stuff like that. And they expect you to pay extra for all of it. It's a ripoff, plain and simple, and even worse is that you get very little for the outrageous prices of the packs. A couple new outfits and a couple colors per pack. I don't know how much they run for these days, but they were about $15-$20 when they came out. For each one. And there was like 5 or 6 of them. On top of the $50 program.
In summary, DO NOT BUY THIS PROGRAM. It's too limited to be of any use, you will be mocked for using it and no one will take any of your comics seriously, and it's just plain a complete ripoff and not worth the money at all. Avoid at all costs.

A great visual novel with fleshed out characters and a believable story. The art is also more than acceptable, but it is not the leading edge in animation.
It is not voiced, which I do not mind, and it is not animated, which I once again do not mind. However, sometimes it seems like the game refreshes or reloads assets. The images vanish, leaving a white screen, before they return. The music also resets randomly it seems. My final complain is the grammatical errors that the English translation has. Every now and then you would find mistakes, but they would not be making the sentence confusing or impossible to understand. They are also rare enough that they do not become a problem. More an annoyance every x minutes. The Japanese one was mostly flawless.
As for the characters and story development, the pacing is very good. It holds back information just enough that you are at the edge of your seat and sometimes wish for nothing more than for the character to say it. However, that is the great part. You really feel that the characters have their secrets, doubts and troubles. At the same time the story is driven by each character's hopes and goals in this world. They live normal, hard lives and have to make compromises as they go. These compromises and the decisions they face really feel like something a human with their personality would make.

Highly recommended for the full price, a must for anything lower.

The central idea of the game is to have 7 Counselors go against Jason Vorhees, trying to survive the 20 minute match however possible.
:
You have a few options of how to apporach a match.  You can either repair a car/boat to escape.  You can repair the phone box and call for the police, which starts a 4 minute timer with a designated safe-zone to escape to (better hope you found a map to see where it is).  You can call Tommy Jarvis to the scene, whom one player assumes after being murdered by Jason.  Or, you can use your wits to avoid him through the entire match.
You also have weapons at your disposal - things to knock him out with, like bats and wrenches.  A flare gun or firecrackers to temporarily blind his senses.  And pocket knives to shove in his neck when you inevitably end up in his grasp.
:
You kill.  All of them.  Well, as many as you can.  There are a few different incarnations of Jason's available to play as, taken from the movies.  Each has pro's/con's and a different weapon.  And you kill for Mommy!
Both the Counselors and Jason have a load-out to choose from to better suit your play style.  The former has things like keeping you hidden from Jason's senses, keeping your cool under tough situations, etc.  Jason has different fatalities you can unlock and equip him with, and you get more points for varying your kills in the match.
Jason
be killed.  It involves some serious team cohesion, a bit of luck, and patience.  I haven't done it yet, and I've avoided articles and videos about it to not spoil it for me (I know the mechanics of how to do it, but I haven't seen it done).
There are 3 maps, each centered around Crystal Lake, Packanack, or Higgins.  Their all camp-grounds, so it's easy to confuse them for each other, especially if you're a noob.  And you spend the better moments of starting out trying to get your bearings.  More maps would be nice, but I'm not complaining - I'm still intimately learning the in's and out's of the ones provided.
:
-There is a 20 minute timer.  While I understand the need for this, it just seems so goofy that Jason stops the hunt.  I guess Saturday the 14th 12 AM is Jason's time to clock off, and it's nifty that he adheres to this with no guff.
-Tommy Jarvis shows up with a hunting rifle... with one bullet.  Really, Tommy?  You got a call that Jason freakin' Vorhees is at it again, and you chose to show up to "send him to hell" with one bullet?
-The Counselors repair the car and drive off.  Why they wouldn't just run away on the same path they take with the car is beyond me, and I get it serves the games purpose, but it's as silly as Jason stopping the hunt abruptly after 20 minutes.
-The spawning is kinda bonked.  Too many times do I spawn next to a car, which seems to be the first place every Jason but me goes to (I like to take out the power boxes first).  If this happens, this is pretty much game over and an 18 minute wait to the next match, if you didn't have enough time to gather a hold-out weapon or any other form of defense.  Which means less points, which means less progress, which means less fun, to me.
-There are a few sniggles in the server.  Sometimes I move through a cabin too fast, sometimes I get kicked from the game, sometimes others just leave.
-You must complete the 20 minutes, either in-game as a survivor or dead as a spectator.  This is good in theory, to keep those from game-hopping, but I've been stuck watching a Jason and the final survivor simply messing with each other for minutes on end.  Not in an entertaining way, either, just in a troll way like people do.
-If you run into Jason with the car, he stalls it.  I think it would be better if you hit him on purpose and could stun him.  I'd like the car to still stall out on this, but I think you should be able to ram into him.  Alternately, I'd like it if Jason could initiate his own attack on the car to stall it.
As you can see, those are more design gripes than mechanics.  But I always enjoyed the NES F13, and I always thought Jason would do good in this type of game.  There is nothing quite like (no, Dead by Daylight is nothing like - all you can do in that game are tinker with generators, throw down wooden palettes, and get camp hooked).  This does the franchise well, and the options for both the Counselors and Jason make this a pretty fun multiplayer title.
It's a good game, and if you die and are spectating the right players, can be an awesome little horror movie in it's own right.  If you have any interest in the franchise, or in this type of gameplay, I highly recommend it.  It's addicting, it can be nerve-racking, and it can be rewarding (wap Jason with a bat and stun him right as you're making it to the cops is quite an accomplishing feeling).

After 8 years of waiting, the third game, sequel to the second, insanely well made Warfare game that was played more than 33 million times and has the rating of 93, comes Warfare Online, its not flash or retro warfare anymore, its in real 3D and modern, the famous tug of war game where you strategicaly try to counter whatever your enemy is sending and reach the other side of the map to win is back and possibly better than ever, debetable but possibly. Ive played alot of matches, heres my review of the good with the bad.
-The most in-depth installment in the franchise and as a game, its still with quite some depth, the game offers quite sizeable platoon customization, as of right now, you have multiple types of troops and vehicles to make your platoon out of, name it, choose a nation, choose your support assets, unlockable gear and operations to make your very own unique little army that best suits your play style that you most enjoy playing with, theres alot to choose from and there will be even more in the future, albeit you ofcourse have to work for them while also being able to accelerate the rate at which you unlock them. Avaivable content right now has a good amount.
-The graphics was never mandatory to be great, but they are, they are realy good, the franchise has trascendend into 3D beautifully, the design choices of the main menu and in match UI interface look rather well, and the effects of shots, fire, artillery, explosions, etc. look beautifull, its a great looking game.
-Theres multiple maps to play on, 4 as of right now at the moment and you betcha there will be more, each of them are very unique from on another in terms of setting, location, weather and whats there, the original first one features alot of light cover in the middle but barely any near the outposts/bases that need to be destroyed to win, theres a winter ice map which has alot of cover near the outposts, but no cover whatsoever in the big long middle part with a impassable crack in the middle lane, forming the famous ''no mans land'' that fans of WWI like Warfare 1917 will be familiar with and maybe in love with too, great maps.
-Vain Glory is a mobile moba game that is well known to not be toxic like League of Legends for example, Warfare Online uses this practice by replacing the chat with a quote, expresion, pre set sentence emotes you can call out to your opponent if you want to share emotions, greet, congratulate them or show that you feel pretty dominant among few of them. This isnt a moba so a chat is less neccesary thus possibly a good idea.
-Your infantry isnt bound to only one lane anymore, they will go either middle, bottom, or top lane, depending on which cover you have activated infront of them and even if their top while activated cover is bottom, they will go to it if they get close to it before encountering enemies
-The AI is smart with well made pathfinding and your units move very smoothly and organized and units that are made to counter what their supposed to, they will, such as the AT teams will focus vehicles and buildings or infantry if their near, as will tanks whom will focus vehicles before infantry if both are present and infront but if units are out of range for their intended targets, they will fire at the closest target which is a understandable game mechanic, there may be some glitches and bugs where infantry may stop moving or vehicles taking odd paths, but those are problems of the closed beta, which this is not, i personaly havent seen these things so its safe to assume for me, that their gone and your units perform as intended.
-Very strategic game, you have to take into account not only the benefits of your gear and support assets, you have to take care with the drawbacks and enemy support assets which you can see when their used, aswell as what operations they have when beginning a match to perhaps give you an idea what is to come that will help you predict what will be used against you, you have to take into consideration the ranges of your units like Snipers, MGs, Assaults, while snipers have the lowest heath and thus have to be protected by infantry infront of them, MGs need to be placed into position in advance, otherwise they will be caught in the open and to maximum vurneability. Each unlock has a positive but also a negative effect that can help suit your needs and remain balanced without there being only positives on the unlockable gear.
-The music is epic (atleast in the main menu) while if theres any background soundtrack while fighting, it is good, alot of games dont even bother having background soundtracks, and the sounds are great, from firing weapons and assets, to units announcing their arrival and situations, each unit having their own voices, multiple different sentences for the same unit, and even being able to tell you what they are facing, Warfare games always have had absolutely great voice acting but its very clear this time, albeit some dialogue is missing for now.
-Everything in the game can be earned and unlocked completly for free (without paying), the biggest cost of that being time needed to work towards unlocking the gear and assets you want to use for your platoon with the system of active daily missions, daily wins and 3 wins in a row and winning after losing 3 times will earn you gold needed to buy supply boxes that will grant you support assets to customize your platoon, and the buisness model is more than fair, you can purchase premium to help you gather more xp and more credits which helps not just you unlock gear faster but also gives a 10% increase in your opponents xp gain, which in turn feeds the devs, thus, everyone wins, and if you buy premium now, it wont be wasted, the exact amount of time will be returned to you when EA is done (which is estimated to be around 2 months), with even a 10% bonus time to the exact premium time youve bought (because progress will be wiped when early access is finished) and the game becomes officaly launched and the core being finished for future updates and content to be implemented later on. If you realy enjoy the game, theres other things to purchase aswell. The game is not P2W.
-The game will feature multiple nations and countries over time, there will be various armies representing individual counties, its EA so theres only two but be assured that there will be more to come, each nation's armies will look vastly different from eachother (vehicles esspecialy), the units all sound different from eachother and will do call outs on what they face, the emotes will even be different and apropriatly unique to each nation, absolutely love the Russian emotes ''Greetings Komandir!'' love it.

BeamNG.drive is a vehicle simulation video game developed and published by Bremen, Germany-based video game developer BeamNG. The game features unique soft-body physics, and was released into Steam Early Access for Microsoft Windows on 29 May 2015.
Contents  [hide]
1	Development
2	Gameplay
2.1	Physics
3	Reception
4	References
5	External links
Development[edit]
On 28 May 2012, BeamNG released a YouTube video titled "Revolutionary soft-body physics in CryEngine3".[1] Originally, BeamNG.drive was to be based on CryEngine 3, but its use in a driving game uncovered numerous bugs, leading development to be rolled over to Torque.[2] BeamNG.drive relies heavily on coding in Lua, and uses packets of local data using the Lua network system while the game is operating in order to complete the complex physics equations during gameplay.
BeamNG's website,
, was opened on 8 May 2012, to begin rolling out news of their development of the simulator.[3]
The game was placed on an open vote on Steam Greenlight on 12 February 2014,[4] and was greenlit eight days later.[5]
On 29 May 2015, the game was released to Steam Early Access.[6]
Gameplay[edit]
BeamNG.drive features three modes: Scenarios, which are checkpoint-to-checkpoint-based races, Campaign Mode, which is a collection of small scenarios which are scored based on different factors such as damage, time, etc., and there is Free Roam Mode, the player can drive and crash several different vehicles on a few provided default environments. The game implements its soft-body physics to both control vehicle dynamics as well as to control the collisions between objects and vehicles.[7][8][9]
Physics[edit]
BeamNG.drive uses a real-time, soft-body dynamics physics structure to simulate its vehicles. Algorithms have been written for the physics equations to be carried out.[10] Vehicles in the game consist of a soft-body, node-beam structure, similar to the vehicle structure in Rigs of Rods. The physics engine simulates a network of interconnected nodes and beams which combine to form an invisible skeleton of a vehicle with realistic weights and masses. In terms of soft-body physics, vehicles realistically flex and deform as stresses to the skeleton, such as impacts from collisions are applied. The game's engine constantly calculates physics equations and problems in real-time during gameplay.[11]
Reception[edit]
Jack Stewart of BBC mentioned that BeamNG.drive "has received interest from the film industry to model vehicle stunts, so that they can be prototyped and tested exhaustively – but cheaply – before a stunt driver smashes up a car on set."[9] Polygon's Nick Robinson lauded the game's simulated physics and user-created content support, leading him to create an ongoing video series for Polygon, "Car Boys", in which he and Griffin McElroy spotlight new BeamNG.drive content each week.[12][13]

So 23hrs so far, I want to go on the record and say I had some reservations about this game but I also didn't play the betas. I feared this would have the same over hype like the division to only die out with lack of end game content.
Single player: I've only played through 6 missions on the knight's story line and I'm liking it so far, I do like the incentive of engravings for completing the story on hard and realist. The Story is more of an interactive tutorial that teaches you the basics of each hero type. Some may like this, me, I don't like how it force the game to pause just to give you a prompt. I will say the story seems alil bland but Ubi had to come up with a weird premise that pit Vikings, Knights, and Samurai against each other. 5/10
Multiplayer: Be prepaired to rage and I mean rage. Duels are balanced and comes down to player skill same with elemination matches with multiple players. Some people are honorable and others are not. If you are looking for an honorable fight, don't jump into dominion. Dominion is a 4v4 player v player or player v AI where you must capture points  and kill the team to win (COD Dominaion anyone?). I have had the most fun with this mode by baiting players for the throw and throwing them off the ledge (yes cheap, you either become the hero or live long enough to see yourself become the villian). This mode also provides loot drops to enhance your look and the feats and abilities of you selected hero. 7/10
Verdict: If you are having a hard time in multiplayer... "Get Gud" but in all honesty, just play through the story, find a hero class that you want to get good with and practice. Have fun, play with a friend, and throw people off ledges. I give this game a perfect 5/7. Joking aside, 7/10.

Even though Amnesia: The Dark Descent will always be and always remain the best horror game I have ever played (mainly because I am a fan of gothic and lovecraftian horror), SOMA isn't far off. It's immersive, it's atmospheric, it has an incredible soundtrack, and the overall design of the game once again proves to the world that when it comes to survival horror, few companies can measure themselves with the niche Frictional Games has found for themselves. And now it seems that Frictional Games has set the bar a little higher with the most amazing and thought-provoking sci-fi story I have ever had the fortune and pleasure of playing.
Those who are expecting this to be a common "hide-and-run" game are only halfway right. The majority of the game does not rely on cheap scares, but rather the story, the ambience and the very enviroment around you. It will downright put you in a place where you will neither feel comfortable or safe, and leave you little option but to either persist and continue on this nightmarish journey or chicken out with the Save and Exit option.

Yet another game to come out in the Multiplayer Survival genre.
Nether claims to be a full release, but it is far from that as most alphas I have played recently are more refined.
The graphics, while pretty in some places, are one of the glitchiest things with this game. Buildings and monsters are sometimes completely invisible, as well as players whom inevitabley kill you. When sprinting the model of your helmet/mask will often bob around on the screen, catching your eye and distracting you. Textures rarely line up and often cause death. I cannot count how many times I fell through the world and died, or fell off a tower because the ramp up was disconnected by at least 3 feet.
When it comes to controls, the game actually does pretty well... when they want to work. After numerous updates and 'fixes' I still have yet to be able to hold my breath with a sniper, turn my flashlight on and off, use a taunt, and blocking only seems to work 50% of the time. The hit confirmation also seems to be a bit off from what I've experienced.
FPS-wise, it is horrible. I have two cross-firing Titans, and I often get 30 frames or below.
The animations are decent on the monsters (with some exclusions), but the human animations are dreadful and often seize up causing people to slide around in front of you... and then kill you.
The world, while being a pretty decent size, feels very plain and boring. Half the map is a destroyed wetlands, and the other half is the same city block over and over with some minor differences. The one this I was really excited about, and something they did a decent job of hyping up, was the subways. This were a huge disappointment. There are barely any monsters down in the subway, it pretty bright, and there are maybe two city blocks worth before you have to get back up onto the surface. I think if they expanded the subway to encompass the entire city it would be a heck of a loot more interesting.
The last two major complaints I have is the 'group missions' and 'tribes' I'm only going to briefly cover these as there really isn't much to say that you couldn;t read everywhere else.
The idea of group missions is flawless. Getting everyone to band together to take down one of the most powerful monsters. The problem with this is that there's no real incentive to working with anyone else. The strong monster is called a 'Reaper' and it can easily be taken down by one person. So you often just end up with a crazy fire-fight over who gets to be the one to fight it. Give a greater threat to band the players together.
I was actually interested in the tribe feature. Basically there are 8(?) tribes you can join, then you can run around the map and capture areas for for bonuses which affect all other tribe members in the area. There's even a rep system between the tribes. The only major problem is that there is absolutely no penalty for killing members of your own tribe. So often do I hold my fire on a tribe mate just to have them shoot me and grab all my stuff. This really needs to be adressed.

This ain't the NES Friday the 13th!
The central idea of the game is to have 7 Counselors go against Jason Vorhees, trying to survive the 20 minute match however possible.
:
You have a few options of how to apporach a match.  You can either repair a car/boat to escape.  You can repair the phone box and call for the police, which starts a 4 minute timer with a designated safe-zone to escape to (better hope you found a map to see where it is).  You can call Tommy Jarvis to the scene, whom one player assumes after being murdered by Jason.  Or, you can use your wits to avoid him through the entire match.
You also have weapons at your disposal - things to knock him out with, like bats and wrenches.  A flare gun or firecrackers to temporarily blind his senses.  And pocket knives to shove in his neck when you inevitably end up in his grasp.
:
You kill.  All of them.  Well, as many as you can.  There are a few different incarnations of Jason's available to play as, taken from the movies.  Each has pro's/con's and a different weapon.  And you kill for Mommy!
Both the Counselors and Jason have a load-out to choose from to better suit your play style.  The former has things like keeping you hidden from Jason's senses, keeping your cool under tough situations, etc.  Jason has different fatalities you can unlock and equip him with, and you get more points for varying your kills in the match.
Jason
be killed.  It involves some serious team cohesion, a bit of luck, and patience.  I haven't done it yet, and I've avoided articles and videos about it to not spoil it for me (I know the mechanics of how to do it, but I haven't seen it done).
There are 3 maps, each centered around Crystal Lake, Packanack, or Higgins.  Their all camp-grounds, so it's easy to confuse them for each other, especially if you're a noob.  And you spend the better moments of starting out trying to get your bearings.  More maps would be nice, but I'm not complaining - I'm still intimately learning the in's and out's of the ones provided.
:
-There is a 20 minute timer.  While I understand the need for this, it just seems so goofy that Jason stops the hunt.  I guess Saturday the 14th 12 AM is Jason's time to clock off, and it's nifty that he adheres to this with no guff.
-Tommy Jarvis shows up with a hunting rifle... with one bullet.  Really, Tommy?  You got a call that Jason freakin' Vorhees is at it again, and you chose to show up to "send him to hell" with one bullet?
-The Counselors repair the car and drive off.  Why they wouldn't just run away on the same path they take with the car is beyond me, and I get it serves the games purpose, but it's as silly as Jason stopping the hunt abruptly after 20 minutes.
-The spawning is kinda bonked.  Too many times do I spawn next to a car, which seems to be the first place every Jason but me goes to (I like to take out the power boxes first).  If this happens, this is pretty much game over and an 18 minute wait to the next match, if you didn't have enough time to gather a hold-out weapon or any other form of defense.  Which means less points, which means less progress, which means less fun, to me.
-There are a few sniggles in the server.  Sometimes I move through a cabin too fast, sometimes I get kicked from the game, sometimes others just leave.
-You must complete the 20 minutes, either in-game as a survivor or dead as a spectator.  This is good in theory, to keep those from game-hopping, but I've been stuck watching a Jason and the final survivor simply messing with each other for minutes on end.  Not in an entertaining way, either, just in a troll way like people do.
-If you run into Jason with the car, he stalls it.  I think it would be better if you hit him on purpose and could stun him.  I'd like the car to still stall out on this, but I think you should be able to ram into him.  Alternately, I'd like it if Jason could initiate his own attack on the car to stall it.
As you can see, those are more design gripes than mechanics.  But I always enjoyed the NES F13, and I always thought Jason would do good in this type of game.  There is nothing quite like (no, Dead by Daylight is nothing like - all you can do in that game are tinker with generators, throw down wooden palettes, and get camp hooked).  This does the franchise well, and the options for both the Counselors and Jason make this a pretty fun multiplayer title.
It's a good game, and if you die and are spectating the right players, can be an awesome little horror movie in it's own right.  If you have any interest in the franchise, or in this type of gameplay, I highly recommend it.  It's addicting, it can be nerve-racking, and it can be rewarding (wap Jason with a bat and stun him right as you're making it to the cops is quite an accomplishing feeling).

Evil Genius is what happens when Dungeon Keeper and James Bond villains have a child together. You play, as the game's title says, an evil genius, bent on destroying the forces of good and conquering the whole world. You start off on a small island paradise, with only a handful of minions, 250,000 dollars, and a single henchmen. From there, your task is to build a complex base of operations into the mountainside,  complete with traps, training facilities, and more, while at the same time plundering riches and fighting off the constant intrusions from the forces of justice. Evil Genius manages to bring out the worst in all of us, and you'll be surprised to find yourself stalking the despised well-doers as they land on your little shred of land, eager to find out how they will meet your demise. And with ways ranging from bazooka-wielding Russians, to a complex set of bee-related traps, you'll find dozens of ways to amuse yourself with their death.

World End Economica is a "kinetic" visual novel (meaning no choices) by the writer of Spice and Wolf.  The writing really takes front seat in this one, as the artwork is limited and much of the story actually takes place over black screens.  If that bothers you, take comfort in the knowledge that the author makes his living writing actual novels which are carried entirely by the text.  And the writing here lives up to that expectation of excellence.
Just like in Spice and Wolf, Isuna Hasekura proves once again that you don't necessarily need to understand all the details of the plot to fall in love with a story and its characters.  I have a difficult time wrapping my head around economic concepts, so often failed to understand elements of the plot in this VN.
It probably doesn't help that it's merely an adequate translation from Japanese, either.
But none of that matters, because the stakes are clear and the setting and characters are great.  The ending caught me by surprise, and I can't wait to read the next one.
Highly recommended for fans of story-driven VNs.  Just be aware, although there are hints of romance, this is no waifu-hunter.  There's much more at stake here than only personal drama.

reinstate and heavy armor assist.
dev has a very bad sense of pricing cards.
reinstate can instantly spawn a tank with the cost of 2
all you gotta do is deplete all the tank only and voila! you get a fresh new tank!
heavy armor assist costs 6 to instant spawn a tank.
all you gotta do is don't have any units on the field then voila! you get a fresh new tank!
let's say you have 2 cards of reinstate and heavy armor assist.
hmm. oh! and the reinforcement skill on the tank too!
oh! and why don't we have operation set that also increases vehicle assets?
let's see.. you will deal with.. minimum 7 f-ing tanks.

There have been a lot of 2D platformers hitting the various download services recently. In order to stand out you need to do something different and do it well. Ethan: Meteor Hunter aims to mix the precision and difficulty of the Super Meatboys of the world with some old fashioned block/tile sliding puzzles (the things that used to drive us mad as kids and when you could never get the last piece in the right place).
You play a mouse named Ethan who needs to navigate a number of platform/puzzle levels while gathering chunks of meteor and eating cheese.  While it might not sound that original it certainly does things a bit differently. The platforming elements are handled in pretty much the same way as a Cloudberry Kingdom or Super Meatboy, that being that they require precision jumps and timing with constant traps and dangers ready to kill you instantly.
Ethan is more about precision than breakneck speed and your character handles differently than you may expect. Handling has changed a little from the PS3 game and there is a better flow to your movement. This allows for the more fluid run that the levels seem to be designed for. There are also numerous checkpoints to avoid having to repeat large sections and the improved handling does help to lower the frustration, however it is still a very difficult game.
The main gimmick is the ability to use telekinetic powers to move blocks around to create platforms and solve puzzles. This, for the most part, works really well and adds variety to the game. Sometimes you’ll be simply moving blocks around to get to the next area, while at others you’ll need to be in a constant flow of jumping and pausing to move blocks to block flames or traps as you pass by. It’s in sections like this that the game really comes to life and the creativity of the development team really shines through.
Levels themselves are designed to the highest standard and just about every conceivable way of twisting the basic mechanics is brought to the table. This means the game is always throwing something new at you or asking you to think about how to use your skills and abilities to reach the next area.
Players need to stay sharp as this is a tough game from the start. You will die and die often and it’s certainly the type of game to cause controller smashing. Most of the time this is due to the player but there are odd occasions where the controls will let you down (it is much less prevalent than the PS3 version though). There are also a few minor issues that add to frustration. The main one of these involves small cut scenes or animations, especially when fighting bosses. You really don’t need to see a five second animation sequence over and over every time you die and it can tarnish the experience at times.
Another minor irritation is the timing of some of the sequences. In areas where things drop from the ceiling or roll along it seems that, on occasion, they don’t start quickly enough. This means that after death you then have to wait a few seconds for the object to get moving before you start charging off as otherwise you end up in the wrong place at the wrong time and die again. These are all minor issues but in a game as difficult as this it does add to the frustration when you have to repeat a section a large number of times.
Overall, Ethan: Meteor Hunter is a brash, inventive and challenging platformer. It has strong level design and a lot of imagination through its fifty or so levels. It certainly shows a lot of potential, the few minor issues with timing and controls seems to have been smoothed out somewhat since the PS3 release which creates a more enjoyable experience. For those looking for more platforming action this is another must have, just be prepared to smash a few pads on your way to conquering the game.

Since the game has changed so much since I made my review, I am redoing it.
And sadly I can no longer recommend the game in its current state.
Now I know there will be those people that will down rate my review simply because I am pointing out game flaws and am not raving on how awesome the Devs are, but I feel it is important for the potential buyers that check reviews before buying to have a clear list of the current issues I feel are making the game bad.
And those are:
-
This is the biggest one giving me bad feelings about the future of this game and how development is going in general.
Instead of having their modelers/animators working on missing dinosaurs from the progression trees, they have them working on Hyper strains. Now Hyper strains are only going to be obtained by a very very small amount of people. It makes more sense to me to finish progression trees that fix progression issues before doing exclusive Dino's, but they aren't. This worries me, because if they're going to focus on what's 'cool' and make those over what's actually NEEDED, it's not going to go well for the game
Update: As of March 04, 2017 new concepts do not seem to be shared on the Steam forums, and as such I cannot see what is being worked on now. It could still be strains that hardly anyone will get to use, or it could be useful dinosaurs. It is now in the dark and not being shared on Steam forums.
-
march 04, 2017 Update: No change to survival / progression since November. Nesting is a new issue, see new section at bottom of review.
A survival game should be fun at all levels, not just the end one. People should enjoy every tier's play style, going from something that sneaks around a lot to something that can can be more confident
But that is not the case. It is final tier, or the current broken Dino of the month, or nothing. There is no incentive to play lower tiers, there is no reward to actually play the game
- Survival
I have to disagree that the game is survival because of long progression times.
In my opinion, survival would involve skill and challenging situations. At the point the game is right now, that is not the case.
You have a couple of situations right now in game:
1.) group packs that slaughter everything in their path, letting even bad players achieve apexs through being hand held the whole way. This isn't skill based survival, this is mobbing and winning through superior numbers and requires no skill beyond pressing forward and right clicking with several others
2.) the AFK strategy where one eats and drinks and then hides until they can progress. Some skill might come into play to get food, or they might scavenge. Or in the case of Spinos , never have to eat at all.
3.) lone wolves who ambush and hunt using skill, but are often killed by the mega packs or spawn killed when they progress.
As the state he game is now, it is not a skill based survival game. If it was, we would have a LOT less apexes running around.
The game right now is 'who has the most time and the most friends' game. If you have a lot of time you can AFK strategy. If you have a lot of friends you can do the mob strategy where skill isn't required.
