I was excited for this new work by Isuna Hasekura long before it was released and I was not disappointed. This is an advanced read and I learned a lot from it -- not just in terms of vocabulary, but also in how the stock market works. Told from the perspective of a runaway sixteen-year-old, everything was thoughtfully described like any Hasekura work, while maintaining the spunky additude of a male adelecent. And the stakes in the story? I think there are moments when WORLD END ECONOMiCA is equally humerous and even more thrilling than Hasekura's other series: Spice & Wolf. In short, the story itself is solid.
The two, maybe three, main characters are complex, some of the secondary characters could use a little more exposition, but I'm hopeful in the sequels to come. The music selections are very appropriate for each moment with a few particularly memorable tracks. The character sprites are decent, some better than others, the CGs are even better even though some are re-used in the story.
The complaints I have could possibly be linked to the switch to the Ren'Py engine in such a rush. In my Mac version of the game (Ren'Py was used to accomodate Mac and Linux), there were moments throughout when coding issues thew me out of the loop of the story. Lots of extra/missing quotation marks or periods, sentences that were chopped between one too many frames, missing nameplates when characters are talking, etc. Every song in the game had looping issues where it would play about 10 seconds into the loop and then jump back to the beginning again. The most heinous mistakes were when the character sprite was supposed to make a slight shudder or a nod and it ends up jumping around the screen sporadically. It was so bad that when a sprite actually made a reasonable movement, it made me sigh in relief, still removing me from the story.
In summary, WORLD END ECONOMiCA was a fantastically written story by Hasekura that is pleasing to the ear, the eye, and the mind, but the number of glitches throughout the game is criminal when coupled with a wonderful tale. I have e-mailed screenshots of all of the glitches I caught to their support group, and I hope they take the time to fix them in the future. If they ever do fix them that will restore a point or two in my rating, but for now, I anxiously await the next installment at the end of the year.
My score for WORLD END ECONOMiCA by Isuna Hasekura: 7.5/10

Bought this in the hopes that it would be more fun than it looked like. I was wrong. I may only have 7 hours in, and maybe I'm not the audience it's geared for, but after giving it a chance, I'm rather unimpressed with it. Game glitches aside (and there are _plenty_ of those to go around), the game mechanics themselves are just....dull. Work with the other survivors (or not, doesn't truly matter) towards one of several ways to escape Jason. Except that just because you helped doesn't mean you'll get to benefit (find the battery + the gas, but not keys? Someone else might just have keys and drive off without you. lol). It also just makes the game dilute. There's so much to potentially do, and so little coordination without a full group that you really wander kinda aimlessly for most of the game. When you are found, it _is_ possible to escape, with some really witty play, and good stealth stats, and some decent luck. However 90% of the time, once Jason finds you, either you die, or the guy that gets between you and him dies (then you die). Add to this the forced video intro/outro that are annoying at best, the two generations old (or worse) quality graphics (seriously....it's not pretty), and a heavy lean towards luck vs. skill gameplay, it's bland. I've played for 7 hours (maybe not a whole lot, but enough for like 30 rounds), and I've enjoyed about 3 minutes total. (I had a pretty epic escape in a car in which I managed to dodge Jason twice, which, given how brokenly bad the controls are, was a miracle). Compare this to Dead by Daylight where after some 600+ hours (though to be fair, probably 200 of that was queue times) I _still_ get adrenaline rushes and genuine fun out of at least one in ten games, if not more frequently, and definitely enjoy the majority of rounds. I've read a bunch of reviews praising the multiple routes to victory in this over DbD, but really, the singular goal in DbD is what adds the intensity. There's a single focus on what needs done, and a lot goes wrong enroute.

Rarely does a fighting game invent enjoyable new mechanics. The left-right-up block circle turns some of the fighting from proactive to reactive, though most characters seem to have enough options to not make the game too defensively slanted. There's single player too, but it's sort of eh whatever as is the case in many fighting games. It'll give you a nice 6 hours or so to get used to the game's core mechanics, but besides that and unlocks it gives on higher difficulties the game is all online.
Fair mechanics, high skill cap and decent character balance is crucial to the competitive scene in fighting games. For Honor is nice for the core mechanics are fairly quick to learn and there aren't too many moves for each character to study. The skill floor for enjoying online fights is low enough for many to enjoy it at least this early on. Sure, some of the characters seem to be better off than others, but as with every fighting game, the ability to execute your own character's moves and read & react to your opponent is what actually wins engagements. This is exceedingly important in the duel and brawl modes. In addition, I'm guessing balance patches will be fairly common for the game.
4v4 modes are where I feel like the game should get some more updates and balancing. The whole thing about leveling up gear is what I don't like too much. It lets you substitute skill with your character simply being stronger than your opponent in 4v4 modes. And to add to that, many fights in those modes usually have people ganging up against single enemies with little chance to actually fight. The matchmaking makes me to question how it's done at times too. Region is obvious, but I have no idea what "player skill" even is, as it's never disclosed. You seem to be locked into your own language too, even if you know multiple languages and could easily play with them. You can't adjust the matchmaking parameters either, which sucks. I see constantly matches where I'm thrown against way stronger opponents gear-wise.

I want to disclose that I really like this game, but my recommendation will stay as a "No" until they fix at least some of the below problems.
It's also worth noting that the 1v1 and 2v2 modes are largely fine, but any other mode outside of those suffers from the issues I list (which is awful because that's at least half the game).
Of course this is all my personal opinion and includes a few anecdotes.
Short of it -
No balancing in 'matchmaking', frequent disconnects, breaking up groups after lobbies fail, the game straight up freezing, and gear significantly affecting stats (the better of which is locked to most casual players) all plague For Honor and make it so I'm not able to give it a positive recommendation.
In detail -
-When putting players into a match it seemingly fills one team before the other, meaning if you have 5 non-grouped players it will put 4 in one team and then the other 1 player by themself.
-It also doesn't seemingly take into account item score of each player and try to make them even, despite item score having a huge impact on gameplay you're more likely to see unbalanced games, rather than balanced ones.
-P2P would've actually been fine, had the transition from hosts actually worked. Instead if multiple people leave/host leaves you'll often just get disconnected from the game, with no rewards or recognition that you just spent 15 minutes + playing.
-If you join a lobby in a group with your friends but the lobby doesn't start for what ever reason, the system will kick you out AND break up your group so you have to make another one. It wouldn't be too bad but it happens after almost every game.
-Past week I think I've had at least 1 freeze per day. Seems to have started happening after the most recent update.
-Gear affecting stats is stupid, while feats are just annoying in most cases. This is basically a 3d fighting game, and we have gear that lets you 2-hit people. Gear that lets you abuse revenge mode, becoming effectively invulnerable (even in 1v1 situations). Admittedly it wouldn't be TOO bad if everyone was on the same footing and had access to the same gear, but of course the better items are locked behind levels meaning if you want to try a new character or are just new to the game you're instantly disadvantaged in terms of stats.

There aren't many games I can compare the overall experience of Pyre to. Perhaps The Banner Saga, in parts, but nothing else really comes to mind. The game oozes creativity, and feels like such a fresh experience. It's easily one of the best games I've played this year.
Pyre is nothing short of incredible. The artwork & animation are absolutely beautiful - some of the most beautiful I've ever seen. The music is lovely, and complements the atmosphere of the game perfectly. The quality of the writing throughout the entire game was phenomenal, honestly better than 99% of the books I've read. The game gives you choices that can actually have a significant impact on the outcome of the game - yet you're never left feeling like you made the wrong decision.
The characters have clearly been designed with meticulous thought, and are full of personality. The narrator of the rites is one of my favourite video game narrators of all time (if you loved the narration in Bastion, then you'll have an idea of what to expect).
I wasn't sure how I felt about the rites at first, with the reviews of others having left me prejudiced. I quickly grew to love them. The rites can be incredibly intense. They begin relatively simple in order to tutor you (as expected), but steadily develop into a complex, genre-defying sport/game that works fantastically. There are a whole number of options for perks, talismans, characters and more which keep the rites feeling fresh and interesting throughout the game.
Having taken the time to write this and think back on my experience of the game, I would rate it 10/10, on the basis that I can't think of anything I would consider a flaw, or in need of improvement.

Commonwealth is a fantasy land where you can get a life sentence for stuff like terrorism, war crimes, literacy or having no family. Exiled into the dark Downside, your only chance at freedom and absolution is to collect a team and win a game of magical football.
Well, that's about it. The game is a mix of interactive novel and sports, quite a new experience from Supergiant. On the other hand, you get all the good stuff: the sense of fleeting beauty, longing and desperation, music that is a vital part of the game and changes along, breathtaking visuals. But the best thing so far is the characters: your teammates and opponents have their personalities and agenda, and the more you get to know them, the more their history is revealed. Both your wins and losses progress the narrative in a very natural way, the relationships between the charaters develop, and you get to make some hard choices.
I found the beginning of the game to be a bit slow-moving, with some empty dialogue and little meaningful interactions, but that changed for the better. The action itself can become a bit repetitive, but the diversity of charaters and an urge to change things up from time to time barely fixes that problem. The world was a bit too heavy on lore, but that one's completely optional.
I also found myself not caring too much about the “big picture” of the game mission, and getting overly attached to particular characters. I'd say overall music, action and emotional impact worked better in Transistor.
Pyre is beautifully made, with plot variability and nice replay value, and full of living creatures of all shapes to get your sympathy, compassion, hatred, disgust, admiration — anything except indifference.

So I just finished the campaign and the whole experience left me kind fo puzzled, but in a good way.
It is certainly interesting from a game design point of view and I think it is almost worth playing just to see the unique way the story and gameplay are presented.
The game really provides you with a flavorful and different outcome for all your choices and while the overarching story is short and straightforward, they really took giving every player a different experience to an extreme - even the music that plays during the credits is customized to your personal achievements. Of course the depth of story is going to suffer a little if so much breadth is provided, but in my eyes this was done very carefully and didn't devalue the experience. Rather it left me wanting to know more about a fascinating world that I'm still not even beginning to understand and wondering, what other facettes of personality the characters I learned to care for might have, which I didn't get to see in the short time we shared.
The core gameplay of the rites is very interesting and works well. The performance of the computer controlled enemies is a bit all over the place - sometimes mercilessly exploiting your weaknesses, sometimes just staring puzzled at what you are doing. At higher difficulties or with a few boni to the enemies attributes the game is seriously challenging. At normal difficulty I managed to only lose a few games, but there are many options to make the game easier or more difficult and I suggest you use them to find a level of challenge that is enjoyable for you. I am kind of curious how the story would have turned out had I simply played on a higher difficult setting. My biggest complaint is probably that the filler matches outside of certain key points in the story don't really feel like there is much at stake.
Other notes: I definitely recommend playing with a controller. The graphics look great and fit the style and tone of the game perfectly. The soundtrack is simply amazing and beautiful!

It was good at first, when the concept was about as simple as it could get. Spawn in map, find unmarked targets, shoot targets. Then it went the way of every other modern military shooter and decided to start pouring in gimmicks that ended up with many very one-sided matches as one team would be far better equipped than the other and the gameplay suffered horribly.
In the middle of a match, I pointed out that I couldn't tell if people weren't taking damage because of lag or because of body armor- and in my opinion, both of those reasons are bull sh!t. The time to kill early on was deliciously low when no one had more of a foot up than anyone else. Then kevlar came in and it started taking half a magazine to kill one guy in close quarters.
Also after a certain point, every single bullet I took started to cause massive bleeding. I could only assume that this is a random generated thing - what causes bleeding and at what rate - and if it's not, I wouldn't believe whoever told me otherwise. I was forced to take medkits or die after literally every gunfight, even if I had only been scratched by just ONE pistol round. Medkits also cost ten times the amount as grenades for arbitrarily no reason.
While I like that the guns are a little more realistically loud, they really need to work on the sound in general. It felt like anyone within 70 meters firing their gun was firing it from inside my brain. It made it damn near impossible to pinpoint where you were being shot from at times, or where exactly a fight was going down. It was just pure volume.
Bear traps. Along with the body armor, these just feel like an unnecessary gimmick for a deathmatch game. I'm of the opinion that adding more gimmicks like these has only made games more shallow than fuller.
If I could suggest a fix to this particular gripe, I would say make bear traps a maiming tool rather than a disgustingly cheap instant kill. I don't know of any creature that dies instantly from stepping within a meter of a steel trap. If they were going the
route, then the bear trap would just make a guy start to bleed quickly while crippling their legs and stopping them from being able to sprint or creep. There. Perfect fix. Maintains integrity, offers you a chance to realize your mistake while allowing you to still act and puts you at a severe disadvantage that you can overcome if you have a medkit or if your aim/reaction time is still better.
Spawn camping is a pretty surefire way to win any match. Alpha, beta, what the ♥♥♥♥ ever:
Map design. The maps are awesome- better than any game on market that I know of. The foliage on every map is so dense that it's possible to disappear if you find the right spots and hold still. It leads to some pretty campy gameplay, yes, but then I was honestly surprised to find that many of the maps have sections that seem to be rarely used that offer both long and direct flanking routes. Typically each map seemed to have a section that was radioactive or otherwise volatile that harmed you or messed with your vision but they offered the fastest route from one side of the map to the other, adding a subtle element of risk vs. reward. I mentioned earlier that I'm not a fan of the "gimmicky" nature of modern military shooter games and the constant dependence on gadgets, but I did like the idea of being able to equip gas masks and oxygen tanks at the cost of mobility to allow you to navigate these areas because the drawback is about as significant as the reward.
Opportunity cost, muthaf*ckas.
The leveling system and the character customization looked promising. I wasn't prepared to spend money myself but I appreciated that it was an option. The general appearance of the armor looked great. The talent system looked promising as well- normally I'm not a fan of stat increases in a shooter, but if they're trying to be STALKER, it's a step in the right direction. Plus it helped set up a specific playstyle- like investing points in talents that facilitate mobility or camping.
It was a brief, almost entirely cosmetic experience with decent gunplay that's not breaking any molds that made me uninstall before clocking just six hours of gameplay. It wasn't awesome. I'm not sure if I could say it was even "decent" or "okay," Survivarium is just a game that exists and that's about it. If the developers really shock people and change the way the whole game operates by the time it's out of early access, I might try it again- but it's just another mediocre game for now.
I will say it was almost infinitely more fun and less frustrating than Heroes & Generals, but that's comparing free apples to free potatoes.
Oh, and I'd heard a lot of pay to win claims, but I didn't play very long to see any validity to those claims. The guns you all get for free (read:
) all seem to be perfectly capable of standing on their own. Some guns may need balancing, yes, but for what it's worth, I did like where they were at. I appreciated the respect given to caliber versus rate of fire. I'd also heard that match-making could take a long time and didn't seem to have much a problem with that personally. Survivarium is picking up reputation so that came to little surprise.
While the thought is on my mind, a lot of people are going to defend the game based on it being free to play- and it's true, we shouldn't torture ourselves playing games we apparently can't stand when it cost us nothing to acquire it. As with other F2P games, when criticisms are brought to light, these are the first two things very loudly shouted by those who enjoy the game.
Let's start with this: "free" does not a good game make. A dev could

Secondly: if your defense of a game is basic, targeted attacks on someone else, you aren't doing anything for this thing you apparently love. But if you want this misshapen block of clay to stay lumpy and unworked, by all means.
In closing, I'm just going to say this: your words are petty and meaningless, and you further depthen the reason why almost every game crapped out in the last five years is worse than the last. The bar for approval is set constantly lower and it's already pretty much on the floor. Be a little more staunch in your opinion. Do it for them, okay? The devs? I just want to start off by saying this game is not finished, and still has a lot of potential. I love the survival idea and I like the idea of progression, since it prevents servers from hosting too many of the same dinosaurs, as Im sure everybody would play as hypo if it was still sandbox. But this game still has a lot of work to be done. For instance, this game has no place for solo players. If you play solo, there is a lot of waiting around and sneaking to avoid groups of carnivores. And even when you progress into a large and powerful creature, you still have to watch out for groups since they will again, kill you. Also, its not so much the groups of same species as it is with mixed species of carnivores as now they have the advantage of each carnivore's strengths to take you down. If they could eliminate that somehow, and encourage more competition between each species, I think it could eliminate these extremely powerful and aggressive groups and even take the attention away from the little guys from time to time.
The map is also a problem as well. The size I could care less about, but its design is terrible. You have these vast amount of spaces that nobody enters, either because its too mountainous or there is no food and water in these areas, and it makes traversing and finding prey a real hassle. Plus when you do reach the lakes and waterholes with food and water, the name of the game goes from survival to king of the hill. Some of you may say, "Well in real life animals congregate at waterholes for food and water and compete with each other." Yes they do, but not all year! During the dry season when water is low, animals will form masses around these little pools of water. The rest of the year, there is plenty of water for everybody so that they are not crowded. I think rain should be implemented so that pools fill in the forest that after so many uses will disappear until the next rain, and encourages more plants to grow that again will not regenerate until next rain. This not only will simulate real life, but increase everybodies chance of survival and not have to walk half the Earth to get food and water as a taco. There might be other ways too im sure, but for now the current system encourages king of the hill behaviour.
My last complaint is about the dinosaurs. It would seem that some of these guys are at a definite advantage than the others. An example would be when I played as an allo, a utah raptor found me in a bush and began attacking me. I got up and chased after him. Not only is he faster, he is way more agile too. I could not for the life of me get a hit on him and died, as I was not fast enough nor did I have a good turn radius. This to me is unfair as yes some dinos will have an advantage over others and in most confrontions win, but it should not be possible for one dino species to be at a complete disadvantage to another and die every time they encounter eachother. This kind of thing will ruin the game, as like in sandbox mode, people will definitely pick certains progression trees over another if it means they will die to another easily and render that progression tree obsolete. We already saw this when nobody would play as allo because allo got stuck on trees and would die since allo players could not escape from other players.
Like I said, this game is still in development. A lot could change, whether it be good or bad. For the time being, I would suggest buying this game only if you have friends to play with and are a casual gamer who does not get angry or annoyed easily. If you are a solo player who likes dinosaurs, stick with Primal Carnage for now, as this game has not welcomed that part of the community yet.

It was on sale, I'm happy that I bought the game and went through the story. I choose to believe it was less about the "boy meets girl," and more of having self worth in your own thoughts. With technology advancing, rapidly replacing labor that was once done by humans; this rather alternative view gave me some comfort.

It's a nice series of circuit puzzles with interesting constraints.  I liked taking some moments just to look at the puzzles as minimalist works of art -- they are rather pleasing in construction.
I would have liked to see some of the mechanics explored more, for instance those hooks which have to simultaneously retract, but the game is well worth the price as it is.
One thing I felt myself wishing was for a mechanic which made the hook retraction order matter, perhaps junctions which only stay alive while certain hooks are present.  This would prevent the strategy of retracting one hook at a time.  Or, with less change to the mechanics, it would be interesting to replace lives with an undo feature and keep track of the least button pushes per puzzle.
The game appealed to my crisscrossing mazelike line following tendencies.  I give it one knot theorist seal of approval.

It was quite hard for me to actually write a review about this game, so this is what I came up with:
There's been a bit of controversy lately about games which "look a bit like Limbo", and while the frankly excellent Feist largely dispensed with the intense puzzle-solving antics of (the apparently now "classic") Limbo in favour of extremely clever combat mechanics, Collisions can perhaps be seen as the "yin" to Feist's bloodthirsty "yang". Not only will you NOT DIE hundreds of times over, as you are surely doomed to do in Limbo/Feist (your "character" in this instance is a ball making its way through semi-industrial, pinball-styled "landscapes")...but furthermore, the nature of Collisions' puzzles are perhaps best described by the very "zen" catchphrases which appear on screen, such as "Patience is the companion of wisdom". Indeed.
Normally I'm not a great fan of such Buddhist-y musings, but in the context of this game they're perfectly appropriate, if not exactly groundbreakingly profound. So who would I recommend this game to? Well, anyone who can get behind a non-violent, mostly timing-based puzzle game, which isn't all that "long" (it took me a little over an hour to complete) or especially "hard" (I'm actually quite rubbish at these kinds of games)...yet has a nice visual and aural aesthetic which ushers one into a state of relative calm and so on and so forth and blah-blah-blah. In fact, it's a wonderful antidote to the frequently "troll"-ish nature of gaming and the internet in general, as it has a tendency to tell you when you're "doing great!" and what-not; as opposed to, say, a game of Left 4 Dead 2 Versus, in which you will be informed by teammates of how "♥♥♥♥" you are at least once every two to three minutes of gameplay (and that's if you're playing with the NICER folks who play Left 4 Dead 2...the TRUE ♥♥♥-holes would've simply "kicked" you two to three minutes INTO the game, period).
So if it's a relatively serene, laid-back, and only ever-so-slightly "frustrating" time you're looking for, and you have about an hour to spare, this could well be a game for you. I'm not too sure about the four dollar price-tag (I got it for two), and there's obviously a ♥♥♥♥-tonne of very angry people out there in Steamland who will complain even if they pay well under a buck for a mere hour's gameplay, so if you're one of those people...YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED. It's short, you don't get to shoot anyone, and there aren't any virtual lap-dances. So if you fancy a game which makes you feel like a bad-♥♥♥, mo'-♥♥♥♥in' PIMP, this may not be for you. A "nice" enough game, just the same...

Bought this in the hopes that it would be more fun than it looked like. I was wrong. I may only have 7 hours in, and maybe I'm not the audience it's geared for, but after giving it a chance, I'm rather unimpressed with it. Game glitches aside (and there are _plenty_ of those to go around), the game mechanics themselves are just....dull. Work with the other survivors (or not, doesn't truly matter) towards one of several ways to escape Jason. Except that just because you helped doesn't mean you'll get to benefit (find the battery + the gas, but not keys? Someone else might just have keys and drive off without you. lol). It also just makes the game dilute. There's so much to potentially do, and so little coordination without a full group that you really wander kinda aimlessly for most of the game. When you are found, it _is_ possible to escape, with some really witty play, and good stealth stats, and some decent luck. However 90% of the time, once Jason finds you, either you die, or the guy that gets between you and him dies (then you die). Add to this the forced video intro/outro that are annoying at best, the two generations old (or worse) quality graphics (seriously....it's not pretty), and a heavy lean towards luck vs. skill gameplay, it's bland. I've played for 7 hours (maybe not a whole lot, but enough for like 30 rounds), and I've enjoyed about 3 minutes total. (I had a pretty epic escape in a car in which I managed to dodge Jason twice, which, given how brokenly bad the controls are, was a miracle). Compare this to Dead by Daylight where after some 600+ hours (though to be fair, probably 200 of that was queue times) I _still_ get adrenaline rushes and genuine fun out of at least one in ten games, if not more frequently, and definitely enjoy the majority of rounds. Has nothing to do with p2p, which has been fine, and everything to do with the balancing of the 4v4 modes revolving around revenge gear. For context Revenge is a comeback mechanic, for long fights and 1v2 situations. It grants a tempoary HP buff, unlimited stamana, and a large damage boost  for a short time (these stats can be increased further with gear). The Problem is gear is capable of turning oponents monsterous rage machines, and matches frequently pit players with gears scores of 100+ against players in the 20-30 range. How is it remotly balanced or fun if one guy gets rage at 1/2 HP in a 1v1, parries you onto your butt and then 2 shots you? It blows my mind that this passed any sort of testing. Matches like these are vexing to an extreme. If your team doesnt not want to fight the enemy 1v1 prepare for your opponent to back to back rage requiring you to chew through several hp bars whilst avoiding massivly damaging attacks. Its even worse against defensive based classes. It would be like saying a character in Mortal Combat or Street Fighter can fill their super meter at x4 the rate their opponets can.
At its core this game is one of the best fighting games I've had the pleasure of playing. The first week was amazing, but as people became geared, matches more imbalanced and toxic I can not Recomend this game unless you want to stick to the 1v1 mode.  Until gear (or really, revenge) is either matched with like gear or balanced I can not tell you that this game is fun. Its often a misserable slog of team mates yelling at eachother or the enemy. ITs a crime, because the core game is so much fun. I want to love this game so badly.
the above has been fixed with rebalance of gear

Transistions and black screens are really poorly done from what I experienced, if I had a complaint that would be it.  Way too many black screens and the transistions had a tendency to loop on me.

I love this game, but i hate how Ubisoft has managed it.
The Great:
- Gameplay: The combat is enough alone to make me love this game, it is simple enough to grasp early on but has a huge skill ceiling. While there may be only 4 archetypes of class, there is enough differentiation between the way each race represents them that each of the current 12 characters feels unique.
- Graphics: Visually this game is stunning, and as far as i have expereinced well optimized.
- Meta Progression: Plenty of visual customisation in each of the classes alot of space to build on but plenty for an initial release.
The Good:
- Sound Design: Each race / class has a fairly unique sound to them which does a whole lot to make you "feel" who you are playing. Ambient audio effects are everywhere, it does well to make you feel like you are a part of a battle, opposed to the whole battle itself.
- Single Player Campaign: Surprisingly good single player experience albeit although the trailers spoilt the majority of the interesting narrative posibilities. It does a solid job of giving you each of the classes to you throughout the story, although could does miss a couple of them. Realistic mode is certainly an interesting experience, lets hope they include some UI'less mode in Multiplayer.
(SPOILER) The trailer basically slaps you in the face with the fact that Apollyon wants war, then the whole story tries to slowly reveal it to you? (END SPOILER)
The Average:
- Level Design: From a gameplay standpoint the levels are functional but dont exactly do anything new or incredibly exciting. The levels are obviously tied together in the story progression wise so why not tie together some sort of short multiplayer campaign (Start off in the woods > Progress to the Lower Wall > Progress into the Castle) then swap around recording how far the attacker gets each time? That would have been interesting. Does well to represent each combination of players though, (4v4) (2v2) (1v1). The whole "Faction War" thing seems like a grander idea that got hacked down into what it is now, my experience of it so far is that as an individual player you dont have much of an effect, and is essentially just a roulette wheel that chooses a faction at the end of the period to give some rewards to.
- Networking IN-GAME: I will get into the matchaking and general overall system later but this needs to be represented. Im all for the peer-to-peer-to-peer networking, yes Dedicated servers are always preferred but frankly i think they are on the way out for small multiplayer games like this. The majority of the world has significant enough internet these days that it is a waste of resources to throw money at dedicated servers when your clients are perfectly capable of providing their own networking. The old 1 player hosts everyone else connects system is outdated and unbalanced however so i think the introduction of a peer-to-peer web system is clever. That way everyone can share the load out and we dont have to have one person with great internet providing the whole system for everyone else. I have noticed very little lag in the current system when i am actually able to connect to and stay in a game and thats from an Australian living with pretty below average internet 4+ hours away from any significant populations.
The Bad:
The Awful:
- Networking Management: From my experience this has been to this point god awful, and has been that way since the closed beta. It is fairly common for me to get into three games in a row that i get kicked from to the title screen just before the game ends, lossing all my time and effort. While i have said before i am a fan of the peer-to-peer system they have going in function, i am fairly concerned with the security implications (broadcasting players ip's to all other players).  And the constant stalls when a player disconnects are a massive hindrance (not sure exactly how it works but from my understanding while the gameplay is a peer to peer web there is still a assigned host which is what causes the need for a migration?)
Final Thoughts: Hopefully Ubi pulls a R6:Siege with this one and manages to pull the networking together and maintain an actual effort to produce content post-release (Yes they have agreed to doing it but there is a difference between doing something to appease requirements and doing something because you are genuinely dedicated to keeping it going) Sooner rather than later.
TLDR: Great game, terrible networking management. Hopefully Ubisoft pulls it together ASAP before people are too bitter to come back if / once it gets sorted out.

The gameplay on The Darkness is pretty good. It's fast paced and the "4 arms" gimmick will feel confusing at first, but it'll grow on you as you start ripping people apart (the game is pretty graphical that way) and getting new powers with the skill system.
The story is pretty good and moves at a nice pace, but then again, the game is easily finished in about 5 hours, wich is pretty bloody short, even by "modern" FPS standarts... However it does offer a New Game+ option, witch is always nice. You get to keep all the collectibles you found and skills you purchased so that your second time arround is even bloodier and more violent (if something like that is possible). However, the original ending was a bit of a dissapointment, so here's hoping for an alternate ending on NG+!
Also, the characters are pretty well presented, especially the Darkling, who helps us during most of the game and serves as a comical relief.
In addition to the single player campaign, there is a co-op campaign with 4 different characters, all with a specific set of skills and limited use of weapons and the Darkness (you know, those 2 devilish arms). It sounds good enough, but it actually takes away the biggest part of the gameplay that makes it great: the "quad-wield"... and of course, the story. Still, any co-op mode has potential for fun!
I'd recommend this on sale or included in a bundle (like the current 2K one, go check it out, for 1$ you get this, Bioshock and The Bureau), since for 30€ you won't get your moneys worth in terms of lenght...

Let me start by saying this, I can't remember the last time a game got me so hooked that I played it solidly to finish in a couple days.
This game probably has one of the most intense stories that I've ever had the pleasure to play through. Playing as Jackie Estacado, head of a mob family you weild the power of the darkness to tear your way through your enemies in pursuit of the culprits behind a sudden attack at a resturant. It may sound like your typical mob family story, but its anything but. Not to mention this game has probably one of my favourite sidekicks of all damn time.
This game throws guns at you to use at yoru disposale but let me tell you this, you should rarely be using them as a primary weapon, with the power of the darkness which takes form as two demon serpents which you control as you see fit, you can brutally rip your enemies, pull their spines through their *ss and eat their hearts out, why would you use a gun.
The gameplay and combat is smooth and at later parts of the game really require you to use your surroundings to your advantage. No matter what difficulty you play on there will be that challenge and that satisfaction of your success.
Now thats not to say this game is without its flaws. The voice of the 'darkness' tries to sound menacing but in all reality, its a little bit dull for a voice you expect the ultimate evil to have. On top of this you can't use your demonic powers in the light, which is a nice touch, but when your getting constantly told by the darkness to 'stay away from the light', especially in places where it can't be helped, it gets really, REALLY annoying.
I also encountered a couple of times where I couldn't actually activate a button or trigger an event because the prompt wouldn't show up, I fixed it by restarting the checkpoints but it took several attempts.
So yes, a fantastic game coupled with fluant gameplay/combat mixed in with an intruiging, albeit irritating ally, the Darkness II is well worth its price. Best part is though? Its only a dollar on humble bundle right now so there is no excuse not to give this a try.

This game is pretty hit or miss. There is a very solid foundation of a good, fun game, plagued by bugs and development problems.
The bad:
-Most of my problems don't occur within the game itself, rather I have problems with the launcher and server list not loading or being extremely bugging. Server stability is unreliable at best. Often times I will wonder around for 15-30 min, only to find out the server has been "frozen" the entire time and nothing I've done has counted. There are days I have to try 4 or 5 servers before I can get properly connected.
-Additionally, I'm a little concerned that the developers seem too focused on content instead of optimization. The game is very beautiful at times, but I too often encounter strange textures, floating grass, and other oddities. I would also like to see more graphics options in the pause menu. Currently you have to edit video settings from the config file. Finally, I have had trouble with key bindings and the way items stack in your inventory is not intuitive and makes it hard to manage your items.
-There definitely is a learning curve. At the beginning, you while probably die and lose some good loot several times. But there is a leveling system that persists through death, and your cumulative experience will make each fresh start easier. At first, deaths were frustrating but the more you play the more you will realize Its not too hard to come back.
-Hitbox detection ranges from the absolute best to the absolute worse I've ever seen. Using a gun is more or less a crap shoot, but finding a server that works well for you can partially resolve this.
The good:
-Damn this game is atmospheric. There are times when I am sitting at the top of a building at night tracking 2 player in my scope and I all I can think about how exciting this game is.
-There is tons of area to explore (even if much of it is empty wasteland) and there are plenty of little areas you can examine and get a little blurb like "I ate at this cafe once". There aren't a whole lot of them but I'm hopeful this will expand in the future to help you better figure out the back story of this game (side note, the story is somewhere between nonexistent and meh at this point).
-Though lots of people complain about it being impossible to face more experienced players, I just don't think its true. The game is well balanced enough you can fight low-level nethers as a beginner. Most of this game is learning what areas to loot and what areas/nethers to avoid. Most of the time I'm able to craft a high-tier guns with just an hour or two of scavenging. Also I've been able to go from start to the highest level without a gun more than once.
-There's no grand strategy or overarching objectives. So the game is what you want it to be. You can spending your time carrying cardboard boxes across the map for a cash reward, or trying to make a shotgun out of dismembered zombie flesh. There's not a huge variety of things to do, I think the fact that different players are trying to accomplish different goals makes encounters interesting. You have to decide if you are going to be the kind of person that shoots on sight or try to cooperate. (side note, i'd say about half the people I meet will just shoot on sight. There have been plenty of times I've run into friendly players who want to team up or trade)
Final verdict: 6.5/10

Ugly, over-sized user interface that is terribly organized and difficult to understand and navigate. Unintuitive camera controls that are very difficult to smoothly and comfortable operate(You can't change the keybindings for the important functions either). In combination with unsmooth camera controls it performs very poorly, I'm on a I7-4790k, GTX 760 4gb with 32gb ram and I cannot get over 30 fps with various settings, except for the first 5-10 minutes of battle. If you look on youtube, there isn't a single video of this game with good performance either. The sound engine doesn't feel directional or realistic at all, you can barely tell where sounds are coming from. If you zoom all the way out, most things sound as if they were happening right next to you, not far away. The use of extremely complex symbols for tiles -that have no tooltips, text or any other way of finding their actual meaning. These are crucial because they tell the statistics of tiles to place your troops, you have to memorize them or you will not be able to play the game effectively, and they are not easy to memorize at all. As a comparison, I've memorized the entire nato counter symbology and that made much more sense and was much easier. The mode of the game where you are not in battle, but in the wargame-style tactical map was also pretty confusing, it has an excellent tutorial that covers all of the functions, color coding and symbols for that, but I still came to completely dislike the entire design and flow of the game. The UI is ♥♥♥♥ing huge, you have to scroll through pages or so of unit information that could easily be smaller and your entire army could fit on the screen. Instead, you can't even fit a whole company of your units in the order of battle because just the button that has the name of the company is  1/5 the size of your entire screen.
Hearts of Iron, War in the East, Advanced Tactics Gold, Men of War, Theatre of War, anything is better than this. In my opinion this game is a waste of money, it is unenjoyable and I doubt I will play it again. I'm not sure how this game got so many good reviews, but I at very least recommend getting Operation Star instead of Mius-Front. When I first got this game 2 months ago, I gave up after 2 hours as I thought it was very boring and mediocre. However once I was bored I decided to boot it up again and try once more, and boi was I happy.
The Reason why is because, as the game progresses and the story starts building up, it starts getting very interesting. I'm not going to spoil anything but I will say it's very, very thought provoking, however only if you get invested in the story. For example, there are some multiple choice decisions that really makes you think, makes you feel sad and are really thought provoking, however it dosnt change the outcome of the game, but if you ignore that though and immerse yourself, it really just  works, I recall thinking about one decision well after I had stopped playing. There are also some notes that you read on computers that explains some things that are otherwise mysterious.
Other than the story, the game is actually quite atmospheric and scary without having to rely on jumpscares, sometimes. I can remember some points in the game where you are being chased, and boi is it heart-racing! Besides the point, minor spolier here about the enemies, no story spoliers though.
However, the game is very cliche in some points, we've seen it a milion times, you go into a map with lots of corridors, have to get to point A from point B, with a monster trying to hunt you down. But if you dont mind this, then it's fine.
The game is also visually stunning! The games artstyle works well for creating an atmosphere, with good optimization this game looks fantastic while being a smooth 60fps.
Voice acting is a big thing in story driven games, and i'm happy to say this game's voice acting is absolutely brilliant, Simon, the main character is very good in communicating his moods and thoughts in well written dialogues. Catherine, the supportive role, is also extremely good, and the two characters play off of one-another. Making for some really interesting conversations between them.
Overall, this game is absolutely a must buy!

1. What is "Pyre"?
The game "Pyre" was made by Supergiant Games and was released on the 25th of July in 2017. After "Bastion" and "Transistor" this is their third game. "Pyre" is an indie-action-rpg, which story is mostly told in form of a novel. The gameplay is very different to the experience you probably made in "Bastion/Transistor", which lead a few people to put a negative review on steam. Now you will no longer play as one single character like before, but you are responsible for a group of exiles. The gameplay at it´s heart can be declared as 3 parts:

part 1 contains travelling/exploring the world
part 2 contains social interactivity with your group (talking/trading/decision-making)
part 3 contains to take part in the rites, that means a fast-paced action ball game (3 vs 3) without        a planning phase (like in "Transistor")
2. Technical details
-the game runs fine on my windows 10 64 bit machine and it needs about 8.2 gb space of your hard drive. Unfortunately the game runs bad on old machines, because you need about 4 gb ram to run it without an error (my other 3 gb ddr2-system couldn´t run it, I received a ram-error-message when starting the game).
-controls with mouse+keyboard or gamepad are good and well implemented.
3. What does the game right?
-great rpg-novel-mixture as a whole unique and emotional experience
-despite the linear progression (mentioned "phases/parts" above) the game stays interesting enough to continue
-a colourful and fantastic world to explore (no open-world)
-great character-design and a good variety of different creatures, which affects the gameplay during the rites
-beautiful artstyle with a lot of detail and smooth animations
-believable and fleshed-out storyline (NOT "black and white") with a personalised ending!
-wonderful soundtrack (mostly ambient)
-the creatures of the world speak their own language, subtitle is displayed in old-fashioned English
-rites: the thrilling-faced-paced-action-game has a lot of depth to it (skill tree/character selection/items/area of the rite)
-selectable difficulty level (rites can be optionally restartet), which can be changed during the game (+ "titan-mode": advanced challenges you can add separately like in "Bastion/Transistor")
-meaningful and emotional decisions to be made (I´m looking at you mass effect), thankfully there are no dead-ends but different endings (personalised!)
-"Pyre" is "2-3 times" longer compared to "Bastion"/"Transistor" without getting boring
-good mouse+keyboard and gamepad support
-"versus-mode": you can play against friends together on your pc or alone against CPU (with all the characters in the game!)
4. What does the game wrong?
-the fast-paced-gameplay during the rites can be very fast and too stressful at times (I experienced some unfair situations here and there)
-controls are sometimes not precise enough, especially when the gameplay is getting hot
-hardware requirements (like "Transistor") with 4 gb ddr-ram are over the top regarding old rigs with dual-core cpu´s
-some minor bugs during the rites (ball gets stuck, switching between characters over distance, bad camera angles over distance)
-"versus mode" can only be played as local multiplayer
-no bonus material for fans at all
5. tl;dr
Pyre offers a fantastic but linear action-rpg-experience with a great story, which is told in form of a novel with a personalised ending. The gameplay is a mixture of exploration, social interactivity and a 3 vs 3 ball-sports-game. The level of creativity considering world-building, character design, music and the way the story is being told is on an insanely high level. If you liked "Bastion" and "Transistor" you need to know that you don´t play just as one character anymore. But what you can expect is a game with a heart, just like their games before. Pyre is in my opinion a masterpiece and the best Supergiant game so far.
6. Final thoughts
As a child of the 80´s I played a lot of pc games. Sometimes I look back and remember how I bought game boxes from a company called "Lucas Arts". There were times I didn´t even inform myself about the upcoming games, I just bought them because I loved their games I purchased before. For me Supergiant reached that status in the present time.
Until the stars align!

I'm a big fan of SG's other games, in terms of gameplay, story, and overall aesthetic. Pyre is a strong new entry from a solid indie studio and one of my favorite games of the year. The scenery and character design is gorgeous, the voice acting in its own language subtly adds to the world building, the soundtrack is beautiful and very unique, and the gameplay and writing is also excellent. While the gameplay can sometimes get tedious while you alternate between lots of dialogue (although I am a visual novel and literature fan so I don't mind reading lots of text) and the sports/combat aspect (the Rites), the character and world building makes up for it as you and your fellow exiles grow on the journey together. I loved nearly every second of the 12 hours I spent in my first playthrough, and the incredibly well-written characters (Hedwyn and Tariq being my favorites) and unique gameplay brought the world and the Rites to life for me. There are choices to make - I'm interested to give it another playthrough in a couple months or so to do some things differently because I will admit part of the ending did not go how I expected it to and undermined my own strategy - that affect the gameplay and create different outcomes with different characters. I highly recommend this game and the incredible soundtrack! Also Jodariel is mom.

Rayman has always been a fun franchise.  Legends is no exception.  Quick, fast-paced gameplay keeps you engaged while a great soundtrack provides a suitably energetic backdrop for  the polished graphics.  To clarify, what I'm talking about is, if you've ever heard the phrase "polished to a mirror finish" only they started with mirrors and polished THOSE to a mirror finish.  The graphics on this game are less graphics and more just plain art.  The game is teeming with environments and characters that are vibrant and full of humor while some rotating challenges give you reason to pick up the game even after not playing for a while.  Between the slick platforming that smartly straddles the line between fun and annoying and the zany characters, you could theoretically get a good number of hours out of this.
It's a shame that none of that matters.  Rayman isn't tarnished by some small issue, it's not marred by some defect, it's truly maimed, defenestrated then lit on fire and run-over by a garbage truck named Uplay.
If you're unfamiliar with Uplay, I want you to imagine something which is both uninteresting and yet rage-inducing.  A program which is supposed to launch other programs but magically doesn't when you want it to.  Imagine something which takes up disk space, memory and wants to start at startup just like a real program but isn't useful.  A program which, and I don't want to cause you to panic, makes EA Origin look like a decent launcher.
If you're having a good time imagining that, you should call Ubisoft HR because I bet they'd love to have you working for them.  Then again, if you're on Steam, you might not be "out of touch with the gaming community as a whole" which is apparently a job requirement for working there.

A refreshing (although clearly unfinished) work which really emphasizes the value of cover (trees, walls and anything else which will stop a bullet) and concealment (bushes and anything that keeps you from being spotted), movement and teamwork. The bonuses for being near a friendly player who makes a kill and benefiting from his kill when you have done some damage to the same target are good.
Weather and environmental effects such as sunlight, radioactive areas and areas with poisonous gases make for some unusual barriers as well as an interesting influence on play style. You learn quickly for example, that it is better to shoot out of the sun than into it, higher up is better but not always best and you cannot run through contaminated areas without the proper equipment and survive.
The fact that you can spawn just about anywhere at the later stages of a round keep the spawn campers to a minimum but there is still a lot of spawn killing.
Since it is a beta version I assume that the complete lack of penalties for team killing will be added once they decide what is appropriate. The crazies take advantage of this fact sometimes and can really ruin a match if not dealt with.
That was my 2 cents worth ;)

*EDITED REVIEW*
I have much to say about how this game has turned out, but I will try my best to summarize my experiences.
This game is getting progressively worse each patch. It's early access, I know, but you'd expect at least some level of thought to be put into each patch. Often times patches are released with gamebreaking bugs or poorly thought out mechanics that could have easily been avoided with a bit of common sense. For example, a patch currently came out that introduced baby dinosaurs. Sounds great right? Nope.
-You spawn at the edge of the map as a slow baby, no food or water nerby and no chance of reaching anything before dying, and you aren't fast enough to suicide off of a mountain+ the amount of fall damage taken is the same as for the adult version of the dinosaur you're playing so even if you do find a mountain it probably won't kill you. How could this easily be fixed? Give baby dinosaurs the custom spawn points of psittacosaurus. It would take no time at all.
-Baby dinosaurs do the same amount of damage as the adults. So for example, a hatchling acrocanthosaurus would inflict 20 bleed on anything it could bite, which is basically instant death. How could this be fixed? You literally type in the damage values for every baby.
-You begin as a starter tier hatchling, then progress to the adult of that hatchling. Once you progress to the adult version, you progress to the next dinosaur you want to be and start out as a hatchling again making you extremely vulnerable as if you hadn't been progressing at all the entire time. This entire process can take hours and is not in any way engaging gameplay.
-When you relog in the server as a hatchling, you are set to the maximum growth of that hatchling.
-Plants were said to be fixed, but aren't. Meaning herbivores can't progress or survive.
-All of this was implemented without nesting even being in the game yet.
This is merely one example of poorly thought out patches.
[Deleted section about dev behavior]
The current progression system is utterly idiotic. The devs love to brag about how people don't like progression because it's "hardcore." In which case, their idea of hardcore must be killing or scavenging something and then sitting in a bush for literal hours on end waiting to progress. Progression requires absolutely no skill whatsoever and is painstakingly boring. Ironically, it used to be better in the first iterations where you actually had to kill things. Corpses didn't last as long because their food values were much lower, and a single austro or herrera could only get 2 or 3 bites out of a corpse before it disappeared.
To sum it up, right now the game feels like random stuff is being thrown into it with no thought at all. No EA game releases patches that are so buggy and poorly thought out, or treats community members with this level of disrespect.

BeamNG.drive turned out to be a stellar gem of a vehicle sandbox game and a respected work by the BeamNG team as it matched my expectations if not excelling them. I primarily purchased BeamNG.drive while in the process of looking for a driving game that focused more on realism and physics. After all, vehicles are complicated objects and it's quite an understatement to say it's difficult to make them feel and act realisticly within virtual enviroments given all their various factors. Ranging from mass, weight-balance, friction, handling, velocity simulation, body-physics, momentum and more. Nonetheless, the BeamNG team aced it. I hope that the developers commitment and dedication to this game continues until it's a masterpiece. I've been playing this since 9 Dec, 2014 and will have an amazing time playing this game for the unforeseeable future.
I'd presume most people believe BeamNG.drive isn't a racing game and more of a crashing simulator. However, after a few hours of sheer entertainment it became evident that it's utter brilliant for racing and has such a huge amount of potential for greatness. It's a fun game to play for thirty minutes or for hours upon hours. Even more so if you're using a wheel, stick shift and pedals. It uses the open source game engine Torque3D by GarageGames and currently has several maps, a few short campaigns, a lot of scenarios, some time trials and a freeroam mode. It has lots of vehicles and each single vehicle can be modified and tuned. Content such as this is added to the game quite often. You can also at any time effortlessly switch between the game and the game/map editor by simply pressing [F11]. The enviroments and graphics are stunning. There's an amazing and thriving modding community that pumps out a ton of incredible vehicles, maps and mods. I'd love to have the Steam Workshop implemented but in due time I presume.
I rarely recommend games that are still within their early access stages. However, BeamNG.drive is one of those rare exceptions as it's one of the few Steam paragons. In essence, I highly recommend this game to everyone. Especially those who enjoy car racing and to anyone who has ever pondered or contemplated about vehicle physics or crashes.
Posting your own experiences with BeamNG.drive whether good or bad assists potential newcomers in making their decision to purchase the game or not.

I backed this game on kickstarted a couple days after it was started. I spent the 50 dollars to buy my copy of the game as well as the savini skin and the counselor clothing packs. here is a nice handy list of pros and cons i can personally think of in the game
Pros:
-Outstanding movie quality visuals.
-Accurate portrayal of the villan in 7 different versions of the character.
Cons:
-The perk system is broken, iv lost something like 3000 CP because of their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ choice of RNG on the perk "roller" that results in either a really bad perk being rolled turning 500 CP into 100, or if you are lucky, 500 CP into 200, you wont want to buy any counseler perks until your jason is maxed out but you play counselor's 95% of the time so you pretty much have to buy these 500 CP a pop slot machine roles just to get any sort of a chance at winning.
-Jason is overpowered beyond the point of it, his skills start off slow, this forces counselors to do most of the important stuff early in the game when they have a chance of escape.but about 5 minutes in he gets his 4th skill and all of a sudden his twin teleports and sense both come up every couple of seconds. so if he catches sight of you, you have a very slim chance of getting away, he will just keep coming unless you get super lucky or if something distracts jason's attention like the car or phone, and once Jason grabs you, unless you have a pocket knife which there are about 3 or 4 total on the whole map between up to 8 councelors, once he grabs you his insta kill animations come into play, usually he will immediately be able to put you in a kill move, the game states that a high composure helps with breaking free of his grab, yet even with a composure of 10/10 you still cant get out of his grab in time to dodge the kill move. so it comes down to you getting extremely lucky and having his kill moves blocked for the 3 or 4 seconds you need to break free, or you need a pocket knife, option 1 rarely ever happens.
-Jason's animations are broken, so this is a couple of different points in itself, first of all his shift animation is broken so when he breaks shift with either an attack or grab the attack or grab goes off about a second or two before his model reappears on your screen, resulting in basically a garenteed grab or attack every time, next we have his morph being broken in that if he teleports near you, you cant see him on your screen or minimap for about 3 or 4 seconds after the morph is complete, this usually happens once every two games or so. Then we have the plethora of bugs caused when jason tries to pull a counselor out of something while the counselor is trying to do something at the same time. these of course rarely happen but they happen.
-the game is stingy with items, this game has something like 100 drawers to open around the whole map, with about 30 of these actually having something in them, from what i can tell, there are 1-2 sets of keys, 1 fuse, 4-5 of each, firecracker, pocket knife, map, walkie talkie, first aid spray. The rest are empty, iv opened 15 drawers in a row and not found a single item, and this is common for multiple players to have happen to them in one game, Honestly there could be twice as many of each item on the map and it would make the game a whole lot more fun. this would put less emphasis on jason spamming insta kill grabs and more on actually landing hits with throwing knifes and auto attacks,
-years of waiting and millions of dollars and it doesnt feel like it was used wisely, the visuals may be good but the gameplay behind them is pretty lacking, i dont really want to play the game knowing im going to get screwed 8 out of 10 games i play, im only going to get to play jason once every 20 matches or so, and even if i win im going to get basically no CP. my last 5 matches have been 3 loses then 2 wins, iv gotten the same amount of CP from all 5 of them it seems and the game doesnt tell you how much CP you are getting or from what sources, you just have to hope your CP goes up a good amount, but unless you are buying a jason kill move you are more than likely taking a huge dump on your CP and then lighting it aflame.
-For all this time and money, the game release was pretty shoddy, and as far as new games go, it might as well be early access, and until the afore mentioned bugs get fixed and the game gets a little more balanced. I wont be recommending it to anyone, i can barely bring myself to play it let alone recommend it.

I love this game...'s story. (Scroll down for TL:DR)
Pros: This game's story is absolutely breathtaking. From the amount of detail in most characters to how certain areas are framed to emphasize the story even if just through mechanics. The visuals are very well done, and the world itself is nearly fully explorable with little in the way of invisible/illogical barriers.
It's a great piece on what makes us human with a world that presents a challenge to our initial bias.
Cons: Though the visuals are GOOD, they aren't optimized very well. Occasional FPS drops here and there. The gameplay itself...is honestly lacking. There were no enemies in the game that truly frightened me. Some I laughed at because of how easy they were to walk around, while others annoyed me with how cheap they felt.
On the subject of non-frightening things...this game is NOT scary. The only reason I bring that up, is because it was MARKETED as a horror game; and it isn't. It REALLY isn't. There are cheap jumpscares, and sometimes good semi-creepy atmosphere, but nowhere in the game was I actually scared (even while using the mindset of WANTING to be scared).
Also, while I LOVED the story, I felt the ending was just kinda tacked on there to prevent us leaving the game feeling depressed. The ending as it fades, to me, is perfectly done. It leaves the player,
, to reflect on what it all means, and what they have done.
All in all, the TL:DR version is this:
SOMA is a great story-driven psychological "thriller" with twists and turns, but if you're looking for a great horror GAME, play something else

I'm a big fan of wargames; I grew up playing Combat Mission, really enjoy GMT board games, Paradox's strategy games, so it's not like i'm coming into this expecting Starcraft or Company of Heroes. Those are both great games but not the same genre, and I get that.
But if I've put a good 5 hours into playing tutorials and attempting to get a handle on the gameplay mechanics and still totally fail, well that's when I put the game down for a time, maybe forever.
The interface and user feedback is just a mess overall, and even when I found something I didn't understand and looked in the manual to try and figure it out, for example the command points system, there was a one sentance description that did nothing to clarify how it worked.
A multititude of vague icons and colors will indicate status' on units, but there's no way inside the game to find out what they mean if you don't already know. Would it really be that hard to have some nice tooltips on things? Even when tooltips are present they are often unhelpful or even more confusing.
And I dare someone to try and find uglier menu graphics in a game that otherwise looks this pretty. Or to try and understand the after action report screen. (5/200% of what??)
This is all aside from other things i've seen that could either be a bugs in the combat engine/AI or interface and readabilty issues:
I've had tanks with no apparent damage, morale, or ammo issues, refuse to fire at enemy tanks a stone's throw away.
Infantry carrying AT grenades run up to enemy armor then just stop and lay prone, or slowly crawl away, while the armor resolutely ignores them.
Halftracks circling each other literally a couple feet apart, one unshooting, the other taking no damage whatsoever, for about 5-6 minutes.
Infantry often seem to ignore heavy MG fire, and will jog straight up through an open field under heavy fire and murder the crew, with little or no damage.
Some or all of these could be bugs or things I missed in the interface that the game was trying to tell me about, I just have no idea.
Good complex games don't have to have bad interaces and tutorials. Crusader Kings 2 or Unity of Command are great examples of complicated games that are relatively easy to learn thanks to good tutorials, and give you all the needed information in game once you're there.
If you're really interested in this, at least watch a few long videos, or wait to see if they come out with some patches. I really hope they can improve things, because I can see the potential here, it's just not in a state I could recommened at the moment.

I recommend this game with some caveats.
If you don't think you'd like a party-based visual novel with branching story choices where the only gameplay mechanic is fantasy basketball, then I'm not sure this game is for you. Just understand that what I described is done *really* well.
Art is beautiful. Music is amazing. Voice acting is engaging as hell. Writing is tremendous. Fantasy Basketball is a little simple but ends up quite fun as you get new characters with varied abilities.

I have always loved the Graviteam games. I have all of the previous ones. I was very excited about this game because it's been in development for so long and promised so many new and wonderful things.
I'm dissappointed.
This is basically a map pack. And not a very good one at that. They dressed up the UI a bit and tweaked a few things, but really, if you've played the others, you've played this one.
The Maps: Large stretches of land that are mostly flat with some rolling hills. The towns are just different arrangements of the same towns you saw in the previous games. There's not much strategy involved with such bland maps. If you have AT guns just pick a hill and they'll pick off the piecemeal attacks the AI sends your way.
The Graphics: I guess they were upgraded, but I don't see it. It's that weird kind of upgrade that some games try that actually makes things look worse.
The AI: I'd love to see some sort of fight being put up, but haven't yet. It's a drizzle of a tank or two, a squad or two, but nothing challenging. Not like the mass human waves you saw in Shilovo. It's like the enemy is content just probing, continuously.
The Environment: Please for the love of God give me the winter back. I have no idea what environment they were trying to create here. It's dark and gloomy with the sun shining in the background. It's dingy brown with fresh spring grass growing. It's confused.
The Campaign: Make a flat boring map, a generic arrangment of houses and dirt roads, and add in three times as many units for both sides. Voila! You have Mius Front.
The Bugs: Still there from the previous games. See a tank, see a tank disappear, see a tank appear, see a tank disappear. Hit a tank, wait ten seconds, hear tank get hit, wait ten seconds, see tank lose track. Fun.
Play the older games, this is garbage.

SOMA is a first person horror/adventure games from the creators of the acclaimed Amnesia franchise. It takes place in a mysterious underwater research structure where something has clearly gone horribly wrong.
+Amazing story. I don't think I've ever played a horror game where the plot is so relevant and poses such amazing questions to the player. I can't really say much about this for the sake of keeping this review spoiler-free, but trust me when I say that it's a really, REALLY breathtaking experience.
+Atmosphere. Even when you're relatively safe, the ominous depths of the oceans, the claustrophobic corridors of the underwater station you're in and the creepy background noises will keep you anxious. This game does a great job at being scary even when there is probably no real threat at that given point. Plus, the whole location is really frightening and... alien (no foreshadowing intended).
+The actual horror. This is the least scary Frictional game so far (though that's highly debatable in my opinion), but that doesn't mean it'll go easy on you. Apart from the terrorizing and oppressive atmosphere, you will find a good amount of monsters and other threats that will make you jump from your chair or cry in horror.
+Graphics. They're not top notch per se, but lightning and post-processing do an awesome job at increasing the game's immersion and haunting beauty.
-Padding. Sometimes I just felt bored by the overly long fetch-quests or complicated puzzles the game tasked me with. Ok, the puzzles are not that hard. I just suck at puzzles. Yet, there are moments in the game i felt would have a bigger impact if they were shorter. This game has a decent length (about 10 hours with some much needed exploration), but I feel shortening some sections would have been better.
-Exploration vs. monsters. This game has a truly astonishing lore, which deserves to be fully explored. There are lots and lots of text, audio and documents scattered around the maps, but it's quite hard to read them carefully when a freaking monster is shambling next to you. No wonder one of the highest rated mods on the Workshop is a "pacifist" mod that renders all enemies peaceful (although they will still react to noise and follow you, creeping the crap out of you). I suggest you play the game the intended way, then play it again with that mod activated, in order to have an easier time fully understanding the background.
-Lag. A truckload of lag, mostly because (i don't know if it's my system, but having an i7 4770k @3.50 GHz, a GTX 970 gpu and 16 GB of RAM, it's safe to say it's probably not) the game struggles to load new areas. Egregious examples are the transitions from open waters to the inside of the facility, but there are other occasions as well. It's not game breaking, but it's there and it's annoying.
You liked previous games by Frictional? Buy this, personally I think it's their masterpiece. You like horror games? This will give you the scares you want. You like a good plot? This one's amazing, buy this freaking game right now. The only reasons not to buy SOMA are a)you're more of an action game guy or b)you don't like scary games. That's basically it. BUY IT DAMMIT!

I really want to love this game, as Bastion and Transistor are two of my favorite games, but I don't think Pyre will live up to their greatness. First of all, props to Supergiant for creating such a unique world and backstory; the art is very beautiful and stylized, the characters are diverse, but something just seems lacking. Although I love the world that Pyre takes place in, there is wayyyy too much dialogue compared to actual gameplay. This is very different to both Bastion and Transistor where the story is weaved into the gameplay. With Pyre, it feels as if the gameplay is weaved into the story. While I love a good story, they did not focus enough on making the gameplay fleshed out. Bastion and Transistor kept things fresh by giving the player new weapons as the story progressed, vastly changing how you would play the game. As for Pyre, while there are different characters which each have different playstyles, the upgrade paths feel underwhelming (Talismans and Masteries). This makes the gameplay feel stale after a few hours. I think that the combat system is very creative and a good idea, but there is not enough depth to it (and IMO an odd default control setting for M+KB).
I don't think that Pyre is necessarily a bad game, but it's hard to reccomend with so much dialogue, lack of depth in the only gameplay mechanic, and living up to Bastion and Transistor. If you've never played Bastion or Transistor, I'd reccomend picking those up instead and passing on Pyre unless you really love dialogue based games that reveal themselves to you as you progress and would rather have gameplay be a non-major element.
