I love survival games, and this one had me excited. This game has potential, but they HAVE to fix some silly issues that don't make any sense.  Perhaps I'm a little picky as a game dev myself, but the FTUE (First time user experience) for me is lacking.
My consolation is that I purchased it during summer sale, so I don't have too much remorse.
****Here are my pros:
-Art is fine, style seems seems to fit the mood.  I like the retro feel and 2d layout.  A little inconsistent from screen to screen (Loading screen text actually has two different resolutions, and the in-map pixel resolution is far better than in-game; this looks sloppy and breaks the style.)
-I like the 'family of four' idea.  Not many games include children as players in such a bleak scenario, but it makes it interesting.
-Character customization is cool, although I wish I could distribute skill point myself rather than just sticking to presets.
-Crafting is always fun; I like deciding what inventory items I need from an expedition.
****Cons:
- Devs must hire a UI/UX guy , and consider an overhaul.  So many issues that seem obvious really dampen the experience.  Example:
> When full screen at 1920x1080, the character portait/UI completely covers the ladder and hatch into the bunker...which happens to be the ONLY way in and out.  So annoying.  Good luck selecting the character if they wander behind the UI panel.
> Character selection is spotty and a pain.  I constantly have to check the upper left panel to see if the correct character is chosen.  I should know if Ive selected my character just by looking at him, perhaps w some UI marker.  Can't tell you how many times I've told the wrong character to do something because my click didn't take.
> If one character is scanning frequencies on the radio, and has a circle marker indicating thirst, hunger, etc above his head, it completely obscures the incoming transmission icon!  I actually have to move the listening character out of the way to access the transmission icon.  Oi vey.
> That robot 'auto' icon is huge and so distracting.
- Why, oh WHY does my expedition party need my approval to check out a location I already selected for them on the map? If I select FARM on the map, then I obviously I want them to check the Farm for resources.   The party will bypass the location otherwise?  That's silly.  This feels like the devs are forcing unnecessary clicks just to keep the player multitasking, when it makes zero sense in-world.  The only time this might make sense is if they encounter some potential danger preventing access to the location, in which case you may want to avoid an encounter that might injure the character.  Oh, and how does the expeditionary party have a radio to check in anyway?
- Inventory space is precious, I get it.  But to have a book of matches take up as many slots as 3 stacked bags of cement is simply ridiculous.
- Arbitrary and silly requirements for crafting.  In the wiki and website, one of the first steps recommended is to upgrade the workbench to level2.  Except you can't because it requires SEVEN hinges (?) and SEVEN rope to upgrade my workbench to level 2, and I start with zero.  I'm lucky if I find 1 hinge after exploring 4 or 5 locations, since loot seems to be random.  Seven hinges...really?  What am I crafting, an apothecary chest for Pottery Barn?  What table needs 7 lengths of rope?
- Toys and books can ONLY be stored in toy chests and book shelves?  Really?  Because storing those items in the cardboard box w everything else is a big survival no-no.  Again, an arbitrary rule that make no sense, to justify the player having to gather a bunch of crap to build.
- One character failed to shower for four days and was throwing up from food poisoning.  Really?   Showers when surviving after the apocalypse should be a luxury, not a requirement.  People lived just fine w/o indoor plumbing for hundreds of years, and I'm sure they weren't all barfing in the streets everyday.  Also, do I need to use that much water to clean my hands, which is what matters?  Let's be reasonable.  Otherwise, it feels like a silly burden forced on the player which doesn't make sense.
- Why do I need a hazmat suit to go fix the vent above, but my character on expedition is fine w only a gasmask?  And why is a gasmask only good for one trip, regardless of the amount of locations you visit?  Again, an arbitrary limitation invented to keep the players making stuff, which don't make sense, and is frustrating.
I can go on and on.
I *really* want to enjoy this game, but all the little things add up.  While I don't recommend it right NOW, I  DO hope people keep watching it to see what it becomes.  I'm not sure why the reviews are so positive with so many distracting errors; I feel it gives the devs the wrong idea when the game needs improvement.  Good luck, I hope to see some updates!

The level designs have greatly improved since Rayman Origins. You now have the help of Murfy the Greenbottle guy.
So in this game you have a ranking whatever you played offline or not. Each world and each levels have their own cups and each cup give you points to level up your rank. You can get copper, silver, gold and also platinum cup. Also you earn cup doing online challenges, depending of your ranking at the end of each challenge.
In this Rayman, you get some brand new worlds, levels, bosses and also a "karaoke" mode. The online challenge is pretty new too.
So depending of the amount of lums you got at the end of a level, you get a cup. Also you need to save the teensies, all if you can. When you are good enough you unlock lucky tickets that may reward you with a random gift such as : a creature, lums, a teensy or a level of "Rayman Origins".
You'll also unlock time trials levels, where you need to rush to the teensies before the evil foes launch them with rockets.
At the end of each world you'll have a boss level fight and after that a "karaoke" level. The karaoke level, feature a music with "voices" if we call that voices, where you need to rush continuously until you reach the end. One of it great aspect is that the rhythm of the music and voices are linked to your moves.
"Back to Origins" world and levels are the replica of the original Rayman Origins levels. Only several levels are missing. In this one you'll find normal levels, shooting levels with the mosquito, rushing levels with the moving chest, and last levels with a boss at the end.
Finally the online challenges will be required in order to have all achievements and it will take time until you reach the needed rank. Hopefully you can earn a lot of cups in a week and a lot of points if you're good enough. (16 cups each week)

A lot of attention & detail has went in to the audial end of this game, From the environment hearing the wind whistle in your ears to the blades of grass colliding with each other to the sounds of the foot steps when people walk to the weapons firing. You will be able to hear every footstep & gunshot every little detail in stunning beautiful deafening glory. The weapon sounds are especially great! they really pack a punch!
Survariums post-apocalyptic atmosphere leaves absolutely nothing left to be desired, From its Abandoned cities & schools with over grown vegetation, To its Decaying waste lands, Ruined industrial sites & Its crumbling military bases, As mother nature begins to once again take over & rule with anomalies expanding across the planet with terrifying speed. There is so much beauty in this game. This game has a erie, creepy feel to it as well with its enemy AI in the form of mutants and environmental hazards such as anomalies.
The game is very solid it feels very realistic, From your player moving sluggish from having to much armor on or carrying heavy weaponry, To the penalty of not having enough armor on to protect you. The inventory system is very well thought out having to plan ahead for certain situations due to your player only being able to carry so much, Only having 2 profile customizations really makes you think on what items would be best for close quarters or long range, Am I going to be carrying to much weight etc. The games main system is so well thought out it really makes you think & mix & match things up trying to find that perfect combo of weapons & armor & items without feeling like a 500 pound gorilla walking around.
The weapons in this game are superb, From the way that they sound to the way they handle its very realistic & weapons really pack a huge punch!. The iron sights took me awhile to get used to but once I got the hang of it I was doing pretty decent. I can't stress this enough the guns in this game really pack a serious punch, Bullets really hurt if you get hit by a 7.62 bullet in the head you're dead period end of story you're done man you can't shrug off bullets like you can in other games. Like I said before with the bullets, But with armor it allows you to survive certain types of aommunition hits & this causes bleeding, You can bleed from any number of body part, Head, Chest, Legs, Arms & you have to bandage that up. The recoil on the guns is fantastic & as real as you can get, Example of this is the AK74M or AKM that thing kicks like crazy the recoil is extremely realistic but handles just great. The Isle is great & has some amazing potential, the makings of a fantastic game are here already.
Remember that this is an Early Access game in an Alpha State (not feature complete & far from finished) this review is based on the current state of The Isle and any future features mentioned are subject to change depending on balance/developer changes over time.
Thank you for taking the time to read this, and since you are, you are most likely trying to determine if The Isle is a game you'll enjoy, on this list of reviews you will see many examples of barely literate raging people who do not understand what an Early Access game is or how massively it can change as the developers progress towards the end goal, their completed vision for their game.
The finished product will be an open world, survival game that is designed to be difficult.
Like nature in reality, The Isle is a cruel place and those too weak or too stupid will not survive.
Currently only 2 of the planned 4 playable "factions" are in game - carnivorous and herbivorous dinosaurs.
You start at the bottom of the food chain and as your small herbivore or carnivore you must survive long enough to progress to the next tier of animal, becoming larger and more capable as you do.
To succeed you must play to the strengths of your chosen dinosaur, carnivores must hunt prey that is the right size, flee from fights you cannot win, track footprints through the woods to find your quarry, position yourself for ambush and stay quiet until its time to strike
Herbivores must be ever vigilant for danger, group up as there is strength in numbers, move carefully to not fall into an ambush, migrate for food or safer water sources and not run around making noise for no reason.
The best The Isle has to offer is the thrill of the hunt!  As the swift Carnotaurus chasing down your prey as it attempts to evade you or as a lone Stegosaurus fighting off a pack of hungry Allosaurus through a dense woodland valley, desperate for the kill. If this sounds interesting to you, you may find it hard to pull yourself away from The Isle once it has its claws in you.
This game is not fair, and it never will be.  This game is not easy, and it never will be.
You will make a mistake. You will die.  You will start from the bottom & rise again.  There are consequences to your actions.  Risk VS Reward.  Life and death.
Thank you again for reading, if you are planning to purchase please READ the store page in FULL, make sure your computer meets the system requirements, update Windows & your drivers.

I bought this game for the awsome crashes.
I stayed because it offers So. Much. More.
Obviously, the soft body physics of the cars in the game are what make this game stand out from the rest, and is likely why you heard of this game. I know such becaus eit is how I came along this game in the first place. And this mechanic is really, really fun to mess around with, pushing the collisions to the max that the game, or even your PC can handle. And combined with an up to 100x slow mo, it becomes really satisfying to see the parts bend, shred and rip appart from the vehicle. On top of that, it's a car driving simulator, which means that the driving is also intended to be realistic. Not knowing how to drive myself, I cannot guarantee the realism, but many reviews here collectively claim so. This driving simulator really simulates everything about the car you drive in game, from the gears needing to be changed, to the engine being crushed as it was driven at 100 Mph into a concrete wall.
And yet, amasingly, this is not all that this game has to offer. With new missions by the developpers that range in difficulty, as well as a handful of detailed maps (with Uhta being the best in I believe general opinion) on which you can drive sensibely or not, this barely scratches the surface of content that this game has to offer. In fact, this game has a seemingly endless amount of additionnal content, free of charge, entirely thanks to a massive modding community who regurgitate a constant flow of new things to play with.
And these guys, well, they do EVERYTHING. Vehicles, objects, maps, car modifications, sounds, AI upgrades, flying planes, missions and so, so much more. This game may cost 23 euros right now, but this is 23 euros of limiteless content. And this is why I believe that this game is one that you should at least pick up to try if you are interested in the game. With this much free content at such a low price, it can bring so many hours of fun alone or with friends.
I may not have all that many hours on this game compared to others (about 50hrs at time of review), but it is enough to know if I will keep playing this game for many more or never again. And trust me, if you read this review in several months/years, and the number of hours I have on this game have not highly risen, I'm either dead, or held a gun point to never play this game again. And then I would be dead, because it's that good.

There comes a moment in every creatures mind when he questions the existence of itself. "Why I'm here?", "What's my purpose of existence?", "Is God real?" and, of course, "How do you do it?". The creature is, most often, in his early age when this event happens. He decides to ask the most valuable source of information, his parents. But, an almost irrational fear comes in, the shame. He realises that this is a taboo.
In our case, a rather she-creature is observed to behave in an expected way. Having provided items of joy, named as toy dolls, she grabs them and takes off the clothing right after she saw her mother leave. She realises, instinctively, that clothes need to be taken off in order to realise the fornication. But she lacks the rest of knowledge from the field of intimacy, just like a young spider lacks the knowledge of web creation, and she presumes that the fornication implies lots of hugs.
She moves her dolls in diverse, interesting ways, trying to mimic what could be considered as "amateur procreation". But, in a surprisingly short time of absence, her mother returns. The creature tries to hide the evidence while shame strikes again. Then her mother leaves again and the cycle of life and death, once again, continues.

Alpha Prime is generic and uninspired in every aspect.  Shooting, action, environments, sound design, voice acting, writing... all as plain and unmemorable as you can possibly get.  I used ridiculous-looking and wildly underpowered weapons to shoot the exact same "spaceman commando" character models inside of the same dark space station corridors over and over again.  I stopped occasionally for a couple of bigger set piece moments and once for an awkward, floaty jaunt across the planet's surface in a vehicle that is definitely NOT the Mako (wink wink).  I tried to kill people with grenades that don't actually kill people.  I fought a 2 minute boss battle that uses the same "shoot him until he gets into the thing to recover his health and then hack the machine to kill him" mechanic that I've seen a dozen times before.  I sat impatiently through long dialogues of contrived nonsense that did nothing but interrupt the flow of the game and left me more confused than before.  Not dreadful so much as thuddingly uninspired and incoherent.  Possibly worth a quick 5-6 hour playthrough if you can get it for a dollar or less but in this age of virtually unlimited gaming options for low prices, you're better off almost anywhere else.

I'd recommend if you have a number of friends who own it, for just some random mess around games until it gets it's own servers.

This game is EXCELLENT. If you like the sci-fi shooters such as Red Faction, Mass Effect, Dead Space, Lost Planet,... then you will enjoy this game! The only thing you should do is edit the settings config file to manually Enable V Sync. Because in-game options do not have v sync setting. Go to your install folder and edit settings.cfg. Find "vsync 0" and change it to "vsync 1". More info and original post by slimak:
The reason you should enable vsync is the exact same reason you should ALWAYS enable it in every game. Because you don't need your game to run at 5000fps, to run hot and use extreme amounts of electricity whilst generating large amounts of heat and GPU load. That's why you lock it down to 60 / 75fps or whatever your display's screen refresh is. Alpha Prime uses about 230 Watts to run on a high end gaming computer. The same game runs at only 160 Watts with exact same settings, graphics card fan is quiet and low heat after enabling vsync. Wattages meassured computer's power consumption at the wall socket during play. Enable vsync and enjoy this fantastic game.

I have always had a soft spot for 2D platformers and this is probably my favorite of the genre at the moment. It has got bright colorful graphics, great controls, interesting level design and it offers a good level of challenge without being unfair or frustrating, something Rayman Origins often missed the mark on.
The main part of game world is divided up into 5 different paintings, each with 9-10 levels based on different theme.  The paintings all end with a boss and a musical level, where the action in the level follows the background music. I loved the musical levels and I wish there were more of them. There is an extra unlockable painting that let’s you play the musical worlds again with added challenges, but it is basically the same level.
The game has tonnes of content with invaded levels, daily/weekly challenges, and you can unlock most of the levels from Rayman Origins. You certainly get your money’s worth here.

Pyre is one of the best stories I've ever experienced.
The world in the characters are incredibly vivid and colorful (both literally and figuratively), and the narrative devices the game uses are some of my favourites in a video game ever. This game, like Bastion, did a masterful job at finding and pulling my heart strings.
The art is also some of the best I've ever seen. I've never been a fan of comics or graphic novels, but something about the vivid imagery and subtle animations really got me over any qualms I might have had. I was
The music is great. Darren Korb is a little bit more traditional on this game than he was previously, with more of an emphasis on acoustic guitars and vocals.
The gameplay can be roughly split into two parts, one being a kind of text-heavy point and click adventure, and the other being something like a further demented Space Jam (basketball game). The former leverages the extensive investment in sound and art to put together a relatively effective traditional game, but the latter is entirely novel, and might rub some people the wrong way.

This game probably doesn't even need a review. You've probably already heard about how amazing this game is, so let me just reassure you... This game is awesome.
If you enjoyed games like Amnesia: Dark Descent, you are going to love this game as well. This has all the same mechanics: Run or die, Grab and pull, Explore and learn.
I would love to talk about the masterpiece of a story they've written here, but I don't want ruin anything for you. What I will say, is this game touches on a lot of tough subjects, and forces you into those situations. You both love, and hate being thrust into these decisions.
By the end of this game, I was both happy and sad that it was over. I can't usually play these horrors games, but this game is totally worth playing. My first playthrough took just over 13.5hrs. $30 is a steal for a AAA game like this. I look forward to doing another play through.... in a few months after I recover from the first time 'round.
There are quirks to this game where it's both good and bad. There's very little game music, which makes the atmosphere very ominous, but can also get pretty boring. When the music does come in, it scares the crap out of you.
Visually, this game is very well done. The graphics aren't super realistic, but real enough for you to be able to experience the immersion. The effects, and lighting are done just right. You can almost always see what you're doing, but it's dark enough to keep you nervous and jumpy. The creatures in this game are creepy, and definitely have you running away in fear.
Controls... This is a touchy topic for me. I play with mouse and keyboard. This game handles very well, although it did feel like the mouse sensitivity could have been better. Other than that, there's no real inventory to speak of, which is fine, but the style of inventory they used needs better explanation. I didn't know what it was until almost the very end of the game. Overall, the actual movements, and mechanics were great.
If I were to rate this game, I would give it a 9/10. This game amazing, and I don't hand out scores like that lightly. Everything from the story, right down to small opened tin cans with bits of food still in the bottom. This game is lovingly crafted, and it shows. Buy this game.

Hook is a relatively simple puzzle game requiring you to untangle a mess of rods by retracting them in the correct order. It starts out extremely simple and gradually introduces more mechanics in the progression of the game. They're actually somewhat interesting, but just as it starts getting fun the game abruptly ends after barely an hour of gameplay. There is very little replayability. Solving the individual levels is probably not as satisfying as it could be. More mechanics, more complicated levels, an endless mode or simply a target of minimum moves would go a long way in improving the game.
I really like the minimalist art style. The sounds are decent, though I deactivated them after 10 minutes via the Windows mixer. This hits on an annoying problem of the game: There are no in-game options. I had to read the steam forums to figure out that you could put the game into the (much more convenient) windowed mode via Alt+Enter. There is no GUI for quitting the game, just for (laboriously) cycling through the stages. This level of interaction I would expect from a tablet app, but not a PC game. At least I never encountered an error, bug or crash.
The positives barely outweigh the negatives and only do so given the minimal price. The idea and graphic design had potential, the gameplay implementation is lackluster and lazy. Buy this during a sale, if at all.

So now that I have over 600 hours in this game I feel I can write a review based on some pretty extensive experience.
Pros
-This game gives you a hardcore survival experience.  Where when you die you actually lose something specifically your time.
- The developers have done a great job of creating an environment that is very visually appealing as well as having great ambient sound to help with immersion.  It does still have some bugs, but what early access game doesn't.
- The Dinosaurs have been modeled very well from the models themselves to their movements, and the sounds.
- Dev's are very active with lots of updates.
Cons
- Dev team can be a bit harsh so if you are someone who feels entitled to have the game built your way then you will have some issues. (Personally this is a pro for me but for a lot it isn't)
- If you are someone who gets easily upset by having your progress reset which can include up to 5-6 hours or more.  Then this game is most definitely not for you.  You will be Killed on Sight (KOS'd) its part of the game, and it isn't against any rules to have it done to you.
- During different parts of the dev cycle they will add and remove different dino's or game modes so that things can be tested. This does not give you an excuse to write a bad steam review or post some trash in the discussions section about how you've been cheated.  Its an early access game and when you sign up for that you are going to test what the dev's need to be tested.

PROS:
+ A superb atmosphere that makes you feel the inner agony and tragedy of Jackie Estacado.
+ A very good storyline that will never make you bored or underwhelmed.
+ Your Darkness powers make you a major badass. Jumping in the middle of a group of enemies and tearing them apart limb by limb, gunning them down at the same time, and all in the span of just a few seconds, make you feel awesome! You are capable of literally giving hell to anyone who stands in your way.
+ Controls are quite easy and effective once you get the hang of it.
+ Graphics of the game has its own style and it really suits the atmosphere of the game.
+ The thing that affected me most: the voice-over for this game is OUT OF THIS WORLD. It has one of the best voice-over performances in the last few years. Just incredible.
+ There is not a single unnecessary power. All of them are effective.
CONS:
- Short. As in, 6 hours short. Thankfully, there is also a co-operative campaign which goes parallel to the main campaign, and that extends the gameplay to 9 hours. For people like me, who don't have many player friends, the co-op campaign can be played offline.
- Sometimes the fights may prove too dificult.
An excellent game all around. Only if it was a few hours longer, it would truly be awesome. As it is, I give it an 8.

Being a Hero’s of Might and Magic noob and quite pedantic (every hero must visit every shrine for every upgrade) the game played quite well, even after I read that you should rush the stages quickly to keep the next levels army size down (it’s refreshing to be punished for taking a stupid amount of time). The battles were fun, large affairs that took time and patience to win, but every battle felt rewarding, and there was a sense of achievement. I breezed through the first few races, then I come to the Sylvan (elf) quest line and I swear the game is broken. I swear there is no way to finish some of these missions. Units that should be able to be removed from a garrison can’t be after a certain level patch, which makes re-enforcing your home town impossible. The only way around is to have a running battle with weak sacrificial units and hope you do enough damage each turn to whittle them down before they hit your main town.  Other than that 1 glaringly painful part of the game, it was quite fun to play. Each race plays differently (they are all unique), and while you could make most hero’s semi similar with loadouts, they work well enough with their faction’s units that I didn’t feel a need.
I found the plot interesting and it contained enough twists and turns early on to keep me invested until I finished it. The characters dialogue is well written, and while some of the humor falls flat I found myself chuckling enough when it was trying to be humorous.
The two expansions also play very well, although I found some of the balancing made some races/units very over powered. I thought the overall difficulty increased with the 2 expansions (especially with the tribes of the east expansion). Having the different unit upgrade paths was interesting, and brought new options to the field. Be prepared to sink a lot of time into playing it (this isn’t something you can rush through- though I’m sure someone will prove me wrong in this). If you are a fan of turn based strategy games then I would recommend this. No achievements for this game (it must be one of the few that doesn’t have them).

This is definiately one of those games I enjoy playing a lot. As everybody knows I play mainly adventure, action-adventure games, so every single adventurous game is something I desire to play, a true delight for the adventorous soul!
The game is very smooth, beautifully crafted and interesting. It has a story driven by Apocalyptic War events, where Nazis try to take over and ocuppy everything on their way. This is a very common plot in single player gaming between the years of 2002 - 2008 and it's pretty much as classic as it gets.
You are a female agent, another thing I love a lot about the original single player 3rd person games - they used to introduce a lot of female main protagonists, like in Stolen, BloodRayne, Tomb Raider, Remember Me and more.
Another thing tight into the story of the game is that you're a female agent. If you've ever watched movies connected to WW2 you'd know that there were many female spies and agents sent to observe and report information from all the sources they find. This is pretty much your role in this game.
You're a silent skilled agent killer, who is sent to dispose of her enemies, and find out what they're up to.
I think this is a true masterpiece in the action-adventure genre, especially the stealth genre. Unfortunately very underrated. Every action-adventure gamer should complete this game!

This is a nice blend of an FPS shooter with an FPS sneaker and it's just dripping with atmosphere. Even the game menu is a 3D freeze frame panning around a scene of German soldiers bursting in on you while sniping. Oh, and you an get an x-ray view of shooting someone in the balls. Very satisfying.
The early levels do a very good job introducing you to the mechanics of the game. It starts with the basic controls in the usual way ("press C to crawl through this hole"), cover and shooting. Then it gets more subtle. Early on a tank is introduced in a cutscene and right in the middle of the shot is a bright red gas cap. It didn't dawn on me until later what the game was trying to tell me, "if you shoot red things, they will blow up". I enjoy this sort of more subtle hints at advanced tactics that give you the pieces and let you puzzle it out. A more blunt game would have a big flashing arrow pointing to the gas cap, "SHOOT HERE TO BLOW UP THE TANK!"
Which leads to the next great thing about the game, despite the levels being fairly linear, there's many ways to complete a mission. I didn't figure out how to blow up the tank, but I didn't need to. I avoided it (at one point I snuck right under the turret) and completed my objective. Want to play it as a stealth game? You can do that. A fast paced shooter? You can do that. A subtle assassination game? Each level is a little puzzle to be solved how you like it. I've spent a lot of time surveying the scene, the game will let you take your time.
I'm playing on Sniper Elite mode which removes aim assist. Gravity, wind, heart rate and position must be taken into account. This isn't as hard as it seems, you get used to estimating the range and using the mil marks on the scope. It changes the game from "put the crosshairs on the enemy and click" to something a bit more thoughtful. You don't feel like a super soldier. It's not a stand up fight. Every kill is important.
The enemies act intellegently. They will try to help injured comrades (and you can be a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and use them as bait), outflank you, and use suppressing fire on your last known position. It means you can't just sit in the same spot and blaze away, they will find you and they will overwhelm you.
The game has some serious stability problems. Initially it crashed trying to start a new game. Turning off Steam Overlay fixed that, but then it crashed regularly during an early mission so that I could not proceed. Using recommended settings from Raptr seem to have fixed it... for now. There's various semi-official suggestions on how to fix it, and a dedicated Steam support forum, but it's all very frustrating. If it works for you, great. If it doesn't, be sure to take advantage of the Steam Return Policy.

I have a lot to say about this game and its sequel but I'll try to make this as short yet thorough as I can. This is Doom. Doom is classic. Doom is eternal. With all the flashy, shiny FPS games out right now, sometimes it's nice to take a break and remember the days when aiming up and down weren't an option and your motivation for killing enemies derived from the mere fact that you're playing a video game and that's what you should be doing. And for being over 20 years old, Doom has aged surprisingly well. And I can say that with confidence because I didn't start playing this series until 2016. That should say something.
One of the reasons Doom has remained timeless is, in my opinion, its simplicity in design. You spawn in a map, collect keycards, and shoot everything standing in your way until you reach the exit. No forced story, no scripted sequences, just you and the map. This allows Doom to be something that I find most single player games are missing nowadays (for better or worse): a completely gameplay focused experience. In this case, it works heavily in Doom's favor. And the philosophy of gameplay first translates into the map and enemy design gracefully. Each weapon has its own unique purpose in a given situation, every enemy type offers different ways to fight them, and the map design itself is consistently excellent. Not every map is a winner, I'm looking at you E4M2, but so much of them are that the duds don't really impact the experience as a whole too much. And the gameplay itself feels surprisingly smooth. The shooting is tight, the weapons feel powerful and effective, the shotgun and plasma rifle in particular, and exploring the environment feels fun and rewarding. If there's one thing that hasn't aged well, it's the movement. Which brings me to my next point.
The main reason Doom has endured this long is the community. No other game I know of can sport as many dedicated modders or content creators as the classic Doom series. In terms of how this relates to the movement, the Steam edition of this game comes with Dos box. As such, your mouse contributes to your movement, making the game feel a little bit like you're on ice skates. But here's the kicker. You shouldn't play this game through Steam. You should still buy it,either here or on GoG, but a sourceport such as ZDoom, GZDoom or Zandronium will help your playing immensely, as well as adding new features such as an improved map and mouse look. And launching the game through ZDL, a free, easy to use Doom launcher, will allow you to quickly load Doom with whatever mods you have. Recommended ones to start with are Vanguard, Pirate Doom, Scythe, and of course Brutal Doom.
In conclusion, Doom is a timeless classic with an incredible community that will keep this game relevent for years to come. Its fantastic map design and core gameplay made it a revolutionsry experience when it came out in 1993, and make it an old-school treat in 2016. I cannot recommend this game enough.

In the brief time since FLOWER DESIGN was first released, it has blossomed into something rare. It is obvious that this DEV has a love for beauty (as well as desire to share it), and that love is what motivated him to embark on this project. But he also created something of beauty that encompasses game concepts (and even achievements now!)
When FLOWER DESIGN first launches, few components of flower arraigning are available. The player has a single pot, and very few flowers and accessory plants. The player can select a background, and the related lighting and shadows. At first, I considered that this might be a detriment for appealing to the more impatient of today’s gamers. To actually REQUIRE numerous finished arrangements to be “sold” into the game, to collect game currency in order to access more pots and plants? Would players be willing to wait, and work, to produce more elaborate arrangements, after starting off with possibilities so simple and basic?
But what the DEV has actually done is to give the arranger/player a valuable tool for understanding and appreciating this ancient art. A successful arrangement has nothing to do with the number of items, or the complexity of the finished project. While there may never be a “perfect” arrangement, an arrangement of a single flower, fern or leaf can as closely approach perfection as may an elaborate one, and that is the lesson this DEV very respectfully trusts the player to come to understand (if they don’t begin the game that way.)
Not only is the player required to start minimally (which places the focus on the positioning, color, size and contrast between each and all items), but as players collect currency from “selling” completed arrangements, each player must decide which is to be acquired next. A pot? A flower? An accessory plant? It’s rare to see a DEV take such a risk, and presume that players wish to not only experience a “game” such as this, but to “grow” as an arranger, as does the quantity of components they have access to within the game. For a DEV to create the means for a player to produce their own artistic growth, as they do the same within the game, is quite remarkable.
FLOWER DESIGN is something unusual, and in fact almost unique in computer gaming; something intended to create calm and peace, beauty and contentment. A game with no losing possible, and every attempt as a winning effort. I dare say that there will be those that may be like me; unable to create art or beauty in ANY form, that will find something creative in FLOWER DESGN that they have searched for throughout much of their lives. And for less than $2, I see no way to fail.
(DISCLOSURE: Since the release of this project the DEV has become a friend. I like to think that has nothing to do with my appreciation for his game, and in fact I acquired FLOWER DESIGN through purchase, the same as most players.)

I got this as part of some Humble Bundle, and at one point, I played it. And even though this game really suffers from an inherent lack of polish, I found myself really wanting to like this game. It bring some solid concepts forward to the table as a shooter, such as the hacking interface. It's sort of like Watchdogs as an FPS with this; scan security cameras to check enemy locations and numbers, set up environmental hazards up for remote detonated traps, and even use some of the machinery for surprise attacks. It has good ideas... BUT...
There's a lot wrong with this game. On a presentation scale, it's easily the worst part about the game. For a game released in '07, it looks like it comes from '02, and really doesn't have a lot of the aged visuals that can still look good in the modern day with games like, for instance, Unreal Tournament '99. The voice acting is atrociously bad, though it sounds more like bad localization and English dubs, and a lot of the sound quality is atrocious.
Gunplay is enjoyable, and some of the weapon designs like the gatling rifle and the sniper rifle are appealing, but the difficulty is extremely harsh, and the AI is pretty unforgiving. Even with patches to fix this, it still does put a damper on the gameplay as a whole.
So, I still do find myself really wanting to like this. It's a decently interesting package that does seem appealing, but suffers from some serious issues that drag it down hard. There are definitely other games out there more worth your money, but if it shows up in a good Humble Bundle or something, maybe give it a gander.

Well, I was hoping that I'd like this game but, I had to return it.
The thing is, I just have a huge pet peeve for artificially created difficulty thresholds that make no sense realistically in a survival setting. Even on easy, I found scavenging food to be extremely spotty, so with that in mind when I tried to counter that by building a level 2 trap to catch the bunnies that scampered by often on the surface overhead, I found that even after building a stove, I could not cook the snared bunnies because I needed a freezer, an object that requires a similar amount of scarcely found scavenged components as the stove. That just kills it for me. If I'm starving, and I have a food resource like a dead bunny, AND a working stove, I'm damn well going to cook it to eat, putting the extra step of having a working freezer in order to do so is just so ludicrous! Starving, I'd eat the damn thing raw if I had to being desperate and all, and suffer the consequences.
When I made a thread about it on the forums and found out that this was something that has been brought up to the devs since day 1, but that's about it, that's when I knew that I'd be best off returning the game because very likely, it'd just be a frustrating experience, more than enjoyable.
I'm just making this review to let other likewise minded gamers know that such unrealistic road blocks exist for surviving in this game. If such a thing doesn't bother you, then you'll probably find much enjoyment playing it.

It's a game that doesn't quite know what it wants to be--is this a sort of sports RPG, a visual novel, or what? I'm not sure, and neither are the developers. The problem is that it reaaaallly drags in between the battles. Rather than let you move at your own pace, doing a few matches at a time and then interacting and reading for a while as it suits you, it goes read read read read read play read read read read play read read read play read read play. About 1/3 of the way through the game, I stopped reading the book because honestly, it just wasn't interesting. It's a cheap tourist guide to a world I can't interact with in any way, full of overly fancy writing. 2/3 of the way through, I was barely skimming most of the dialog.
Another problem I had with it is, is that I don't think that your choices in the dialog, or really anywhere else, have much of an effect on the character stories. If this is supposed to be some kind of visual novel thing, shouldn't I have more of an effect on how they turn out? There were like 5 dialog choices in the whole game. That's not an exaggeration. You just click OK after reading the dialog 99% of the time.
Also, as a political scientist who studies the nature of justice and freedom, I'm not sure the writers had any damn idea what they wanted to say with the philosophy here, but it's entirely possible that's because I couldn't be bothered to read the book.

I am struggling to recall a gaming experience I've had that was as thought-provoking, unsettling, and captivating as I did while completing SOMA for the first time.  Admittedly, I was first interested in this game because some comments I initially saw around the game's release drew parallels with the Bioshock franchise.  Being a big fan of that series, as well as Sci-Fi and Horror genre games in general, I purchased SOMA.  Now, I am relatively new to games without defense tactics such as weaponry and SOMA's "run-n-hide' style of gameplay left me, at first, feeling like a stranger in a foreign land; however, this new system of playing quickly became a refreshing aspect and it draws on different tactics as opposed to action/shooter games.
SOMA is immersive.  From the groans of the environmental structures bearing the weight of the ocean to the masterful, eerie soundtrack you feel as if you are experiencing this first hand.  Not to dwell on a single aspect too much, but the atmosphere of the game is largely created by the superb audio work and sound effects.  I cannot tell you how many times I was crawling around (headlamp OFF!) trying to avoid detection only for Simon to bump a nearby object or kick a can on the ground.  The resulting sound is almost deafening with respect to how pin-drop quiet it can be during SOMA's most intense cat-and-mouse encounters.
Additionally, I was not expecting such a meaningful story.  As you progress through SOMA you are often confronted with moral dilemmas that troubled me well after I made my decision.  In fact, SOMA's investigation into existentialism, consciousness, and largely what it means to be human made for an extremely satisfying intellectual experience.  You empathize with the characters in the game and this is assisted by the excellent voice acting and casting.
SOMA also provides outstanding horror elements.  Remember how I mentioned the “run-n-hide” gameplay style?  This instills a feeling of helplessness and vulnerability to the protagonist that adds to the perfectly crafted sense of tension and peril.  After getting past a monster and into a seemingly safe area I felt quite the sense of relief, but there is always the lingering dread of what awaits you behind the next door.  I cannot praise SOMA’s developers enough for producing such a fantastic game.  If you enjoy meaningful science fiction with tinges of horror you cannot pass up this game.

Yes, this game has it's ups and downs, there are lots of people who will murder you on sight and make you lose all your progress, yes there are even people who will befriend you only to kill you seconds later, and yes, the devs can be jerks. But this game is actually pretty great if you look into it.
One thing I've seen a few people complain about is the lack of maps...
Even if there aren't 15+ maps, the ones that exist have an extreme amount of detail and if you take the time to look around, you'll realize why there aren't maps just popping up here, there, and everywhere. The devs care about how the place looks.
And of course, KOSers... another thing even I complain about it... It's OKAY to kill on sight if your starving.. or if you're a hypo and you literally have to eat every 5 minutes... and it's OKAY to kill on sight if you have a friend that needs food... but it's NOT OKAY to go around killing every person you see because your bored.. just.. go watch two dryos fight over a bush or something...
Here's a big one.. progression...  when progression was introduced most people were okay with it... most of us didn't mind, we just had to take a little bit of time to become a bigger dinosaur! No biggie.... WRONG. There were a few people who joined the server before you... and what are they now? Higher tier carnivores... and what do they want? They want you dead.. So you're a little austro, you're about to progress to Utah when all of a sudden.. A utah walks up to you! You exit out of the menu and look up at him in awe, you even friendly call him to see if he'll call back so you can hear the noise it makes.... And it bites you. You're bleeding now. And limping. Oh, you're dead. Yep. Progression.
Nah.. nah.. I'll be serious. Yes progression is when you have to wait around to become a bigger dinosaur, every minute you get a point for surviving.. But you dont get points for hunting, killing, eating, drinking, exploration, etc. Just for being alive, that is the only way you can get points... and yes, it takes a PAINFUL amount of time to get points that way.. and it can take minutes, hours, days, weeks, etc.. to get that ONE dinosaur you want. But Progression does help you from becoming a server full of rexes that are constantly killing eachother. So there's that.
A newer thing that seems to make people unhappy is night time and night vision. Each dinosaur has it's pros and cons... some aren't very fast - some are extremely fast, some dont have an attack - some have an op attack, some dont have much stamina - some have alot. You get the point. But now, there's some dinosaurs with terrible nightvision and some with great nightvision. It's always fun to check out each dinosaur's vision at night. It's not fun to accidently click the night vision button when the sun is directly infront of you- Im getting off track.. anyway, night hunting has also been introduced because of night vision. And many people have started to complain because IF you have a dinosaur with terrible night vision... other carnivores with great night vision take advantage of that....
Now then, my final statement will be this. Dont judge this game too hard.. YET. As it says this game is still in development and there are still many bugs, glitches, and features that no one likes... But for now I would say this game is rather fun. And I would recommend it to people who dont care about losing alot of progress... and people who have friends, packs tend to survive longer then lone players... And remeber to watch your back while you play.. you'll never know if there is someone slowly creepy up behind you.. ready to pounce..

Greetings internet! Today I have for you my review of Soma. Now, I’m not going to make you wait till the end to know my verdict. If you like horror, buy it. If you like immersive atmospheres, buy it. If you like intriguing stories, buy it. And I mean at full price if you can afford it. Frictional games have made a wonderful game, and deserve the support of paying full price. hehe
If you prefer a video check this out!
It seems hard to me to tell much about the story, without giving away too much. You play as Simon Jarratt. Recently you were in a severe automobile accident. Leaving you with brain damage, and your passenger dead. In an attempt to fix the damage done to your noggin, you turn to Mr. Munshi. He is going to scan your brain, and run tests. So that they can fail with the wrong things and not affect you, to find the right thing to do. Things do not go as planned. As the bright light of the scan fades to black, you find yourself in a different place. Quickly finding that things are rather different. Are you dreaming? Dead? Or is this all real. The story will draw you in, the atmosphere will make you live there, and the reality of the world you are then inhabiting will test your morality, sanity, and resolve. The balance and flow of the dread, sad moments, joy of success and shear terror to be had is spot on. It;s a wonderful ride.
Now on to the REVIEW portion.
I’m going to start with my negatives. Lucky me there are only a few.
There could be better optimization of loading. It is far too easy to tell things are going to change when it slows down and the loading brain appears.
I did find a few obvious graphic glitches. Nothing horrid, and easily missed if you are not really searching the rooms.
The voice acting is mostly good, there are a few moments it felt too flat for the situation. Maybe I’m just nitpicking at this point. lol
The creatures do not react to sound as they should. Moving around, they hear, activate a console, they hear, throw a can and they seem to ignore it. *laugh*
Really that is all the negative I have to say about the game. hehe
Now to the much larger positive portion.
The writing is well done. There are many “lore items” in the game so you can get to know the things that have gone down. Some of it is reading, some audio, but almost all entertaining and engaging.
The sound is superb. The music works great with the setting, the sounds of npc’s is spot on. Things moving, sparking, or whatever else they are doing feels right. The sound design does a wonderful job of making you feel you are there, and things are real. Sure, the music CAN take you out of it a bit, but mostly it serves to enhance the feeling of the scene. Not so much a negative, as personal preference, I think Simon should really walk quieter! He makes too much noise, even while crouching. Heel toe man, roll your foot, don’t scuff it!
Graphics are great as well. For an indie team, this is some triple A stuff. Aside from a few moments that I saw watching a creature move, it is well executed. They move realistically and smoothly. Though I once saw the walking a tad off from the movement itself, feet sliding a touch, but it was minor and only once. They put a lot of detail into the art of the world. The creatures look great, the environments are wonderful to look at.
While the gameplay is very fun, it could have an improvement or two. As stated in my negatives, the creatures do not react to sound right, and so we can’t trick them by throwing something and going a different direction. Oh how many times I would have loved to be able to do that. hehe I am a cautious guy, so I spent a fair amount of time crouching, and peeking around corners, standing still and listening as things walked down the halls. Interacting with things had weight to them. Running felt natural. Even being wounded felt as it should. Dependant on your style, you might spend a fair deal of time crouching as I did, or maybe running away from everything you alerted to your presence. Either way, it’s intense and fun.
All in all I found this game to be fantastic. I am not usually a horror player, I play with a 7.1 surround sound headset, in a dark room alone, and I get way too into it. hehe But Soma had the right pacing to keep me engaged, on the edge of my seat, but not so terrified I found myself dreading playing. And it was not just jump scares. Though it had a few. The atmosphere they created here kept me wanting to search all the stuff, but fearful enough to be cautious. The building of the dread, and subsequent horror that would follow was expertly done. Not always doing what you would expect, but always keeping you on your toes. Granted, near the end it kicked up a few notches, and I did have to take a break or two. However the game was so much fun and engaging, the story too interesting, I could not stay away for long!
So if you are interested in a game like this, I suggest you pick it up right away. Don’t wait for a sale, it’s very worth getting at full price. And if you are interested but don’t want to play it yourself, there are plenty of “Let’s Plays” you can watch. I myself did those before this review. So, go here to watch them.

First impression Public Honest review. Beware, this will be a review made by someone who hasnt played the game for too long and its gonna be as honest as it gets.
PHASE 1 - First look , first impression
-Game opened smoothly, presettings for the graphics along with a thank you for supporting the dev`s .Leaves a good impression even though the startup menu looks rudimentary , its gonna be reworked into something better i suppose.
- Server list. First of all, anyone who can play this game on the early times of europe (9 AM Athens/Bucharest approx ) will have to know this : all the low ping servers are mostly empty. You can find 30 -upto 60 people servers at the cost of 190+ping .
PHASE 2- Ingame/Loading impression
Game launched up smoothly and fast, looks optimised enough and the rig ( Radeon R9 380 4 gb /Intel Xeon 3.2 ghz 12 RAM ) didnt encounter any fps spikes. Cons : You start with a selection of race which made me confuse. Cannibals/humans/ herbivore/carnivore? Clicking on the humans doesnt show up anything, i guess its working on it. Second cons : No photo for the dinos. Its a major let-down for any enthusiast to see they didnt bother saving a jpg on each one . A nice idea would be a gif with stats , pros/cons, short description. So the dino select has a minim score.
Game starts smoothly, but nothing explained. Its a pretty basic game, but how can a newbie who never touched the game/seen the map understand where the lake should be/where are the gathering spots? They cant. It would be nice to have a start intro with the whole controls and then giving some directions for 2 minutes (nearest lake/central point of activity) +explanation of herbivore spawn and carnivore, so they can actually understand where they are and where they need to go, what to eat and how to eat.
PHASE 3 - Ingame for 3 hours.
I must admit,its hard to play it alone and confusing, but if you wiki enough you can understand most of it . Although you need to find an experienced person who`s willing to help out, as in you could shorten the amount of time to understand the interest points. Combat is troublesome sometimes but its understanding as in such a complex ecosystem its hard to focus on interesting animations . The bleeding effect is annoying . small paint droplets coming out at a pretty big rate. Smoothing that up, making scratches that actually bleed from inside there and leaving a full trail instead of places with blood would make the game spectacular . Combat should have a better hitting system, as in: 1- Colision should happen, this would give some animals advantage . Like a ram of a t-rex with the head that can spin or drop down another animal. This would give a + to the realistic side of the game. Food and water are well made, nothing to complain except the fact a newbie will need to play about 6 hours to finally understand what and how to do.
Overall , this is an ALFA game so if you can deal with it, its totally worth buying. Dont take that"dev`s suck" / flaming comunity /toxic community as in its a survival game. You get used to dying.
Besides, progressive mode is a challenge. Lets name the dinos on tiers. t1/t2/t3 . Once you have enough prog points for t2 , if someone kills you , you`re going back  to t1. Which is quite annoying but keeps the ecosystem alive. Otherwise everyone would be a huge♥♥♥♥♥t-rex and we dont want that.
A beautiful idea , a game worth buying and i recommend it with all my heart if you can endure the alfa.

Learn all about human anatomy as you find out what makes Nazi's tick one .308 round at a time. A supremely satisfying game to play as the "bullet cam" and "x-ray damage" features keeps the general gameplay grisily and entertaining throughout.
However, the game does suffer from a few flaws. While it seems to encourage stealthy gameplay, it really doesn't seem as if the game mechanics or level design support it very well, oftentimes almost forcing you to go loud or spend ten times the amount of time clearing a level for no additional reward apart from satisfaction.
Co-op play puts one player in the role of sniper while the other is the spotter moving about at ground level and marking targets. While an exceedingly interesting idea, it's nowhere near as fun for the spotter and you'll find you and your friend spend quite a bit of time arguing over who gets to wield the rifle.
Worth a buy on sale. Even after completing it, it's still a game you'll fire up from time to time just to watch Nazi skulls explode in slow motion glory and to try and line your bullet up so it travels through an enemy sniper's scope and into his eye.

Hello, there.
I am just a normal player who plays this game for fun, and now I'm going to be telling you about it.
I think this game is an amazing game, and I support it all the way, but there have been a few changes. There is no longer sandbox, meaning you have to actually play the game to unlock everything else, and that also don't change the fact if you die you have to start all over. I really only unlike the "Die and restart" part, but I'm not against it because this game would be broken without it.
But anyway saying that its going to turn off a lot of people who play the game, because maybe they wanna be overpowered for a while but they cant because they have to wait 7 hours to do so, and then they'll die in the process and have it wait more time. It does get your hours up and its a real cheap way to make you play the game more, but I actually like it. It makes the game way more challenging then it once was. I'd like it if there were more water areas, and less ocean. Its a real pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to finally find water and then find out its just ocean. Maybe make a river dondi on your next map? I don't know. Also its super hilly. It's very easy to break your leg in the game so whoever wants it be careful. Now I'll be talking about the progression system. (How you become better dinos.) (This might also be changed in the future, changing of dinos and points to become, etc.) As a Herbie you start out as a Psittacosaurus, at the bottom of the food chain. It takes 2 points to become Dryosaurus and 25 to 35 points afterwards. After that you can see for yourself. For carnivores you can start off as a herra, Austroraptor, or a juvie trex. Depending on what you are you can become different things. As a Juvie trex, you can become a subadult trex. As a herra, you can become an utah raptor or a allosaur. As a Austroraptor you can become a Baryonyx. All 120 points. Actually I forgot to tell you how to get points. Its different with Herbies and Carnivores, as a meat eater you just wait for points and as a Herbie you eat blue plants. To get 120 points as a Carnivore it takes 2 hours. 1 hour for 60 points. As a Herbie each blue flower is 1 point. How a Herbie eats is red flowers and blue flowers, only blue flowers give you points.
They also are going to add humans in the future, but I'll talk more about that in the future.
Overall, I think this is a really good game. GG Devs.

The Story campain in the game is short but has an acceptable length for a game which had most of it's work put into the multiplayer. From my personal experience it does not have interesting characters, plot twists or anything fasinating. You're told a backstory, you go kill some enemies, take land, rinse and repeat. It's definately fun to play but nothing I want to complete to find out what happens, the story is VERY mediocre. If you're not a big multiplayer fan, there is no point buying this game just for the story. For Honor shines on it's gameplay and the multiplayer. You'd be wasting your money not investing your time into multiplayer.
At first I wasn't fond of the gameplay sword fights because the UI showed you which direction the enemy is going to attack or block, but after getting into the game I don't have much of an issue with it anymore. Personally I would've prefered something comparable to Chivalry in which you can to scrutinize posture, but never the less i've got used to it. Combat is quite in depth, each hero has their own unique move combos which if used effectively will help you dominate the battlefield. There are currently 12 heros available, 4 for each faction. Each has their own unique playstyle, they all counter certain heros and are countered by some. This is the type of compexity I like in multiplayer competitive games, similar to MOBAs. The gameplay is very skilled based, you need to understand the style of movement and attacks you need to use against certain heros. For example, peacemaker is the fastest hero in the game but she has the shortest melee range. The counter would be to dodge her attacks and use her vulnerable spots, also using counter attacks such as parrying and counter bashing. The general gameplay however is very satisfying and fun. The animations on this game are fantastic, from hitting, running and to decapitating another. This needs to be pointed out that For Honor is definately not a realistic, immersive swordplay game because of the healing and buff/debuff mechanics. For example, when you execute players you gain HP, when you're inside a controlled area in domination, you gain HP and heros can use abilities to debuff players. Some abilities also allow you to buff yourself giving you either increased attack, damage and movement speed. If you don't like the sound of that type of gameplay, you'll probably will find it hard to find consitstant enjoyment out of the game.
The graphics in this game are to be expected for a game released in 2017. They look fantastic. I have a i7 6700k at stock, DDR4 16GB 3000MHZ and a GTX 980. I can run this game at max settings (No SSAA) with atleast 60-75 fps, sometimes dropping to 40-50 depending on the environment. Drops only occour when I am playing on the story mode, which is nice for the smoothness in multiplayer. Nothing much to say in this section other than the fact that the graphical options are in depth, have a decent amount of options and that the overall performance is really good.
Other options in the game are good in comparision to some games on PC these days.
Key mapping is easy to use and does the job. Likewise again nothing to say much in this section other than the options that are provided are easy to use, versitile and do the job for a lot of people.
Now this is where a lot of the negitive reviews have come from. The multiplayer is really fun, there are not too many gamemodes just yet but I hope that a competitive mode with ranks will come out soon. The multiplayer doesn't use dedicated servers, it uses Peer-to-Peer. If you don't know what peer-to-peer is, it's a networking method which all people connected to one location will provide internet speeds to keep the server running, so if 8 people connect to one hub and they all have really bad DL/UP bit speeds the server is going to be laggy, everyone will have high ping and it most likely will die. This is one big issue that For Honor has had since release. I only bought the game on the 1st of March so I haven't been playing it since launch, however I can tell you sometimes this has been an issue. No where near as much as people are making it out to be from my own experience. I can imagine that it is being a big issue for some people. Peer-to-peer is a cheaper option than dedicated servers and is commonly used in older games such as the Call of Duty franchise. Whether Ubisoft are going to inpliment dedicated servers or just improve the P2P, I don't know. It's also not an issue for me because I have very fast DL/UP speeds, which I understand that some people don't. Now back to the gamemodes there are 1v1 options, 2v2, and 4v4. Each game mode has it's own system and is played differently. They're all lore friendly to the game and fit very well with the style of the combat. Overall there isn't much complexity with the gamemodes, but I hope in the future there will be more gamemodes like 8v8s, or even 12v12.
If you're a fan of swordplay games, which mainly focus on multiplayer elements, get this game because you'll probably enjoy it a lot. However if you're not the type who can play mulitplayer games for hours and hours on end, you'll probably find that this game wouldn't be a worthy investment.

BeamNG.drive is an amazing physics crash simulator game. There are multiple maps, vehicles and modifications that are available in this game, as well as the BeamNG mod sites which add extra functionality to the game. The game focuses on providing dynamic soft-body physics and realistic driving which it does not disappoint.

I'm surprised that this game was actually playable and enjoyable, given its poor reputation and not so fond memories of it.
The movement is wonky, physics are glitchy, checkpoints are all messed up and story is shallow like a summer puddle. Yet I had fun with it thanks to the good weapon handling [even though hammer and flamethrower were utterly useless, and shotgun and grenades had limited usabilty], hits on target were clearly visible, and the damage- while a bit low, seemed to heave enough force. Some of the better mechanics were definitely this funny "hack vision" and bullet time. The first allowed for some alternative ways to dispose of enemies [shame that level designers completely ignored the potentials it granted, and stopped including it halfway through the game] and gain some view on enemies through cameras; bullet time was used as a rather scarce resource that could grant you a bit more of an upper hand at some of the more dangerous situations, like hard shots or full rooms, so it felt like a fun trump card instead of a core mechanic.
While I found it fun, I can't disagree that it would have benefitted from different design decisions, for example: fov slider, smarter level design [this hack thing could have provided some neat secret stashes around the levels if they weren't so straight forward], more and better balanced weapons, more frequent checkpoints, so you don't save all the time, or "use" function on stray medikits, since you could've picked up a huge health boost for little damage by accident. The last boss is also ridiculously bad, it's just: activate 3 terminals, laugh at the "grand challenge"'s poor aim with rocket launcher [enemies are terrible with it as it's not a hitscan weapon they're so used to], while spamming rockets at his face, taking no damage even though the room is cramped, and finally flip the final switch when he wants to cool down for a bit.
So it's poorly designed, buggy and wonky, the story is dumb, it's short and the music is boring. Yet it's a fun to play single player FPS, that I can recommend for a low price.

Short version: Too much reading in between playing.
If the reviews on this game get too negative, I might go back and change my review to positive. I mean, it's fine. It's not great, but it's fine. It's just a highly disjointed experience. It's a game that doesn't quite know what it wants to be--is this a sort of sports RPG, a visual novel, or what? I'm not sure, and neither are the developers. The problem is that it reaaaallly drags in between the battles. Rather than let you move at your own pace, doing a few matches at a time and then interacting and reading for a while as it suits you, it goes read read read read read play read read read read play read read read play read read play. About 1/3 of the way through the game, I stopped reading the book because honestly, it just wasn't interesting. It's a cheap tourist guide to a world I can't interact with in any way, full of overly fancy writing. 2/3 of the way through, I was barely skimming most of the dialog.
Another problem I had with it is, is that I don't think that your choices in the dialog, or really anywhere else, have much of an effect on the character stories. If this is supposed to be some kind of visual novel thing, shouldn't I have more of an effect on how they turn out? There were like 5 dialog choices in the whole game. That's not an exaggeration. You just click OK after reading the dialog 99% of the time.
Also, as a political scientist who studies the nature of justice and freedom, I'm not sure the writers had any damn idea what they wanted to say with the philosophy here, but it's entirely possible that's because I couldn't be bothered to read the book.

A harrowing experience.  Incredible attention to detail in many regards; sound design, atmosphere, pacing, environment, storyline, etc.  I love how much information can be ascertained from the obvious things such as terminals and data caches (and that I actually had the desire to stop and check these things) but also from less obvious things like the placement of certain objects or the design of an area where you can find clues as to what happened.
There are "puzzles" in the game, which I'm usually not the biggest fan of, but the implementation of these obstacles is excellent.  There is no cheesy highlighting of objects or arrows pointing to an objective, it's laid out for you to piece together, but not incredibly difficult.  Just challenging enough to make you "panic" as you try to piece together how to escape on the fly while narrowly avoiding certain death as the malicious being lurking in the dark breathes down your neck.  It's very satisfying to figure out what to do on your own without someone holding your hand; at the same time it's great relief, because you survived and no one was holding your hand, as you are very much alone.
The interaction system is very good as well, it was good in Amnesia and i like that Frictional stuck with it.  It really helps with pulling you into the in-game world, and giving you a more immersive experience. It also goes well with the no-hand-holding puzzle solving aspect, as you get to "physically" manipulate most objects, so it's not obvious which object you will need to pick up to help you progress or which object you might end up throwing on the ground for the hell of it.  It adds to the experience of this game in that your escape is sometimes dependent upon you have the motor skills to 'unlatch', 'pull' or 'twist' your way to freedom, rather than 'hitting A' to open the automatic door. I think more games should adopt something like this, i've never been so satisfied simply opening a door in a video game.
The story is engaging and I love that half of the 'horror' isn't just from the ever looming threat of something roaming the darkness, but from the existential concepts being conveyed to you that linger on your mind as you traverse the abyss.  The progression of the characters is engaging, and your feelings of them may waver as some of their actions sit in an ethical grey area, and their intentions may seem vague.
This game was a great experience, one that will stick with me, and I thoroughly enjoyed every minute of it, and would recommend it to anyone.

If you liked the other Supergiant games, you'll probably like this one, especially if art and music is a strong factor in your enjoyment of games.
Pyre has been described to me as "Oregon Trail meets NBA Jam," and that description isn't wrong.  Less lethal than Oregon Trail, to be sure, but it takes a structure of "Journey, make decision, resolve event, repeat a couple times, then face an adversary in sports combat."  The fact that it plays more as a sport than a life-or-death battle may make it feel less impactful at first, but once I was invested in the story, the stakes of each battle weighed more heavily on me than any RPG before.
There is lots of text - I'd consider it 40-60% visual novel - but though the pacing flagged at times in the middle of the game, I never felt like I wasted my time reading it.  It gave me a stronger sense of connection to the characters I was traveling with, and the characters I faced in each Rite (the name for the sports-combat encounters).  The story gripped me, and many of my decisions felt like they mattered, whether for future character development or the ultimate outcome of the game.
Pyre raises the stakes by not simply giving you a game over if you lose.  Each victory or loss still moves the story forward, and the simple lack of a reason to reload from a previous save gave me greater and greater investment in each Rite.  Because these Rites had story-driven stakes for everyone involved, I was tempted to throw certain Rites in the favor of my opponent (and did indeed throw one or two).
Also, I totally cried, and not always out of sadness.
The music is wonderful and complements the characters and situations well.  I can only think of one case in which it was distracting, and for the particular character it accompanied, it still made sense.  For the song used in the trailer, I felt like the lyrics were a little too on-the-nose, but when I listened again in the context of the game I warmed up to it.
The art is beautiful and evocative.  It paints an almost whimsical world with a lot of character, appealing on the outside with an undercurrent of the hostility of the land of the Downside (where the game takes place).  The characters themselves are all well-designed, and their paintings give good clues to the surface of their personalities.
The Rites themselves are interesting and fun, too, and do an important job in terms of both pacing and contextualizing the story; they complement the story quite well, but didn't fully click with me.  I still had a lot of fun with them, but a few moments of frustration (but was still able to succeed when I felt I needed to, with some effort).
Conclusion:
I strongly recommend this game to anyone who's willing to put in the time to participate in a great story.  I completed the game for the first time in ~19 hours.  Faster readers could probably complete it more quickly.  I'm tempted to play through again - the ending is significantly influenced by the choices you make and the Rites you win and lose, and I really want to see other potential outcomes for each of the characters I met along the way.

Greetings as always!  I picked up Sheltered a bit ago and ultimately received a refund for it but had forgotten to review it; so… here we are.  Sheltered is a mash up between a management and rpg battle game with a pixel style design.  The graphics and audio are good for what they are meant to be; a callback to old school games and the mechanics themselves are solid for what they are but…
This shelter isn’t for me:  I’ll start by saying I’m not terribly fond of the graphics; not saying they don’t’ have a degree of charm I was just left with feeling a shortcut was taken instead of nostalgia of my childhood.  Part of the issue is I felt too removed from the game through the medium in other games similar I feel that the graphics help push the feeling of struggle and this game did not achieve the same feeling through the use of pixel design.
Why won’t you love me:  I want to like this game but I feel myself going back to my original goal reviewing my games played.  Is this game fun and am I excited to play this?  And the short answer is no.  If anything I found myself wanting to go back to a very similar game called “This War of Mine” which I thoroughly enjoy.  One thing that annoyed me is that this game reminded me a bit of one of my favorite quick games when I was young “Oregon Trail” but…something is missing and I am annoyed I can’t play it better.
Overall, for the current steam sale it is not a bad game; in almost every way it is worth the money, it is just not worth my time.  I feel if I took the time to learn the mechanics thoroughly and do the research and push through some unpleasant experiences I would be much better off and enjoy the game more.  This is more or less how this genre is played but to be honest I’m left with zero desire to do so.  Give it a try if you are bored and don’t have another game to play.  If you like this genre you probably will like this game.  I just didn’t.  Enjoy!

UPDATED REVIEW:
My biggest problem, is that there is not enough content in the game: the campaign is short, the coop missions are too easy and the coop campaign is too short.
So I'd say it doesn't worth the money - if there is a discount maybe (but looking back I definitely wouldn't give more than 5 Euros for it).
However, an interesting game, could have been a very good one. The base idea is interesting. Good gamespeed (in the short campaign you won't feel bored), average story, but it has a certain style (which is not for everyone). Maybe I would recommended for those, who like unique shooter games (FPS), and would like to have a really short game.
The story: i won't make spoiler, it's not bad (i've seen much worse), but a little simple.
The evolution of the skills are well-made, which is absolutely a good point.
There are not so many guns, but that's not a problem, because at least, they are really not the same (i mean, there are real differences between two guns, not just the look of them).
There are 3 major negatives:
1. Graphic is bad. It is like a cartoon, but i think it wasn't a good choice.
2. Story is very short. I walk through the campaign in 1 day.
3. You are overpowered (mainly because of close combat - if you get close, you won). Even on highest difficulty, there aren't really difficult situations (maybe 1 or 2 during whole campaign). You can easily beat the coop missions alone.
I would say, that it's an average game, good for a weekend, but not for more, so in conclusion I don't recommend it.
If there will be a 3rd part, I would be interested in that, given that they change the graphic, and add much more story.
