Here is my review after playing this game for around 15 hours.
First, I have to say that I both enjoy playing as Jason and as counselor.
However, there are things in this game that makes it unsatisfying to play as counselor.
- Shift + Grab + Kill needs to go.
Right now, Jason can teleport right next to you, grab you and kill you.The annoying part is that there is pretty much nothing you can do about it unless you have a pocket knife.
Suggestion : Make it so that Jason can only do his own kill animations if the counselor is injured.

- Even if you have 10/10 stealth, Jason can still know where you are with his sense ability. Also, even if "hide and seek" is a big part of the game, hiding is pretty much pointless since Jason can pretty much know where the counselors are about 90% of the time. The only time he can't know
where they are is if they're too far away.
Suggestion : Make it so that Jason can sense counselors close to him ONLY if they're making noise, or in other words, if they're moving. Jason's last unlocked ability "rage" would make him able to sense counselors even if they're not making noise.
I know Jason is supposed to be overpowered and I think if he wasn't, it would be too easy for counselors. HOWEVER, right now he is TOO overpowered and it feels very unfair most of the time as you're playing counselor.
If the things mentionned above don't bother you and like roleplaying, go ahead and buy it.
I will give it a positive review if either Jason gets nerfed a bit or counselors get buffed.

I've been waiting for Vegas Pro 15 since the release of VP14 and I can't say I'm really dissappointed with my purchase. That isn't to say there isn't a lot of issues with this software. Should I expect more from software that costed me CDN$399? Probably. But VP15 has saved me countless of hours, when it comes to rendering, compared to VP14 & even Premiere Pro CC render times. I now render my videos in 4K 60fps faster than I used to render a 1080p video at 60fps. That is thanks to the increased GPU acceleration and the new Magix rendering option.
So to make it simple, what are all of the pros and cons?
PROS:
- Amazing GPU Acceleration (Tested w/ GTX1080 & 980)
- Improved UI (Dark UI option & more customizable layouts)
- Overall More Streamlined
CONS: (why I currently don't reccomend buying)
- A LOT of crashing. When I say "A LOT," I mean A LOT! (Have you ever heard of the FNV G.E.C.K.?)
- Weird audio issues (e.g. duplicate tracks)
- User interface bugs (layout windows dissappearing)
- Thick bars on every track that can't be hidden, wasting precious vertical timeline space
- Other than UI & amazing renders, not much has changed since VP14
Who should buy this?
- Anyone wanting a VP/editing software that doesn't own VP13/14...
- Anyone who needs to upgrade for the render times (keep the crashing in mind)
- Anyone with a ton of money to blow
I plan on updating this review when (and if) VP15 gets updated to fix the prominent issues.

Just finished my first playthrough... Has there ever been a game as beautiful as this one?
The story, the choices, the music, the artwork; Supergiant somehow managed to outdue themselves.
I had many doubts going into this game, because it was such a departure from their previous works, and the notions of 'Visual Novel' and 'Fantasy Basketball' did not fit into my gameplay worldview. And yet, I learned to love their storytelling; for the depth it allowed and, in my honest opinion, the incredibly compelling mythos it wove of the Commonwealth and the Downside. The rites also grew one me, for both the hiddens layers of strategy they contained, as well as the real challenge they presented, in skill and meaningful story implications.
=============
[Slight Spoilers Below]
Let yourself get lost in the world of Pyre, let yourself lose rites (by which I mean don't restart them until you win), especially Liberation rites, and feel the ripples of those changes, and you'll see a game not about winning, but experiencing as an equal amongst the exiles of the Downside. While I chose a slightly more 'standard' path on this run, I still had unexpected defeats and min-maxless choices that pushed my tale along in unique ways. Possibly the most compelling was the final choice, which, due to my previous actions (and losses), led me to choose opposite what I had planned since the very beginning.
I cannot wait to see what happens when different Triumvarites (teams) succeed and others members of mine are Liberated.
=============
[Slightly More Siginificant Spoilers Below]
My last thoughts, and only real criticisms of the game, are the difficulty spike upon rematching your opponents for the first time, and the relative difficulty of using the Titan Star modifiers.
While in some ways I appreciate the extent to which it threw me and led to unexpected choices, I believe introducing what really can be called arbitrary difficulty spikes should have come much earlier on. I decimated the first 8 rites, and such, wasn't truly forced to learn strategies until a string of back-to-back-to-back defeats immediately after, which definitely resulted in frustration. I persevered, and am all the more satisfied in my eventual clawing back to dominance, but I've discarded games for less, and I worry that there will be some who miss out on the best moments of the game because of it.
I don't believe the gameplay should be easy, just the curve smoothed slightly. Perhaps a slightly more configurable training setup in the Beyonder's Crystal could help too (I actively avoided Versus to avoid any spoilers, however minor, it might have).
On the same note, because of the inherent difficulty even on standard, I felt little room to experiment with the Titan Stars. Those signature Supergiant difficulty modifiers were a major source of replayability in Bastion (and to a lesser extent Transistor) for me, but even the standard play in Pyre was often overwhelming, and almost every time I tried to use one, I was trounced. I foresee myself getting skilled enough to use the more effectively on future playthroughs, but even in my first Bastion run, I had several on at any give point.
I'm not sure how much more easy reduced is, but perhaps it's worth try in order to tailor one's difficulty on a first playthrough.
=============
All in all though, I'm enamoured by this game, and will be replaying it soon and likely often.

A harrowing experience.  Incredible attention to detail in many regards; sound design, atmosphere, pacing, environment, storyline, etc.  I love how much information can be ascertained from the obvious things such as terminals and data caches (and that I actually had the desire to stop and check these things) but also from less obvious things like the placement of certain objects or the design of an area where you can find clues as to what happened.
There are "puzzles" in the game, which I'm usually not the biggest fan of, but the implementation of these obstacles is excellent.  There is no cheesy highlighting of objects or arrows pointing to an objective, it's laid out for you to piece together, but not incredibly difficult.  Just challenging enough to make you "panic" as you try to piece together how to escape on the fly while narrowly avoiding certain death as the malicious being lurking in the dark breathes down your neck.  It's very satisfying to figure out what to do on your own without someone holding your hand; at the same time it's great relief, because you survived and no one was holding your hand, as you are very much alone.
The interaction system is very good as well, it was good in Amnesia and i like that Frictional stuck with it.  It really helps with pulling you into the in-game world, and giving you a more immersive experience. It also goes well with the no-hand-holding puzzle solving aspect, as you get to "physically" manipulate most objects, so it's not obvious which object you will need to pick up to help you progress or which object you might end up throwing on the ground for the hell of it.  It adds to the experience of this game in that your escape is sometimes dependent upon you have the motor skills to 'unlatch', 'pull' or 'twist' your way to freedom, rather than 'hitting A' to open the automatic door. I think more games should adopt something like this, i've never been so satisfied simply opening a door in a video game.
The story is engaging and I love that half of the 'horror' isn't just from the ever looming threat of something roaming the darkness, but from the existential concepts being conveyed to you that linger on your mind as you traverse the abyss. Supergiant Games has created yet another masterpiece. I scarcely call their 'games' just that; as they are works of art just as well as the simple title 'videogame'.
Art Direction: 10/10
Story Concept: 10/10
Animation: 10/10
Music: 11/10 - It's impossibly good and fitting to the style completely.
Character Development: 9/10 - I love lots of backstory and dialogue... but there are times it's a bit much. I suggest more focus on quality over quantity for SG's next game.
Gameplay: 7/10 - I love the gameplay mechanics overall, with the exception of The Rites, which I believe to be the only flaw in this otherwise perfect game.
Combat Gameplay: 5/10 - The Rites. I don't care for it one bit! See below:
When it comes to escaping into a beautiful world full of rich color and characters, Supergiant Games is king. Their art direction, animations, and general ability to lift you up and take you far away, is beyond exceptional. They have inspired me beyond what I thought possible, and let it be said, they are truly a diamond in the rough that is the sea of saturated, terrible games out there right now. This is a masterpiece, and if they receive a negative review /at all/ it's because the reviewer can't see or understand the value of breathtaking art.
That being said, my only complaint about this game is actual combat, aka, 'The Rites Ceremony'. It is in theory, 80% basketball and 20% chess. Except, the twitchy movement style of the 'basketball' component feels clunky, unresponsive and often downright frustrating. I was obsessed with Transistor because I was able to "freeze time" and allow myself to apply strategy and thought before I acted; something I had hoped would carry over for their future games. It did not. The combat in this game has problems. The perspective in which the camera resides leaves it often hard to judge where the base of a character actually is, causing the player to get stuck running into an obstacle, burning their stamina as they clunkily attempt to move around it. It happens a LOT. I realize there are going to be (likely younger generation) players out there who are all going to say "WHAT?! Omg! Get better then scrub! I love the fast-paced, twitchiness!! ROFL" - However, I would hope this review finds Supergiant Games, so they might better understand something about their playerbase.
I would aruge that the majority of Supergiant Game's fanbase are gamers who value, understand and appreciate art. Art in it's most raw form, beautiful abstract paintings and concepts that simply elate the mind. We are NOT players who love twitchy-fast-paced, "precision" combat. It was such a terrible disappointment to see just how twitchy the combat was after I watched the trailers. I was hoping there would be more strategy involved, but really it's just about picking the quickest character and having them juke/rush the NPCs.
Here's my Suggestion for you Supergiant Games:
- It would have been really nice if you gave the player time to actually set up the positioning of their characters before the Rites began, adding a whole new level of strategy to the combat. By the time I can even clunkily select the correct character, the enemy NPC is already diving for my Pyre, often leaping from halfway across the map and straight into the goal. Sigh.
- The movement is not responsive, it has an ease and acceleration/deceleration upon starting or stopping movement. I understand this may be more realistic, but it's just downright frustrating! Getting stuck behind objects or nearly missing the enemies Pyre because of this, really kills the fun.
- How about everything just has it's quickness cut in half across the board? Or, rather than attempting to fuse a twitchy-combat style into a beautiful, relaxing work of art; what's wrong with turn-based strategy?
While this game is a masterpiece, if you are an older gamer and/or you are not one for fast-paced, slippery-precision combat, I would not recommend this game for you, unless you can force yourself to look past it like I did.
Dear Supergiant Games:
I love you so gd much it is my dream to work for you. But please, may I request that your next game have more strategy instead of fast-paced, slippery, twitchy combat? PLEASE? Let me enjoy your work! Transistor had a great solution to this. Bastion, at least it felt better in combat than this.

A rather interesting entry to video games. A saw a couple of people I knew play the original game then eventually picked it up myself. I quite enjoyed it's story though was disappointed in the lack of in-depth lore of the Darkness itself. Eventually the second game was released and it brought both improvements as well as some missing elements.
The biggest change would be the visuals, where the first had a more dark and gritty look to it, the second instalment took on a more comic book art style. In some cases the game looks nice with the change, but sometimes it also looks a bit off. The semi free roaming aspect to the game was removed and the developers made it more linear. It wasn't entirely a bad choice since it meant you weren't getting lost all that much but it also removed the sense of exploration.
The gameplay mechanics got a bit of an overhaul allowing players to now "quad-wield" as you can use dual weapons plus "Lefty" and "Righty" to massacre anyone dumb enough to get between you and your objective. Jackie also has a number of new abilities to distract and tear his enemies apart. He even comes with a mocking side kick who will tear faces off, slip throats and answer natures call all over the enemy. You even get a few segments to play as the Darkling.
The story also explores a bit of Jackie's history as well as the Darkness. We get to see Jackie's guilt over the loss of Jenny as well as his questioning of his sanity and the Darkness' attempts as controlling him. We're also introduced to the cult known as The Brotherhood some of whom have dark essence enabling them to do supernatural abilities.
Multiplayer returns, but this time it focuses in on co-op, providing players with four darkness users each either their own back story and abilities. The missions players can to do are a bit short and fill in a few gaps that you really only hear about briefly through the main game. Still, getting together with some friends and wreaking havoc is always fun.
Overall the game may not be for everyone, even the original release was more of a hidden gem than a well known game. On top of that PC only has the second game for what ever reason, so players won't really know the full story (though the game does an alright job catching you up on events) unless they decide to watch a video walkthrough. But if you like simple mayhem, the supernatural and a little bit of cooperative fun, it's worth checking out.

Ever played a game with dinosaurs and thought to yourself "Man this is cool and all but I would to play as the dinosaur!"
Well then friend this is the game for you. The Isle is a open world survival game where you can choose from a wide variety of dinosaurs both carnivorous and herbivorous to play as.
One of the Isle's main features is a "Progression system" where you start as the smallest dinosaur and work your way up the food chain towards becoming either an apex predator of the Island or joining a herd with your fellow Herbivores, this progression system however is not forgiving as if you die you are dropped down back to the bottom of the food chain, However there is a checkpoint system in the works that should allow players to save their progress and save them from a long fall back down the food chain.
An important note is that the developers are looking for players to help actualy test new features and find any bugs that come with them so that the final game can be more polished and bug free.
Make no mistake this is a difficult and unforgiving game but it is not impossible to play provided you have some friends to play with and a way to communicate with each other.
The Isle has come a long way since it's debut on steam back in December of 2015 and it still has a long way to go as the game will eventually be adding more important features in like the two human factions, the interactive storyline and much more.
Overall I have to give the Isle in it's current state a Positive recommandation as the game is constantly updating and growing and the developers are very vocal and translucent with the community, But if you are someone who does not enjoy difficult games or only has enough time to play casually, take a second thought and read the store page before buying the game just so you know what you are getting yourself into.

Velvet Assassin is a classic stealth action game with all the good and bad things that stem from the old-school approach to this genre. The WWII setting is intriguing and the protagonist Violette Summer most enjoyable in all aspects.
The visuals set the incredible dense atmosphere. Warm colour palettes, lighting effects and the eerie fever dream scenes make Velvet Assassin a beautiful game, despite its dated graphics. Blurry textures and partially choppy animations may stain the overall neat picture but can be discounted due to the age of the title. The crisp sound effects strengthen the stealth gameplay and occasional music cues accentuate feelings of cautiousness, stress or horror. Especially delightful is the writing for the dialogue between the Nazis. The subject matter, phrasing and voices are authentic, opposed to the usual American German gibberish. Adding to the authenticity is the inexplicit display of cruelty and desperation both visually and conceptually.
The character of Violette is a slinky slim beauty with a great and fitting voice and a righteous agenda. The missions are diverse in theory but in the end the gameplay is mostly the same. Apart from a rudimentary character level system involving collectibles and side missions, the meat of the game is the Holy Trinity of sneaking in the shadows, killing enemies silently and hiding the corpses in a pile of bodies in a dark corner. Depending on the assets available at the mission locations, gameplay may vary. While observing enemies to memorize their movement pattern is a classic aspect of stealth games, timing different enemy paths so that an activated grenade blasts off at the right time can add a little more tactics into the usual routine. Slipping into an SS uniform or sniping enemies off the buildings are other infrequent gameplay options.
A major issue though is the worst checkpoint system in a game ever paired with nebulous gunplay coming together during the last missions. As happens so often in stealth games, the inevitable chaos forces the player to dramatically change the strategy from sneaking to going out pants down and guns blazing. Unfortunately and naturally, the handling of guns, especially assault rifles, is not as fleshed out and comfortable as the rest of the mechanics, leaving the player struggling through the end.
Although Velvet Assassin hasn't aged too well in comparison to current titles of the genre, it's still a fun old-school stealth game with a great setting.

This game isn't unfinished. It hasn't even properly begun.
I understand what Early Access is. I understand what it's SUPPOSED to be doing.
This is not it. Not in the slightest.
Just because Early Access allows you to put up a game that isn't fully complete DOES NOT mean you can post something like this. I understand the concept and, quite frankly, I love it. Haven't seen a proper space combat game since, what, Freelancer? And that was back in 2000. I feel the dev wants to make this a memorable experience, and that right there is a commendable initiative.
However, that does not save the fact that this game is barely Beta. Hell, this is pretty much a proof of concept, nothing else. Sure, it's free, but the "Elite Account" is ridiculously expensive for a game like this, even more so than GUISE OF THE WOLF.
Not even kidding. The Elite Account is more expensive than Guise of the Wolf. I'd rather play that for the Narm value if not for the fact that FUN Creators behaved like complete asses. But this? This game DOES NOT WARRANT a 14 euro Elite Account, especially not one that LOCKS MOST OF THE SHIPS. I'm sorry, WHAT?
A free to play game, on Early Access, FAR AWAY from finished, and it has an Elite Account purchasable that allows you to use most of the ships available in-game. This SCREAMS cash-in, it really does. The game, as it stands, does not warrant the Elite Account, as I said.
As for the actual game...
Menus: The options menu is pitiful, and is the first one I've seen that labels VSync as "Level 1" and "Level 2". I've tried both of them and quite honestly didn't notice any difference. You've got 2 mouse speed options, X and Y, which, again, tell you nothing. I assumed Y was vertical, but the actual game is completely 2D, so... what's it for?
The actual in-game menu is ridiculous. The Friends tab doesn't work. The Group tab doesn't work. The Lobby tab shows you the number of people... but not actually the people. It's basically empty UI space. Not to mention the fact that no one ever talks to anyone in the chat.
All in all, 5 buttons work in the menu: Tutorial, Skirmish, Options, Exit and the Elite Account purchase thingy. Hmm.
Tutorial: Jesus. Christ. The tutorial tells you nothing about the game. It's basically "Go here, hit this". It tells you movement... and that's it. I was left honestly confused at the end of it. I mean, what are cocoons? What are defenders, lane support? Not to mention that it was ridiculously easy to just skip past everything and destroy the enemy base IN 5 HITS. I mean, what?!
(I'd like to note here that the game menu is bound to F10. Can't change it. What is this, 2007? ESCAPE, PEOPLE).

Skirmish: The current meat of the game. This is the one and only part that I'd say actually outright sucks rather than being unfinished. After spending 5 minutes in the queue with barely any information about players (besides a basic x/4, which makes no sense, as I ended up on a 3v3), I get into the game, only to find out that everyone was just standing at spawn, doing nothing. They weren't even afk, since when I sneaked into the enemy's spawn, they attacked me. They were literally just standing there, probably confused about the whole thing because, again, THIS GAME DOESN'T TELL YOU ANYTHING.
Mechanics: Overly simplistic. Left click for basic attacks, you can purchase abilities that automatically bind themselves to the number keys. I'd like to note that the upgrade shop is actually quite interesting, and ships do seem to have specific abilities available. Nothing new, but still nice.
I have no idea how to play this game, because I couldn't bother to play it long enough to learn. Maybe a mode where you fight AI, and an improved Tutorial (look at LoL) could make this better.
Map: I played this ONCE. Again, ONCE. The map is... I have no idea what to say. The game is completely 2D, which is REALLY odd for a space combat game, and as such everything on the map is on the same plane (except maybe for that... thing in the middle. Which I have no idea WHAT it is). I really, really, really totally freakin' like the fact that you can go across the boundaries of the map and start taking damage because of it (sarcasm, by the way). I've seen that in many games. NEVER IN A MOBA.
As for the actual map elements... No idea what to say. Game tells you nothing. Confusing as hell.
(I'd like to note here that this game runs like♥♥♥♥♥ It's permanently locked to 30.1 frames, for some forsaken reason, and if you hit the Alt button to get some very basic enemy indicators, THE FRAMERATE IS HALVED. WHAT? WAT?!)
Graphics: Overall, look kinda nice. I've seen worse textures in much more expensive games (I mean AAA expensive). However... the game looks barren. You've essentially got a handful of things floating around, not moving, asteroids and ice chunks that you can destroy... And that's it. They look pretty, but ultimately useless. The backgrounds are nice, but waaaaaaay too colourful.
(I'd also like to note that you can freely clip through the shop. And if you aim the camera properly, you can see the interior of the model, I... whatever)
Final Opinion: This game needs SERIOUS work, and should not be on Steam like this, especially not with a 14 euro Elite Account that LOCKS AWAY FREE USERS FROM MOST OF THE SHIPS. This is THE most blatant pay-to-win game I have ever seen, and that♥♥♥♥♥♥should be fixed.

I was going through a rough time in my life. My parents were fighting constantly, I had no friends, and everyone I met hated me because I was fat. I needed something to prevent me from suicide. I could not find anything I really liked. I tried buying toys, but the store clerks always prevented me from buying anything because I was overweight. I tried making a vlog on YouTube about my troubles, but I was banned from youtube for supposedly impersonating Gabriel Iglesias. Google fined me all of my money until I only had $1.10 left.
The only things I had were things necessary for my survival. I was fed a potato every other day and also given water in a shot glass. Sometimes I forced myself to use the water as a way to bath instead of drinking it. I was locked in my room every day cuz my parents were busy fighting about which console to play on. Well, not entirely.
I had this netbook, one my parents got me for my birthday when I was 12. I used it for school, mostly, until now. I was also lucky enough to have a charger, and all the stuff you need to use the netbook. I decided, maybe give video games a try. No one would judge me there. I was unable to play the f2p games because A. They took too much storage and B. I would be banned whenever I joined a multiplayer game. I remembered the $1.10 I had left.
I knew I had to find something that gave me a reason to live. I looked through the steam store. Jesus almost nothing was $1.10! I was about to give up and just end my life when I found this game. Robot vs Birds Zombies. 99 cents, without 10% tax. It took up all the space on my netbook. After waiting for it to download, I opened up the game. Upon opening it up there was a well made launcher with many options. Once I opened up the actual game, I heard a sweet rock song, and saw some badass looking birds and a cool robot. Was this what I needed to continue living
It was. I am proud to say Robot vs Birds Zombies saved my life. The characters were deep, had personality, and I was able to connect with them. The story was unique, suspenseful, and I shed multiple tears. The graphics were revolutionary, and the soundtrack was the first good thing I had heard in awhile. It, in a way, provided everything I needed to live. The characters were my friends. The game was like a good parent. The game was easy to fap to. I could have just played the game for my entire life. It was amazing. It changed me. Here I am, sitting in my room, now infested with bullet ants and bees, starved half to death and with my throat about to dry up. But you know what? I do not care. Because I have Robot vs Birds Zumbies. And I will always have Robot vs Birds Zumbies. This game is my life now. I am finally happy. I am finally free. I know now the meaning of life. And only because yfyx games spent their time on this godly game.

Time to revamp my review.
After seeing many, many reviews which were either spreading misinformation, ignorant, pure stupidity or people not reading the storepage, I'm going to do a review without that and without sucking Dondis (the main Dev) banana. I'll review the game itself with the simple pro/contra style and say something about the devs.
The Isle:
Pros:
- Beatiful Animations and Models (Yes, the new allo too)
- high-quality, unique but somehow familiar sounds
- overall high-quality graphics and textures
- constant updating, no need to worry that it could be TSL 2.0
- already various "gamemodes", made by the community
- good future plans
- many dinosaurs to play and many upcoming dinos (& other creatures)
- pretty good optimisation compared to other EA-games
Cons:
- Can be buggy sometimes (for instance buggy spawning, not being able to stand up after resting etc.)
- Can be very frustrating at some times
- Can be boring in it's current stage
- Is very time-consuming (not really a con for me tho)
The Isle is a game for people who have time and like to play dinosaurs. However it is not the right games for realism-"I want feathered dinosaurs"-people. It's clearly inspired by Jurassic Park. Most dinos will get a feathered model, so at least it's semi-realistic and pleases both sides.
There are two gamemodes, one is sandbox where you can choose your dino. The other one is progression where you start as a small dino (Velociraptor, Psittacosaurus or Orodromeus) and have to gain points for the next bogger dinosaur. As an example you go from Velo to Herrera, then to Utahraptor and so on.
This mode exists in different variations, such as low-PP (progression-points) and vanilla. On low-PP servers you'll only need half as much points for the next dino. Vanilla is the time-consuming part, but at the same time the funniest and most exciting (for me atleast). There are also servers with different rules. Some are "realism"-server with strict rules to simulate reallife-behaviour; Deathmatch-servers, the name says it all and more. So there are enough playstyles to please most of the people.
Now, if you consider buying this game, READ THE STORE PAGE. Here's the firts paragraph for those who are lazy:
"THIS GAME IS IN EARLY ACCESS. PLEASE DO NOT PURCHASE IT UNLESS YOU WANT TO ACTIVELY SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE GAME AND ARE PREPARED TO HANDLE SERIOUS ISSUES AND POSSIBLE INTERRUPTIONS OF INTENDED GAMEPLAY FUNCTIONALITY."
This is meant to be taken seriously. Be sure to read and check the minimum requirements to run the game. Do not dare to play on a laptop. 80% of the reviews I see are complaints about the game not starting, bugs, gamechanging features, not being a "realistic dino-game" (I mean, there's a hyper-rex mauling a car on the front-page but who cares right?) and the devs.
You might ask why do people not like or even hate the devs? I honestly don't have a clue.
The devs of the Isle are by faaar the most humane and interactive devs I've seen. Most people complain that they got banned or insulted for "nothing". That's wrong because there is a reason everytime. I've seen countless posts about ETA's and other forbidden things, which are clearly stated in the rules. They then obviously get closed and/or deleted. Later I see the exact same people writing reviews about how they got banned for no reason. I mean, seriously?
Lately I've seen some posts from trolls or butthurt people lying that they got banned for meaningless posts. They said that they had "proof", but all they got were screenshots of the ban (without the reason) or fake-accounts. The devs or moderators are pretty good detectives from what I've seen. They countered with actual proof. Proof where you could see everything, including the reasons and posts.
But do you know what they don't like? Stupid human beings. At first, like maybe a year ago, I thought the devs are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s because I read some reviews. My mind changed really fast after joining their discord and watching some of Dondis streams. I've learned to understand why the devs are harsh and honest towards people. Yes I say honest because they usually don't call you an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ radomly.
Another thing I've read often is that Dondi spawns in as a hyperrex and kills everything. Yes he spawns in as an owerpowered dino sometimes. BUT he never kills anything on his sight. I think most of these people are referring to the vid where he kills like 3 or 4 rexes? He did it because they were spamming the broadcast-roar and didn't "fear" the monster. They didn't try to hide or run away. They just stood around him, stared at him and spammed their roars.
Now, the question is: Do I recommend the Isle?
Yes and no. The Isle is a game in developement. That means bugs, changes and testing new, uncomplete features. Take the first paragraph to heart and read the required specs. You don't have to like the devs to play this game. The devs don't do anything to you ingame and have nothing to do with your gameplay experience. If you are butthurt or offended easily, don't purchase the game as there are many trolls. Don't purchase it of you have anger issues either.
Looking for a Jurassic Park-Styled survival game with cannibals, humans and mutations in the future? Then this is the perfect game for you. Looking for a realistic dinosaur-simulator? Then this could also be the right game for you, if you're not bothered by non-feathered dinosaurs or an oldschool Spinosaur. There will be plenty of gamemodes and servers with special rules (such as turning off humans and monsters). To learn the devs and their behaviour better go tho the official Isle discord (you'll find it if you use your brain hehe) and watch some streams by Dondi. Don't ask questions that could easily be answered by using your best friend google. Firts and most important tip: Don't trust any other payer, even if they are the same dino as you and friendly call.
Now good luck and have some fun everyone. If you see any spelling or other errors, keep them to yourself. I am too lazy to structure the text so don't judge me for that.

So far, Survarium is a pretty unique game, setting and gameplay-wise. The atmosphere is spot on, the ambient sounds, the looks, the aesthetics are just perfect. It really helps you immerse yourself in the game.
The gameplay is very different from what I'm used to. It's less of a Call of Duty-style twitch shooting, and more of a game where you actually feel like you're fighting for survival. Team coordination is key, and you'll experience some pretty Hollywood-like moments here and there when someone rescues you from enemy gunfire or the other way around.
So far the game shows lots of potential, but as of yet it is severely lacking in terms of content. I feel like there should be more modes which are much more survival oriented, more character progression and more story content. For example, you're asked to choose a faction to side with, but the thing is that you're never given a description of these factions, what their motives are, what they do, why would I want to join them? This is something which needs to be taken care of IMMEDIEATELY.
Another thing is the optimisation. It outright sucks balls. I'm getting an absolutely horrible framerate, and I wouldn't really say that the graphics justify that, considering that it looks like a PS3 launch title. And the motion blur is just awful - it's like you're drugged at all times, turn it off completely.
So far, Survarium is not the greatest game ever, definitely. But, you can give it the benefit of it being in Early access and turn a blind eye for some of the missing functions. Plus, it's free, so you really lose nothing besides HDD space.
I'm excited to see what becomes of this game in the future.

A sequel of the famed Sniper Elite: Berlin 1945, Sniper Elite V2 felt much like a remastered version of the game. There were many similarities in the plot and gameplay between both of these games. This review does include SPOILERS so be prepared for those.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
You play as an elite American Special Forces sniper that was send to a war-torn city of Berlin during the final days of WW2 in Europe. The once-powerful Third Reich was collapsing at a shocking speed, with British and American forces advancing from the West, and Soviet might marching from the East. It is April 1945, and Soviets are near the city of Berlin, a capitol of the Hitler's Nazi Machine. But the once beautiful city was turned into complete chaos, due to Allied air-bombing and Soviet artillery strikes. The last hope, the Wunderwaffe programme was ceased, and scientists were trying to save themselves from certain death in Soviet gulags by selling their knowledge and V2 rockets. Your role in this madness is to prevent Soviets from receiving all the documents that they may use against the West in the future.
In your journey you will assassinate important scientists and officers, fight both Germans and Soviets and prevent a V2 attack on London and other capitols. You will use a Sniper Rifle, and various other equipment to achieve your goals.
SPOILER END
The main point of the game is to use a Sniper Rifle to kill your opponents (hence the title). The satisfying x-ray kill cams have fantastic amount of detail of what one, single bullet can do inside a human body (and yes you can shoot a guy in the balls and see his nuts pop). The enemies can be challenging at times, but it would be more fun if they would use cover more efficiently. The realism of shooting is superb. On the highest difficulty, you have to watch your Heart Rate, the wind and you have to consider the gravity by estimating the range of the shot. These factors are even more fun when facing enemy snipers, as these can be very challenging to kill.
The graphics of the game are outstanding. The lighting is of very high quality, collapsing buildings, ruins, burned out cars and other things are very good, even by 2015 standards.
So why did this game remind me of Sniper Elite: Berlin 1945? Well the plot is almost EXACTLY THE SAME. The new guy was a typical tough yankee, with no emotional feel at all. I prefered the guy from the first game. The soundtracks are copied and pasted with minor editions done to them.
Multiplayer and Co-op campaign is extremely fun. When facing other players in a match where long-range kills give you the most points is challenging, but a single kill is very satisfying. Co-op campaign is also fun, and often turn co-operation into a competition of who gets a longest range kill.
Pros of this game
+ Graphics
+ Destroyed buildings, shooting sounds etc. add a great feel of what is going on around you
+ Although copied and pasted from the first game, the plot was still decent
+ X-Ray kills
+ Multiplayer is fun
+ Co-op campaign is competitive and fun
Cons of the game
- Felt like a remastered edition of Sniper Elite: Berlin 1945
- I prefered the German Sniper Uniform of the character from the first game
- Soundtrack is almost exactly the same as of the first game
- Zombie Army DLC (are you trying to copy Call of Duty? Did you get that low Rebellion?)
- Enemy AI needs to use cover better
- The main character had no emotional feeling, but was a Holywood-styled tough patriotic Soldier that saved the World
For the games after the Sniper Elite 3 (which I haven't played because it's a copy and paste of V2 as I have heard) I recommend:
* German Sniper Uniform for the character (new or from the previous games)
* Better customization in weaponry
* More Guns (only had a few)
* A setting should be somewhere on the Eastern Front, with possibly a mission in Stalingrad and some missions on the Russian steppe
Overall a satisfying experience, but several things could have been improved. an 7/10 material.

1.) Rocky Launch: I believe the game should be labled as "Early Access" it simply does not feel complete.  The developers promised way more content and as of right now, they do not seem to be making any progress on this...which would be FINE except the game just feels like an empty shell of what it COULD be.  Label it Early Access.  Also I am thinking about the free content they put out to apoligize for the rocky launch... it was very minimual effort.  They reskinned the Part III Jason, which probably took them less than a day, probably less than an hour, and gave everyone 13,000 CP which took them no time.  The new music was the best part and probably took the most work.  Dead by Daylight has put out 2 free chapters which include 2 new playerable characters and 2 playable killers and 2 new maps...that is how you do free content.  I mean it's hard to complain about F13's free content we are sorry update, but don't be fooled, it took the minimual of effort.
2.) Low Content...HIGH PRICE TAG- The developers expect you to shell out 40 bucks for this game full of bugs and lack of content?  They need more meat on the bones to justify that price tag...don't get me wrong, I think they put a ton of work into Jason and it shows.  The rest of the game surrounding him feels...empty and rushed.
3.)Waiting after a match- If you die, or survive you are forced to wait for the conclusion of a match if you want to recieve all your XP, which is nonsense.  I get WHY they do it, to preserve the lobby...but it simply is not fun.  I believe that once you have escaped, or have been killed and the role of Tommy Jarvis is filled you should be allowed to leave and get full XP.
4.)VOIP- Some will disagree with me on this, and that is fine. I HATE that the game uses voip.  I play these games for immersion...and nothing takes you out of immersion more than a 12 year old screaming at you as Jason.  There should be a way to communicate, like canned phrases or a retical wheel for those who don't want to do VOIP.
5.) Playing Jason- Is awesome.  He feels great, he is all around fun.  HOWEVER, it is totally random whether or not you'll get to play as him, and I find the Counselor game is a crapshoot.  Sometimes it is fun, but most of the time it just feels boring.  They need to spice up that gameplay...somehow.  The coolest part of the game and the part they did the most work on is Jason and you'll only play him about 12% of the time.
6.) Bugs and Glicthes- Their are a ton of them and very few bug fixes of patches have come out since launch fixing any of them.  Animations that break, glithcy gameplay in general.  Getting stuck in doors. etc.  The developers need to fix these issues asap,
Overall, Friday the 13th has a ton of potential here, and even though I kind of raked them over the coals you can see that this is a labor of love...however it just has too many issues with the current build and I cannot recommend it at this time.  I would recommend Dead by Daylight instead, much cheaper buy in, way more content, way more patches and I think the gameplay is more fun in general.

WARNING: (First a warning, then the review) THIS GAME IS DESIGNED TO TAKE YOUR MONEY. I bought this game when it was in Alpha because I believed in the concept and in the developers. I wish I hadn't. The first warning of this game being a sleezy cash grab was that there is 3 different versions of the game available for purchase. The next sign is when you first purchase items in the "Safe Zones" (not really safe at all). Many of the cosmetic items are purchased through "Nether Gold" which is buying items with real life money. There is also items that are not comsetics that can be purchased with Nether Gold; don't be fooled these items may seem subtle and meaningless to purchase but those little items make a big difference once you get the hang of the game. Lastly the biggest sign that this game is designed to take your money is the locked containers layed across the world. You can only open them with what are called Golden Keys. This is where all the best loot is located, which means that a lot of the good loot is now locked away behind these containers. It is no longer about exploring the most dangerous places for the best loot, it is about finding a container. Want to play as a Nether creature? Purchase the Potion for in-game currency or Nether Gold only to be able to play as the creature for 3 turns. It is simply made to take your money.
Now, if the whole, "It's made to take your money away" thing didn't scare you away, here's the review:
This game was created on the idea that you had to survive a post-apocalyptic world plagued with monsters called Nether. It is quite a refreshing take from the rest of the post-apocalyptic survival games out there. There is a wide variaty of Nethers to fight and each with a different pattern of behavior. The first person perspective allows you to be more immersed, which really helps to add to the atmosphere because this game really makes you feel as if the world is destroyed and you are alone. Those are what the game should be...the reality is that this game failed to deliver all that. The game has so many bugs that at any moment you start to feel true immersion you get smacked in the face with an animation of a Nether jumping up and down, or getting stuck between 2 cars THAT ARE 10 METERS APART! The Nethers? There is a variety of them, but they range from difficult to kill to pull your testicules (or ovaries) out of yourself and smack the screen with them. I understand that it is supposed to be a brutal game, but there is a difference from enjoying a challenge to simply being having no chance of survival. The game is supposed to be a survival game, not a death trap. You spawn with nothing but a kitchen knife. The most basic enemy can teleport behind you (or any side you may not be looking at) and smacks you. Encounter a screacher and you're done for.
The game allows for leveling up your character. It sounds great in theory, but in practice it makes all players more angry. If you die, all progress made is gone. It hurts more to know you're at a level 32 and you died just because a Nether teleported behind you or another Player shot you. Other players almost always (ALMOST) shoot on site. No complaints there because it is the nature of a survival game. I do not like it very much but it is what it is, there is a system set up to counter act this behavior but it is futile.
The game LOOKS pretty on the screenshots but don't be fulled. To achieve that level of quality you have to access the SystemSettings file in the corresponding folder and manually some of the extra effects. If you do enable the effect, the game will have so little frames-per-seconds and so much screen tearring that you would think you were about to pass through a black hole in space.
Missions? Have you ever wanted to play a Mailman Simulator? Well...this is for you. Carry item from point A to point B and if you die you lose the item, the XP you had gained, and all progress. This is a problem when you realize someone can simply stand outside the delivery destination and shoot you before you deliver the package so they can get the XP. There are 3 other types of missions; Killing the big bad Nether, Escort Missions (technically the same as being a mailman), and defending the safe zone (which is a real dumb ****ing idea since you go to the safe zone TO BE SAFE!) .
Overall? I had fun at first playing this game. Everything seemed to doing just find for the first couple of hours but now...it is just garbage.
PS. If all this does not persuade you into not buying this game, consider this. This game went from Alpha stage to full release without prior warning. The game had not delivered all the promised features it had said it would have and the developers are no where to be found to answer questions. You might notice that the World Map has some areas shadowed out, well those areas were supposed to be open by full release. There was also supposed to be PvE survers, or at the very least PvE areas, and those weren't delivered either. Story or background on the world? NONE. The game is overwhelmed with cheaters and hackers, with things like moving faster, or being able to see people through walls.
If you do not purchase thank you. If you do purchase, well I'll be excited to read your review.

Bejeweled is actually one of my favourite "classic" games. It's one of the original Match-3 style games, with everything done right. From different modes, to combos, to the timers, the sounds, the graphics, everything is satisfying and it has none of the gated frustration of most match 3 games have these days, catering to the mobile in-app purchases crowd. Where candy crush makes me want to punch a baby in annoyance, Bejeweled makes me purr with happiness. And trust me, I'm not that easily pleased.
I do think this game plays better on a touch screen device, I play it a lot on my iPad, but you can get extremely fast matches for high scores once you're used to the keyboard commands. Mouse clicking makes it kinda hard to beat some of the achievement / score timers but still fun. If you are wondering how to beat some of the achievement challenges and you're using the mouse - switch to keyboard matching. It'll be slower at first but once your fingers and brain catch on it's a LOT faster.
If you don't enjoy mindless timewasting match 3 games then you will not enjoy this game - but if you like simple, satisfying puzzles, big combos and lots of challenges, this is one of the best match 3 games I've played - and I've put in hundreds of hours on my iPad that I don't even regret.

By now, most horror enthusiasts have probably played a short retro-looking title called Home that released in mid-2012. It's a game that still stands as one of the more unique horror experiences, despite not having the fancy frills of high end graphics, immersive dialogue, or even modern gaming conveniences. Settled can very much be compared to Home in the way that it's presented, played, and the short-but-thrilling adventure that it houses.
No parent should outlive their children... this chilling adage is repeated numerous times throughout the gameplay; from the beginning, right through until the bitter end. The story has a simple enough concept, you play as a father who has lost his daughter. As the game winds on, it becomes apparent that his kid was either murdered, or died in some preventable attrocity, and the guilt of the man follows him. Players are deliberately led through various conclusions to what happened, but it's within the last 3-5 minutes of the game where the whole picture really becomes clear, and the horrifying, unpredictable, plot twist becomes a sick reality.
The gameplay itself is extremely simple; you use the left and right arrow keys to move, spacebar to examine objects, and the down arrow key to back out of an examination scene. No, there is no save option because Settled only lasts about half an hour even if you explore everything. There's also nothing in the way of a menu, as it's an unnecessary concept. There's little in the way of sound, save for footsteps and some very low atmospheric ambiance. That being said, where the game is lacking in audio appeal, it makes up for with amazing pixel visuals, haunting scenes of gore, and numerous mini-cutscenes.
Just as with Home, you really need to play Settled in order to fully understand it. It's difficult to create a review for it since so much of the event can be spoiled by talking about all of the better parts of the game. Fans of Home, and even Uncanny Valley to a certain extent, will find Settled an excellent addition to this overlooked niche horror sub-genre. Sadly, it doesn't have branching endings, so after the initial 30 minute playthrough it will just sit in your virtual library, collecting virtual dust. With that said, snagging it at a 50% discount is a huge bargain, but the standard price is still worth the quick experience.

I have nearly 500 games in my Steam account, and the vast majority of them are still unplayed. So now I'm dedicating an hour to each of these games and writing a series of One Hour Reviews.
One Hour Reviews - Game 6
Alpha Prime
Purchase Date: 1/16/2014
Alpha Prime is another game I picked up thanks to a Humble Bundle.  18 months later I am finally getting to check it out.  Turns out I could have waited.
Alpha Prime starts out much like one of those B-movies you expect to see on the Sci-Fi channel, with a bit of a cheesy story and some bad acting.  After listing to a laughably bad impression of a drunk guy, I meet my ex-girlfriend and get an exposition dump to explain the start of the game.  So about the first 10 minutes of my hour long review is spent in the opening cutscenes.
Eventually though I end up on a planet and find myself in trouble in no time.  I quickly discover this game has all of the hallmarks of a standard shooter.  It starts me with a crappy melee weapon and slowly but surely I find better weapons to upgrade to.  And it's all the weapons you'd expect to see from pistols, to shotguns, to assault rifles and grenades.
Along with some rather bad acting and dialogue, everytime I would pick up a weapon, the game would tell me "Picked Pistol".  Not picked up.  I started to feel like I was playing Pokemon.  Pistol, I choose you!  Shotgun, I choose you!
The enemy AI seemed pretty dumb, although they were all good shots, so it still added some difficulty to the combat.  You definitely want to quick save the game often, as you will be reloading a lot.  But not necessarily because you died in combat.  Once I had to reload because the entire game crashed.  Another time I was crawling through an airduct (another hallmark of a first person shooter), and I somehow managed to crawl through a fan without the game registering a collision.  So I kept crawling through the airduct but then I ran out of level, and fell out of the world.  Some games when you fall out of the world it will 'reset' you to a nearby save spot.  This game just kills you dead.
The game lets you interact with items in the game, although most of the time it serves no purpose.  There was one time I had to drop a sheet of aluminum over a hole in the floor to run across it.  A few times I opened up air ducts or lockers.  But a lot of objects were just randomly lying around like books or boxes.
My favorite though was the random basketball I ran across.  Not only that but I found it in a room with a basketball hoop.  I wasted several minutes trying in vain to make a shot.  It's hard to actually throw items in the game.  All you can do is drop things, but if you happen to be moving your mouse as you drop it, you can kind of 'fling' things around.  In the end, all I succeeded in doing was get the basketball stuck in mid air.  I even tried shooting it down with my assault rifle, but it wasn't going anywhere.
Between the crash, the glitches, and the bad dialog, you're probably thinking this isn't a very good game, and you'd be right.  The only charm it has is in that B-movie vibe you get from the story, but even then it's pretty cheesy and there are some gaps in logic that make it hard to ignore.
Like Pablo.  Pablo is a character you meet, who is kind of charming with his broken English.  He gets shot during a cutscene and goes on about his shot leg and how he can't go with you.  Then the cut scene ends, and there is Pablo standing up on both legs, watching as I leave.   Meanwhile, 5 feet away is a med station.  I guess the med stations don't work on bulletholes in legs or something.
It's not so much that I dislike Alpha Prime, but there's really just nothing particularly redeeming about it.  There are simply much better games out there to spend your time on.
Overall Recommendation:  Pass

Jackie did not want the Darkness to return - under the circumstances, however, he needs to rely on them and throughout the game you need to find out who and why attacked you in the restaurant.
With the tentacles you can also pick up objects - e.g. the door of a vehicle - and throw them at your enemies. And as you can do some dual wielding with the firearms you can practically say you are doing quad wielding with the two tendrils. How cooler can a game be, am I right? With the killings you can collect what the game calls essence; a substance that eventually lets you purchase new powers or the upgraded version of the ones you already have. It should also be note that as the title refers to it darkness is also Jackie's ally - if you are in an illuminated area the tentacles immediately retract.
Darkness II is a fast-paced action horror game that utilises a cel-shading technique to give the game a comic book influenced visual style. Multiplayer is limited to cooperative gameplay that does not really add anything to the story but lets you enjoy quad wielding with your friends.
I highly recommend it - for 30 EUR it's a bit too much at the moment but you should definitely pick this one up if discounted.

I only play when one or both of my brothers play, so I think that adds to its ability to be fun. Without someone to play with it might not be as enjoyable, but I can't say for sure since I have never played solo. The gameplay itself is solid enough, but you can tell it just came out by some of the balancing and bugs. For example, the server browser used to take over 5 minutes to load, and you couldn't move your mouse or do anything at all until all the servers were loaded. Sometimes you could wind up checking a ton of houses before finding anything, but other times you find a bunch of great items, and then immediateky find more, sometimes multiple times in a row. The store and global inventory are nice; neither the in-game costs nor IRL cash cost of things is too high, and you can buy everything(?) with in-game cash that you can get with IRL cash, and also the global inventory is nice to be able to store stuff for crafting that you don't need to carry all the time or items/weapons for successive lives if you happen to die and lose everything. It's a lot more closed-in, has a smaller map, and is more fast-paced than DayZ (I believe); there are various monsters as opposed to only zombies; and there's a clan system which doesn't eliminate PvP, but at least limits it (for the most part) to players only killing members of other clans. I met a random player from the same clan and he adventured with me without killing me until I died by nether creatures and quit the game.
(When I say DayZ, I mean the Arma II mod, which is the only DayZ I have played, and I'm assuming it plays similar to the standalone DayZ.)

Despite what I go on to talk about, I absolutely love this game and it is♥♥♥♥♥♥tons of fun. However, there are a multitude of issues.
First of all, the servers. Oh god, the servers. For Honor uses a Peer to Peer system, saving Ubisoft a few petty dollars and making the players responsible for hosting servers. This makes for some very dodgy connections and pauses in the middle of games.
Another issue right now is memory leaks. I don't personally know anybody else with this issue, but there are plenty of forum posts about the same exact issue. Basically the game fails to dump memory it doesn't need, and For Honor's RAM usage grows exponentially , until the game freezes, forcing you to restart your PC.
I also find it funny that a game titled "For Honor" produces some of the most dishonorable gameplay that can be found today. The game provides players with ledges to throw opponents off of, providing an instant win. Players will also team up on their opponents, making it almost impossible for the odd one out to be victorious.
Other than that, this game is pretty fun at the moment and has me hooked. If you are not a very picky person, I would strongly recommend picking up this game.

Yes they rushed it so they could make it 50%-80% off but thats because they wanted their community of people to grow so they can fill their servers and actualy LOOK at the game rather than writing it off their list because of some bad reviews. Over the past bit of hours i have died alot and won more back. Im not mad... im not taking this to the review to rage saying "WTF HACKS EVERYWHERE GGWP" no im here to say that this game is absoluetly amazing for a people who enjoy having excitement when in the face of danger, getting stuff to be better than everyone else, sniper elite mlg360noscopers. Now onto the actual review and not me just spouting nonsense. The game is buggy, it has problems, pvp is broken as hell, its hard to get money, everything is too expensive, it takes to long to do everything and you lose everything upon death (not including cosmetics) You see some disadvantages of a game that was rushed for the summer sale. Being in a group makes it fun, meet other people, kill other people, watch somebody being chased by 3 golems, being chased by 3 golems, doing raid boss like events, free-for-all capture the flag and more of positive things you can find if you give this game that requires grinding some ACTUAL time other than playing for 1-12 hours and writing it as a DO NOT BUY game. The Devs should read it and make it better for people to play. I do agree that this long into development they haven't fixed alot of things and that makes them looked down upon on.
To end it off. Buy it if it fits your taste, give it some time and you'll enjoy the thrill it has to offer. Think of it as one of those MMORPGs where you have to grind some exp off farming monsters, and think of it as league of legends, you start at lvl 1 get to lvl 18 win/lose means death in nether and start again! its pretty fun if you think of it in these ways. First off, I've never been a big fan of horror/survival simulators, however I have enjoyed some games, notably, Amnesia, Layers of Fear, Alien: Isolation, Resident Evil and/or even The Long Dark.
However all the great choices, strategies and storylines that make those games great were copied, warped and distressed until we're left with the bones of a good game.
The "story" of SOMA (that so many on Steam tout as the selling point of SOMA) crept by like an ancient slug and at the end of this slime was a very sad and utterly depressing picture of disability and entropy.
Nothing made any sense for hours, forcing strange choices and dialogue without knowledge or purpose; only to reveal that the endless monotony you had endured revealed no pleasant surprises, or intrigue. They hand you overwhelming torment, a big letdown and then its over.
The lack of tutorials leave you wasting resources by trying them out and dying ten times before you figure out you had to open a door first and then pull a lever second, not the other way around.
The entire time I had no option to wield weapons, carry a realistic inventory or lure enemies into traps.
You must simply watch enemies from some corner, decide when to sprint and try to pull a switch, open a door, activate a generator before these enemies see you.
OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND...OVER AGAIN.
Vague and intriguing moral choices built into the game are surprising and feel fun at first.
However, making Choice A over Choice B yields no different or apparent results than making Choice B.
This game is a interactive click-fest, so many objects can be wielded, drawers open, books, drawings and notes can be picked up, rotated and looked at, even tools you have in the game and instruction booklets are interactive in real time as opposed to opening in a game UI screen.
This is a great style choice, but again it led to SO much confusion.
Staring at drawings that have random scribble all over them and trying to decipher what random word means anything leads you to wandering all over a single room for 30 minutes trying to figure out if a drawing of a switch, code or diagram matches up with the room your in.
If you could carry these around with you, the game could be played in half the time.
Instead of interactivity being a beautiful selling point; it creates an annoying, boring grind in this game.
Spend your well-earned money on a better title like the ones I've listed above.

I don't even know where to begin with this game.
Supergiant have done it again. I adored Bastion and Transistor, but this one is my new favourite from their hand. Having just finished the campaign, clocking in around 12 hours (in one sitting mind you), I can say that the pacing is quite good. If you like the 'combat' in this game, then I'd encourage you to buy it. The story is phenomenal.
The 'combat':
This is about half of the time you'll be spending with the game's campaign. It's a kind of sports-like combat system, where you are trying to extinquish an enemy's Pyre (flame). The only way to do this is to carry or shoot a ball-like object into said Pyre. Once you've dealt enough damage to the Pyre, you win. The matches are always 3v3. However, there are different characters you unlock along the way. They all have different abilities and ways to play them. Some are high speed, but low damage, whereas others are high damage but low speed and such. I'd recomend you watch TotalBiscuit's video on the game to see it in action, as it's quite hard to explain the system in text form.
Overall I can end off with the combat system being a weird mix between simple and complex at the same time. I like it a lot.
Seeing as I don't want to spoil anything in this review, I'm not going to say anything else about the story. It's good. One thing to note, however, is that it is largely text based now and not narrated as in other Supergiant games. It's a lot of text as well, so be prepared to read if you want the lore of the world and the story as a whole. Some parts are still narrated, such as the matches, which have a sports-like commentator narrating them.
And last but not least, the soundtrack. I mean, what is there to say. It's a Supergiant game, what do you expect. It's great. Same level as Transistor or Bastion, whose soundtracks I adored, if not better.
TLDR:
This game is worth your time and money if you think the combat system looks interesting and you aren't afraid to read quite a lot of text.

Having played through the game end-to-end, with a handful of reloads in-between to try out different options, I feel like I've had enough time now to enjoy and put together a halfway decent review.
To preface, I loved Bastion, I played it (and the bonus/side-content) through three or four times. The music, the art style, the story, it was fantastic. The gameplay wasn't groundbreaking, but it also wasn't the focus. The world and story was, and rarely did the gameplay get in the way of that.
Transistor, on the other hand, I felt as though I spent way more time thinking about the game than enjoying the story/music/art, which to me is a major minus. I'm not buying a Supergiant game for gameplay, at least that isn't the driving force. I'm buying it for the art, music, and storytelling.
So. Pyre.
Let's get the negative bits out of the way first. I felt like the "tutorial" part of the game, which is essentially all the way up till your first liberation rite, is a little long. If it were up to me, I'd have back-loaded the longer "seasons" of the rites instead of front-loading them. That said, the snappy dialogue and likable characters make it enjoyable despite the slowness, and you'll reach your destination soon enough.
There are a couple of rite locations that can be buggy, depending on your actions, but it's nothing game breaking. I also found that the in-game things keeping track of locations you've visited and pages you've found for your book to be lacking and it makes it hard to be sure you've gotten everything.
I also feel like the end "villain(s)" were introduced a little bit late in the story, but that depends on how you look at it, and what choices you take.
Mostly, my issues are nitpicking, not any real fatal flaw.
On to the good stuff...
The rites can be a lot of fun, especially if you're rotating lineups to try and keep all your characters pretty even on XP/level (which you should). The variation in play styles, when you add in different trinkets and what-not, really allow you to figure out how you want to make your different teams work.
I especially like some of the late-game items you get from the slug market, even if they do kinda feel like joke items more than the high-risk/high-reward they're positioned as, it was entertaining to play around with them.
The cast of characters is fantastic, and while I feel like there were 1 or 2 that were sort of unnecessary, that may have been the point? Some of them have grand ambitions, others are just along for the ride, but that would make sense given that all the exiles are not created equal. You've got everyone from the corrupt rich to volunteers to rebels and war criminals, not everyone is going to be a hero or villain, some people are just trying to get by.
In the end, Pyre made me care a
about more characters than I thought I would end up caring about, so much so that I really wish I'd had more "seasons" and time to get to know them.
In summation, Pyre is great game that might be a little too long in some places, and a little too short in others, but the experience provided is more than enough to make up for any small shortcomings in one area or another.
Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have an alternate plan I need to try on another playthrough.

Something I believe I should note right off the bat is that
That doesn't mean Pyre is bad. No, it's the direct opposite of that. However, compared to their other games, this one might be harder for some to enjoy due to its heavy visual novel elements. Now that that's out of the way, I think the one word to describe how I felt after finishing this game is
Even if this is a more niche title, it doesn't change the fact that
is one of the best games 2017 has to offer.
By Supergiant standards, this is the best they've done in the visual department. While all of their games look great, this one was eye candy from start to finish. All of the different areas really set the tone, and the character designs are extremely diverse and unique. There isn't much to say here, but there isn't anything about the graphics I can fault. I don't think there's any way they could've done it better, because the game is absolutely gorgeous to look at.
Pyre's weakest aspect is its gameplay, however it's not bad at all. At worst, there was a lot of missed potential, but at best, you have an extremely interesting and unique take on football/basketball. There's no denying that Pyre's gameplay is extremely unique, and it's extremely fun. It's not completely polished, as certain characters like Ti'zo and Fae/Dae/Bae/etc. are ridiculously OP, but the concept is there and it works. I loved experimenting with the different playable exiles and adapting to the fairly dynamic (and constantly exciting) Rites, and the game encourages flexibility. That being said, the Rites themselves don't actually get all that interesting until about 1/3 of your way into the game, where more gameplay options are provided to you. It's quite understandable if you find yourself slogging through the first part of the game. But once you get passed that, the gameplay becomes far more complex and interesting. Also, it's important for me to mention, this game has awesome online multiplayer potential. I was surprised to hear this game didn't have online multiplayer, because the Rites are very enjoyable once you get through the beginning stages. Overall, the gameplay's still good, but definitely where Pyre falls short.
story made me feel a wide range of emotions. At some points, I was getting teary-eyed, and at other times I was audibly yelling at my monitor in excitement. It felt like a real journey, and it was so fascinating to watch all of these problems unfold and see how the characters respond to it. But that's where
is at its best - the characters. I loved every single one of them. Every single Nightwing who joins you is fleshed out and three-dimensional, you can tell plenty of time and care was put into making them lovable. One thing I also liked is that the game did take certain character clichés and flip them on their heads, one example being my favorite character, Rukey. The way he's portrayed at first gives you the vibe that he's going to be a shady, self-centered, and annoying prick who will want to make you bash your head into a wall. Instead, without getting too much into spoilers (but I'll censor it anyway just in case),
Anti-trends like this are pretty common with all of the characters, and it made me love everyone, even the exiles you face off against.
is probably one of the most deep and open-ended games I've ever played, with there being a ridiculous amount of lore and ways for the game to play out. It's definitely going to overwhelm some, but if you power through it, you will find that this game is very immersive and keeps you on the edge of your seat from start to finish.
Supergiant games have always had a great soundtrack to back them up, but they went above and beyond with this game. Each piece feels different and fits their intended tone. There wasn't a single piece that felt out of place. The songs with vocals, however, were the highlights. Darren Korb and Ashley Barrett have beautiful voices, and every time they sang, I got goosebumps. While some might be disappointed by the lack of Logan Cunningham's normal narrator voice, the one they had for this game fit the theme a lot better in my opinion and I was perfectly fine with him. This game's narrator especially got more entertaining as the game progresses, although explaining why would lead to spoilers. To conclude, just like the game's story and visuals, I can't find anything to fault here.
The amount of replayability in this game surprised me. There's a LOT of different outcomes to the game, and with the incredible story, I'm considering going through it again just to see what other interactions I can find between the charming ensemble of exiles. It's a shame that the game doesn't have online multiplayer, though, otherwise I would be even more hooked on this game than I already am.

is most certainly unique and an incredible experience, I think a good game that it can be compared to is

If you only ever play one horror game, make it this one.
There are so many horror games out there that go the same way, you wake up alone, abandoned, not knowing what to do and your only goal is to get out of "creepy place X." This is the same but different, you know who you are, but you suddenly find yourself wreched out of your life and in the future, in a station at the bottom of the ocean.
The horror gameplay is similar to other horror games by Frictional, there are monsters, some terrifying, some a little laughable, but you're essentially defenseless and have to figure out how to progress around the creatures with their various rules, from enemies that only see you when you see them, to blind monsters that track you through sound.
But the true value of the game are the parts between the monsters, the huge, rich story discovered through audio logs, documents, human "black-boxes" and even a rare person or two. There is nothing mandatory in the game, you can just ignore everything and progress to the end, but the decisions you make, and what you will or won't sacrifice to ensure your own safety will truly weigh on you and make you think about what sort of person you are.
It's possibly the best story in a horror game to date, and while the main character is an absolute moron at more than a few times, he's still relatable and understandable.
Seriously, even if you're the sort of person who has to play with all the lights on, the sound down low and a person with you to ensure you don't crap yourself, it's still worth it to play this, just to have the experience.

The Darkness II is a phsycological horror first-person shooter sequel to The Darkness, a console only game released back in 2009. The original game was interesting despite its flaws, and was a highly enjoyable game in terms of story and gameplay. Its sequel, The Darkness II, goes above and beyond to deliver an absolute gem of a gaming experience, and a masterpiece of the art form.
You play as Jackie Estacado, the head of a feared crime family, who is the host to an ancient evil known as The Darkness - this evil resides inside Jackie and gives him supernatural powers. Jackie constantly wrestles for control, and The Darkness forced him to stand by and watch as his girlfriend, Jenny, was murdered.
Jenny's murder is the driving force of this entire game. Throughout the game, Jackie experiences hallucinations of Jenny, and interacts with her as she if she never died. These moments are the soul of the game; Jackie and Jenny are beautifully acted, and you can genuinely feel the emotion in these scenes. This made the story a compelling and enjoyable one, and I felt personally compellled to stick this game through to the end.
In between cutscenes and interaction with Jenny and other NPC's, Jackie will engage in numerous combat situations. This game uses a unique and innovative combat system, in that the player is able to 'quad-wield'; the player is able to dual wield one handed firearms in combination with the demon tendrils produced by The Darkness. These tendrils let you rip, slash, throw, tear and stab your enemies in a variety of highly entertaining ways, but be warned that these kills are extremely gory and not for the faint hearted. In fact, the entire game is extremely dark, and contains very dark subject matter beyond the usual video game. The player also has to avoid street lights and other artificial lights and shoot them out where possible, as you cannot regenerate health or use Darkness abilities whilst in the light.
This game is beautiful in every aspect. The game engine employs a distinct comic-book inspired aesthetic like the Borderlands games, and it really helps make the game look and run nice at the higher settings. Substantial effort and polish has gone into the production of this game, and it really shows; character models look and move realistically, and environments are dazzling to look at.
In addition to the perfected single player campaign (which I have been careful not to spoil) there is a mini co-op campaign, which allows you to play with 3 friends and use a wide range of guns and abilities to kill enemies. This mode emphasises fun and action, and lacks the depth of the single player campaign. However, it was certainly fun, and I didn't feel like it detracted from the campaign in any way.
Overall, The Darkness II is a masterpiece of the gaming industry. A brilliant, well constructed tale of love and loss and eventually redemption, this is a game for the ages. I can't recommend it any more than I already have, which is why this game earns a 10 / 10.
