Just how can one express the raw emotion feelings that game has given. Not only is the horror element of the game really immersive, but the story is just beautiful. Although there isn't much to do other than a few puzzles here and there the story makes up for it by taking you on a depressing yet adrenaline rushing ride where you will always be at the edge of your seat.
This is not your typical run of the mill horror game where its all cheap jumpscares and silly props that you get used to and just laugh rather than cower in your seat. SOMA takes it so much more in depth, yeah there are a few little jumpscares but the way the ai or monsters or whatever you shall call them coincide with the extremely atmospheric settings are well done..
*Potential spoilers*
All in all my final thoughs or opinion of SOMA would be
[Story] 9/10

There is so much you learn about earth and what your going through to make humanity survive you look at everyones sacrafice and what it really took to make it all possible. It is a story with an ending that will leave you speachless while you figure out whether you made the right choices.

[Theme as a horror title] 8/10
While the scenery is just breathtakingly beautiful and rich and the music is spot on giving you that edgy feeling the ai can seem a little fun to play with. In no way am i saying they arn't terrifying because everytime I had to quietly work myself around one or more I felt no comfort other than hiding in a vent or two and laughing as I picked up a box and tossed it into the face of what seemed like a sad puppy who couldnt get to his treat! "they cant reach into vents" Few times I had a problem in which I would toss an object to distract them to have them only come straight to where i tossed it from so i guess they arn't perfect but no ai are. Overall the game is somthing to play with the lights off and headset up loud for you will be intensly focused on whats going on but its more story driven, not saying that's a bad thing!
[Overall look/ recommendation] 9/10
While i'll sound like a broken record and repeat myself this game will have you question so much and you'll spend more time reading logs, journals and listening to the final moments of people before they succumbed to their doomed fate at the bottom of the ocean! Yes it is a scary game and I would play it again if i had the chance. Even though it is more story driven it did well on my personal lust to be scared and have me checking my own sholders every once in a while! I will say at the end of the game, you will both feel accomplished and dissapointed with the aftermath SOMA plays with your emotions and did a hell of a job! *Though as a side note if you try to just push through the game without exploring you will miss out on so much! So please, remember to check every desk, locker, and corner because you might not realize how much you could easily miss!*
Grab the game when you have the chance, or add it to the wishlist for it is a gem!

Rayman Legends (Orgins) This was always a classic for me considering I first played Rayman on the PS1 as a kid. Awesome platform that always caught my attention. I'm glad to see Rayman has been remade for the PC.
This game has no graphic options at all but it doesn't need it because its a 2D platform with amazing graphics and art design. It's very well programmed and the colors are eye catching and beautiful.
The characters in the game of course is Rayman and now you can unlock Hero's to play which feels slightly different then playing Rayman. Each hero has many skins to unlock as well.
The enemys are well desgined and some look really epic and deadly.
The controls are simple. I use a USB 360 controller of course and the game's physics and mechanics are not difficult to figure out and is actually programmed rather well. The movement is simple and basic but yet one wrong move equals instant death. Game is playable to a 5 year old but becomes difficult enough for an adult while a child can still enjoy the difficulty as the game progresses.
The platforms are awesome and the levels are super creative its almost genius. Lots of hidden secrets in every level.
There are so many levels to play and unlock its insane how much work was put into the length of the game. You simply cannot get bored but many breaks will be taken.
The sound effects are neat. While the music really sells it for me. There is also an online type challenge everyday and one that lasts 7 days. You compete for the Bronze, Silver or Gold cup. Which is great if you like a good challenge.
I'm running this game on an AMD ASUS Sabertooth 990 FX, AMD 8-Core, 16gb Ram, Nvidia GT 750 2gb LP. Windows 7
no issues at all running this game or any crashes.

Alpha Prime is a terrible game, and I kind of like it that way.
It's chock full of awful encounters, you fight the same three enemies the entire game, half the guns are useless and the other half only slightly less so, and levels seem to stretch on endlessly as they blur together. "Balance? To hell with that" you can hear Black Element yell as a barely discernible enemy on the other side of the room head shots you with a shotgun. Elements from other games are unglamorously fitted into parts of the game, like a patchwork quilt of design that's been out of style for years and manages to be significantly worse still than what they were lifted from.
There do not currently exist words in the English language strong enough to properly describe the true horror that is Alpha Prime's writing, such an elongated mess of horrendous characters, dialogue unfit for a B movie, plot lines thrown out and then just left there, and a bit of casual misogyny thrown in just for flavor. It's agonizing to listen to, stilted voice acting keeping it from even being somewhat amusing, and there is so, so much of it.
Alpha Prime is bad; a masterwork of mediocrity at the best of times. But again...I kind of liked it, maybe because for as miserable as it most certainly is, it's strangely polished in ways that made it kind of endearing if only ever so slightly. It feels like a game that might have been an obscure hit a decade ago, and I guess part of me still enjoys the sort of game that is so unmistakably rubbish, but its developer still clearly put a ton of effort into making it so I'm willing to go along for the ride even as I ask myself what is wrong with me. It's not broken, well, mostly. It's just bland, tedious, uninspired and a posterchild for dreadful videogame writing (though I will definitely be using "total lamers" as an insult).
Can I recommend it? Probably not. Would I play it again? Not on your life! Do I regret playing it? I wouldn't say so.

One of my absolute favorite games of all time.  The graphics and animations show their age, but hold up a lot better than a lot of games its age.  If you enjoy the d20 system (especially D&D 3.5e), you'll really enjoy the game, as it's pretty faithful to how the system works.  Once you learn how to optimize characters, it becomes a pretty easy game, but this isn't really a game you play for the challenge of it.  The finished story is phenomenal, even more so if you're a big Star Wars fan and like the lore of the Old Republic.  The final boss is easily my favorite villain of all time, in any genre or medium.  The depth and nuance to the story in this game, both in your interactions with the NPCs and your party members, is just out-of-this-world.
That said, you absolutely need to play this game with the Restored Content Mod installed (you can find it as the top subscribed item in the Workshop for this game). It fixes all the problems the game had due to the rushed holiday release (including the buggy crashes, as I've had none after two 30-50 hour playthroughs) and fills in a ton of the missing story that may have left you scratching your head and wondering what was going on if you played at release.  If you haven't played with that mod installed, you're missing out.

The Good: Beautiful visuals, nice WWII setting
The Bad: Boring story, broken stealth mechanics, technical flaws
I have really given this game some time and I tried to forgive it. I rented this on Xbox 360 when it first came out and gave up after the second level. I bought this as a cheap Steam sale about a year ago and have just had it sitting on my HDD since then. I have gone back here and there to try to beat or continue this game. I just can't do it and have finally given up. After two years of giving this game a chance I doubt it will become better over time. The paper-thin story, poor stealth mechanics, and technical flaws just bring this promising game down.
You play as a British spy infiltrating Germany during World War II and other occupied territories for...I don't know really. The story is presented in flashbacks that don't really explain much other than why Violet is at that current location. You have various goals you have to complete, but there are enemies in between that you have to kill off or avoid. A stealth game has to have great stealth mechanics like sneaking, killing, and gadgets which Velvet fails in every category. First off, she moves way to slow when crouching. You can never catch up to enemies who are walking because they just leave her in the dust. This is extremely difficult when you are trying to quickly kill someone before you are spotted. The kill moves are pretty cool, but you have to be in the exact position the game needs you to be before you can trigger it. You also have to be extremely close which is ridiculous. This isn't Splinter Cell where you can trigger the kill at a reasonable distance.
You get a few items to help you kill these Nazis. You can use Morphine shots to become invisible, freeze time, and do an automatic kill. This is useful for a guard that has spotted so you can take him down really quick. You get a silenced pistol, but ammo is hard to come by so use it wisely. Some times you can also use a Nazi uniform as a disguise, but if you get too close to enemies they will recognize you. The game has shadow stealth which means if you hide in the shadows you will have a blue aura around you and enemies won't see you. This game has some of the dumbest enemy AI I have ever seen. You can whistle to lure a guard to some shadows but he won't see you even though you are two feet in front of him. If you are seen and try to hide the enemies know exactly where you are and you can't hide from them. What kind of lame crap is that?
The game looks good and has a nice visual art style, but there are some technical flaws here. Animations are pretty bad with some terrible sound effects. The footsteps all sounds the same and the animations just seems floaty and canned. I also found some of the guards patrols to be very long and the overall patterns are hard to work around. It's difficult to figure out how to take out enemies because there are no natural hints or obvious paths most of the time.
Overall, Velvet Assassin was a promising stealth action game set in World War II but has a pointless story, broken stealth mechanics, and some technical flaws. The game looks good, but other than that there is no reason for you to pick this up. Rent this if you want to play a stealth game with a sexy protagonist, otherwise look elsewhere.
~Score: 5.5/10

I would call this game decent in almost every aspect. The graphics are not bad for a 2007 release I think. OK, it's not Crysis but that game was way ahead of it's time. Compared to the more typical games from that year, it holds up well. The sound is probably the weakest part of the game. Guns and other sound effects are really not that interesting.
There are quite a lot of cutscenes with spoken dialogue in the game. Storyline and voice acting is again, decent. Certainly not the on the level of the more big budget releases but that's ofcourse understandable. I've seen and heard worse. The AI baddies have very limited dialogue. The "Go go go!" and "Quickly fallback!" can get on your nerves quickly, especially when you encounter larger groups. Just kill them... quickly (or fallback :)
The game lends some aspects of some well known FPS games, like the resupplying of health from dispensers on the walls, like in Half-Life. (So no health regeneration) The slowmo from F.E.A.R. although it doesn't seem to work that well, like in F.E.A.R. I ended up not using it that much.
Along the way you pickup various weapons. Nothing like we've never seen before. There's a melee weapon, pistol, shotty, machine gun, a sniper like weapon, flamethrower and rocket launcher. Oh and of course, your grenades :)
Don't expect this game to be a walk in the park. It can be really challenging on normal or hard difficulty. The AI is deadly accurate and you take a lot of damage really fast. It can lead to frustration fast if you are not careful enough.  It's not a game were you can storm into every room Rambo style to shoot everything that moves. Luckily you can quicksave the game instead of having a checkpoint system. You can also hack security camera's, often giving you the ability to see what's in another room. There's also the ability to lean, wich works well and is a welcome addition to this type of shooter.
The game doesn't do anything new or something that you will remember for years to come. It's more of a short blast. If you are into a more simplistic shooter, with above average difficulty, this is an interesting game to look at. Especially giving the fact that the game barely costs anything.
Highly recommending this game to all players looking for an rpg with a fantastic storyline and characters even if you're not a Star Wars fan.
